weeks.title: Walking by Faith When You Can't See the Way

lessons.title: Faith When the Road Ahead Is Unclear
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you've chosen to spend part of your day with me. Whether you're listening on your way to work, sitting at home with your Bible, getting ready for the day, or simply taking a few quiet moments with the Lord, I'm glad you're here.
Today is a special beginning. We've completed our six-week journey through the Faith Through the Fire Companion Workbook. Six weeks of learning, growing, praying, and studying God's Word together. And now, we're stepping into something new.
Over the next six weeks, we're going to continue building upon everything we've learned. We're going to explore what it means to trust God when life is uncertain. How to remain faithful during seasons of waiting. How to find joy even when circumstances aren't perfect. And how to prepare our hearts for Christmas and the beginning of a new year.
But today, we're beginning with something foundational. Faith.
Not faith when everything makes sense. Not faith when every prayer has already been answered. And not faith when we can see exactly where life is taking us.
We're talking about faith when the road ahead is unclear.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever been driving somewhere unfamiliar at night? Maybe you're following directions. Maybe the road is winding. And maybe there aren't many streetlights.
You can see what's directly in front of your vehicle. But you can't see every turn ahead. You don't know exactly what the road looks like five miles from where you are.
So what do you do? You keep your eyes on the road. You pay attention to the directions. And you continue moving forward carefully.
Now, sometimes our journey with God feels a little like that. We want to know what's coming next. We want to understand why certain things are happening. And we want reassurance that everything will work out exactly the way we've planned.
But faith doesn't always come with a complete picture. Sometimes it means trusting God with the next step. Even when we can't see the entire journey.
And that's what we're going to talk about today. But first, let's pray.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the opportunity to begin this new week of Bible study. Lord, today we're talking about faith. And You know that sometimes trusting You can feel difficult. Especially when we're facing uncertainty. When we're waiting for answers. Or when life isn't unfolding the way we expected. Father, help us understand what Your Word teaches about faith. Give us wisdom to recognize Your truth. Courage to obey Your instruction. And patience to trust Your timing. May everything we study today draw us closer to Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — HEBREWS 11:1 Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 11, verse 1. The King James Version says: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen."
Let's read that again. "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen."
Now, that's a familiar verse. You may have heard it preached in church. You may have memorized it when you were younger. Or maybe it's a verse you've turned to during a difficult season.
But today, I want us to slow down and think about what it actually means. Because biblical faith is more than positive thinking. It's more than wishing something would happen. And it's more than believing that every situation will turn out exactly the way we want.
Biblical faith is rooted in who God is. His character. His promises. And His faithfulness.
Now, Hebrews chapter 11 is often called the Hall of Faith. Throughout this chapter, we read about people who trusted God in extraordinary circumstances. People like Noah. Abraham. Sarah. Moses. And many others.
But here's something important. These weren't perfect people. They faced uncertainty. They experienced difficulties. And some of them struggled along the way.
Yet Scripture remembers their faith because they trusted God's promises and responded to Him.
Now, let's look at the first part of our verse. "Faith is the substance of things hoped for."
The word translated "substance" communicates assurance or confidence.
And that matters. Because Christian hope isn't simply wishful thinking. It's confidence rooted in the trustworthy God who has spoken.
Now, that doesn't mean we can confidently claim every personal desire as a promise from God. We have to distinguish between what God has actually promised in Scripture and what we personally hope will happen.
For example, we can trust God's promise of eternal life through Jesus Christ. We can trust that He hears His people. And we can trust His character even when circumstances are difficult.
But that doesn't mean every job opportunity will work out. Every relationship will be restored. Or every difficult situation will end according to our preferred timeline.
Faith isn't controlling the outcome. It's trusting God.
Now, let's look at the second part of the verse. "The evidence of things not seen."
Now, here's something I want you to understand. Biblical faith doesn't mean believing something simply because there's no evidence. The writer of Hebrews points us toward God's faithfulness and His promises.
Faith trusts the God we cannot physically see. And it responds to what He has revealed.
Now, think about that. We don't see God with our physical eyes. But through Scripture, we learn about His character. His works. His promises. And His plan of salvation through Jesus Christ.
And that gives us a foundation for trust.
KEY TRUTH Here's today's key truth. Faith means trusting God's character and promises, even when we cannot see the entire path ahead.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we confuse faith with certainty about our circumstances.
We think that if we have enough faith, we'll know exactly what's going to happen. But that's not what Scripture teaches.
Faith isn't knowing every detail of tomorrow. It's trusting the Lord who holds tomorrow.
LET'S UNDERSTAND IT TOGETHER Now, let's turn to another Scripture. Second Corinthians chapter 5, verse 7. Paul says: "For we walk by faith, not by sight."
Now, let's talk about the context. In Second Corinthians chapter 5, Paul is discussing our earthly lives and our future hope with the Lord. He reminds believers that our ultimate hope reaches beyond what we can presently see.
And that's why he says we walk by faith, not by sight.
Now, that verse is often applied to seasons of uncertainty. And there's a valuable principle there. But I want us to understand that Paul is speaking about a life shaped by confidence in God's promises, especially our hope in Christ.
Now, let's make that practical. Maybe you're facing a decision about your future. Maybe you're considering a new opportunity. Maybe you're praying about a relationship. Or maybe you're waiting for something important to happen.
Now, what does it mean to walk by faith in those circumstances? It doesn't mean ignoring wisdom. It doesn't mean refusing to make plans. And it doesn't mean making reckless decisions while assuming God will protect us from every consequence.
Walking by faith means seeking God's wisdom. Examining our decisions in light of Scripture. Praying. Listening to wise counsel. And taking faithful action with the information we have.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes faith looks like taking a step forward. And sometimes faith looks like waiting patiently.
Sometimes it means saying yes. And sometimes it means having the courage to say no.
The important thing isn't simply whether we're moving. It's whether we're seeking to honor God.
ABRAHAM — FAITH WITHOUT THE FULL MAP Now, let's look at someone who understood what it meant to walk by faith. Abraham.
In Genesis chapter 12, God called Abram to leave his country, his relatives, and his father's household. And God promised to show him the land where he was to go.
Now, think about that. Abram was being called to leave what was familiar. His home. His surroundings. And much of what he knew.
But he didn't receive a complete explanation of every challenge he would face.
Genesis chapter 12, verse 4 says: "So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him."
Now, I want you to notice something. Abram responded to God's instruction.
He didn't know every detail of the journey. But he trusted the One who had called him.
Now, Hebrews chapter 11, verse 8, reflects on that moment. It says: "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went."
Now, that's powerful. "He went out, not knowing whither he went."
Now, Abraham wasn't simply wandering without direction. He was responding to a particular command God had given him.
And that's an important distinction. Because we shouldn't assume every desire or idea we have is automatically a direct instruction from God.
But Abraham's example teaches us that genuine faith responds obediently to what God has revealed.
Now, here's a question. Have you ever wanted God to show you the entire plan before you were willing to take the next step?
Maybe you've prayed... "Lord, just show me how everything is going to work out."
"Show me what happens next." "Show me when things are going to change." "Show me how this is going to end."
Now, I think many of us can relate to that. Because uncertainty can be uncomfortable.
But sometimes the most faithful thing we can do is obey what we already know Scripture teaches while trusting God with what we don't yet understand.
FAITH DOESN'T MEAN WE NEVER FEEL AFRAID Now, I want to talk about something important. Because sometimes people think having faith means never feeling afraid.
But that's not true.
You can trust God and still feel nervous about a difficult situation. You can have faith and still grieve. You can believe God's promises and still have questions.
Faith doesn't require us to pretend that our emotions don't exist.
Now, think about the Psalms. Throughout Scripture, we see God's people expressing fear, sorrow, confusion, and distress.
But we also see them bringing those emotions before the Lord.
And that's something we can learn from.
When we're afraid, we don't have to hide that fear from God. We can pray honestly. We can ask for wisdom. And we can remember His faithfulness.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Courage isn't always the absence of fear. Sometimes courage means doing what is right even when we're afraid.
And faith can help us find that courage.
PROVERBS 3:5–6 — TRUSTING GOD WITH OUR DIRECTION Now, let's turn to Proverbs chapter 3, verses 5 and 6. The King James Version says: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."
Now, I love these verses. Because they remind us that our understanding is limited.
We don't always know what the future holds. We don't always understand why circumstances change. And we don't always recognize the best decision immediately.
But God calls us to trust Him.
Now, let's look at the phrase... "Lean not unto thine own understanding."
That doesn't mean we should stop thinking. It doesn't mean we should ignore facts. And it doesn't mean we should refuse wise advice.
It means we shouldn't treat our own limited perspective as the highest authority.
Instead, we seek God's wisdom.
And we acknowledge Him in our decisions.
Now, here's something practical. When you're facing uncertainty, ask yourself three questions. First... What does Scripture teach that applies to this situation?
Second... What wise counsel or reliable information do I need before making a decision?
And third... Am I willing to obey God even if the right choice isn't the easiest choice?
Now, those questions won't always give us an immediate answer. But they can help us approach decisions faithfully.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's take a moment to pray. Heavenly Father, You know the uncertainties we're facing. You know the decisions we're trying to make. And You know the questions we're carrying. Lord, help us trust You with what we cannot see. Give us wisdom to recognize what is right. Courage to obey Your Word. And patience when answers don't come as quickly as we'd like. Father, when fear begins to overwhelm us, remind us of Your faithfulness. And help us continue walking with Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
WHEN THE ROAD CHANGES UNEXPECTEDLY Now, I want us to talk about something that many people experience. Unexpected changes.
Sometimes we make plans. We work hard. We pray. And we believe we're moving in the right direction.
But then something happens that changes everything.
Maybe a door closes. Maybe we receive difficult news. Maybe a relationship changes. Or maybe life takes a direction we never expected.
Now, those moments can be difficult. Because suddenly, the future looks different from what we imagined.
And sometimes we ask... "Lord, what am I supposed to do now?"
Now, here's something I want you to remember. An unexpected change doesn't mean God has stopped being faithful.
And it doesn't necessarily mean we've done something wrong.
We live in a world where difficult things happen. And sometimes circumstances change for reasons we don't fully understand.
But we can continue seeking God's wisdom through those changes.
Now, I've learned something through my own journey. Sometimes the hardest part of faith isn't believing that God exists. It's trusting Him when life looks nothing like what we expected.
There have been seasons in my life when I had questions. Seasons when I was grieving. And seasons when I couldn't understand why certain things were happening.
But those experiences have taught me the importance of returning to Scripture. Of praying honestly. And of remembering that God's character doesn't change simply because my circumstances do.
Now, I don't claim to understand every difficult thing I've experienced. And I don't believe we should pretend that every painful situation has an easy explanation.
But I do believe we can continue trusting God even when we don't have every answer.
And maybe someone listening today needs that reminder.
You may not know what tomorrow holds. You may still be waiting for an answer. And you may not understand why your plans have changed.
But you can take the next faithful step.
THE LAMP FOR OUR FEET Now, let's return to a Scripture we studied during Week Six. Psalm 119, verse 105. It says: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
Now, think about that picture. A lamp provides light. It helps us recognize where we're stepping. And it allows us to move forward more safely.
But a lamp doesn't necessarily illuminate everything in the distance.
Sometimes it simply helps us see the path immediately before us.
Now, that's a beautiful reminder of the guidance Scripture provides.
God's Word teaches us His truth. It reveals what honors Him. And it helps us recognize the path of faithful obedience.
Now, we may not know every detail of the future. But we can know how God calls us to live today.
We can practice kindness. We can pursue honesty. We can forgive. We can pray. We can seek wisdom. And we can love others.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to understand every step of your future to obey God today.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions. If you're using a journal, this is a wonderful time to write down your thoughts. And if you're listening while driving, you can return to these questions later.
Our first question is... What uncertainty am I facing right now?
Maybe it's something involving your family. Your health. Your work. Your finances. Or your future.
Take a moment to identify what feels uncertain. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Am I trusting God's character, or am I demanding certainty about the outcome?
Now, that's an important distinction. Because sometimes we think we're trusting God when we're actually trying to control what happens.
But biblical faith invites us to surrender our need for complete control.
Our third question is... What has God already revealed in Scripture that can guide my next step?
Maybe you need to act with honesty. Maybe you need to seek wise counsel. Maybe you need to practice patience. Or maybe you need to stop delaying something you already know is right. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What would faithful obedience look like today?
Not next month. Not next year. Today.
Maybe it's having a difficult conversation. Maybe it's taking responsibility for something. Maybe it's asking for help. Or maybe it's choosing to wait instead of making a rushed decision.
Now, take a moment and think about that. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION Now, I want us to bring everything back to Jesus. Because Christian faith isn't simply confidence that life will improve. It's trust in Jesus Christ.
Our hope rests in His life. His death on the cross. And His resurrection.
And through Him, we have the promise of salvation and eternal life.
Now, think about the disciples. They followed Jesus. They listened to His teaching. And they witnessed His miracles.
But when Jesus was arrested and crucified, they experienced fear and confusion.
They didn't fully understand what was happening.
Yet the resurrection revealed that God's saving purpose was being accomplished through events they had struggled to comprehend.
Now, that doesn't mean every difficult situation in our lives will have the same kind of dramatic resolution. But it reminds us that our hope is rooted in the risen Christ.
And that's the foundation of our faith.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You don't have to know everything about tomorrow to trust the God who has revealed Himself through Jesus Christ.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we become discouraged when we don't have all the answers.
But faith isn't a test of how much uncertainty we can tolerate without emotion. It's a growing relationship of trust in the Lord.
And when you struggle, you can bring that struggle before Him.
LIVING IT OUT Now, let's make today's lesson practical. I want you to choose one uncertainty you're facing.
Write it down. Then write a prayer about it.
Now, after you've prayed, ask yourself... What is one faithful action I can take today?
Maybe you need to gather information. Maybe you need to speak with someone. Maybe you need to study Scripture. Or maybe you need to be patient while circumstances develop.
Now, remember. Trusting God doesn't mean refusing to act. And it doesn't mean acting without wisdom.
It means seeking to honor Him in whatever step comes next.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the uncertainty I'm carrying today is...
Take a moment to finish that sentence.
Our second prompt is... One truth from Scripture that helps me trust You is...
And our third prompt is... The next faithful step I can take is...
Now, if you're writing these down, don't rush. Take time to pray over your answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I may not see the entire road ahead, but I can trust the God who guides my steps through His Word.
Now, say that again. I may not see the entire road ahead, but I can trust the God who guides my steps through His Word.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Second Corinthians chapter 5, verse 7. "For we walk by faith, not by sight."
And each morning this week, pray: "Lord, help me trust You with what I cannot see and obey You in what I already know."
Now, throughout the day, pay attention to opportunities to practice faithful obedience.
AROUND THE FIRE Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire. Everyone has had an opportunity to share. And I ask you this question. What is one time in your life when you had to move forward without knowing how everything would work out?
Now, think about that experience. What did you learn? How did you respond? And looking back, what would you want to remember if you faced another uncertain season? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something else to consider. What would you say to someone who's struggling to trust God because their future feels uncertain?
Maybe you'd remind them of God's faithfulness. Maybe you'd encourage them to pray. Maybe you'd help them find a Scripture to study. Or maybe you'd simply sit beside them and listen.
Because sometimes people don't need us to explain everything. Sometimes they need compassion, encouragement, and someone willing to walk beside them.
CLOSING REFLECTION Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought. You may be standing at the beginning of a road you've never traveled before.
Maybe it's a new opportunity. A difficult decision. A season of waiting. Or a change you never expected.
And maybe you're wondering what comes next.
Now, I can't promise that every road will be easy. I can't promise that every question will be answered immediately. And I can't promise that everything will happen according to your plans.
But I can point you toward the God who has revealed His faithfulness through Scripture and through Jesus Christ.
And I can encourage you to keep seeking Him.
Keep praying. Keep studying His Word. Keep asking for wisdom. And keep taking faithful steps.
Because faith isn't about seeing the entire journey. It's about trusting God as we walk.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for reminding us that faith is rooted in Your character and promises. Lord, You know the uncertainties each of us is facing. You know the questions we carry. The decisions we're trying to make. And the situations we cannot control. Father, help us trust You. Not because we know exactly what tomorrow will bring. But because we know You are faithful. Give us wisdom when we need direction. Courage when obedience feels difficult. Patience when we must wait. And humility when we need correction. Lord, I pray for the person listening today who's facing a difficult decision. Help them seek wise counsel and make choices that honor You. I pray for the person who's waiting for an answer. Give them strength for today. I pray for the person who's afraid of what the future may hold. Remind them of Your love and faithfulness. And I pray for the person who's struggling to understand why life has changed. Help them bring their questions before You honestly. Father, thank You for Jesus Christ. Thank You for His perfect life. His sacrifice on the cross. And His resurrection. May our faith remain firmly rooted in Him. And may we continue walking according to Your Word. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Seven, Day One. And I'm excited about everything we're going to study together during these next six weeks.
Tomorrow, we're going to continue our study of walking by faith. And we'll talk about what happens when God calls us to take the next step before we feel completely ready. Our lesson will be called... Taking the Next Step — Obedience Before Understanding.
Until then, remember... You don't have to understand every detail of tomorrow to walk faithfully with God today. Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep trusting the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Taking the Next Step: Obedience Before Understanding
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you've chosen to spend part of your day with me. Whether you're listening on your way to work, getting ready for the day, sitting at home with your Bible, or simply taking a few quiet moments with the Lord, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Seven, Day Two of our journey together. And we're continuing our study called Walking by Faith When You Can't See the Way.
Yesterday, we talked about faith when the road ahead is unclear. We studied Hebrews chapter 11, verse 1. And we learned that biblical faith isn't simply wishing for something to happen. It's trusting the character and promises of God.
We also learned that faith doesn't always mean knowing what tomorrow holds. Sometimes it means trusting God with the next step.
But today, we're going to take that lesson a little further. Because there's something that often comes after faith. And that's obedience.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever known what you needed to do, but you kept putting it off because you didn't feel ready?
Maybe it was having a difficult conversation. Making an important decision. Taking responsibility for something. Or stepping into an opportunity that felt bigger than you.
You knew something needed to happen. But you wanted more time. More information. More reassurance. Or maybe you simply wanted to feel completely comfortable before taking action.
Now, I think many of us can relate to that. Because uncertainty can make obedience feel difficult.
Sometimes we want God to explain everything before we're willing to move. We want to know how the situation will turn out. We want to know what challenges we'll face. And we want to know whether we'll feel prepared when we get there.
But here's something we're going to discover today. Faithful obedience doesn't always require complete understanding.
Now, I want to be careful with that statement. Because it doesn't mean we should make reckless decisions. It doesn't mean we should ignore wisdom. And it certainly doesn't mean that every idea or feeling we have is automatically a command from God.
But when God has clearly revealed something through His Word, we're called to respond faithfully. Even when obedience feels uncomfortable.
And today, we're going to look at a man who understood that. Abraham.
Our lesson is called Taking the Next Step — Obedience Before Understanding. And our main passage is Genesis chapter 12, verses 1 through 4. But first, let's pray together.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the opportunity to learn what it means to walk faithfully with You. Lord, You know that sometimes we hesitate. Sometimes we're afraid of making mistakes. Sometimes we want every answer before we're willing to take the next step. And sometimes we struggle to obey what we already know is right. Father, give us humble hearts today. Help us understand Your Word. Give us wisdom to recognize what You have truly commanded. And courage to respond with faithful obedience. May everything we study draw us closer to Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — GENESIS 12:1–4 Now, let's turn to Genesis chapter 12. Before we read, I want to give you a little background.
At this point in Genesis, we've already read about creation. The entrance of sin into the world. The flood. And the scattering of people following the events at Babel.
Now, beginning in Genesis chapter 12, the focus shifts toward Abram. The man who would later be called Abraham.
And God begins unfolding His promises through Abram and his descendants.
Now, let's read Genesis chapter 12, verses 1 through 4, from the King James Version. "Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed. So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran."
Now, let's slow down and think about what we've just read. God called Abram to leave what was familiar. His country. His relatives. And his father's household.
And God told him to go to a land that He would show him.
Now, think about that. Abram wasn't being handed a detailed travel itinerary. He wasn't given a complete explanation of every challenge he would face. And he wasn't told exactly how every part of the journey would unfold.
But he was given something far more important. A promise from God.
And in verse 4, we read these words. "So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him."
Now, that's the part I want us to focus on today. Abram departed.
He responded to God's instruction.
And that brings us to our first important truth.
KEY TRUTH Faithful obedience means responding to what God has revealed, even when we don't understand everything that lies ahead.
Now, let's talk about that. Because sometimes we confuse obedience with certainty.
We think that before we can obey, we need to know exactly what will happen.
But Abram's example reminds us that we can trust God's character even when the future isn't completely clear.
Now, here's something important. Abram had received a particular command from God. That doesn't mean every believer should leave their home or make a major life change simply because they feel restless.
We need to interpret Scripture carefully. And we need to distinguish between God's clear commands and our own personal impressions or desires.
But the principle of faithful obedience still applies.
When Scripture teaches us to be honest, we should pursue honesty. When Scripture teaches us to forgive, we should take forgiveness seriously. When Scripture calls us to love others, we should look for ways to show that love.
And when following Jesus requires us to make difficult choices, we can ask God for the courage to obey.
ABRAHAM'S FIRST STEP Now, let's imagine what Abram's situation might have felt like.
He was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
Now, think about that. At an age when many people might expect life to become more settled, Abram was beginning a major journey.
He was leaving familiar surroundings. And he was traveling toward a land God had promised to show him.
Now, the Bible doesn't tell us every thought Abram had. We shouldn't pretend to know exactly what he was feeling.
But we can recognize that this was a significant act of obedience.
And Hebrews chapter 11 helps us understand its importance. Let's turn to Hebrews chapter 11, verse 8. It says: "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went."
Now, I want you to notice the connection. "By faith Abraham... obeyed."
Faith and obedience belong together.
Now, that doesn't mean our obedience earns salvation. Scripture teaches that salvation is by God's grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
But genuine faith changes the way we respond to God.
When we trust Him, we want to take His Word seriously.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Obedience isn't simply about doing something difficult. It's about responding faithfully to God's truth.
WHEN WE WANT THE WHOLE PLAN Now, let's talk about something many of us struggle with. Wanting to know the whole plan.
Have you ever prayed... "Lord, just tell me how this is going to work out."
"Show me what happens next." "Tell me how long I'm going to have to wait." "Help me understand why this is happening."
Now, those are understandable questions. Because uncertainty can be uncomfortable.
We like to plan. We like to prepare. And we like to know what to expect.
But sometimes life doesn't give us that kind of clarity.
Maybe you're waiting for an important answer. Maybe you're facing a decision about your future. Maybe you're trying to rebuild something that has been damaged. Or maybe you're stepping into a new responsibility.
Now, in those situations, it's wise to gather information. It's wise to pray. And it's wise to seek counsel from trustworthy people.
But here's something important. We shouldn't allow our desire for perfect certainty to keep us from doing what we already know is right.
For example... Maybe you know you need to apologize to someone. But you're waiting until the conversation feels comfortable.
Maybe you know you need to be honest about a situation. But you're afraid of the consequences.
Or maybe you know someone needs practical help. But you keep waiting for a more convenient time.
Now, those are everyday situations where obedience can require courage.
And here's something I want you to remember. Sometimes the next faithful step is small.
It may not involve moving to another country. Starting a ministry. Or making a dramatic life change.
Sometimes it's simply choosing to do what is right today.
PROVERBS 3:5–6 — TRUSTING BEYOND OUR UNDERSTANDING Now, let's turn to Proverbs chapter 3, verses 5 and 6. It says: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."
Now, we read these verses yesterday. But I want us to return to them because they connect so beautifully with today's lesson.
The writer tells us to trust in the Lord with all our hearts.
Not simply when things make sense. Not simply when the path is easy. And not simply when we're confident about the outcome.
We're called to trust Him.
Now, let's look at the phrase... "Lean not unto thine own understanding."
That doesn't mean we should stop thinking. It doesn't mean we should ignore facts. And it doesn't mean we should refuse wise advice.
It means we recognize that our own understanding is limited.
We don't see everything. We don't know everything. And we don't always understand the consequences of every decision.
But God is perfectly wise.
And His Word gives us a trustworthy foundation for living.
Now, here's something practical. When you're facing a decision, ask yourself... What does Scripture teach about this?
What wise counsel do I need?
What information am I missing?
And am I willing to do what is right, even if it isn't the easiest choice?
Now, those questions can help us approach decisions with wisdom and humility.
OBEDIENCE DOESN'T ALWAYS FEEL COMFORTABLE Now, I want to talk about something important. Because sometimes we think that if God wants us to do something, it will automatically feel easy.
But Scripture doesn't teach that.
Obedience can require sacrifice. It can require patience. And it can require courage.
Think about Abraham. He left familiar surroundings.
Think about Moses. He was called to confront Pharaoh.
Think about Esther. She faced a dangerous decision when she approached the king on behalf of her people.
Now, their circumstances were different. But each example reminds us that faithfulness can require courage.
And here's something important. Feeling nervous doesn't automatically mean you're making the wrong decision.
But feeling excited doesn't automatically mean you're making the right one, either.
That's why we need wisdom. Prayer. Scripture. And careful discernment.
Now, I want you to remember this. We shouldn't measure God's will simply by how comfortable a decision feels.
We should examine whether our choices are consistent with His Word.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's take a moment to pray together. Heavenly Father, You know the decisions we're facing. You know the areas where we're hesitant. And You know the things we're afraid to address. Lord, give us wisdom. Help us recognize what Your Word clearly teaches. Give us courage to obey. And protect us from confusing our own desires with Your instruction. Father, help us trust You without becoming careless or impatient. And teach us to walk faithfully with Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
PETER — OBEDIENCE AFTER DISAPPOINTMENT Now, let's look at another example of obedience. This time, from the life of Peter.
Turn with me to Luke chapter 5.
Jesus was teaching near the lake of Gennesaret. And He saw fishermen washing their nets.
Now, Simon Peter and the others had been fishing through the night. But they hadn't caught anything.
Now, think about that. They had worked. They had spent time and effort. And they had nothing to show for it.
Then Jesus told Simon to go out into the deep water and let down the nets.
Now, listen to Peter's response in Luke chapter 5, verse 5. "And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net."
Now, I love that phrase. "Nevertheless at thy word."
Peter acknowledged the difficulty. He acknowledged that they had already worked all night. But he also responded to Jesus' instruction.
Now, the passage tells us that they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to break.
But here's something important. The point of this passage isn't that every act of obedience will produce an immediate material reward.
The miracle reveals Jesus' authority. And it leads into His calling of Peter and the others to follow Him.
Now, here's what I want us to notice. Peter's obedience was grounded in the word of Jesus.
He wasn't simply taking a random chance. He was responding to the Lord.
And that's the lesson for us.
We should seek to obey what Christ has taught.
Even when obedience challenges our preferences. Even when it requires humility. And even when we don't fully understand the outcome.
WHEN OBEDIENCE REQUIRES PATIENCE Now, here's something else I want us to consider. Sometimes obedience means taking action. But sometimes obedience means waiting.
And waiting can be difficult.
Maybe you're waiting for an opportunity. Maybe you're waiting for a situation to change. Or maybe you're waiting for an answer to prayer.
Now, sometimes we become so frustrated with waiting that we're tempted to force something to happen.
We want to take control. We want to speed up the process. And we want to make the uncertainty disappear.
But here's something important. Not every delay is a command to act. And not every opportunity is one we should pursue.
Sometimes faithful obedience means exercising patience.
It means refusing to compromise our integrity. It means continuing to do what is right. And it means trusting God while circumstances develop.
Now, we're going to spend more time talking about waiting in Week Eight. But today, I want you to remember that obedience isn't always dramatic.
Sometimes it looks like quiet faithfulness.
JAMES 1:22 — DOING WHAT WE KNOW Now, let's turn to James chapter 1, verse 22. It says: "But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves."
Now, we studied this verse during our earlier weeks together. But it fits perfectly with today's lesson.
Because James reminds us that hearing God's Word isn't enough. We must also respond to it.
Now, think about that. We can listen to sermons. Attend Bible studies. Read devotionals. And memorize Scripture.
But if we're unwilling to apply what we learn, we're missing an essential part of discipleship.
Now, here's something I want you to consider. Is there an area of your life where you already know what Scripture teaches, but you've been hesitant to put it into practice?
Maybe it's forgiveness. Maybe it's honesty. Maybe it's controlling your words. Or maybe it's showing compassion toward someone who's struggling.
Now, don't answer that question with condemnation. Answer it with honesty.
Because recognizing an area where we need to grow is an opportunity to turn toward God.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions. If you're using a journal, take a moment to write down your answers. And if you're listening while driving, you can return to these questions later.
Our first question is... What does Abraham's obedience teach me about trusting God?
Maybe it reminds you that you don't have to understand every detail before responding to God's Word. Maybe it teaches you the importance of trusting God's promises. Or maybe it reminds you that faith requires action. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Is there something I know is right, but I've been delaying because it feels uncomfortable?
Now, take a moment to think about that. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... Am I seeking God's wisdom, or am I simply looking for reassurance that my own plans will succeed?
Now, that's an important distinction. Because sometimes we pray for guidance when we've already decided what we want to do.
But faithful discernment requires humility. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What would one small act of obedience look like today?
Maybe it's having a conversation. Maybe it's telling the truth. Maybe it's offering forgiveness. Or maybe it's choosing patience. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus. Because Abraham's obedience points us toward a larger biblical story.
God promised Abraham that through him, all the families of the earth would be blessed.
And the New Testament helps us understand how God's promise finds its fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
Galatians chapter 3, verse 16, connects God's promise to Abraham with Christ.
Now, that's important. Because the story of Abraham isn't simply about a man who made a courageous decision. It's part of God's unfolding plan of redemption.
And that plan leads us to Jesus.
Now, think about Christ's obedience. Jesus perfectly obeyed the Father's will.
And through His death and resurrection, salvation is made available to those who place their faith in Him.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our obedience doesn't make us our own saviors. Jesus Christ is our Savior.
We obey because we belong to Him. Because we love Him. And because His grace is transforming our lives.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You don't have to understand every detail of God's plan to obey the truth He has already revealed.
Now, think about that. Because sometimes we become so focused on what we don't know that we overlook what Scripture has already taught us.
We know we're called to love others. We know we're called to pursue truth. We know we're called to pray. And we know we're called to follow Jesus.
Now, those are things we can practice today.
LIVING IT OUT Now, let's make today's lesson practical. I want you to identify one area where you need to take a faithful next step.
Maybe it's something you've been avoiding. Maybe it's a responsibility you need to address. Or maybe it's a habit you want to begin.
Now, write it down. Then ask yourself three questions. Is this consistent with Scripture? Have I sought the wisdom and information I need? And what is one responsible step I can take today?
Now, remember. The goal isn't to rush into a major decision. It's to practice faithful obedience.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, one area where I've been hesitant to obey is...
Our second prompt is... The fear or uncertainty I've been carrying is...
And our third prompt is... One faithful step I can take today is...
Now, take time to pray over your answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek God's wisdom, trust His Word, and take the next faithful step with courage and humility.
Now, say that again. I will seek God's wisdom, trust His Word, and take the next faithful step with courage and humility.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize the final part of Genesis chapter 12, verse 4. "So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him."
Now, throughout the day, ask yourself... Am I willing to respond to what God has clearly taught me?
And choose one practical act of obedience.
Maybe it's an act of kindness. Maybe it's a step toward reconciliation where doing so is appropriate and safe. Maybe it's choosing honesty. Or maybe it's simply spending time in prayer and Scripture.
Whatever you choose, let it be an expression of faithfulness to Christ.
AROUND THE FIRE Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire. And I ask you this question. Can you remember a time when doing the right thing required courage?
Maybe you had to speak honestly. Maybe you had to make a difficult decision. Or maybe you had to take responsibility for something.
Now, think about that experience. What made it difficult? What helped you move forward? And what did you learn? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would you say to someone who's afraid to take the next step because they don't feel completely ready?
Maybe you'd encourage them to pray. Seek wisdom. Study Scripture. And remember that they don't have to understand everything before doing what is right.
CLOSING REFLECTION Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought. Sometimes we spend so much time waiting for perfect circumstances that we miss opportunities to practice faithfulness in ordinary moments.
We want to feel ready. We want to feel confident. And we want every question answered.
But sometimes the next step is already clear.
Maybe it's an apology. A truthful conversation. An act of kindness. Or a decision to begin a healthier habit.
Now, those steps may seem small. But faithful obedience matters.
And here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to become fearless before you can do what is right.
You can acknowledge your uncertainty. Seek God's wisdom. And move forward with humility and courage.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for the example of Abraham. And thank You for reminding us that faith and obedience belong together. Lord, You know the areas where we're hesitant. You know the decisions we're facing. And You know the things we're afraid to address. Father, give us wisdom. Help us recognize what Scripture teaches. Give us courage to obey what is right. And patience when we need to wait. Lord, protect us from making careless decisions. Help us seek wise counsel. And teach us to distinguish between our own desires and Your revealed truth. Father, I pray for the person listening today who's facing a difficult decision. Give them clarity and wisdom. I pray for the person who's afraid to take responsibility for something. Give them courage and humility. I pray for the person who's waiting for an answer. Help them remain patient and faithful. And I pray for the person who's struggling to trust You because the future feels uncertain. Remind them of Your character and promises. Father, thank You for Jesus Christ. Thank You for His perfect obedience. His sacrifice on the cross. And His resurrection. May our faith remain firmly rooted in Him. And may our lives increasingly reflect His love and truth. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Seven, Day Two. And I hope today's lesson has encouraged you to think about what faithful obedience looks like in your everyday life.
Tomorrow, we're going to continue our study of walking by faith. And we're going to talk about something that many of us struggle with. Fear.
Our lesson will be called... Faith Over Fear — Trusting God When You're Afraid.
We'll explore what Scripture teaches about fear, courage, and trusting God's presence during difficult seasons.
Until then, remember... You don't have to understand every detail of tomorrow to obey God today. Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep taking the next faithful step.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Faith Over Fear: Trusting God When You're Afraid
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're here with me today. Whether you're listening while getting ready for work, driving down the road, sitting at home with your Bible, or taking a few quiet moments to yourself, I'm glad you've chosen to spend this time in God's Word.
Today is Week Seven, Day Three. And we're continuing our study called Walking by Faith When You Can't See the Way.
On Day One, we talked about faith when the road ahead is unclear. We learned that biblical faith isn't simply wishing for something to happen. It's trusting God's character and promises, even when we cannot see the entire path ahead.
Then yesterday, we talked about obedience. We studied Abraham and learned that sometimes following God means taking the next faithful step before we understand every detail.
But today, we're going to talk about something that can make both faith and obedience difficult. Fear.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever been afraid of something that hadn't even happened yet?
Maybe you were waiting for test results. Maybe you had an important meeting coming up. Maybe you were worried about your family. Or maybe you were facing a situation where you had absolutely no idea what was going to happen next.
And even though nothing had happened yet, your mind had already imagined every possible outcome.
You started thinking... What if this happens? What if that happens? What if things don't work out? What if I make the wrong decision?
And before you knew it, you were carrying the weight of a future that hadn't even arrived.
Now, I think many of us can relate to that. Because fear has a way of making tomorrow feel heavier than today.
But here's something I want you to understand right from the beginning. Having faith doesn't mean you'll never experience fear.
It means you can learn to bring your fears before the Lord instead of allowing them to become the final authority over your decisions.
Now, I want us to be careful with something today. Because sometimes Christians hear the words "faith over fear" and begin to believe that feeling afraid means they're failing spiritually.
But that's not what Scripture teaches.
Throughout the Bible, we see faithful people experiencing fear. David experienced fear. The disciples experienced fear. And even the apostle Paul described moments of weakness and trembling.
Fear is a real human emotion. Sometimes it warns us about genuine danger. Sometimes it arises because we're facing uncertainty. And sometimes it becomes overwhelming.
But whatever the reason, we can bring our fears honestly before God.
And that's what today's lesson is about. Not pretending we're fearless. But learning to trust the Lord when we're afraid.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Lord, today we're talking about fear. And You know the things that weigh on our hearts. You know the concerns we haven't shared with anyone. The questions we're afraid to ask. And the situations that leave us feeling uncertain. Father, help us understand what Your Word teaches about trusting You. Give us wisdom to recognize real dangers. Courage to do what is right. And peace as we place our concerns before You. Remind us that we don't have to pretend we're strong when we're struggling. We can come to You honestly. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — ISAIAH 41:10 Now, let's turn to Isaiah chapter 41, verse 10. The King James Version says: "Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness."
Now, let's read that again. "Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness."
Now, I want us to slow down and look at these words. Because there's something beautiful about the way this verse is written.
God doesn't simply say, "Don't be afraid." He gives a reason.
"For I am with thee."
Now, that's important. Because the foundation of this encouragement isn't the absence of difficulty. It's the presence and faithfulness of God.
Now, let's talk about the context. In Isaiah chapter 41, the Lord is speaking to Israel, His covenant people. He reminds them that He has chosen them and has not cast them away.
And then He gives this powerful assurance of His presence and help.
Now, as Christians reading this passage today, we should remember that these words were originally addressed to Israel. But they also reveal something important about God's character. He is faithful. He is powerful. And He is able to sustain His people.
And through Jesus Christ, believers have the assurance that the Lord will not abandon them.
Now, here's something I want you to notice. God says... "I will strengthen thee." "I will help thee." "I will uphold thee."
Now, those are words of divine assurance.
And I want you to think about something. The verse doesn't say that God's people will never face difficulties. It doesn't say they will never experience uncertainty. And it doesn't say every situation will unfold exactly as they hope.
Instead, the emphasis is on God's faithfulness and sustaining power.
Now, that brings us to today's key truth.
KEY TRUTH Courageous faith doesn't mean the absence of fear. It means learning to trust God's faithfulness while facing what frightens us.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we spend so much time trying not to feel afraid that we forget to ask God for wisdom about what to do with our fear.
And there's a difference.
WHEN FEAR TAKES OVER OUR THOUGHTS Now, let's talk about something many of us experience. The way fear can affect our thoughts.
Have you ever had one small concern turn into a hundred different worries?
Maybe someone didn't answer your phone call. And suddenly you began imagining that something terrible had happened.
Maybe you received an unexpected letter. And before you even opened it, your mind started preparing for the worst.
Or maybe you were waiting for important news. And every hour felt longer than the one before.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes our concerns are based on genuine circumstances. And those situations may require practical action.
But sometimes our minds begin filling in details we don't actually know.
We imagine outcomes. We make assumptions. And we start treating possibilities as though they're already facts.
Now, that's when we need to slow down.
Not because our feelings don't matter. But because our feelings don't always tell us the whole story.
We can acknowledge our fear while still asking... What do I actually know? What information do I still need? What can I responsibly do today? And what do I need to entrust to God?
Now, those questions can help us respond thoughtfully rather than simply reacting to our fear.
DAVID — TRUSTING GOD WHILE AFRAID Now, let's turn to Psalm 56, verse 3. David says: "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee."
Now, I love that verse. Because David doesn't say... "I will never be afraid."
He says... "What time I am afraid..."
Now, notice that. David acknowledges the reality of fear.
And then he declares where he will place his trust. "In thee."
Now, let's talk about the background. The heading of Psalm 56 connects this psalm with a time when the Philistines took David in Gath.
David was facing serious danger. This wasn't simply a moment of mild uncertainty.
And yet, in the middle of that situation, he expressed his trust in God.
Now, here's something important. David's trust didn't require him to pretend that danger wasn't real.
He could acknowledge the danger. And still turn toward the Lord.
Now, maybe that's what someone listening today needs to hear.
You don't have to deny that something is difficult. You don't have to pretend you're comfortable when you're not. And you don't have to hide your concerns from God.
You can pray honestly.
You can say... "Lord, I'm afraid."
"I don't know what happens next." "I'm struggling to understand this situation." "But I want to trust You."
Now, that kind of prayer doesn't require impressive words. It requires honesty.
And God already knows what you're carrying.
FAITH DOESN'T MEAN IGNORING DANGER Now, I want to pause here and talk about something very important.
Because when we encourage people to choose faith over fear, we need to be careful about how we explain that.
Trusting God doesn't mean ignoring genuine danger.
If you're in an unsafe situation, it's appropriate to seek safety. If you're facing a medical concern, it's appropriate to seek medical care. If you're dealing with a serious financial problem, it's appropriate to gather information and seek qualified guidance.
And if you're experiencing overwhelming anxiety or emotional distress, asking for support is not a failure of faith.
God has given us the ability to seek wisdom, recognize danger, and make responsible decisions.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faith and wisdom belong together.
We can trust God while also taking practical steps to protect ourselves and care for others.
And sometimes courage means asking for help.
JESUS CALMS THE STORM Now, let's turn to Mark chapter 4.
This is one of my favorite passages to study when we're talking about fear.
Jesus and His disciples were crossing the Sea of Galilee.
And while they were traveling, a great storm arose.
Now, the disciples were in a boat. The wind was strong. And the waves were coming into the vessel.
This was a frightening situation.
But Jesus was asleep.
Now, let's read Mark chapter 4, verses 37 through 40. "And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?"
Now, let's think about this scene. The disciples were afraid. The storm was real. And they believed they were in danger.
So they woke Jesus.
And listen to the question they asked Him. "Master, carest thou not that we perish?"
Now, think about that. They weren't simply asking Jesus to help them. They were questioning whether He cared.
And I wonder how many of us have asked a similar question during a difficult season.
"Lord, do You see what's happening?" "Do You know how much I'm struggling?" "Do You care that I'm afraid?"
Now, maybe you've never said those exact words. But perhaps you've felt something similar.
And here's something beautiful about this passage. Jesus demonstrated His authority over the storm.
He spoke. And the wind ceased.
Now, we need to understand the central point of this miracle. It's revealing who Jesus is.
The disciples go on to ask in verse 41... "What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?"
Now, that's the question the passage wants us to consider.
Who is Jesus?
He isn't simply a teacher offering comforting words. He is the Son of God, possessing authority over creation.
And that's where our confidence belongs.
Now, this passage doesn't promise that every storm in our lives will immediately disappear when we pray.
But it does point us toward the authority and identity of Jesus Christ.
And that gives us a reason to trust Him.
WHEN WE QUESTION WHETHER GOD CARES Now, I want us to return to the disciples' question. "Master, carest thou not that we perish?"
Because sometimes fear can affect the way we understand our circumstances.
When life becomes overwhelming, we may begin to wonder whether God sees what we're experiencing.
Maybe you've prayed about something for months. Maybe you've been waiting for an answer. Or maybe you've experienced a painful situation that you never expected.
And perhaps you've wondered... "Lord, where are You in all of this?"
Now, I want you to understand something. Asking questions during suffering doesn't automatically mean you've abandoned your faith.
Throughout Scripture, we find people bringing difficult questions before God.
The Psalms contain prayers of lament. Job wrestled with suffering. And the prophet Habakkuk questioned the violence and injustice he saw.
Now, those passages remind us that we can approach God honestly.
We don't have to pretend that everything makes sense.
But we can continue seeking Him through the questions.
And here's something important. Our circumstances don't always give us a complete picture of God's care.
That's why we return to Scripture.
And ultimately, we look to Jesus Christ.
Because the cross reminds us of the depth of God's love.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's pause for a moment. And I want you to think about one fear you've been carrying.
Maybe it's something you've told other people about. Or maybe it's something you've kept to yourself.
Whatever it is, bring it before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the fears we're carrying. You know the situations that leave us feeling uncertain. And You know the questions we haven't been able to answer. Lord, help us remember Your faithfulness. Give us wisdom to recognize what we can responsibly do. And give us peace as we entrust our concerns to You. Father, when fear becomes overwhelming, help us reach for the support and guidance we need. And remind us that we can come before You honestly. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
GOD HAS NOT GIVEN US A SPIRIT OF FEAR Now, let's turn to 2 Timothy chapter 1, verse 7. The King James Version says: "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind."
Now, this is another familiar verse. But let's talk about the context.
Paul was writing to Timothy. He was encouraging him to remain faithful in his ministry. And he reminded Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony of the Lord.
Now, Paul wasn't simply giving Timothy a motivational statement. He was encouraging him to remain courageous and faithful in the work God had entrusted to him.
And notice the three things Paul mentions. Power. Love. And a sound mind.
Now, I want us to think about those. Power reminds us that God strengthens His people through His Spirit.
Love reminds us that Christian courage isn't simply about being bold. It's about acting in ways that reflect Christ's love.
And a sound mind points toward self-control and disciplined judgment.
Now, that's important. Because biblical courage isn't recklessness.
It's not ignoring consequences. And it's not making decisions without thought.
It's courage guided by love, wisdom, and faithfulness.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Godly courage doesn't require us to abandon wisdom.
Instead, it helps us act faithfully when fear might otherwise keep us from doing what is right.
FEAR ABOUT THE FUTURE Now, let's talk about something that can affect all of us. Fear about the future.
Sometimes we worry about things we cannot control.
We worry about our families. Our health. Our finances. Our relationships. And the things that may happen tomorrow.
Now, some of those concerns require planning. And planning can be wise.
But there's a difference between responsible preparation and allowing worry to consume our thoughts.
Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 4, verses 6 and 7. Paul writes: "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."
Now, the word "careful" here refers to anxious concern.
Paul is encouraging believers to bring their concerns before God in prayer.
And notice that he includes thanksgiving.
Now, why does that matter? Because gratitude can help us remember God's faithfulness.
When we're overwhelmed by uncertainty, we may become so focused on what we fear that we forget the ways God has already sustained us.
Now, that doesn't mean gratitude magically removes every anxious feeling.
But it helps direct our attention toward God's goodness.
And Paul reminds us that God's peace guards our hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Now, here's something important. That peace isn't necessarily the same as knowing exactly how everything will turn out.
It's the peace of belonging to Christ and bringing our concerns before our Heavenly Father.
WHEN FEAR MAKES US HESITATE Now, let's connect today's lesson with what we studied yesterday. Obedience.
Because sometimes fear keeps us from taking a step we know is right.
Maybe we're afraid of rejection. Maybe we're afraid of failure. Maybe we're afraid of what other people will think. Or maybe we're afraid that we won't be able to handle what comes next.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Not every fear should be ignored. Sometimes fear is warning us that we need more information or that a situation is unsafe.
But other times, fear can become an obstacle to faithful action.
And that's when we need wisdom.
We can ask ourselves... Is this fear pointing toward a genuine danger? Or is it keeping me from doing something I already know is right?
Now, that's an important question.
Because the answer may help us understand what our next step should be.
PSALM 23 — GOD'S PRESENCE IN THE VALLEY Now, let's turn to Psalm 23, verse 4. David says: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me."
Now, I love the picture this verse gives us. David doesn't say that the valley doesn't exist.
He says... "Though I walk through the valley..."
Now, that's important. Because following God doesn't mean we'll never face difficult seasons.
There will be valleys. There will be uncertainty. And there will be times when life feels frightening.
But David points toward the presence of the Lord. "For thou art with me."
Now, think about that. The comfort comes from the Shepherd.
And as Christians, we recognize Jesus as the Good Shepherd.
He knows His sheep. He cares for them. And He calls them to follow Him.
Now, maybe you're walking through a valley today.
Maybe it's grief. Maybe it's illness. Maybe it's uncertainty about your future. Or maybe it's a difficult situation you never expected to face.
Now, I won't pretend to know exactly what you're experiencing. But I can encourage you to turn toward the Lord.
Bring Him your questions. Bring Him your fears. And continue seeking His wisdom through Scripture and prayer.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions. If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What fear has been weighing most heavily on my heart?
Now, be honest. You don't have to give an answer that sounds spiritual.
Simply identify what you've been carrying. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... How has this fear been affecting my thoughts or decisions?
Maybe you've been avoiding something. Maybe you've been assuming the worst. Or maybe you've been struggling to focus on the present. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What truth from Scripture can help me respond to this fear faithfully?
Maybe it's Psalm 56:3. "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee."
Maybe it's Isaiah 41:10. "Fear thou not; for I am with thee."
Or maybe it's Philippians 4:6–7, reminding us to bring our concerns before God. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What practical step can I take to respond wisely to this situation?
Maybe you need to gather information. Maybe you need to ask for help. Maybe you need to have a conversation. Or maybe you need to stop trying to control something that is beyond your control. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because our confidence as Christians isn't rooted in our ability to become fearless. It's rooted in our Savior.
Jesus Christ came into the world. He lived a perfect life. He willingly gave Himself on the cross. And He rose again.
Through Him, we have the promise of forgiveness and eternal life.
Now, that doesn't mean believers will never experience fear or suffering.
But it means our ultimate hope rests in the One who has conquered sin and death.
And that's a foundation that goes beyond our circumstances.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You can acknowledge your fear and still choose to trust God.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we become discouraged simply because we're afraid.
But fear doesn't have to be the end of the conversation.
We can bring our fears before God. Seek His wisdom. And ask for courage to do what is right.
LIVING IT OUT Now, let's make today's lesson practical. I want you to try something today.
Take a piece of paper or open your journal. And write down one fear you've been carrying.
Then, underneath it, write a Scripture that reminds you of God's faithfulness.
Now, after that, write down one responsible action you can take.
Maybe it's making a phone call. Maybe it's asking for support. Maybe it's gathering information. Or maybe it's setting aside time to pray.
Now, here's the important part. Don't use Scripture as a reason to avoid taking necessary action.
Instead, allow God's Word to guide you as you respond wisely.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the fear I've been carrying is...
Our second prompt is... One truth about Your character that I want to remember is...
And our third prompt is... One faithful step I can take today is...
Now, take time to pray over your answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. Even when I feel afraid, I can bring my fears before God and trust Him to guide me through His Word.
Now, say that again. Even when I feel afraid, I can bring my fears before God and trust Him to guide me through His Word.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Psalm 56, verse 3. "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee."
Now, throughout the day, whenever fear begins to overwhelm your thoughts, return to that verse.
Pause. Pray. And ask yourself what wise action you can take.
Now, don't expect yourself to become instantly fearless.
Instead, practice bringing your concerns before the Lord.
AROUND THE FIRE Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire. And I ask you this question. Can you remember a time when you were afraid, but you found the courage to do what was right?
Maybe it was having a difficult conversation. Maybe it was asking for help. Maybe it was making an important decision. Or maybe it was choosing to leave an unsafe situation.
Now, think about what helped you. Was it prayer? Support from someone you trusted? Wisdom from Scripture? Or simply recognizing that you needed to take action? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would you say to someone who believes that being afraid means they don't have enough faith?
I hope you'd remind them that Scripture shows us faithful people experiencing fear.
And that we can turn toward God honestly, even when we're struggling.
CLOSING REFLECTION Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
You may not be able to control everything that happens tomorrow.
You may not know how a situation will unfold. And you may not have every answer you're hoping for.
But you can bring your fears before God today.
You can seek wisdom. You can make responsible decisions. And you can continue trusting the Lord.
Now, remember David's words. "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee."
Not if I'm ever afraid. Not after every fear disappears.
But when I am afraid.
That's when I will turn toward the Lord.
And maybe that's the encouragement you need today.
You don't have to wait until every fear disappears before you begin practicing faith.
You can start right where you are.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for reminding us that we can come before You honestly. Lord, You know every fear represented by the people listening. You know the concerns about family. Health. Finances. Relationships. And the future. Father, give us wisdom to respond to those concerns faithfully. Help us recognize genuine dangers. Give us courage to seek safety and support when needed. And teach us to bring our anxieties before You in prayer. Lord, I pray for the person who's waiting for difficult news. Give them strength for today. I pray for the person who's facing an uncertain future. Help them seek wisdom and make responsible decisions. I pray for the person who's afraid to take the next faithful step. Give them courage. And I pray for the person who's struggling with overwhelming fear. Surround them with compassionate support and help them receive the care they need. Father, thank You for Jesus Christ. Thank You for His love. His sacrifice. And His resurrection. May our hope remain firmly rooted in Him. And may we continue learning to trust You through every season. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Seven, Day Three. And I hope today's lesson has reminded you that feeling afraid doesn't mean you've failed in your faith.
Tomorrow, we're going to continue our study of walking by faith. And we're going to talk about something that can be especially difficult. Trusting God when the answer is no.
Our lesson will be called... When God Says No — Trusting His Wisdom Over Our Plans.
We'll explore what Scripture teaches about unanswered requests, disappointment, and continuing to trust God when life doesn't unfold the way we hoped.
Until then, remember... You can acknowledge your fear and still trust the Lord. Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep walking faithfully with Jesus Christ.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: When God Says No: Trusting His Wisdom Over Our Plans
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you've chosen to spend part of your day with me. Whether you're listening on your way to work, sitting at home with your Bible, getting ready for your day, or simply taking a few quiet moments with the Lord, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Seven, Day Four. And we're continuing our study called Walking by Faith When You Can't See the Way.
Over the past three days, we've talked about faith when the road ahead is unclear. We've talked about obedience when we don't understand every detail. And yesterday, we talked about fear. We learned that having faith doesn't mean we'll never feel afraid. It means we can bring our fears before the Lord and continue trusting Him.
But today, we're going to talk about something that can challenge our faith in a very personal way.
What happens when we pray for something... And the answer isn't what we hoped for?
What happens when we've asked God to change a situation... But the situation doesn't change?
What happens when we've prayed for healing... But the illness continues?
When we've prayed for a relationship to be restored... But reconciliation doesn't happen?
Or when we've prayed for a door to open... And instead, that door closes?
Now, those are difficult experiences. And I want us to approach today's lesson with compassion. Because sometimes people hear a message about unanswered prayers and immediately begin wondering whether they've done something wrong.
They ask themselves... Did I not pray enough? Was my faith too weak? Did I say something wrong? Or is God disappointed in me?
Now, I want you to hear something important. An unanswered request does not automatically mean you've failed in your faith.
And we should be careful about assuming we know exactly why God has allowed a particular situation.
Sometimes Scripture gives us insight into why God answered a particular person's prayer in a certain way. But that doesn't mean we can explain every painful circumstance in our own lives.
Today, we're going to study a passage where the apostle Paul prayed repeatedly for something to be removed. And the Lord's answer was not what Paul had requested.
But through that experience, Paul learned something profound about God's grace and strength.
Our lesson is called... When God Says No — Trusting His Wisdom Over Our Plans.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Lord, today we're talking about something that can be painful. The prayers we have prayed. The answers we've hoped for. And the situations that haven't changed the way we wanted. Father, You know every person listening today. You know the disappointments they're carrying. The questions they haven't been able to answer. And the prayers they may still be waiting to see answered. Lord, help us approach Your Word with humility. Give us wisdom to understand what Scripture teaches. And remind us that we can come before You honestly, even when we're disappointed. May today's lesson strengthen our trust in Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — 2 CORINTHIANS 12:7–10 Now, let's turn to Second Corinthians chapter 12.
Before we read, I want to give you a little background. The apostle Paul was writing to the believers in Corinth. And throughout this letter, he addressed questions about his ministry, his suffering, and the nature of Christian strength.
In chapter 12, Paul describes an experience he refers to as a thorn in the flesh.
Now, the Bible doesn't tell us exactly what this thorn was. Over the years, people have suggested different possibilities. Some have wondered whether it was a physical condition. Others have suggested some form of opposition or ongoing hardship.
But Scripture doesn't identify it with certainty. So we shouldn't pretend that we know.
What we do know is that it caused Paul distress. And he prayed for it to be removed.
Now, let's read Second Corinthians chapter 12, verses 7 through 10, from the King James Version. "And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong."
Now, let's slow down and think about what we've just read.
Paul was dealing with something painful. Something he wanted removed.
And he prayed about it. Not once. Not twice. But three times.
Now, notice something important. Paul wasn't someone who lacked faith.
He was an apostle. A man who had encountered the risen Christ. A man who preached the gospel. And a man who endured extraordinary hardships for the sake of Jesus.
Yet Paul still experienced suffering. And he still had prayers that weren't answered in the way he requested.
Now, that should challenge the idea that faithful Christians will always receive exactly what they ask for.
Because here we see a faithful servant of God being told that the thorn would remain.
But we also see the Lord giving Paul something deeply important. Grace.
