KEY TRUTH Here's today's key truth. God's faithfulness is not measured by whether every prayer is answered according to our plans.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we begin measuring God's love by our circumstances.
When things go well, we feel close to Him. When prayers are answered the way we hoped, we feel encouraged. But when life becomes difficult, we may begin to question whether God still cares.
Now, I understand that struggle. Because disappointment can affect the way we see everything.
But God's character doesn't change simply because our circumstances do.
And that's something we need to remember.
PAUL'S THREE PRAYERS Now, let's return to verse 8. Paul says: "For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me."
Now, think about that. Paul prayed specifically.
He didn't simply say... "Lord, whatever happens is fine."
He asked for the thorn to be removed.
And I think that's important. Because sometimes people believe that trusting God's will means they shouldn't ask for anything specific.
But Scripture encourages us to bring our requests before the Lord.
We can pray for healing. We can pray for provision. We can pray for reconciliation. And we can pray for difficult circumstances to change.
Now, we should do so with humility, recognizing that we don't control the outcome.
But we don't have to hide our desires from God.
Paul didn't.
He asked. And he asked repeatedly.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Trusting God doesn't mean pretending we don't have hopes or desires.
It means bringing those desires before Him while remaining willing to submit to His wisdom.
MY GRACE IS SUFFICIENT FOR THEE Now, let's look at the Lord's response. Verse 9 says: "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness."
Now, I want us to slow down here. Because these words are powerful.
Paul asked for the thorn to be removed. But the Lord directed his attention toward divine grace.
"My grace is sufficient for thee."
Now, that doesn't mean Paul's suffering was imaginary. It doesn't mean the thorn was easy to endure. And it doesn't mean Paul was wrong to ask for relief.
But it does mean that Christ's grace would sustain him in the midst of his weakness.
Now, here's something important. The Lord didn't tell Paul that he was strong enough on his own.
He pointed Paul toward the strength of Christ.
And that changes the way we understand spiritual strength.
Because sometimes we think being strong means never struggling. Never crying. Never asking for help. And never admitting that we're overwhelmed.
But Paul learned that his weakness could become a place where the power of Christ was displayed.
Now, that doesn't mean weakness is enjoyable. And it doesn't mean we should seek suffering.
But it reminds us that our limitations don't place us beyond the reach of God's grace.
WHEN THE ANSWER ISN'T WHAT WE EXPECTED Now, let's bring this into everyday life.
Maybe you've prayed for something for a long time.
Maybe you've asked God to change a situation. Maybe you've prayed for someone you love. Or maybe you've been hoping for an opportunity that hasn't happened.
Now, sometimes we receive a clear answer. Sometimes circumstances change. And sometimes a request remains unresolved.
But here's something important. We shouldn't automatically label every delay as a no.
Sometimes we simply don't know what the outcome will be.
And we should be careful about claiming to understand God's hidden purposes.
Now, in Paul's situation, Scripture records the Lord's response. But in our own lives, we may not receive that kind of direct explanation.
So what do we do?
We continue praying. We continue seeking wisdom. We take responsible action when appropriate. And we entrust the outcome to God.
Now, I want you to remember this. Faith doesn't require us to explain every unanswered prayer.
Sometimes faith means continuing to trust God while living with questions.
WHEN DISAPPOINTMENT BECOMES PERSONAL Now, I want to talk about something that can be difficult to admit. Sometimes disappointment with circumstances begins to feel like disappointment with God.
Maybe you've prayed faithfully. Maybe you've tried to do what is right. And maybe you've hoped for something with all your heart.
But the situation didn't change.
And somewhere along the way, you began wondering... "Lord, why didn't You answer?"
"Why did this happen?" "Why am I still dealing with this?"
Now, I want you to understand something. You can bring those questions before God.
Throughout Scripture, we find people expressing sorrow, confusion, and disappointment.
The Psalms contain prayers of lament. Job wrestled with suffering. And Habakkuk asked difficult questions about injustice.
Now, those passages don't give us permission to accuse God falsely. But they do show us that we can approach Him honestly.
We don't have to pretend that everything makes sense.
We can acknowledge our disappointment. And continue seeking Him through it.
JESUS IN THE GARDEN OF GETHSEMANE Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 22.
This passage brings us to the garden of Gethsemane. Jesus was approaching His arrest and crucifixion.
And Luke records His prayer. Let's read Luke chapter 22, verse 42. Jesus prayed: "Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done."
Now, let's think about those words.
Jesus expressed the weight of what lay before Him. And He submitted Himself to the Father's will.
Now, we need to understand that this moment is unique. Jesus was approaching the cross, where He would accomplish the work of redemption.
His suffering wasn't simply another example of ordinary human disappointment. It was central to God's saving plan.
But His prayer also teaches us something about submission to the Father's will.
"Nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done."
Now, that's not always an easy prayer.
Because sometimes we know exactly what we want. We know how we'd like the situation to change. And we know what outcome we're hoping for.
But when we pray according to God's will, we acknowledge that His wisdom is greater than ours.
Now, here's something important. Submitting to God's will doesn't mean refusing to seek help. It doesn't mean remaining in an unsafe situation. And it doesn't mean neglecting responsibilities.
It means seeking to honor God while trusting Him with what lies beyond our control.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's pause for a moment.
I want you to think about a prayer you've been carrying.
Maybe it's something you've prayed about for a long time. Maybe it's a request that hasn't been answered. Or maybe it's something that turned out differently from what you hoped.
Now, bring that request before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the requests we've brought before You. You know the hopes we've carried. And You know the disappointments we've experienced. Lord, help us trust Your wisdom. Give us patience when we don't have answers. Strength when circumstances remain difficult. And humility to seek Your will above our own. Father, remind us that we can come before You honestly. And help us continue following Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TRUSTING GOD WITHOUT UNDERSTANDING WHY Now, let's return to Proverbs chapter 3, verses 5 and 6. The King James Version says: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."
Now, we've returned to these verses several times this week. And there's a reason for that.
Because they remind us that our understanding is limited.
We don't know everything. We don't see every consequence. And we don't always understand why certain circumstances unfold the way they do.
But God is perfectly wise.
Now, here's something I want us to be careful about. Trusting God's wisdom doesn't mean we should invent explanations for other people's suffering.
Sometimes people say things like... "God must have done this because..."
And then they offer an explanation that Scripture hasn't actually given.
But we need humility.
We don't always know why a particular tragedy happened. We don't always know why a prayer remains unanswered. And we don't always know what the future will bring.
Now, that uncertainty can be difficult.
But it doesn't mean we have to stop trusting the Lord.
We can trust His character without pretending to understand every part of His providence.
ROMANS 8:28 — GOD'S PURPOSE Now, let's turn to Romans chapter 8, verse 28. It says: "And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose."
Now, this is a beautiful verse. But it's also one that we need to understand carefully.
Paul isn't saying that every event is good.
Suffering isn't automatically good. Injustice isn't good. And tragedy isn't something we should pretend to celebrate.
But Paul is teaching that God is working according to His purpose for those who belong to Him.
And the surrounding verses help us understand that purpose.
Romans chapter 8, verse 29, speaks about believers being conformed to the image of God's Son.
Now, that's important. Because God's ultimate purpose is much greater than simply making our present circumstances comfortable.
He is working toward the completion of His saving purpose in Christ.
Now, that doesn't mean we can explain exactly how every painful experience fits into that purpose.
But it gives believers a foundation for hope.
God's purposes are not defeated by the difficulties we face.
WHEN A CLOSED DOOR HURTS Now, let's talk about something many of us have experienced. A closed door.
Maybe you applied for a job. Maybe you pursued an opportunity. Maybe you hoped a relationship would work out. Or maybe you were preparing for something you believed would become part of your future.
But it didn't happen.
And now you're trying to understand what comes next.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A closed door doesn't automatically mean God is punishing you.
And it doesn't always mean the opportunity was wrong.
Sometimes circumstances simply don't unfold the way we hoped.
Now, we can learn from those experiences. We can evaluate what happened. We can seek wisdom. And we can consider other possibilities.
But we don't have to interpret every disappointment as evidence that God has abandoned us.
His faithfulness isn't dependent on whether our plans succeed.
JAMES 4 — HOLDING OUR PLANS WITH HUMILITY Now, let's turn to James chapter 4.
James speaks to people who make confident plans about the future without acknowledging their dependence on God.
Let's read James chapter 4, verses 13 through 15. "Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that."
Now, let's think about that. James isn't saying that planning is wrong.
Planning can be wise. Preparing for the future can be responsible. And working toward goals can be a good thing.
But James reminds us that we don't control tomorrow.
Our plans should be held with humility.
Now, here's something practical. It's okay to make plans. It's okay to pursue goals. And it's okay to hope for certain outcomes.
But we should remember that our lives ultimately belong to God.
And when circumstances change, we can return to Him for wisdom about what comes next.
GOD'S GRACE IN OUR WEAKNESS Now, let's return to Paul's words in Second Corinthians chapter 12.
Because I don't want us to miss the beauty of what he learned.
The thorn wasn't removed.
But Paul discovered that Christ's grace was sufficient.
Now, I want you to think about that. Sometimes we spend so much time asking God to change our circumstances that we overlook our need for His strength within those circumstances.
Now, that doesn't mean we should stop praying for change. Paul prayed. And Scripture encourages us to bring our requests before God.
But we can also pray for strength. Wisdom. Patience. And endurance.
We can ask God to help us remain faithful while we're waiting.
And we can ask Him to shape our hearts through His Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God's grace is not limited by our weakness.
We may feel overwhelmed. We may feel discouraged. And we may not know what happens next.
But we can continue depending on Christ.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions. If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What prayer or hope has been difficult for me to surrender?
Maybe it's something you've been carrying for months. Maybe it's something that hasn't happened. Or maybe it's an outcome you deeply wanted. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Have I been measuring God's love by whether my circumstances change?
Now, think about that honestly.
Have you found yourself feeling close to God when things go well, but distant when life becomes difficult? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What does Paul's experience teach me about God's grace?
Maybe it reminds you that faithful believers can experience suffering. Maybe it teaches you that weakness doesn't place you beyond God's care. Or maybe it reminds you to seek Christ's strength when you feel overwhelmed. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I continue following Jesus faithfully while I wait for an answer?
Maybe you need to continue praying. Maybe you need to seek counsel. Maybe you need to make a responsible decision. Or maybe you need to focus on the responsibilities already before you. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because the greatest foundation for our trust in God isn't that every prayer will be answered according to our preferences.
It's the saving work of Jesus Christ.
Through His death and resurrection, we have the promise of forgiveness and eternal life.
Now, think about the cross.
To those watching, the crucifixion may have appeared to be the end of Jesus' ministry.
But through His death and resurrection, God's plan of redemption was accomplished.
Now, we shouldn't use that truth to claim that every tragedy in our lives will lead to an outcome we can clearly recognize as good.
But it reminds us that our ultimate hope rests in Christ.
And that hope remains even when our present circumstances are painful.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. God's grace can sustain you even when your circumstances don't change the way you hoped.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we begin believing that God can only help us by removing the difficulty.
But Paul's experience reminds us that Christ's strength can sustain His people in weakness.
LIVING IT OUT Now, let's make today's lesson practical. I want you to think about one situation where you're struggling with disappointment.
Maybe it's a prayer that hasn't been answered. Maybe it's a closed door. Or maybe it's a plan that didn't work out.
Now, write that situation down.
Then write two prayers.
The first prayer should be honest about what you want.
You might write... "Lord, this is what I'm hoping for."
And the second prayer should express your willingness to trust God's wisdom.
You might write... "Lord, help me honor You even if the outcome is different from what I've requested."
Now, take time to pray over both.
And remember that surrender doesn't mean pretending you don't care.
It means bringing your desires before God with humility.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the prayer I've been struggling with is...
Our second prompt is... The disappointment I need to bring before You is...
And our third prompt is... Help me trust Your wisdom by...
Now, take your time with those questions.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. Even when God's answer isn't what I hoped for, I can continue trusting His character, seeking His wisdom, and depending on His grace.
Now, say that again. Even when God's answer isn't what I hoped for, I can continue trusting His character, seeking His wisdom, and depending on His grace.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Second Corinthians chapter 12, verse 9. "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And whenever you begin feeling discouraged about something that hasn't changed, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for strength. Wisdom. And patience.
AROUND THE FIRE Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
And I ask you this question. Can you remember a time when something didn't work out the way you hoped?
Maybe it was an opportunity. A relationship. Or a plan you had been looking forward to.
Now, think about that experience. How did you respond? What did you learn? And what helped you move forward? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would you say to someone who's struggling because they believe God hasn't answered their prayers?
Maybe you'd remind them that Paul prayed repeatedly for his thorn to be removed.
Maybe you'd encourage them to keep bringing their concerns before God.
Or maybe you'd simply sit beside them and listen.
Because sometimes people don't need us to explain why something happened.
Sometimes they need compassion.
And sometimes the most faithful thing we can do is remind someone that they don't have to carry their disappointment alone.
CLOSING REFLECTION Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Sometimes we ask God to remove the difficulty. And sometimes He does.
Sometimes we ask Him to open a door. And sometimes that door opens.
But sometimes the situation remains difficult. Sometimes the answer isn't what we hoped for. And sometimes we're left with questions.
Now, in those moments, we can remember Paul's experience.
He prayed. He asked. And he received an answer that redirected his attention toward the sufficiency of Christ's grace.
Now, maybe today you need to hear those words. "My grace is sufficient for thee."
Not because your situation is easy. Not because your disappointment doesn't matter. And not because you should stop seeking help or taking responsible action.
But because the strength of Christ is not limited by our weakness.
And that's a beautiful reason to keep trusting Him.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for the example of Paul. And thank You for reminding us that Your grace is sufficient. Lord, You know every unanswered prayer represented by the people listening. You know the disappointments. The closed doors. The hopes that haven't been fulfilled. And the questions that remain. Father, help us bring those things before You honestly. Give us wisdom when we need to make decisions. Patience when we must wait. And strength when circumstances remain difficult. Lord, I pray for the person who's grieving an outcome they deeply hoped for. Bring comfort. I pray for the person who's waiting for healing. Give them strength and surround them with compassionate care. I pray for the person who's facing disappointment in a relationship. Give them wisdom, peace, and healthy support. And I pray for the person who's beginning to question whether You care. Remind them of Your love revealed through Jesus Christ. Father, thank You for the cross. Thank You for the resurrection. And thank You for the promise of eternal life through our Savior. May our hope remain firmly rooted in Him. And may we continue following You faithfully, even when we don't understand every part of the journey. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Seven, Day Four. And I hope today's lesson has encouraged you to remember that God's faithfulness isn't measured by whether every prayer is answered according to our plans.
Tomorrow, we're going to continue our study of walking by faith. And we're going to talk about what it means to remain faithful when the journey becomes difficult. Our lesson will be called... Keep Walking — Faithfulness When the Journey Gets Hard.
We'll explore how Scripture encourages us to persevere, remain steadfast, and continue following Jesus even when we feel weary.
Until then, remember... God's grace can sustain you even when circumstances don't change the way you hoped. Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep trusting the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Keep Walking: Faithfulness When the Journey Gets Hard
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're here with me today. Whether you're listening while driving, getting ready for work, sitting at home with your Bible, or taking a few quiet moments with the Lord, I'm glad you've chosen to spend this time with me.
Today is Week Seven, Day Five. And we're continuing our study called Walking by Faith When You Can't See the Way.
Now, over the past four days, we've talked about some important parts of our journey with God. We've talked about trusting Him when the road ahead is unclear. We've talked about taking the next faithful step before we understand every detail. We've talked about fear. And yesterday, we talked about something that can be especially painful. When our prayers aren't answered the way we hoped.
But today, I want to talk about something that connects all of those lessons. Perseverance.
Because sometimes the hardest part of walking by faith isn't taking the first step. It's continuing when the journey becomes difficult.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever started something with excitement and determination... Only to discover that the journey was much harder than you expected?
Maybe you began working toward a goal. Maybe you started a new responsibility. Maybe you committed yourself to changing a habit. Or maybe you stepped into a season of life that required more strength than you thought you had.
At first, you were motivated. You were hopeful. And you believed you were ready.
But then the difficulties came.
Things took longer than expected. Obstacles appeared. And progress became slower than you'd hoped.
And somewhere along the way, you began feeling tired.
Not just physically tired. But emotionally tired. Mentally tired. And maybe even spiritually tired.
Now, I think many of us can relate to that. Because life has a way of stretching us.
Sometimes we carry responsibilities that feel overwhelming. Sometimes we experience disappointments. And sometimes we simply become weary from trying to remain faithful through difficult circumstances.
Now, here's something I want you to understand right from the beginning. Feeling weary doesn't automatically mean you've failed in your faith.
Even faithful believers experience exhaustion.
And Scripture doesn't call us to pretend that we're never tired. Instead, it encourages us to continue trusting God, seek His strength, and remain faithful in what He's called us to do.
Now, today's lesson is called... Keep Walking — Faithfulness When the Journey Gets Hard.
And we're going to explore what Scripture teaches about perseverance. But we're also going to talk about something equally important. Rest.
Because sometimes continuing faithfully means taking another step. And sometimes it means recognizing that we need to stop, rest, and receive help.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Lord, You know the people listening today. You know the responsibilities they're carrying. The struggles they're facing. And the situations that have left them feeling weary. Father, some of us are tired. Some of us are discouraged. And some of us are wondering how much longer a difficult season will last. Lord, help us understand what Your Word teaches about perseverance. Give us wisdom to recognize when we need rest. Courage to remain faithful. And strength to continue following Jesus Christ. May today's lesson encourage every person who feels overwhelmed. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — GALATIANS 6:9 Now, let's turn to Galatians chapter 6, verse 9. The King James Version says: "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."
Now, let's read that again. "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."
Now, I want us to slow down and think about those words. Because this verse is often quoted when people are feeling discouraged.
And it contains a beautiful encouragement. But we need to understand what Paul was teaching.
In Galatians chapter 6, Paul is encouraging believers to live according to the Spirit. He talks about restoring those who have fallen into sin with gentleness. Bearing one another's burdens. And sowing to the Spirit rather than to the flesh.
Then he tells believers not to grow weary in doing good.
Now, that's important. Because Paul isn't simply encouraging people to keep pursuing any goal they've chosen.
He's encouraging perseverance in godly living.
Doing what is right. Loving others. Serving faithfully. And continuing to live according to the Spirit.
Now, let's look at the phrase... "Let us not be weary in well doing."
Now, notice that Paul recognizes something. Doing good can become tiring.
Sometimes serving others requires sacrifice. Sometimes remaining honest is difficult. Sometimes forgiving someone takes emotional strength. And sometimes doing what is right doesn't produce immediate results.
Now, Paul isn't denying that those things can be hard.
He's encouraging believers not to abandon faithfulness simply because the results aren't immediate.
And that brings us to today's key truth.
KEY TRUTH Faithful perseverance means continuing to honor God through difficult seasons while depending on His strength and wisdom.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because perseverance isn't simply refusing to stop.
It's remaining faithful to God.
And sometimes remaining faithful requires us to change our plans. Ask for help. Or recognize that we need rest.
Now, let's talk about that.
WHEN DOING GOOD BECOMES EXHAUSTING Have you ever been trying to do the right thing... But it seemed like everything was working against you?
Maybe you've been helping someone. Maybe you've been serving in your church. Maybe you've been caring for a family member. Or maybe you've been trying to rebuild your life after a difficult season.
And you've been doing your best to remain faithful.
But you're tired.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes we become discouraged because we expect doing good to produce immediate results.
We think... "If I'm doing the right thing, surely this should become easier."
But Scripture doesn't promise that.
Sometimes doing what is right requires patience. Sometimes it involves sacrifice. And sometimes the results aren't visible for a long time.
Now, that doesn't mean we should remain in every difficult situation indefinitely.
There are times when wisdom requires us to establish boundaries. There are times when we need support. And there are times when we need to step away from unhealthy circumstances.
But when we're pursuing what is good and honoring to God, we shouldn't assume that difficulty means our faithfulness has been wasted.
THE HARVEST IN DUE SEASON Now, let's return to the second part of Galatians 6:9. "For in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."
Now, I want us to understand this carefully. Because sometimes people interpret this verse as a promise that if we keep working hard enough, we'll eventually receive whatever outcome we want.
But that's not what Paul is teaching.
The surrounding passage speaks about sowing to the Spirit and reaping everlasting life.
Paul is pointing believers toward the lasting significance of faithful living.
Now, that doesn't mean every good action will produce an immediate earthly reward.
Sometimes we do what is right and still experience disappointment. Sometimes we serve others and receive no recognition. And sometimes we work faithfully without seeing the results we hoped for.
But our obedience to God is never meaningless.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithfulness matters even when the results aren't visible.
HEBREWS 12 — RUNNING WITH PATIENCE Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 12.
The writer uses the picture of a race to describe the Christian life.
Let's read Hebrews chapter 12, verses 1 and 2. "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."
Now, let's think about that picture. A race requires endurance.
You don't finish a long race simply because you started with enthusiasm.
You need perseverance. Focus. And the willingness to continue through difficulty.
But notice something important. The writer doesn't simply tell believers to run harder.
He tells them where to look. "Looking unto Jesus."
Now, that's the center of the passage.
Our confidence isn't rooted in our ability to endure everything through our own strength.
It's rooted in Jesus Christ.
He is the author and finisher of our faith.
And the writer points us toward His endurance of the cross.
Now, the suffering of Jesus was unique. Through His death and resurrection, He accomplished the work of salvation.
But His endurance also encourages believers to remain faithful.
Now, let's read Hebrews chapter 12, verse 3. "For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds."
Now, I love that. Because the writer recognizes that believers can become weary.
And he directs their attention toward Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. When the journey becomes difficult, don't lose sight of Jesus.
LAYING ASIDE EVERY WEIGHT Now, let's return to something in Hebrews chapter 12, verse 1. "Let us lay aside every weight..."
Now, think about that. If someone is running a race, carrying unnecessary weight makes the journey harder.
And the writer uses that picture to encourage believers to remove obstacles that hinder their spiritual endurance.
Now, he specifically mentions sin.
But the image of laying aside weights can also prompt us to examine what may be distracting us from faithful living.
Maybe we're carrying responsibilities that need to be shared. Maybe we're holding onto unrealistic expectations. Or maybe we're allowing constant comparison with other people to discourage us.
Now, here's something important. Not every burden can simply be put down.
Some responsibilities are real. Some circumstances are difficult. And some challenges require ongoing care.
But we can still ask God for wisdom about how to carry those responsibilities faithfully.
Sometimes that means asking for help. Sometimes it means establishing healthier boundaries. And sometimes it means recognizing that we cannot do everything.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithfulness doesn't require you to carry every burden alone.
WHEN WE FEEL LIKE GIVING UP Now, I want to talk about something that many people experience. The feeling of wanting to give up.
Maybe you've been working toward something for a long time. Maybe you've been caring for someone. Maybe you've been trying to make positive changes in your life. Or maybe you've been facing one difficult situation after another.
And you're tired.
Now, I want you to understand something. Sometimes exhaustion makes everything feel heavier.
Decisions become harder. Problems seem bigger. And even ordinary responsibilities can feel overwhelming.
Now, when that happens, we need wisdom.
We need to recognize whether we're simply discouraged... Or whether we're genuinely overwhelmed and need rest, support, or a change in circumstances.
Now, here's something important. Perseverance doesn't mean ignoring your limits.
And it doesn't mean continuing in a harmful situation simply because you've been told to keep going.
Sometimes the faithful next step is asking for help.
Sometimes it's taking a break.
And sometimes it's recognizing that a particular path needs to change.
But through all of those decisions, we can continue seeking God.
ISAIAH 40 — STRENGTH FOR THE WEARY Now, let's turn to Isaiah chapter 40.
This chapter contains beautiful reminders of God's greatness and power.
Let's read verses 28 through 31. "Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding. He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength. Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."
Now, I love this passage. Because it begins by reminding us who God is.
He is the everlasting God. The Creator of the ends of the earth.
He doesn't become exhausted. He doesn't lose strength. And His understanding is beyond ours.
Then the passage reminds us that He gives strength to the weary.
Now, think about that. Even young people become tired. Even strong people experience limitations.
But God is not limited in the way we are.
Now, the promise of renewed strength isn't a command to ignore our physical needs.
It points us toward the Lord as the source of hope and strength.
And as believers, we can seek His help while also caring responsibly for the bodies and minds He has given us.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to pretend you're strong when you're weary.
You can acknowledge your limitations. And turn toward the Lord.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's take a moment to pray.
I want you to think about an area of your life where you've been feeling weary.
Maybe it's a responsibility. A relationship. A difficult situation. Or something you've been waiting to see change.
Now, bring that before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the burdens we're carrying. You know the responsibilities that feel overwhelming. And You know the situations that have left us discouraged. Lord, give us wisdom. Help us recognize when we need rest. When we need support. And when we need courage to continue doing what is right. Father, strengthen our faith. And help us keep our eyes on Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
JAMES 1 — GROWING THROUGH TRIALS Now, let's turn to James chapter 1.
James writes to believers who are facing trials.
And he encourages them to understand the spiritual significance of perseverance.
Let's read James chapter 1, verses 2 through 4. "My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing."
Now, let's talk about that. The word translated "temptations" here refers to trials or testing.
James isn't telling believers to enjoy suffering.
He's encouraging them to recognize that God can use trials to develop steadfastness.
Now, here's something important. We shouldn't assume every painful experience has a simple explanation.
And we shouldn't tell someone who's suffering that they need to be happy about what happened.
But we can recognize that spiritual growth sometimes occurs through difficult circumstances.
Patience can develop. Endurance can grow. And we can learn to depend more deeply on the Lord.
Now, that doesn't make suffering good in itself.
But it reminds us that hardship doesn't have to make spiritual growth impossible.
WHEN PROGRESS FEELS SLOW Now, let's talk about something that can be frustrating. Slow progress.
Maybe you've been praying for change. Maybe you've been working toward a goal. Or maybe you've been trying to grow in a particular area of your life.
But progress feels slow.
Now, sometimes we become discouraged because we compare ourselves with other people.
We look at what someone else has accomplished. We see where they are in life. And we begin wondering why our journey looks different.
But here's something important. Comparison can distract us from the responsibilities and opportunities God has placed before us.
Now, I want you to think about a garden.
Different plants grow at different rates. Some produce fruit quickly. Others require more time.
And growth isn't always visible above the ground.
Now, spiritual growth can be similar.
Sometimes we're learning patience. Sometimes we're developing self-control. And sometimes we're learning to trust God in circumstances we cannot change.
Now, those changes may not be obvious to everyone around us.
But they matter.
And here's something I want you to remember. Don't measure your spiritual growth only by what other people can see.
Look for the ways God's Word is shaping your character.
JESUS INVITES THE WEARY TO COME TO HIM Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 11.
Jesus gives a beautiful invitation to those who are weary and burdened.
Let's read Matthew chapter 11, verses 28 through 30. "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."
Now, I love these words.
Because Jesus doesn't say... "Come to me once you've become strong enough."
He doesn't say... "Come to me after you've solved every problem."
He says... "Come unto me."
Now, that's an invitation.
And the rest He offers is deeply connected to coming under His gracious lordship and learning from Him.
Now, here's something important. Following Jesus doesn't mean we will never have responsibilities. It doesn't mean we will never face suffering. And it doesn't mean life will always be easy.
But it means we don't have to seek spiritual rest apart from Him.
We can come to Christ. Learn from Him. And depend on His grace.
Now, maybe someone listening today needs that reminder.
You don't have to wait until you're completely exhausted before turning toward the Lord.
You can come to Him today.
REST IS NOT FAILURE Now, I want to spend a few moments talking about rest.
Because sometimes people become so focused on perseverance that they begin treating rest as weakness.
They feel guilty for slowing down. They feel guilty for asking for help. And they feel guilty when they cannot accomplish everything they planned.
But here's something important. Rest isn't automatically a sign of failure.
God created human beings with limitations.
We need sleep. We need nourishment. We need relationships. And we need time to recover from physical and emotional demands.
Now, sometimes we need to evaluate our responsibilities.
Are we trying to do too much? Are we refusing help because we think we have to handle everything ourselves? Or are we neglecting important needs because we believe slowing down would disappoint someone?
Now, those are questions worth considering.
Because faithful living requires wisdom.
And sometimes wisdom means recognizing our limits.
PSALM 27 — WAIT ON THE LORD Now, let's turn to Psalm 27, verse 14. David says: "Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD."
Now, notice the connection between waiting and courage.
Sometimes waiting requires tremendous strength.
Especially when we don't know how long a difficult season will last.
But David encourages us to place our hope in the Lord.
Now, waiting on God doesn't mean refusing to act when action is necessary.
It means trusting Him while continuing to live faithfully.
And sometimes that involves patience.
Sometimes it involves perseverance.
And sometimes it involves choosing to rest.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions. If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... Where have I been feeling most weary?
Maybe it's physically. Emotionally. Mentally. Or spiritually.
Take a moment to identify what you've been carrying. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Have I been trying to carry responsibilities that I need help with?
Now, think about that honestly.
Sometimes we take on more than we can reasonably manage.
And sometimes asking for help is an important step toward wisdom. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What does Galatians 6:9 teach me about remaining faithful?
Maybe it reminds you not to abandon doing good simply because the results aren't immediate.
Maybe it encourages you to keep serving others. Or maybe it reminds you that faithful living has lasting significance. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What would wise perseverance look like in my life right now?
Maybe it means continuing something important. Maybe it means changing your approach. Maybe it means establishing a boundary. Or maybe it means taking time to rest. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because our ultimate example of faithful endurance is Jesus Christ.
He endured the cross. He accomplished the work of salvation. And He rose again.
Now, we don't earn salvation through our own perseverance.
We are saved by God's grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
But as believers, we're called to continue following Him.
And Hebrews reminds us to keep our eyes on Jesus.
Not on our own strength. Not on our accomplishments. And not on how much we can endure without help.
But on our Savior.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. Faithfulness isn't about never becoming tired. It's about continuing to depend on Christ through every season.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become discouraged when we reach our limits.
But our limitations can remind us of our need for God's grace.
And we can seek His strength while also making wise choices about rest and support.
LIVING IT OUT Now, let's make today's lesson practical. I want you to identify one area where you've been feeling discouraged.
Write it down.
Then ask yourself three questions. First... Is this something God has clearly called me to continue doing?
Second... What support, wisdom, or rest do I need?
And third... What is one faithful step I can take today?
Now, remember. The goal isn't to prove how much you can endure.
It's to honor God with the responsibilities and opportunities He's placed before you.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the area where I've been feeling weary is...
Our second prompt is... One burden I need wisdom or help carrying is...
And our third prompt is... One way I can remain faithful while caring for my limits is...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. When the journey becomes difficult, I will keep my eyes on Jesus, seek His strength, and continue walking faithfully with wisdom and perseverance.
Now, say that again. When the journey becomes difficult, I will keep my eyes on Jesus, seek His strength, and continue walking faithfully with wisdom and perseverance.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Galatians chapter 6, verse 9. "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."
Now, throughout the day, look for one opportunity to continue doing good.
Maybe it's encouraging someone. Helping a person in need. Practicing patience. Or simply remaining faithful in an important responsibility.
And here's the second part of the challenge. Make time for appropriate rest.
Because perseverance and wisdom belong together.
AROUND THE FIRE Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
And I ask you this question. Can you remember a season when you felt like giving up, but you found the strength to continue?
Maybe it was a difficult responsibility. A season of grief. A challenging goal. Or a situation that required patience.
Now, think about what helped you. Was it prayer? Encouragement from someone you trusted? Support from your church? Or simply taking things one day at a time? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would you say to someone who's feeling exhausted and discouraged today?
Maybe you'd remind them that it's okay to ask for help. Maybe you'd encourage them to rest. Maybe you'd offer practical support. Or maybe you'd simply sit beside them and listen.
Because sometimes encouragement isn't about telling someone to push harder.
Sometimes it's about helping them recognize that they don't have to carry everything alone.
CLOSING REFLECTION Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
There may be seasons when the road feels long.
When progress is slow. When responsibilities are heavy. And when you wonder whether you have the strength to continue.
Now, in those moments, remember the words of Galatians 6:9. "And let us not be weary in well doing..."
Not because we're expected to be endlessly strong.
But because faithfulness to God matters.
And remember the invitation of Jesus. "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
Now, maybe today you need courage to keep going.
Or maybe you need wisdom to slow down.
Whatever your circumstances, continue seeking the Lord.
Keep your eyes on Jesus.
And remember that your worth isn't measured by how much you can accomplish.
Your hope is found in Christ.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for reminding us that we can depend on Your strength. Lord, You know every weary heart represented by the people listening. You know the responsibilities they're carrying. The disappointments they've experienced. And the situations that have left them feeling overwhelmed. Father, give them wisdom. Help them recognize when they need rest. When they need support. And when they need courage to continue doing what is right. Lord, I pray for the person who's caring for someone they love. Give them strength and surround them with support. I pray for the person who's discouraged by slow progress. Help them remain patient. I pray for the person who's struggling with exhaustion. Give them wisdom to care for their physical and emotional needs. And I pray for the person who's wondering whether their faithfulness matters. Remind them of the lasting significance of living according to Your Word. Father, thank You for Jesus Christ. Thank You for His sacrifice. His resurrection. And the rest He offers to those who come to Him. May we keep our eyes on our Savior. And may we continue following Him faithfully. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Seven, Day Five. And I hope today's lesson has encouraged you to remember that perseverance isn't about pretending you're never tired.
It's about continuing to depend on Christ. Seeking His wisdom. And remaining faithful through every season.
Tomorrow, we're going to gather Around the Fire for our Week Seven reflection. We'll look back over everything we've studied this week. Faith. Obedience. Fear. Disappointment. And perseverance.
And we'll talk about how those lessons can help us continue walking with God when the road ahead is unclear.
Until then, remember... You don't have to see the entire journey to take the next faithful step. Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep your eyes on Jesus.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Around the Fire: Trusting God When the Road Is Unclear
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're spending this time with me today. Whether you're listening from home, riding down the road, enjoying a quiet morning, or taking a few minutes away from a busy day, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Seven, Day Six. And that means it's time for something special. We're gathering Around the Fire.
Now, if you've been walking through these Bible studies with me, you know that Around the Fire is our opportunity to slow down. To reflect. To talk honestly about what we've learned. And to consider how God's Word applies to our everyday lives.
Because Bible study isn't simply about collecting information. It's about growing in our understanding of God. Allowing His Word to shape our hearts. And learning to follow Jesus Christ more faithfully.
And this week, we've been studying something that touches every one of us. Walking by faith when we can't see the way.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever looked back over a season of your life and realized just how much uncertainty you were carrying?
Maybe you didn't know how a situation would turn out. Maybe you were afraid of what might happen. Maybe you were waiting for an answer. Or maybe you were simply trying to make it through one day at a time.
And looking back, you can remember the questions. The worries. The difficult decisions. And the moments when you wondered whether you had the strength to keep going.
Now, sometimes when we look back, we can see ways God sustained us that we didn't recognize at the time.
But sometimes we still have questions. Sometimes the pain hasn't completely disappeared. And sometimes the situation remains unresolved.
And that's important to acknowledge. Because faith doesn't require us to pretend that every difficult experience has a simple explanation.
Faith invites us to continue trusting God, even when we don't understand everything.
And that's what we're going to reflect on today.
We're going to revisit the five lessons we've studied this week. We're going to ask ourselves some honest questions. And we're going to spend time in prayer.
So, if you have your Bible and journal nearby, go ahead and get comfortable. And if you're listening while driving or working, you can simply listen and return to the reflection questions later.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the lessons we've studied this week. Thank You for reminding us that faith is rooted in Your character and promises. Lord, as we gather Around the Fire today, help us slow down. Help us reflect honestly. And help us recognize the areas where we need to grow. Father, You know the uncertainties we're carrying. You know the decisions we're facing. The fears we're struggling with. And the prayers we're still waiting to see answered. Lord, give us wisdom. Give us courage. And help us continue following Jesus Christ. May this time of reflection draw us closer to You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUR FOUNDATION — WALKING BY FAITH Now, let's begin with the Scripture that has guided our study this week. Second Corinthians chapter 5, verse 7. The King James Version says: "For we walk by faith, not by sight."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "For we walk by faith, not by sight."
This verse comes from Paul's discussion of the believer's hope beyond this present life.
He reminds Christians that our confidence rests in God's promises, even while we await what we cannot presently see.
And that truth has implications for the way we live today.
We don't know everything about tomorrow. We don't know how every circumstance will unfold. And we don't always understand why certain things happen.
But we can continue trusting the Lord.
Now, here's something I want us to remember. Walking by faith doesn't mean closing our eyes to reality.
It doesn't mean ignoring facts. It doesn't mean refusing wise counsel. And it doesn't mean pretending that difficult circumstances don't exist.
Instead, it means living with confidence in the God who has revealed Himself through Scripture and through Jesus Christ.
Now, let's look back at our first lesson.
DAY ONE — FAITH WHEN THE ROAD AHEAD IS UNCLEAR On Day One, we studied Hebrews chapter 11, verse 1. It says: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen."
Now, we learned that biblical faith isn't simply wishful thinking.
It's confidence rooted in God's character and promises.
And we talked about how difficult uncertainty can feel.
Sometimes we want God to show us the entire journey before we're willing to take the first step.
We want to know what happens next. We want to know how long a difficult season will last. And we want to know whether our plans will succeed.
But faith doesn't always come with that kind of certainty.
Sometimes it means trusting God with what we cannot see.
Now, I want you to think about your own life.
Is there an area where you've been demanding certainty before you're willing to move forward?
Maybe it's a decision about your future. Maybe it's something involving your family. Maybe it's a responsibility you're hesitant to accept. Or maybe it's simply a season of waiting.
Now, here's something important. We shouldn't rush into decisions simply because we're afraid of waiting.
But we also shouldn't allow our desire for perfect certainty to keep us from doing what we already know is right.
So here's our first Around the Fire question. What uncertainty am I carrying right now, and how can I bring it before God honestly? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, if you're writing in your journal, take a moment to finish this sentence. "Lord, the part of my future I'm struggling to trust You with is..."
Now, don't rush. Be honest. Because God already knows what you're carrying.
DAY TWO — TAKING THE NEXT STEP Now, on Day Two, we studied Abraham.
We looked at Genesis chapter 12 and Hebrews chapter 11. And we learned that Abraham responded to God's call even though he didn't know every detail of the journey.
Hebrews chapter 11, verse 8, says: "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went."
Now, I love the connection between faith and obedience.
Abraham trusted God. And he responded.
But here's something important. Abraham had received a particular command from God.
That doesn't mean every idea or feeling we have is automatically a direct instruction from the Lord.
We need wisdom. We need Scripture. And we need humility when making decisions.
But when God's Word clearly teaches us something, we're called to respond faithfully.
Now, think about that. Sometimes obedience isn't dramatic.
Sometimes it's choosing honesty. Sometimes it's apologizing. Sometimes it's showing kindness. And sometimes it's refusing to compromise our integrity.
Now, here's our second Around the Fire question. Is there something I already know is right, but I've been delaying because it feels uncomfortable? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, maybe you're thinking about a conversation you need to have. Maybe you're thinking about a responsibility you've been avoiding. Or maybe you're thinking about a habit you need to change.
Whatever it is, ask God for wisdom.
And remember that faithful obedience isn't about proving how brave we are.
It's about honoring the Lord.
DAY THREE — FAITH OVER FEAR Now, on Day Three, we talked about fear.
And I think this is something that many of us struggle with.
Because fear can affect the way we think. The way we make decisions. And the way we understand our circumstances.
We studied Isaiah chapter 41, verse 10. And we talked about God's assurance of His presence and help to His people.
But we also looked at Psalm 56, verse 3. David said: "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee."
Now, I love those words. Because David didn't pretend he would never experience fear.
He acknowledged it.
"What time I am afraid..."
And then he declared where he would place his trust. "In thee."
Now, that's important. Because sometimes people think having faith means never feeling afraid.
But Scripture shows us faithful people experiencing fear.
And we learned that courage doesn't always mean the absence of fear.
Sometimes courage means doing what is right while acknowledging that we're afraid.
Now, here's something else we talked about. Faith doesn't mean ignoring genuine danger.
If you're in an unsafe situation, seeking safety is appropriate. If you're facing a medical concern, seeking medical care is appropriate. And if you're struggling with overwhelming anxiety, asking for help isn't a failure of faith.
God calls us to live wisely.
Now, here's our third Around the Fire question. What fear has been influencing my thoughts or decisions, and what would a wise, faithful response look like? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, think about that.
Maybe you need to gather information. Maybe you need to ask for support. Maybe you need to have a conversation. Or maybe you need to stop treating possibilities as though they're already facts.
Now, remember David's words. "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee."
DAY FOUR — WHEN GOD SAYS NO Now, on Day Four, we studied something that can be especially difficult. When our prayers aren't answered the way we hoped.
We looked at the apostle Paul's experience in Second Corinthians chapter 12.
Paul described a thorn in the flesh.
And he prayed three times for it to be removed.
But the Lord's response was different from what Paul requested.
Second Corinthians chapter 12, verse 9, says: "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness."
Now, those words are powerful.
Because Paul wasn't someone who lacked faith.
He was an apostle. A servant of Jesus Christ. And a man who endured extraordinary hardships for the gospel.
Yet he still experienced suffering.
And he still had a request that wasn't answered in the way he hoped.
Now, that reminds us of something important. An unanswered prayer doesn't automatically mean we've failed spiritually.
And we should be careful about assuming we know exactly why God has allowed a particular situation.
Sometimes we simply don't know.
But we can continue bringing our requests before Him.
We can pray honestly. Seek wisdom. And trust His character.
Now, here's our fourth Around the Fire question. Is there a disappointment or unanswered prayer that I need to bring before God with honesty and humility? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, maybe you've been praying for healing. Maybe you've been praying for a relationship. Maybe you've been hoping for an opportunity. Or maybe you've been carrying a request that hasn't been resolved.
Now, I want you to remember something. You don't have to pretend that disappointment doesn't hurt.
You can acknowledge it.
You can bring it before the Lord.
And you can continue trusting Him while seeking the wisdom and support you need.
DAY FIVE — KEEP WALKING Now, yesterday, we studied perseverance.
Our lesson was called Keep Walking — Faithfulness When the Journey Gets Hard.
And we looked at Galatians chapter 6, verse 9. It says: "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."
Now, we learned that Paul was encouraging believers to remain faithful in doing good.
Not simply to keep pursuing every personal goal indefinitely.
But to continue living according to the Spirit.
To keep doing what is right. To keep loving others. And to keep honoring God.
Now, here's something important. Faithfulness can be tiring.
Sometimes serving others requires sacrifice. Sometimes doing what is right is difficult. And sometimes progress feels slow.
But we also learned something else. Rest isn't failure.
Asking for help isn't failure. And recognizing our limits isn't failure.
Now, sometimes the faithful next step is continuing.
And sometimes it's slowing down.
Sometimes it's asking someone to share the burden.
And sometimes it's recognizing that a particular responsibility needs to change.
Now, here's our fifth Around the Fire question. Where have I been feeling weary, and what would faithful perseverance look like in this season? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, maybe you need encouragement. Maybe you need rest. Maybe you need practical support. Or maybe you need to remember why something matters.
Whatever the situation, bring it before the Lord.
THE CONNECTION BETWEEN ALL FIVE LESSONS Now, I want us to look at something beautiful.
When we put these five lessons together, we begin to see how they connect.
Faith teaches us to trust God when we cannot see the entire road.
Obedience teaches us to respond to what He has revealed.
Courage helps us face our fears with wisdom.
Surrender reminds us that God's wisdom is greater than our plans.
And perseverance encourages us to remain faithful when the journey becomes difficult.
Now, think about that.
These aren't five completely separate ideas.
They're connected parts of the Christian life.
Because sometimes we need faith to take the next step.
Sometimes we need courage to obey.
Sometimes we need humility when our plans change.
And sometimes we need perseverance to continue following Jesus through a difficult season.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Walking by faith is a daily practice of trusting God, seeking His wisdom, and responding faithfully to His Word.
THE LAMP FOR OUR FEET Now, let's return to Psalm 119, verse 105. It says: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
Now, we studied this verse during our earlier weeks together. But I want us to think about it again.
Because a lamp helps us see where we're stepping.
It provides light for the path before us.
But it doesn't necessarily illuminate every mile ahead.
Now, that's a beautiful picture of the guidance Scripture provides.
God's Word teaches us His truth. It helps us recognize what honors Him. And it gives us wisdom for faithful living.
Now, we may not know every detail of tomorrow.
But we can know what Scripture teaches us about how to live today.
We can practice kindness. We can pursue honesty. We can forgive. We can pray. And we can love others.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to understand every detail of your future to obey God today.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's take a moment to pray.
I want you to think about one area of your life where you need God's wisdom.
Maybe it's a decision. A fear. A disappointment. Or a responsibility that's become difficult.
Now, bring that before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for the lessons we've studied this week. Thank You for reminding us that faith is rooted in Your character and promises. Lord, help us trust You with what we cannot see. Give us courage to obey Your Word. Wisdom to respond to fear. Humility when our plans change. And strength to persevere when life becomes difficult. Father, help us recognize when we need rest and support. And remind us that we can come before You honestly. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
A PERSONAL MOMENT AROUND THE FIRE Now, I want to take a few moments to speak from the heart.
One thing I've learned through my own journey is that faith doesn't always look the way we expect.
Sometimes we imagine that having strong faith means we'll always feel confident.
That we'll always know what to do. That we'll never question anything. And that we'll always feel spiritually strong.
But real life can be complicated.
There are seasons when we're confident. And seasons when we're uncertain.
There are moments when we're encouraged. And moments when we're discouraged.
And there are times when we're simply trying to remain faithful through something we don't fully understand.
Now, I don't believe we need to pretend those difficult moments don't exist.
I believe we need to bring them before the Lord.
And that's one of the reasons I love studying Scripture together.
Because God's Word reminds us that we aren't the first people to experience uncertainty.
Abraham faced uncertainty. David experienced fear. Paul endured suffering. And the disciples struggled to understand what was happening around them.
Now, their circumstances were different from ours. But their stories remind us that faithfulness doesn't require perfect circumstances.
And maybe someone listening today needs that encouragement.
Maybe you're in a season where nothing feels settled.
Maybe you're waiting for an answer. Maybe you're facing a difficult decision. Or maybe you're simply tired.
Now, I can't promise that everything will become clear tomorrow.
But I can encourage you to keep seeking the Lord.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep asking for wisdom.
Because faith isn't about pretending we know everything.
It's about trusting the God who does.
AROUND THE FIRE — DEEPER REFLECTION Now, I want us to spend a few moments reflecting more deeply.
Imagine we're sitting together around the fire. There's no pressure to impress anyone. No need to pretend that everything is perfect. And no expectation that you have every answer.
We're simply taking time to reflect on God's Word.
Now, here's my first question. Which lesson from this week spoke most directly to your current season of life?
Was it faith? Obedience? Fear? Disappointment? Or perseverance?
Now, think about why that lesson stood out to you. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... What have I learned about God's character this week?
Maybe you've been reminded of His faithfulness. His wisdom. His grace. Or His sustaining power.
Now, take a moment to think about that. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What have I learned about myself?
Maybe you've recognized an area where you struggle with control. Maybe you've realized that fear has been affecting your decisions. Or maybe you've recognized that you need more rest and support.
Now, don't answer that question with condemnation.
Answer it with honesty and humility. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What is one faithful step I can take as I move into the next week?
Maybe it's making a decision. Maybe it's having a conversation. Maybe it's asking for help. Or maybe it's simply setting aside time each day to study Scripture. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION Now, before we move toward our closing reflection, I want us to bring everything back to Jesus.
Because our faith isn't simply confidence that life will become easier.
It's trust in Jesus Christ.
He lived a perfect life. He gave Himself on the cross. And He rose again.
Through Him, we have the promise of forgiveness and eternal life.
Now, that's the foundation of our hope.
Not our ability to predict the future. Not our ability to control every circumstance. And not our ability to remain strong through every difficulty.
Our hope rests in Christ.
And that's why we can continue walking by faith.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You don't have to see the entire road ahead to continue walking faithfully with God.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on what we don't know that we overlook what God has already revealed.
His Word teaches us how to live. His promises give us hope. And Jesus Christ is the foundation of our faith.
LIVING IT OUT Now, let's make today's reflection practical.
I want you to take five minutes today and look back over the lessons we've studied.
Write down one truth from each day.
Day One — Faith. Day Two — Obedience. Day Three — Courage. Day Four — Surrender. Day Five — Perseverance.
Now, after you've written those down, ask yourself... Which one do I need to focus on most right now?
And what is one practical step I can take to apply that truth?
Now, remember. The goal isn't to accomplish everything at once.
It's to grow in faithfulness. One day at a time.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the lesson that challenged me most this week was...
Our second prompt is... One area where I need to trust You more deeply is...
And our third prompt is... As I move into the next week, help me to...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will walk by faith, seek God's wisdom, and trust His Word to guide my next faithful step.
Now, say that again. I will walk by faith, seek God's wisdom, and trust His Word to guide my next faithful step.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Choose one Scripture from this week's lessons and memorize it.
Maybe it's Hebrews 11:1. Maybe it's Psalm 56:3. Maybe it's Second Corinthians 12:9. Or maybe it's Galatians 6:9.
Now, write that verse somewhere you'll see it.
And throughout the day, return to it in prayer.
Ask God to help you understand what it teaches. And consider how you can apply it faithfully.
CLOSING REFLECTION Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
There may be seasons when the road ahead feels uncertain.
When you don't know what tomorrow holds. When you're afraid of making the wrong decision. When your prayers haven't been answered the way you hoped. Or when you're simply tired of trying to figure everything out.
Now, in those moments, remember what we've studied this week.
Faith. Obedience. Courage. Surrender. And perseverance.
These aren't simply ideas to remember. They're truths we can practice as we follow Jesus.
And here's something important. You don't have to practice them perfectly.
We all need God's grace. We all need wisdom. And we all have room to grow.
But we can continue seeking the Lord.
We can continue learning from His Word.
And we can continue taking faithful steps.
One day at a time.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us through another week of Bible study. Thank You for the truths we've learned. And thank You for the opportunity to reflect on Your Word. Lord, You know every person listening today. You know the uncertainties they're facing. The fears they're carrying. The prayers they're waiting to see answered. And the responsibilities that have left them weary. Father, help us trust You. Give us wisdom to make faithful decisions. Courage to obey what is right. Patience when we must wait. And strength when the journey becomes difficult. Lord, I pray for the person who feels overwhelmed by uncertainty. Help them focus on what they can responsibly do today. I pray for the person who's afraid. Give them courage and wise support. I pray for the person who's disappointed. Remind them of Your grace and faithfulness. And I pray for the person who's weary. Help them find appropriate rest and encouragement. Father, thank You for Jesus Christ. Thank You for His sacrifice. His resurrection. And the promise of eternal life through Him. May our hope remain firmly rooted in our Savior. And may we continue walking by faith. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for gathering Around the Fire with me today. We've officially completed Week Seven, Day Six. And I hope this time of reflection has encouraged you to think about everything we've studied this week.
Tomorrow, we'll close Week Seven with a special day of encouragement, prayer, and practical application. Our lesson will be called... One Step at a Time — Trusting God with Tomorrow.
We'll bring together everything we've learned about walking by faith and prepare our hearts for the next chapter of our Bible study journey.
Until then, remember... You don't have to see the entire road ahead to take the next faithful step. Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep your eyes on Jesus.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: One Step at a Time: Trusting God with Tomorrow
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WELCOME TO DAY SEVEN Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today. Whether you're listening while getting ready for your day, traveling down the road, enjoying a quiet moment at home, or sitting with your Bible and a cup of coffee, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Seven, Day Seven. And that means we've reached the final day of our first week of original Bible studies together.
Now, I want you to think about that for a moment. We've spent this entire week talking about what it means to walk by faith when we can't see the way. And I don't know about you, but I think that's a lesson we can return to again and again throughout our lives.
Because no matter how much we grow spiritually, there will still be moments when we don't know what comes next. There will still be questions. There will still be decisions. And there will still be seasons when the future feels uncertain.
But here's something I've been thinking about. Sometimes we become so focused on tomorrow that we forget to be faithful with today.
We worry about next week. Next month. Next year. We wonder what will happen with our families. Our finances. Our health. Our relationships. And the dreams we've been carrying.
And before we know it, we're trying to carry the weight of a future that hasn't even arrived.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever spent an entire day worrying about something that might happen tomorrow?
You thought about it while getting ready. You thought about it while driving. You thought about it while working. And then you laid down at night, only to find yourself thinking about it all over again.
And sometimes, after all that worrying, tomorrow arrives and things don't happen the way you imagined.
Other times, the difficulty really does come. And we discover that we still have to face it one day at a time.
Now, I want you to hear something important. God hasn't asked us to control tomorrow. He's called us to trust Him and live faithfully today.
And that's what we're going to study together. Our lesson is called... One Step at a Time — Trusting God with Tomorrow.
Today, we're going to talk about what Jesus taught concerning worry. We're going to reflect on everything we've learned this week. And we're going to prepare our hearts to enter a new week of Bible study.
But first, let's pray.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for carrying us through this week of study. Thank You for the lessons about faith, obedience, courage, surrender, and perseverance. Lord, You know the things we're worried about. You know the questions we're carrying. And You know the situations that make tomorrow feel uncertain. Father, help us slow down today. Help us focus on what Your Word teaches. Give us wisdom for the responsibilities before us. And remind us that we don't have to know everything about the future to trust You. Lord, prepare our hearts for this time together. And may everything we study draw us closer to Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — MATTHEW 6:33–34 Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 6.
We're going to look at verses 33 and 34. But before we read them, I want to talk about the context.
These verses come from Jesus' Sermon on the Mount. And in this part of His teaching, Jesus addresses worry about everyday needs.
He talks about food. Clothing. And the concerns people carry about how their needs will be met.
Now, these weren't imaginary concerns. Food and clothing were real necessities. And Jesus wasn't telling people that those needs didn't matter.
Instead, He was teaching His followers to seek God's kingdom and trust their Heavenly Father's care.
Now, let's read Matthew chapter 6, verses 33 and 34, from the King James Version. "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
Now, let's read that last verse again. "Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
Now, I want us to slow down and think about those words. Because Jesus is teaching something that can change the way we approach everyday life.
He tells His followers not to be consumed by anxiety about tomorrow.
And notice the reason He gives. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
Now, isn't that the truth?
Sometimes today already has enough responsibilities. Enough decisions. Enough challenges. And enough things that require our attention.
But then we begin adding tomorrow's worries. And next week's worries. And all the possible things that might happen months from now.
And suddenly we're carrying more than we can reasonably manage.
Now, here's something important. Jesus isn't telling us never to plan. He's not telling us to ignore our responsibilities. And He's not telling us to avoid preparing for the future.
Planning can be wise. Saving money can be responsible. Preparing for important decisions can be necessary.
But there's a difference between preparing for tomorrow and being consumed by anxiety about tomorrow.
And that's the difference Jesus is helping us understand.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH We can prepare wisely for tomorrow without allowing tomorrow's uncertainties to consume today.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we think trusting God means we shouldn't make plans.
But that's not what Scripture teaches.
Trusting God means acknowledging that our plans are limited. That our understanding is incomplete. And that our ultimate confidence belongs in Him.
WHEN TOMORROW STEALS TODAY Now, let's talk about something I think many of us have experienced. When tomorrow begins stealing our peace today.
Maybe you have an appointment coming up. And you're worried about what you might hear.
Maybe you're waiting for an important phone call. And every time your phone rings, your heart starts racing.
Maybe you're facing a financial decision. And you're trying to figure out how everything will work out.
Or maybe you're simply worried about someone you love.
Now, those concerns are real. And sometimes they require action.
But here's something I want you to think about. How much of your energy have you spent worrying about things you cannot change today?
Now, I'm not asking that question to make anyone feel guilty. Because worry can be difficult to manage. And sometimes anxiety becomes overwhelming.
But I want us to consider how we respond to uncertainty.
Sometimes we keep asking questions that nobody can answer yet.
What if this happens? What if that happens? What if things don't work out?
And we begin treating every possible outcome as though it's already happening.
Now, here's something practical. When you find yourself overwhelmed by tomorrow, ask three questions. What do I actually know? What can I responsibly do today? And what remains outside my control?
Now, those questions won't solve every problem. But they can help us separate today's responsibilities from tomorrow's uncertainties.
And sometimes that's an important first step.
