SEEK FIRST THE KINGDOM OF GOD Now, let's return to Matthew chapter 6, verse 33. Jesus says: "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you."
Now, I want us to notice the order. "Seek ye first..."
Jesus directs our attention toward God's kingdom and righteousness.
Now, that doesn't mean our everyday responsibilities don't matter.
It means our relationship with God and our commitment to His ways should shape the way we approach those responsibilities.
We seek to honor Him in our decisions. In our relationships. In the way we handle money. In the way we treat people. And in the way we respond to difficult circumstances.
Now, here's something important. This passage shouldn't be turned into a promise that every Christian will become wealthy or never experience material hardship.
Jesus is teaching His followers to trust the Father's care and prioritize His kingdom.
And that's different from treating faith as a guarantee of a comfortable life.
Now, here's a question I want you to consider. When you're worried about the future, what becomes your first priority?
Do you immediately begin trying to control every detail? Do you allow fear to guide your decisions? Or do you take time to pray, seek wisdom, and remember what Scripture teaches?
Now, I think that's something all of us can grow in.
Because seeking God's kingdom first is a daily practice.
THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN PLANNING AND WORRYING Now, let's talk about something practical. Because I don't want anyone to leave today's lesson thinking that making plans means they don't trust God.
Planning and worrying aren't the same thing.
Planning asks... What can I responsibly do to prepare?
Worry often keeps asking... What if everything goes wrong?
Planning looks for information. Worry can become trapped in possibilities.
Planning helps us identify our next steps. Worry can make us feel as though we must solve every possible problem before it happens.
Now, sometimes planning itself can become excessive. And sometimes what we call preparation is actually an attempt to eliminate every uncertainty.
But we need to remember that we cannot control everything.
And here's something important. We don't have to.
We can make responsible plans. Seek wise counsel. And take appropriate action.
Then we can acknowledge the limits of our control.
Now, that's not always easy. But it's something we can practice.
THE LAMP FOR TODAY Now, let's turn to Psalm 119, verse 105. The King James Version says: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
Now, we've returned to this verse several times throughout our Bible studies. And I think it's especially meaningful today.
Because a lamp provides light for the path.
It helps us recognize where we're stepping.
Now, think about walking outside at night with a flashlight.
You may not be able to see the entire road.
But you can see enough to take the next careful step.
And as you continue walking, more of the path becomes visible.
Now, that's a helpful picture of how God's Word guides us.
Scripture doesn't tell us every detail about our personal future.
It doesn't tell us exactly what will happen next month. Or how every decision will turn out.
But it reveals God's character. His commands. His promises. And the wisdom we need for faithful living.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God's Word gives us truth for today, even when tomorrow remains uncertain.
WHEN WE WANT ALL THE ANSWERS Now, I want to ask you something. Have you ever prayed... "Lord, just show me what happens next"?
Maybe you've said... "If I could just know how this turns out, I could finally relax."
Now, I think many of us have felt that way.
Because uncertainty can be uncomfortable.
We want answers. We want reassurance. And we want to know that everything will be okay.
But here's something important. Even when we receive answers to one question, another question may eventually arise.
Life continues changing. Circumstances develop. And new decisions appear.
So if our peace depends entirely on knowing everything about the future, we're going to struggle.
That's why Scripture directs our attention toward the Lord.
Not because our questions don't matter. But because our confidence needs a stronger foundation than our ability to predict what comes next.
PROVERBS 3 — TRUSTING GOD'S WISDOM Now, let's return to Proverbs chapter 3, verses 5 and 6. It says: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."
Now, we've studied these verses throughout Week Seven.
And I want you to notice how beautifully they connect with today's lesson.
We don't understand everything.
We don't know every outcome. And we don't always recognize the best path immediately.
But we can seek God's wisdom.
Now, here's something important. Trusting God doesn't mean refusing to think carefully.
It doesn't mean ignoring facts. And it doesn't mean assuming that every personal desire is a message from God.
Instead, it means approaching life with humility.
We recognize that our understanding is limited. And we seek to align our decisions with God's Word.
Now, that may involve prayer. Studying Scripture. Seeking wise counsel. And gathering information.
But ultimately, we remember that our lives belong to the Lord.
A MOMENT TO PAUSE AND PRAY Now, I want us to take a moment.
Think about something you've been worrying about.
Maybe it's an upcoming appointment. A family situation. A financial concern. Or an important decision.
Now, ask yourself... Is there something I can responsibly do about this today?
If there is, ask God for wisdom to take that step.
And if there isn't, bring that uncertainty before Him. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the concerns we're carrying about tomorrow. You know the questions we haven't been able to answer. And You know the situations that feel uncertain. Lord, give us wisdom for today. Help us recognize the responsibilities we can address. And help us acknowledge what remains outside our control. Father, teach us to trust You without becoming careless or irresponsible. And remind us that our hope rests in Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
GOD'S MERCIES ARE NEW EVERY MORNING Now, let's turn to Lamentations chapter 3.
I want us to look at verses 22 and 23. The King James Version says: "It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."
Now, I love those words. "They are new every morning."
But let's remember the context. Lamentations is a book filled with grief. It reflects the devastation surrounding Jerusalem's destruction.
These words of hope are spoken in the midst of sorrow.
Now, that's important. Because the writer isn't pretending that everything is wonderful.
He's acknowledging suffering while remembering God's mercy and faithfulness.
And I think that's a beautiful reminder for us.
Sometimes a new morning doesn't mean every problem has disappeared.
Sometimes we wake up facing the same responsibilities. The same uncertainties. And the same difficult circumstances.
But God's character hasn't changed.
His mercy and faithfulness remain.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A new day doesn't require a perfect life to be an opportunity for faithful living.
Maybe yesterday was difficult. Maybe you made a mistake. Maybe you were overwhelmed. Or maybe you simply didn't accomplish everything you planned.
Now, today is an opportunity to return to the Lord. To seek His wisdom. And to take another faithful step.
YOU DON'T HAVE TO FIX EVERYTHING TODAY Now, I want to speak to someone who may be feeling overwhelmed.
Maybe you're carrying several responsibilities.
Maybe you're trying to care for your family. Manage your work. Handle difficult circumstances. And still find time for yourself.
And sometimes it feels like everything needs your attention at once.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to solve every problem in one day.
Now, some responsibilities really are urgent. And some situations require immediate action.
But not everything has to be completed at once.
Sometimes wisdom means prioritizing.
It means identifying what's most important. It means asking for help. And it means recognizing that some things can wait.
Now, here's something practical. When you're feeling overwhelmed, write down the things that need your attention.
Then separate them into three groups. Things that must be addressed today. Things that can be planned for later. And things that are outside your control.
Now, that simple exercise can help you recognize where your attention is needed.
And it can remind you that you don't have to carry every uncertainty as though it's an immediate responsibility.
LOOKING BACK OVER WEEK SEVEN Now, before we move into our final reflections, I want us to look back over everything we've studied this week.
On Day One, we talked about faith when the road ahead is unclear.
We learned that biblical faith is rooted in God's character and promises.
On Day Two, we talked about obedience.
We studied Abraham and learned that faithful obedience doesn't always require complete understanding.
On Day Three, we talked about fear.
We learned that experiencing fear doesn't automatically mean we've failed spiritually.
We can bring our fears before God and seek His wisdom.
On Day Four, we talked about unanswered prayers and disappointment.
We studied Paul's thorn in the flesh. And we were reminded that Christ's grace is sufficient, even when circumstances don't change the way we hoped.
On Day Five, we talked about perseverance.
We learned that remaining faithful doesn't mean ignoring our limits.
Sometimes we need courage to continue. And sometimes we need wisdom to rest.
Then yesterday, we gathered Around the Fire.
And we reflected on how all those lessons connect.
Faith. Obedience. Courage. Surrender. And perseverance.
Now, today, we're bringing those lessons together with one final truth.
We can trust God with tomorrow while remaining faithful today.
PHILIPPIANS 3 — PRESSING FORWARD Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 3.
I want us to read verses 13 and 14. Paul writes: "Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus."
Now, let's think about that. Paul describes a life directed toward Christ.
He acknowledges that he hasn't reached perfection.
But he continues pressing forward.
Now, that doesn't mean he literally forgot everything that happened in his past.
It means he refused to treat his past as the final measure of his spiritual future.
And he continued pursuing the goal set before him in Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to consider. Are you allowing yesterday to keep you from living faithfully today?
Maybe you're carrying regret. Maybe you're disappointed about something that didn't work out. Or maybe you're constantly thinking about mistakes you've made.
Now, our past can teach us important lessons.
And sometimes we need to take responsibility for things that happened.
But we don't have to remain trapped in endless regret.
Through Christ, we can seek forgiveness, make appropriate changes, and continue growing.
Now, that's an important part of walking by faith.
We learn from yesterday. We live faithfully today. And we entrust tomorrow to the Lord.
WHAT IF TOMORROW IS DIFFICULT? Now, I want us to consider something honestly.
What if tomorrow is difficult?
What if the appointment doesn't bring the news we hoped for? What if the situation doesn't change? What if the answer is disappointing?
Now, I don't ask those questions to make anyone afraid.
I ask them because biblical faith isn't built on the assumption that life will always be easy.
Jesus never promised His followers a life without hardship.
But He did call them to trust Him.
Now, if tomorrow brings difficulty, we can seek wisdom. We can ask for help. We can pray. And we can take the responsibilities of that day one step at a time.
Now, we may not feel strong. We may not have every answer. And we may need support from others.
But we can continue turning toward Christ.
And that's where our hope belongs.
WHAT IF TOMORROW BRINGS SOMETHING BEAUTIFUL? Now, let's consider the other side.
What if tomorrow brings something beautiful?
What if you receive encouraging news? What if an opportunity opens? What if you experience a moment of joy you never expected?
Now, sometimes we become so focused on what might go wrong that we forget to recognize the blessings already around us.
We become so consumed with future concerns that we overlook today's opportunities for gratitude.
Now, I want you to think about something. What is one thing you can thank God for today?
Maybe it's a person you love. Maybe it's an answered prayer. Maybe it's a quiet moment. Or maybe it's simply the opportunity to spend time in His Word.
Now, take a moment to thank Him. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through our final reflection questions for Week Seven.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What have I been worrying about that I cannot control today?
Now, think about that honestly.
Maybe it's a future outcome. Maybe it's another person's decision. Or maybe it's something that hasn't happened yet. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... What responsibility has God placed before me today?
Maybe it's caring for your family. Maybe it's completing an important task. Maybe it's showing kindness. Or maybe it's spending time in prayer and Scripture. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What truth from Week Seven has encouraged me the most?
Was it trusting God when the road is unclear? Taking the next step? Facing fear? Surrendering disappointment? Or persevering through difficulty? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What is one faithful step I can take as I enter a new week?
Now, don't make this complicated.
Think about one realistic action. One way to apply what you've learned. One opportunity to honor God. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — OUR HOPE FOR TOMORROW Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because I don't want us to finish this week thinking that walking by faith is simply about becoming better at handling uncertainty.
It's about knowing and following Jesus Christ.
Our hope isn't rooted in positive thinking. It's not rooted in our ability to control circumstances. And it's not rooted in believing that everything will happen according to our plans.
Our hope is rooted in the Savior.
Jesus lived a sinless life. He died on the cross for our sins. And He rose again.
Through Him, we have the promise of forgiveness and eternal life.
Now, that is the foundation of Christian hope.
And because of that hope, we can face tomorrow with confidence in God's character.
Not confidence that every circumstance will be easy. But confidence that our Savior is faithful.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's our final Grace Note for Week Seven. You don't have to carry tomorrow's burdens before tomorrow arrives. Seek God's wisdom, be faithful with today, and entrust the future to Him.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so overwhelmed by what might happen next that we forget what God has placed before us right now.
Today is an opportunity to pray. To learn. To love. To serve. And to grow.
And that's something worth remembering.
LIVING IT OUT — YOUR NEXT FAITHFUL STEP Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a few minutes and write down three things.
First... One thing you're grateful for today.
Second... One concern about tomorrow that you need to bring before God.
And third... One faithful action you can take today.
Now, look at what you've written.
You have gratitude for what God has already provided. You have an opportunity to bring your concerns before Him. And you have a practical step you can take.
Now, that's a meaningful way to approach the day.
Not by pretending the future doesn't matter. But by refusing to allow tomorrow's uncertainties to consume today's opportunities.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the concern about tomorrow that I've been carrying is...
Our second prompt is... One way I can seek Your kingdom first today is...
And our third prompt is... As I move into a new week, help me trust You by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
And remember that you don't have to write the perfect prayer. God knows your heart.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek God first, live faithfully today, and trust Him with the uncertainties of tomorrow.
Now, say that again. I will seek God first, live faithfully today, and trust Him with the uncertainties of tomorrow.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's our final Faith Challenge for Week Seven. Memorize Matthew chapter 6, verse 34. "Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
Now, throughout the day, whenever you find yourself becoming overwhelmed by tomorrow, return to that verse.
Ask yourself... What can I responsibly do today?
And what do I need to entrust to God?
Then choose one practical action.
Maybe it's making a plan. Maybe it's having a conversation. Maybe it's asking for help. Or maybe it's taking time to pray.
AROUND THE FIRE — OUR FINAL WEEK SEVEN MOMENT Now, before we close, I want us to imagine we're sitting together around the fire one more time.
We've spent this entire week talking about faith.
And I want to ask you something. If you could speak to the version of yourself who was afraid to take the next step, what would you say?
Maybe you'd say... You don't have to know everything.
Maybe you'd say... It's okay to ask for help.
Maybe you'd say... Don't let fear make every decision for you.
Or maybe you'd say... Keep your eyes on Jesus.
Now, I want you to think about that. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] And here's my encouragement to you. Whatever season you're walking through, don't measure your faith by how perfectly you handle every situation.
We all have moments of uncertainty. We all experience fear. And we all need God's grace.
But we can keep returning to Him.
We can keep learning from His Word.
And we can keep taking faithful steps.
One day at a time.
PREPARING OUR HEARTS FOR WEEK EIGHT Now, before we close, I want to share something about where we're going next.
This week, we've focused on walking by faith when we cannot see the way.
But next week, we're going to talk about something closely connected to faith. Waiting.
Because sometimes we know what we're praying for. We know what we're hoping for. And we know what we'd like to see happen.
But we don't know when anything will change.
And waiting can be difficult.
Sometimes waiting brings uncertainty. Sometimes it brings disappointment. And sometimes it reveals just how much we want to control the timing of our lives.
But Scripture has so much to teach us about patience, hope, and trusting the Lord.
So next week, our theme will be... Trusting God's Timing in the Waiting.
And we're going to begin with a lesson called... When God Makes You Wait — Finding Faith in the In-Between.
We'll talk about what it means to wait on the Lord without losing hope. And we'll explore how Scripture encourages us to remain faithful during seasons when answers haven't arrived.
FINAL WEEK SEVEN REFLECTION Now, before we pray, I want to leave you with one final thought.
You may not know what tomorrow holds.
You may not know how a situation will turn out. You may not know when an answer will come. And you may not know exactly what the next season of your life will look like.
But you can know the One who holds your future.
And through Jesus Christ, you can have a hope that goes beyond your present circumstances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faith doesn't require you to see the entire journey.
Sometimes it simply calls you to take the next faithful step.
And then another.
And another.
Not because you have everything figured out. But because you're learning to trust the Lord.
So as we close Week Seven, I want you to remember these words.
You don't have to solve tomorrow today.
You don't have to understand everything before you pray.
And you don't have to become perfectly strong before you can follow Jesus.
You can come to Him just as you are.
With your questions. Your concerns. Your hopes. And your uncertainties.
And you can continue walking faithfully with Him.
One step at a time.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us through another week of Bible study. Thank You for every lesson we've learned. Thank You for reminding us that we can trust You even when the road ahead is unclear. Lord, You know every person listening today. You know the things they're worried about. The decisions they're facing. The prayers they're waiting to see answered. And the burdens they've been carrying. Father, help us focus on what You've placed before us today. Give us wisdom to make responsible decisions. Courage to obey Your Word. Patience when we must wait. And strength when the journey becomes difficult. Lord, I pray for the person who's overwhelmed by tomorrow. Help them recognize what they can responsibly do today. I pray for the person who's afraid of an uncertain outcome. Give them wisdom and surround them with compassionate support. I pray for the person who's discouraged by unanswered prayers. Remind them of Your grace and faithfulness. And I pray for the person who's simply tired. Help them find rest, encouragement, and the support they need. Father, as we prepare to begin a new week of Bible study, help us grow in patience. Teach us what it means to wait on You. Help us remain faithful when answers don't come quickly. And remind us that our hope rests in Jesus Christ. Thank You for His sacrifice on the cross. Thank You for His resurrection. And thank You for the promise of eternal life through Him. May we continue walking by faith. Not by sight. And may our lives reflect Your love and truth. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Seven, Day Seven. And that means we've finished our first full week of original Bible studies together!
I'm so thankful you've been part of this journey. And I hope these lessons have encouraged you to keep opening your Bible, keep praying, and keep growing in your relationship with Jesus Christ.
Tomorrow, we'll begin Week Eight. And our new theme will be... Trusting God's Timing in the Waiting.
Our first lesson will be... When God Makes You Wait — Finding Faith in the In-Between.
Until then, remember... You don't have to know everything about tomorrow to live faithfully today.
Keep your eyes on Jesus. Keep trusting His Word. And keep taking the next faithful step.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

weeks.title: Trusting God's Timing in the Waiting

lessons.title: When God Makes You Wait: Finding Faith in the In-Between
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WELCOME TO WEEK EIGHT Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today. Whether you're listening while getting ready for work, driving down the road, sitting at home with your Bible, or taking a quiet moment with the Lord, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Eight, Day One. And we're beginning a brand-new week of Bible study together.
Last week, we spent seven days talking about walking by faith when we can't see the way. We talked about trusting God when the road ahead is unclear. Taking the next faithful step. Facing our fears. Trusting God's wisdom when our prayers aren't answered the way we hoped. And persevering when the journey becomes difficult.
Then, on our final day, we talked about taking life one step at a time. Trusting God with tomorrow while remaining faithful today.
But today, we're moving into something that connects with every one of those lessons. Waiting.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever prayed for something... And then waited?
And waited.
And waited some more.
Maybe you were waiting for a phone call. Maybe you were waiting for test results. Maybe you were waiting for a relationship to heal. Maybe you were waiting for a financial situation to improve. Or maybe you were waiting for something you believed would become an important part of your future.
And at first, you were patient.
You prayed. You trusted. You tried to remain hopeful.
But as time passed, you began wondering... Lord, how much longer?
Have You heard me? Am I supposed to keep waiting? Or am I supposed to do something different?
Now, I think many of us can relate to those questions. Because waiting can be one of the most difficult parts of life.
Sometimes the difficulty isn't knowing what we want. It's not knowing when anything will change.
And sometimes, if we're being honest, we become frustrated because our timeline and our circumstances don't match.
We had a plan. We had expectations. And we imagined that certain things would happen by a particular time.
But then life unfolded differently.
And now we're living in the space between what we hoped for and what has actually happened.
I call that the in-between.
The place where we've prayed, but we don't yet know the outcome.
The place where we've taken responsible steps, but we're still waiting for circumstances to change.
The place where we're trying to remain faithful, even though we don't have every answer.
Now, here's something I want you to understand right from the beginning. Waiting on God isn't the same as doing nothing.
Sometimes waiting involves prayer. Sometimes it involves preparation. Sometimes it involves making responsible decisions. And sometimes it involves recognizing that we cannot control the timing of every outcome.
But through it all, we can continue seeking the Lord.
And that's what we're going to study this week. Our theme is... Trusting God's Timing in the Waiting.
And today's lesson is called... When God Makes You Wait — Finding Faith in the In-Between.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the opportunity to begin a new week of Bible study. Lord, today we're talking about waiting. And You know how difficult waiting can be. You know the prayers we've prayed. The answers we're hoping for. The decisions we're facing. And the situations that haven't changed. Father, help us understand what Your Word teaches about patience, hope, and trust. Give us wisdom to recognize what we can responsibly do. Give us peace as we bring our concerns before You. And help us remain faithful during seasons of uncertainty. Lord, prepare our hearts to receive Your Word today. And may everything we study draw us closer to Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — PSALM 27:13–14 Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 27.
We're going to begin with verses 13 and 14. The King James Version says: "I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living. Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD."
Now, let's read verse 14 again. "Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD."
Now, I want us to slow down and think about those words. Because David gives us a powerful picture of what it means to wait on the Lord.
But first, let's talk about the context. Psalm 27 is a psalm of confidence and prayer.
David speaks about the Lord as his light and salvation. He describes opposition and danger. And he expresses his desire to seek the Lord's presence.
Now, this wasn't a situation where everything in David's life was easy.
He was facing real concerns. And yet, he continued placing his confidence in God.
Then, near the end of the psalm, he says... "Wait on the LORD."
Now, I want you to notice something. David connects waiting with courage.
"Be of good courage..."
Now, why would waiting require courage?
Because waiting can be difficult.
Sometimes waiting means living with unanswered questions. Sometimes it means facing uncertainty. And sometimes it means continuing to trust God when our circumstances haven't changed.
Now, here's something important. David doesn't tell us to place our hope in a particular timeline.
He tells us to wait on the Lord.
And that brings us to today's key truth.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Waiting faithfully means placing our hope in God while continuing to live according to His Word.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we think waiting means putting our lives on hold.
We think... Once this situation changes, then I'll be happy. Once I get that answer, then I'll have peace. Once that door opens, then I'll be able to move forward.
But here's something important. We can continue growing spiritually while we're waiting.
We can continue loving others. We can continue serving. We can continue learning. And we can continue honoring God in the responsibilities already before us.
Now, waiting may be part of our circumstances. But it doesn't have to become the only thing that defines our lives.
THE DIFFICULTY OF THE IN-BETWEEN Now, let's talk about something many of us experience. The difficulty of living in the in-between.
Maybe you've made a decision. You've submitted an application. You've attended an appointment. Or you've had an important conversation.
And now there's nothing more you can responsibly do until you receive an answer.
Now, that can be frustrating.
Because we often feel more comfortable when we're taking action.
We like knowing that we're making progress. We like checking things off our lists. And we like seeing results.
But waiting doesn't always give us that sense of accomplishment.
Sometimes it simply requires patience.
And sometimes patience is difficult because we don't know how long the waiting will last.
Now, here's something I want you to consider. Have you ever found yourself constantly checking for an update?
Checking your email. Checking your phone. Checking the status of something. And wondering whether anything has changed.
Now, sometimes checking for updates is necessary.
But sometimes we begin checking so frequently that it consumes our attention.
And even when there's no new information, we keep looking.
Now, here's something practical. When you're waiting for an answer, it can help to identify when a follow-up is appropriate.
Maybe there's a date when you should check again. Maybe there's someone you need to contact. Or maybe you've already done everything you can reasonably do.
Now, once you've identified those responsibilities, you can give your attention to the things that need you today.
Because waiting doesn't mean your life has stopped.
ABRAHAM — WAITING FOR GOD'S PROMISE Now, let's turn to Genesis chapter 15.
We're going to revisit Abraham.
Because last week, we studied his obedience. We talked about how he followed God's call even though he didn't know every detail of the journey.
But today, we're going to look at another part of Abraham's story. Waiting.
God had promised Abraham that he would become a great nation.
But Abraham and Sarah did not have a child together.
And as time passed, that promise raised difficult questions.
Now, let's read Genesis chapter 15, verses 2 through 6. "And Abram said, Lord GOD, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus? And Abram said, Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir. And, behold, the word of the LORD came unto him, saying, This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness."
Now, let's think about that. Abraham had received a promise from God.
But the circumstances around him didn't yet reflect the fulfillment of that promise.
He was growing older. Sarah was growing older. And they still didn't have the child God had promised.
Now, I want you to notice something. Abraham brought his concern before the Lord.
He didn't pretend that he had no questions.
He asked how the promise would be fulfilled.
And God responded by reaffirming His promise.
Now, here's something important. Abraham's situation involved a specific promise that God had directly given him.
That doesn't mean every personal desire we have is a promise from God.
We need to distinguish between what Scripture actually promises and what we hope will happen.
But Abraham's story does teach us something about God's faithfulness.
God was faithful to the promise He made.
And Abraham was called to trust Him.
WHEN THE WAIT IS LONGER THAN EXPECTED Now, let's move forward in Abraham's story.
In Genesis chapter 21, we read about the birth of Isaac.
Let's read Genesis chapter 21, verses 1 through 3. "And the LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did unto Sarah as he had spoken. For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him. And Abraham called the name of his son that was born unto him, whom Sarah bare to him, Isaac."
Now, notice those words. "At the set time..."
God fulfilled the promise He had made.
But Abraham and Sarah experienced a long period of waiting.
And their story wasn't without mistakes.
They struggled. They made decisions that created complications. And they experienced the consequences of those decisions.
Now, that's important. Because sometimes we imagine that faithful people always wait perfectly.
But Scripture shows us something different.
Abraham and Sarah were real people. They experienced uncertainty. And they made mistakes.
Yet God's faithfulness remained.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God's faithfulness doesn't depend on our ability to handle every season perfectly.
We still need to take responsibility for our decisions. We still need to seek wisdom. And we still need to grow.
But our hope rests in God's character.
WHEN WE TRY TO CONTROL THE TIMING Now, let's talk about something that can happen during seasons of waiting.
Sometimes we become impatient.
And when we're impatient, we may begin trying to force an outcome.
Maybe we rush into a decision. Maybe we ignore warning signs. Maybe we pressure someone to give us an answer. Or maybe we make a choice simply because we're tired of waiting.
Now, here's something important. Not every delay means we should remain passive.
Sometimes circumstances require action. Sometimes we need to make a decision. And sometimes waiting too long can create problems.
That's why we need wisdom.
But we should be careful about allowing impatience to become the primary reason for our decisions.
Now, ask yourself something. Am I making this decision because it's wise and responsible?
Or am I making it because I simply want the uncertainty to end?
Now, that's an important question.
Because sometimes the desire to escape uncertainty can lead us toward choices we haven't thought through carefully.
And that's when we need to slow down. Pray. Gather information. And seek wise counsel.
WAITING IS NOT THE SAME AS BEING FORGOTTEN Now, I want to speak to someone who may be feeling overlooked.
Maybe you've been waiting for something for a long time.
And you've watched other people move forward.
You've watched them receive opportunities. Reach milestones. And experience things you've been hoping for.
And somewhere along the way, you've begun wondering... "Lord, what about me?"
Now, I want you to understand something. We should be careful about measuring God's love by comparing our circumstances with someone else's.
Different people experience different opportunities. Different challenges. And different timelines.
And we don't always know the full story of what someone else is carrying.
Now, here's something important. A delayed outcome doesn't automatically mean God has forgotten you.
But it also doesn't mean every desired outcome is guaranteed to happen eventually.
Sometimes the answer may be different from what we hoped. Sometimes circumstances change. And sometimes we have to make new plans.
But through those experiences, we can continue trusting God's character.
And we can remember that our worth isn't determined by how quickly we reach a particular milestone.
LAMENTATIONS — HOPE IN THE WAITING Now, let's turn to Lamentations chapter 3.
I want us to read verses 25 and 26. The King James Version says: "The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD."
Now, let's think about the context.
Lamentations is a book filled with grief. It reflects the devastation surrounding Jerusalem's destruction.
And yet, in the middle of that sorrow, we find words of hope.
Now, that's important. Because waiting on the Lord isn't something Scripture discusses only during comfortable seasons.
Sometimes waiting takes place in the middle of suffering.
Sometimes it involves grief. Uncertainty. And unanswered questions.
But the writer reminds us of the goodness of the Lord.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Hope isn't the same as pretending that everything is easy.
Hope means continuing to look toward God's faithfulness even when circumstances are difficult.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about something you've been waiting for.
Maybe it's an answer. A decision. A change in circumstances. Or an opportunity.
Now, ask yourself... What have I been feeling during this waiting season?
Maybe it's frustration. Fear. Discouragement. Or exhaustion.
Now, bring those feelings before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the things we're waiting for. You know the answers we're hoping to receive. And You know the uncertainty we're carrying. Lord, help us trust Your character. Give us wisdom to recognize what we can responsibly do. Patience when circumstances remain unresolved. And courage when we need to make difficult decisions. Father, help us continue growing spiritually during seasons of waiting. And remind us that our hope rests in Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
ISAIAH 40 — RENEWED STRENGTH Now, let's turn to Isaiah chapter 40.
We're going to read verses 28 through 31. The King James Version says: "Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding. He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength. Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."
Now, I love this passage.
Because it begins by reminding us who God is.
He is the everlasting God. The Creator of the ends of the earth.
He doesn't become exhausted. He doesn't lose strength. And His understanding is beyond ours.
Now, think about that. We become tired. We become discouraged. And sometimes we reach our limits.
But God is not limited in the way we are.
And the passage reminds us that He gives strength to the weary.
Now, here's something important. This doesn't mean believers should ignore physical exhaustion.
It doesn't mean we should refuse medical care. And it doesn't mean we should continue carrying responsibilities that require additional support.
But it does remind us that we can seek strength from the Lord.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Waiting on God doesn't require pretending you're never tired.
You can acknowledge your limitations. Seek appropriate rest. And continue depending on Him.
WHAT CAN GOD TEACH US WHILE WE WAIT? Now, let's talk about something important.
Sometimes we become so focused on the outcome we're waiting for that we overlook opportunities for growth in the present.
Now, I want to be careful here.
We shouldn't assume that every delay has been arranged to teach us one particular lesson.
We don't always know why something is taking longer than expected.
But we can still ask how to live faithfully while we wait.
Maybe this season gives us an opportunity to practice patience.
Maybe it reminds us to seek wisdom.
Maybe it reveals areas where we've been trying to control things that aren't ours to control.
Or maybe it encourages us to pay attention to the responsibilities and relationships already in our lives.
Now, those are meaningful opportunities.
Because spiritual growth doesn't have to stop simply because an answer hasn't arrived.
ROMANS 8 — WAITING WITH HOPE Now, let's turn to Romans chapter 8.
We're going to read verses 24 and 25. The King James Version says: "For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it."
Now, let's understand the context.
Paul is discussing the hope of future redemption.
Believers have received salvation in Christ, but we still await the fullness of what God has promised.
And Paul connects that hope with patient endurance.
Now, that's important. Because Christian hope is much greater than simply hoping that our personal plans will succeed.
Our ultimate hope is rooted in Jesus Christ and God's promise of final redemption.
And that hope gives us a foundation for patience.
Even when our present circumstances are difficult.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our greatest hope isn't tied to a particular date on the calendar. It's tied to Jesus Christ.
HEBREWS 10 — THE NEED FOR PATIENCE Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 10.
We're going to read verses 35 and 36. The King James Version says: "Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward. For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise."
Now, these words were written to believers who needed encouragement to remain faithful.
They were facing pressure and hardship.
And the writer reminded them not to abandon their confidence.
Now, I want you to notice something. "For ye have need of patience..."
Patience is something we need.
Not because waiting is always easy. But because following Christ involves endurance.
Sometimes we don't see immediate results. Sometimes we face opposition. And sometimes we must continue trusting God's promises while living through difficult circumstances.
Now, here's something important. The promise in this passage is connected to the believer's ultimate hope in Christ.
It's not a guarantee that every personal goal will eventually be fulfilled.
But it does encourage us to remain faithful.
THE DANGER OF COMPARING TIMELINES Now, let's talk about something that can make waiting even harder. Comparison.
Maybe you've watched someone else receive something you've been hoping for.
Maybe someone else got the opportunity. Reached the milestone. Or experienced the change you've been praying about.
And you found yourself wondering... "Why them and not me?"
Now, I think that's a feeling many people understand.
But here's something important. Comparison can make us overlook the life God has placed before us.
We become so focused on someone else's circumstances that we lose sight of our own responsibilities and opportunities.
Now, that doesn't mean we shouldn't celebrate other people's blessings.
And it doesn't mean we shouldn't acknowledge our own disappointment.
We can do both.
We can be genuinely happy for someone else. And still bring our own sadness before the Lord.
Now, that's a mature and honest response.
Because another person's progress doesn't determine our worth.
And another person's timeline doesn't tell us everything about our own future.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What am I waiting for right now?
Maybe it's an answer. A change. A decision. Or an opportunity.
Take a moment to identify it honestly. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... How has this waiting season been affecting my thoughts and emotions?
Have you been feeling impatient? Discouraged? Afraid? Or overwhelmed?
Now, don't judge yourself for those feelings. Simply acknowledge them. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What can I responsibly do while I wait?
Maybe you need to prepare. Gather information. Seek advice. Or continue fulfilling your current responsibilities. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What truth about God's character can help me remain hopeful?
Maybe it's His faithfulness. His wisdom. His mercy. Or His sustaining grace. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — OUR HOPE IN THE WAITING Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because I don't want us to finish today's lesson thinking that waiting faithfully is simply about being patient enough to receive whatever we want.
Christian hope is much greater than that.
Our hope rests in Jesus Christ.
He lived a perfect life. He died on the cross for our sins. And He rose again.
Through Him, we have the promise of forgiveness and eternal life.
And Scripture teaches us to look forward to the fullness of God's redemption.
Now, that hope doesn't remove every difficulty from our present lives.
But it gives us a foundation that goes beyond our circumstances.
And that's why we can continue trusting the Lord.
Even while we wait.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. Your life doesn't have to stand still simply because an answer hasn't arrived. You can keep growing, serving, and walking with God in the waiting.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on what hasn't happened yet that we overlook what God has already placed before us.
Today still matters.
Your relationships still matter. Your responsibilities still matter. And your opportunities to honor Christ still matter.
LIVING IT OUT — FAITHFUL IN THE IN-BETWEEN Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to identify one situation where you're waiting for an answer.
Write it down.
Then ask yourself three questions. First... Is there something I need to do?
Maybe there's a phone call to make. A document to submit. A conversation to have. Or information to gather.
Second... Is there something I need to stop doing?
Maybe you've been checking for updates constantly. Maybe you've been comparing your circumstances with someone else's. Or maybe you've been imagining outcomes without enough information.
And third... What can I continue doing faithfully while I wait?
Maybe it's caring for your family. Serving others. Growing spiritually. Or simply attending to today's responsibilities.
Now, remember. Waiting doesn't have to mean putting your entire life on hold.
You can continue living faithfully. One day at a time.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the situation I've been waiting for is...
Our second prompt is... One way this waiting season has challenged my faith is...
And our third prompt is... While I wait, help me remain faithful by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will place my hope in the Lord, seek His wisdom, and remain faithful while I wait.
Now, say that again. I will place my hope in the Lord, seek His wisdom, and remain faithful while I wait.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Psalm 27, verse 14. "Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD."
Now, throughout the day, return to that verse.
And whenever you begin feeling impatient or discouraged, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom. Ask Him for patience. And ask Him to help you remain faithful in the responsibilities before you.
AROUND THE FIRE — A PERSONAL REFLECTION Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
And I ask you this question. Can you remember a season when you had to wait longer than you expected?
Maybe it was for an opportunity. A decision. A relationship. Or a change in circumstances.
Now, think about that season.
What was the hardest part?
Was it not knowing the outcome? Was it feeling as though everyone else was moving forward? Or was it simply being unable to control the timing? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would you say to someone who's struggling through a waiting season today?
Maybe you'd remind them that it's okay to feel discouraged.
Maybe you'd encourage them to continue praying.
Maybe you'd offer practical help. Or maybe you'd simply sit beside them and listen.
Because sometimes people don't need us to explain why they're waiting.
Sometimes they need compassion.
And sometimes they need to be reminded that their lives still have meaning and purpose, even while a particular situation remains unresolved.
CLOSING REFLECTION — GOD IS FAITHFUL IN THE WAITING Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Maybe you're in a waiting season right now.
Maybe you've prayed. You've prepared. You've taken responsible steps. And now you're waiting for an answer.
Now, I can't promise that the answer will come tomorrow.
I can't promise that the outcome will be exactly what you hoped for. And I can't explain why every delay happens.
But I can encourage you to remember what Scripture teaches about the Lord.
He is faithful. He is wise. And He is worthy of our trust.
Now, waiting may be difficult.
But you can continue seeking Him.
You can continue learning from His Word.
You can continue caring for the people around you.
And you can continue living faithfully.
Even in the in-between.
Now, remember David's words. "Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart."
Not because every answer will arrive according to our preferred timeline.
But because our hope belongs in the Lord.
And that's a foundation worth standing on.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for reminding us that we can place our hope in You. Lord, You know every person listening. You know the things they're waiting for. The prayers they've been carrying. The decisions that haven't been made. And the circumstances that remain unresolved. Father, give us patience. Give us wisdom. And help us recognize what we can responsibly do while we wait. Lord, I pray for the person who's waiting for medical answers. Give them strength and surround them with compassionate care. I pray for the person who's waiting for a financial situation to improve. Give them wisdom and practical support. I pray for the person who's waiting for reconciliation. Help them seek peace while maintaining healthy boundaries. And I pray for the person who's beginning to lose hope. Remind them of Your faithfulness. Father, help us avoid comparing our lives with others. Help us remain grateful for the blessings we have. And help us continue growing spiritually through every season. Thank You for Jesus Christ. Thank You for His sacrifice. His resurrection. And the promise of eternal life through Him. May our hope remain firmly rooted in our Savior. And may we continue walking faithfully with You. Even while we wait. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially begun Week Eight! And I hope today's lesson has reminded you that waiting doesn't mean your life has to stand still.
You can keep growing. Keep serving. Keep praying. And keep walking faithfully with Jesus Christ.
Tomorrow, we're going to continue our study of trusting God's timing. And we're going to talk about something that can be especially difficult. When Waiting Tests Your Patience — Learning to Trust God's Timing.
We'll explore how impatience can affect our decisions and what Scripture teaches about developing patience during seasons of uncertainty.
Until then, remember... Your hope doesn't have to depend on a particular date or outcome. Your hope can remain firmly rooted in Jesus Christ.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: When Waiting Tests Your Patience: Learning to Trust God's Timing
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WHEN PATIENCE RUNS THIN Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're here with me today. Whether you're listening while getting ready for your day, driving down the road, working around the house, or sitting quietly with your Bible, I'm glad you've chosen to spend this time in God's Word.
Today is Week Eight, Day Two. And we're continuing our study called Trusting God's Timing in the Waiting.
Yesterday, we talked about finding faith in the in-between. That place where we've prayed, we've prepared, and we've taken the steps we know to take. But the answer still hasn't arrived.
We talked about Abraham and Sarah. We talked about waiting on the Lord. And we learned that waiting doesn't mean our lives have to stand still.
But today, I want to talk about something that happens when the waiting lasts longer than we expected. Our patience starts wearing thin.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever been waiting for something and thought... Lord, I have been patient long enough!
Maybe you didn't actually say those words out loud. But you were certainly thinking them.
Maybe you've been waiting on an important decision. Waiting for someone to return a phone call. Waiting for a situation to improve. Or waiting for an answer to a prayer you've carried for a long time.
And at first, you handled it pretty well.
You prayed. You stayed hopeful. You reminded yourself that God is faithful.
But then another day passed. And another. And another.
And eventually you started wondering whether anything was ever going to change.
Now, I think many of us can relate to that. Because waiting can test our patience in ways we don't always expect.
Sometimes we become frustrated. Sometimes we become discouraged. And sometimes we begin making decisions simply because we're tired of not knowing.
Now, here's something I want you to understand. Patience isn't the absence of frustration. It's learning to respond faithfully even when frustration is present.
And patience doesn't mean we never take action. Sometimes waiting requires preparation. Sometimes it requires difficult decisions. And sometimes it requires asking for help.
But patience helps us avoid allowing frustration to control our choices.
And that's what we're going to study today. Our lesson is called... When Waiting Tests Your Patience — Learning to Trust God's Timing.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Lord, You know the situations we're waiting through. You know the prayers we've prayed. The questions we've asked. And the moments when our patience has worn thin. Father, help us approach today's Scripture with open hearts. Teach us what patience truly means. Help us recognize the difference between faithful waiting and unnecessary delay. Give us wisdom when decisions need to be made. And help us remain rooted in Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — JAMES 5:7–11 Now, let's turn to James chapter 5.
We're going to read verses 7 through 11. But first, let's talk about the context.
James was writing to believers who were experiencing hardship. And earlier in chapter 5, he addresses the injustice of wealthy oppressors who had withheld wages from laborers.
Now, that's important. Because the encouragement to be patient wasn't given to people whose lives were completely comfortable.
It was given in the context of real suffering and injustice.
And James points believers toward the coming of the Lord.
Now, let's read James chapter 5, verses 7 through 11, from the King James Version. "Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain. Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh. Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned: behold, the judge standeth before the door. Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience. Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy."
Now, let's think about what we've just read. James uses the example of a farmer.
And I think that's a picture we can understand. Because a farmer can prepare the soil. Plant the seed. And care for the field.
But the farmer cannot force the crop to mature overnight.
Growth takes time.
And some parts of that process are beyond the farmer's control.
Now, James uses that illustration to encourage believers to remain steadfast as they await the Lord's coming.
And that gives us an important lesson about patience.
We can be responsible for our actions. But we cannot control every outcome.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Patience means remaining faithful to God while recognizing that not everything happens according to our preferred timeline.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we think patience means sitting still and doing nothing.
But patience can involve action.
It can involve preparation. Prayer. Wise decisions. And continued obedience.
What patience doesn't require is pretending we control everything.
THE FARMER AND THE HARVEST Now, let's return to James' illustration.
Think about a farmer preparing for planting season.
The farmer doesn't simply walk outside, throw a handful of seeds into the yard, and expect a beautiful harvest the next morning.
There's preparation. There's work. There's care. And there's waiting.
Now, some days the farmer may see visible progress.
Other days, there may not be much change at all.
But the farmer understands that growth takes time.
Now, I want us to think about how that relates to our lives.
Sometimes we're working toward something important.
Maybe we're learning a new skill. Trying to rebuild a relationship. Working toward financial stability. Or growing in our understanding of Scripture.
And we want to see immediate results.
But meaningful progress often takes time.
Now, here's something important. James' promise concerns the Lord's coming and the believer's endurance.
It isn't a guarantee that every personal effort will produce the exact result we want.
But the farmer's example reminds us that patience and responsibility can belong together.
We can do what is ours to do. And acknowledge what remains outside our control.
WHEN IMPATIENCE AFFECTS OUR DECISIONS Now, let's talk about something that can happen when we're tired of waiting.
We start rushing.
Maybe we make a decision before we have enough information.
Maybe we accept an opportunity that isn't right for us simply because we're tired of waiting for another one.
Maybe we send a message out of frustration.
Or maybe we pressure someone because we want an answer immediately.
Now, sometimes quick action is necessary.
And there are situations where waiting too long can create real problems.
But here's something I want you to consider. Am I making this decision because it's wise?
Or because I'm frustrated?
Now, that's an important question.
Because frustration can make us feel as though we need to do something right now.
Even when the best choice would be to gather more information. Seek counsel. Or allow ourselves time to think.
Now, here's something practical. When you're feeling impatient, pause long enough to ask... What do I actually know? What action is necessary? And what am I trying to control?
Those questions can help us respond with wisdom rather than reacting out of frustration.
PSALM 37 — REST IN THE LORD Now, let's turn to Psalm 37, verse 7. The King James Version says: "Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass."
Now, let's understand the context. Psalm 37 addresses the temptation to become troubled when wicked people appear to prosper.
David encourages God's people not to allow envy or anger to lead them away from faithful living.
Now, notice the words... "Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him."
That's a powerful invitation.
Because sometimes we become so focused on what other people are doing that we lose sight of what God has called us to do.
We compare our progress. We compare our opportunities. And we compare our circumstances.
And before we know it, our patience begins disappearing.
Now, here's something important. Someone else's success doesn't determine your worth.
And someone else's timeline doesn't tell you everything about your own future.
We can celebrate others without treating their circumstances as a judgment on ours.
And we can continue seeking the Lord while making responsible decisions about our own lives.
ECCLESIASTES — A TIME FOR EVERYTHING Now, let's turn to Ecclesiastes chapter 3, verse 1. It says: "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:"
Now, this is a familiar verse.
And many people find comfort in it.
But let's remember that Ecclesiastes reflects deeply on the changing seasons of human life.
It speaks about birth and death. Weeping and laughing. Mourning and dancing.
And it reminds us that human beings don't control every season they experience.
Now, here's something important. This verse doesn't mean we can predict exactly when something will happen.
And it doesn't guarantee that every personal desire will eventually become reality.
But it does remind us that life unfolds through changing circumstances.
And we need wisdom to respond faithfully to those changes.
Now, think about your own life.
Have you ever looked back and realized that a particular season was very different from what you expected?
Maybe it involved change. Maybe it involved loss. Maybe it involved new responsibilities. Or maybe it brought opportunities you hadn't anticipated.
Now, sometimes we can recognize lessons from those experiences.
Other times, we still have questions.
But through every season, we can continue seeking the Lord.
PATIENCE DOESN'T MEAN IGNORING INJUSTICE Now, I want to return to something important in James chapter 5.
Remember that James was speaking in a context where people had experienced injustice.
And I want us to be careful about how we apply the instruction to be patient.
Because sometimes people tell someone who's being mistreated... "Just be patient."
Or... "Just wait on God."
But patience doesn't mean accepting abuse.
It doesn't mean ignoring injustice.
And it doesn't mean refusing to seek protection or appropriate help.
We can trust God's ultimate justice while also taking responsible steps to address wrongdoing.
Now, that's important. Because biblical patience isn't the same as passivity.
And faithful endurance doesn't require someone to remain in danger.
Sometimes the wise next step is to seek safety. Report wrongdoing. Ask for help. Or establish necessary boundaries.
Now, those actions aren't a failure of patience.
They're part of responding responsibly to difficult circumstances.
THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT Now, let's turn to Galatians chapter 5.
We're going to read verses 22 and 23. The King James Version says: "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law."
Now, notice the word... "Longsuffering."
That's a word closely connected to patience.
It describes the ability to endure difficulty or provocation without quickly giving way to anger.
And Paul includes it among the fruit of the Spirit.
Now, that's important. Because patience isn't simply a personality trait that some people naturally have and others don't.
For believers, patience is part of the character the Holy Spirit produces as we grow in Christ.
Now, that doesn't mean we'll always respond perfectly.
Sometimes we'll become frustrated. Sometimes we'll speak too quickly. And sometimes we'll need to apologize.
But spiritual growth involves learning to respond differently.
We can practice self-control. We can seek wisdom. And we can ask God to help us grow in patience.
PAUSE AND PRAY Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about one situation that's been testing your patience.
Maybe it's a delay. A difficult relationship. An unanswered question. Or something you've been hoping would change.
Now, ask yourself... How have I been responding?
Have I been frustrated? Have I been rushing? Or have I been trying to control something that isn't mine to control? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the situations that have been testing our patience. You know the delays. The unanswered questions. And the moments when frustration has influenced our decisions. Lord, help us grow in patience. Give us wisdom to recognize when action is necessary. Help us avoid rushing simply because we're uncomfortable with uncertainty. And teach us to respond with kindness, humility, and self-control. Father, continue shaping our character through Your Word and Spirit. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
HABAKKUK — WAITING FOR WHAT GOD HAS SAID Now, let's turn to Habakkuk chapter 2, verse 3. The King James Version says: "For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry."
Now, let's understand the context.
Habakkuk was a prophet who wrestled with difficult questions about injustice and God's response to evil.
And in this passage, God gives him a specific revelation concerning what would happen.
Now, here's something important. This verse isn't a general promise that every dream or personal goal will come true if we wait long enough.
It concerns a particular message God gave to Habakkuk.
But it teaches us something about the reliability of God's revealed Word.
God is faithful to what He has truly promised.
Now, we need to distinguish between God's promises and our preferences.
We may hope for a particular outcome. We may pray for something. And we may work toward a goal.
But that doesn't automatically make the outcome a promise from God.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our confidence should rest in what God has revealed, not in our ability to predict the future.
WHEN WE FEEL FORGOTTEN Now, I want to speak to someone who's been waiting for a long time.
Maybe you've been praying for something for months. Or maybe even years.
And you've begun wondering whether God has forgotten you.
Now, I want you to understand something. Your circumstances don't automatically tell you how God feels about you.
A delay doesn't prove that God has abandoned you.
And a difficult season doesn't mean your life has lost its value.
Now, we may not know why a particular outcome hasn't happened.
And we shouldn't pretend to know.
But we can continue seeking the Lord.
We can bring our questions before Him.
And we can remember His love revealed through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes we become so focused on receiving one particular answer that we begin overlooking the rest of our lives.
We forget to enjoy time with people we love. We overlook opportunities to serve. And we become consumed by the thing that hasn't happened yet.
Now, I want you to remember something. Your life still matters while you're waiting.
Your relationships still matter. Your responsibilities still matter. And your opportunities to honor God still matter.
ROMANS 12 — PATIENT IN TRIBULATION Now, let's turn to Romans chapter 12, verse 12. The King James Version says: "Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;"
Now, I love how these three ideas appear together.
Hope. Patience. And prayer.
Now, think about that. Hope reminds us where our confidence belongs.
Patience helps us endure difficulty.
And prayer keeps us turning toward the Lord.
Now, here's something important. Paul doesn't tell believers to pretend that tribulation is easy.
He encourages them to remain patient in the midst of it.
And to continue in prayer.
Now, that means we can bring our frustrations before God.
We can ask for wisdom. We can ask for strength. And we can continue seeking Him.
Even when circumstances haven't changed.
HEBREWS 6 — FAITH AND PATIENCE Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 6, verse 12. It says: "That ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises."
Now, notice the connection. Faith and patience.
These two qualities belong together.
Faith trusts God's character and promises.
Patience continues relying on Him while we await their fulfillment.
Now, this passage isn't teaching that every personal wish will eventually happen.
It's encouraging believers to persevere in their confidence in God's promises.
And that's an important distinction.
Because biblical patience isn't simply waiting for life to turn out exactly as we planned.
It's remaining faithful to the Lord.
PRACTICAL WAYS TO PRACTICE PATIENCE Now, let's talk about some practical ways we can grow in patience.
The first is to recognize what we're feeling.
Sometimes we become frustrated without stopping to understand why.
Maybe we're tired. Maybe we're disappointed. Or maybe we're afraid of what might happen.
Now, identifying those feelings can help us respond more thoughtfully.
The second is to separate what we can control from what we cannot.
We can control many of our own actions.
We can prepare. We can communicate. And we can make responsible decisions.
But we cannot control every outcome.
The third is to avoid making important decisions purely out of frustration.
Sometimes we need to pause. Pray. And gather more information.
The fourth is to remain engaged in the responsibilities already before us.
Waiting for one answer doesn't mean everything else in our lives has to stop.
And the fifth is to continue bringing our concerns before the Lord.
Now, these practices won't make every waiting season easy.
But they can help us respond with wisdom and faithfulness.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What situation has been testing my patience the most?
Maybe it's a delay. A relationship. A decision. Or an unanswered prayer. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... How has impatience been affecting my thoughts or decisions?
Have you been rushing? Becoming easily frustrated? Or trying to control something that isn't yours to control? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What would a patient and responsible response look like?
Maybe you need to wait. Maybe you need to act. Maybe you need to seek advice. Or maybe you need to establish a boundary. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I continue growing spiritually while I wait?
Maybe it's through prayer. Studying Scripture. Practicing self-control. Or showing kindness to others. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — OUR PATIENT SAVIOR Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because our hope isn't rooted in our ability to remain perfectly patient.
It's rooted in Jesus Christ.
He lived a sinless life. He died on the cross for our sins. And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, that's the foundation of Christian hope.
And as we follow Him, the Holy Spirit continues shaping our character.
Including our patience.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn God's love by being patient enough.
We grow in patience as part of our response to His grace.
And when we fail, we can confess our sins, receive forgiveness through Christ, and continue growing.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You don't have to control the timing of every outcome to remain faithful in the waiting.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become exhausted trying to manage things that are beyond our control.
But we can seek wisdom. Take responsible action. And entrust the outcome to God.
LIVING IT OUT — PRACTICING PATIENCE Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to identify one situation that's been testing your patience.
Write it down.
Then ask yourself three questions. First... What am I feeling about this situation?
Second... What can I responsibly do?
And third... What do I need to entrust to God?
Now, take a moment to pray over those answers.
And throughout the day, whenever frustration begins rising, return to those questions.
Remember that patience isn't simply waiting longer.
It's learning to respond faithfully.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the situation that's been testing my patience is...
Our second prompt is... One way impatience has affected my response is...
And our third prompt is... Help me practice patience today by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek God's wisdom, practice patience, and remain faithful even when circumstances don't move according to my timeline.
Now, say that again. I will seek God's wisdom, practice patience, and remain faithful even when circumstances don't move according to my timeline.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Romans chapter 12, verse 12. "Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;"
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
Hope. Patience. Prayer.
And whenever you begin feeling impatient, take a moment to pause before reacting.
Ask God for wisdom. And choose one response that reflects patience and self-control.
AROUND THE FIRE — REFLECTING ON PATIENCE Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
And I ask you this question. Can you remember a time when impatience led you to make a decision you later regretted?
Maybe you rushed into something. Maybe you spoke too quickly. Or maybe you tried to force an outcome.
Now, think about what you learned. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] And here's another question. Can you remember a time when patience helped you make a wiser decision?
Maybe you waited until you had more information. Maybe you sought advice. Or maybe you simply allowed yourself time to think. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something I want you to remember. Patience isn't about never feeling frustrated.
It's about learning how to respond when frustration comes.
CLOSING REFLECTION — TRUSTING GOD'S TIMING Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Sometimes waiting is difficult because we don't know when anything will change.
We don't know when the answer will come. We don't know how a situation will turn out. And we don't always know what we should do next.
Now, in those moments, we can return to God's Word.
We can remember the farmer in James chapter 5.
We can remember the call to patience.
And we can remember that our ultimate hope rests in Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to understand. Patience doesn't mean we never act.
It doesn't mean we ignore problems. And it doesn't mean we pretend that waiting is easy.
It means learning to respond faithfully.
Seeking wisdom. Practicing self-control. And continuing to trust the Lord.
Even when the timing isn't what we hoped for.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for reminding us that patience is part of spiritual growth. Lord, You know every person listening. You know the situations that have been testing their patience. The delays they've experienced. The unanswered questions they're carrying. And the moments when frustration has become overwhelming. Father, help us respond with wisdom. Give us patience when we need to wait. Courage when we need to act. And humility when we need to ask for help. Lord, I pray for the person who's been waiting for an important answer. Give them wisdom about the next responsible step. I pray for the person who's discouraged by slow progress. Help them remain faithful. I pray for the person who's struggling with frustration. Teach them to respond with kindness and self-control. And I pray for the person who's beginning to lose hope. Remind them of Your faithfulness revealed through Jesus Christ. Father, continue shaping our character through Your Holy Spirit. Help us grow in patience. In love. And in faithfulness. Thank You for Jesus. Thank You for His sacrifice. His resurrection. And the promise of eternal life through Him. May our hope remain firmly rooted in our Savior. And may we continue following Him faithfully. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Eight, Day Two. And I hope today's lesson has encouraged you to remember that patience isn't simply about waiting longer.
It's about learning to respond faithfully while you wait.
Tomorrow, we're going to continue our study of trusting God's timing. And we're going to talk about something that can happen when waiting becomes discouraging. Our lesson will be called... When You Feel Forgotten — Remembering God's Faithfulness in the Waiting.
We'll explore what Scripture teaches about God's care and faithfulness when we feel overlooked or forgotten.
Until then, remember... You don't have to control every outcome to remain faithful.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: When You Feel Forgotten: Remembering God's Faithfulness in the Waiting
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — HAVE YOU EVER FELT FORGOTTEN? Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today. Whether you're listening while getting ready for work, driving down the road, sitting at home with your Bible, or taking a quiet moment to spend with the Lord, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Eight, Day Three. And we're continuing our study called Trusting God's Timing in the Waiting.
On Day One, we talked about finding faith in the in-between. That place where we've prayed, prepared, and done everything we know to do, but the answer hasn't arrived.
Yesterday, we talked about patience. We learned that patience isn't simply about waiting longer. It's about learning to respond faithfully while we wait.
But today, I want to talk about something that can happen when the waiting becomes especially difficult.
Sometimes we begin feeling forgotten.
