Or practicing gratitude. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I remain faithful today without making my worth depend on a particular outcome?
Think about the responsibilities already before you.
And the opportunities you have to honor Christ. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE SOURCE OF OUR GROWTH Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because spiritual growth isn't simply about becoming a better version of ourselves.
It's about becoming more like Christ.
Jesus lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, that's the foundation of Christian hope.
And as we follow Him, the Holy Spirit continues shaping our character.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn God's love by growing quickly enough.
We don't earn salvation by becoming perfectly patient.
And we don't have to pretend that we've already reached spiritual maturity.
Our salvation rests in God's grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our growth is part of our response to that grace.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. Your circumstances may not be changing as quickly as you hoped, but you can still be growing in faith, wisdom, patience, and love.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on one unanswered prayer that we overlook the rest of our lives.
But there are still opportunities to learn.
To serve.
And to grow closer to Jesus Christ.
LIVING IT OUT — ONE SMALL STEP TOWARD GROWTH Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to identify one area of spiritual growth you'd like to focus on.
Maybe it's patience.
Maybe it's understanding Scripture.
Maybe it's prayer.
Or maybe it's learning to respond with greater kindness.
Now, choose one small action you can practice this week.
For example, if you want to grow in Scripture, set aside ten minutes each day to read and reflect.
If you want to grow in prayer, begin keeping a simple prayer journal.
If you want to grow in patience, practice pausing before responding when you're frustrated.
And if you want to grow in kindness, look for one practical way to encourage someone each day.
Now, remember. Spiritual growth doesn't have to happen all at once.
We can continue taking faithful steps.
One day at a time.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the area where I want to grow spiritually is...
Our second prompt is... One habit or response I need to change is...
And our third prompt is... Help me continue growing while I wait by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will remain connected to Jesus Christ and continue growing in faith, wisdom, and love, even while I wait.
Now, say that again. I will remain connected to Jesus Christ and continue growing in faith, wisdom, and love, even while I wait.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize James chapter 1, verse 3. "Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience."
Now, throughout the day, return to that verse.
And ask yourself... How can I respond faithfully to the challenges before me?
Choose one small action that reflects spiritual growth.
AROUND THE FIRE — RECOGNIZING GROWTH Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
And I ask you this question. Can you remember a time when you were waiting for something important?
Maybe it was an answer.
An opportunity.
Or a change in circumstances.
Now, think about who you were at the beginning of that season.
And think about what you've learned since then.
Maybe you've become more patient.
Maybe you've learned to ask for help.
Maybe you've developed greater wisdom.
Or maybe you've grown in your understanding of God's Word. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would you say to someone who feels as though their life isn't moving forward?
Maybe you'd remind them that progress isn't always immediately visible.
Maybe you'd encourage them to keep learning.
Or maybe you'd remind them that their worth isn't determined by one particular outcome.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Growth doesn't always look like reaching the next milestone. Sometimes it looks like becoming more faithful in the life you're living today.
CLOSING REFLECTION — YOU CAN KEEP GROWING Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Maybe you're in a waiting season right now.
Maybe you've prayed.
You've prepared.
You've taken responsible steps.
And you're still waiting for an answer.
Now, I can't promise that the answer will arrive tomorrow.
I can't promise that every outcome will be exactly what you hoped for.
And I can't explain why every delay happens.
But I can encourage you to remember that your relationship with Christ can continue growing.
You can continue opening your Bible.
You can continue praying.
You can continue serving others.
And you can continue learning how to respond faithfully to the circumstances before you.
Now, remember Jesus' words in John chapter 15.
"Abide in me..."
Our spiritual growth begins with our relationship with Him.
Not with achieving every goal.
Not with controlling every outcome.
And not with reaching every milestone according to our preferred timeline.
But with remaining connected to Christ.
So if you're waiting today...
Don't assume your life has stopped.
Look for opportunities to grow.
Seek God's wisdom.
And continue living faithfully.
One day at a time.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for reminding us that spiritual growth can continue through every season. Lord, You know every person listening. You know the situations they're waiting through. The prayers they're carrying. And the areas where they're feeling discouraged. Father, help us remain connected to Jesus Christ. Teach us through Your Word. Shape our character through Your Holy Spirit. And help us grow in patience, wisdom, kindness, and love. Lord, I pray for the person who feels as though their life is standing still. Help them recognize meaningful opportunities for growth. I pray for the person who's discouraged by slow progress. Give them patience and encouragement. I pray for the person who's trying to change an unhealthy habit. Give them wisdom, support, and perseverance. And I pray for the person who's simply tired. Help them find appropriate rest and care. Father, remind us that our worth isn't determined by how quickly we reach a particular milestone. Our hope rests in Jesus Christ. Thank You for His sacrifice. His resurrection. And the promise of eternal life through Him. May we continue following Him faithfully. And may our lives reflect Your love and truth. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Eight, Day Five. And I hope today's lesson has encouraged you to remember that spiritual growth doesn't have to stop simply because your circumstances haven't changed.
You can keep learning. Keep praying. Keep serving. And keep growing in your relationship with Jesus Christ.
Tomorrow, we're going to gather Around the Fire for our Week Eight reflection. Our lesson will be called... Around the Fire — Finding Hope and Patience in the Waiting.
We'll revisit everything we've studied this week and spend time reflecting on how we can apply these lessons to our everyday lives.
Until then, remember... Your spiritual growth isn't measured only by the milestones you reach. It's reflected in the way you continue following Christ.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Around the Fire: Finding Hope and Patience in the Waiting
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — COME SIT AROUND THE FIRE Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're here with me today.
Today is Week Eight, Day Six. And that means it's time for one of my favorite parts of our Bible study. Around the Fire.
Now, if you've been walking through these studies with me, you know that Around the Fire is a little different. We still open our Bibles. We still study Scripture. And we still spend time in prayer. But today, I want us to slow down.
I want us to think about everything we've learned this week. And I want us to talk about how those lessons connect with our everyday lives.
Because sometimes we can read a passage of Scripture, understand what it says, and still struggle to apply it when life gets difficult.
And that's why these reflection days matter.
So wherever you are today, I want you to imagine something with me.
Imagine we're sitting together around a warm fire. Maybe there's a cup of coffee in your hand. Maybe you've brought your Bible and your journal. And maybe, for the first time all day, you have a few quiet minutes.
There's no need to impress anybody. No need to pretend everything is perfect. And no need to hide the questions you've been carrying.
We're simply here to spend time in God's Word.
And today's conversation is about waiting.
Not the easy kind of waiting. Not waiting five minutes for your coffee. Or waiting in line at the grocery store.
I'm talking about the kind of waiting that reaches into your heart.
Waiting for an answer. Waiting for a decision. Waiting for circumstances to change. Waiting for healing. Waiting for peace. Or waiting for something you've prayed about so many times that you hardly know what else to say.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever gotten tired of hearing the words... "Just be patient"?
Maybe somebody meant well. Maybe they were trying to encourage you. But they didn't understand how long you'd already been waiting.
They didn't know how many nights you'd spent praying. How many times you'd checked for an answer. Or how many disappointments you'd carried along the way.
And sometimes, when we're hurting, the last thing we need is a simple explanation from someone who doesn't understand the situation.
Sometimes we just need someone to listen.
And that's the spirit I want us to bring into today's study. We're going to listen to what Scripture teaches. We're going to reflect honestly. And we're going to remember that our hope is rooted in Jesus Christ.
Today's lesson is called... Around the Fire — Finding Hope and Patience in the Waiting.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together today. Thank You for another opportunity to open Your Word. Lord, You know the things we've been waiting for. You know the prayers we've prayed. The disappointments we've experienced. And the questions that remain unanswered. Father, help us approach today's study with honest hearts. Teach us to recognize Your faithfulness. Give us wisdom when action is necessary. Patience when we need to wait. And strength when we're feeling weary. Lord, help us encourage one another. Help us listen with compassion. And help us remember that our ultimate hope rests in Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
RETURNING TO OUR FOUNDATION — PSALM 27 Now, let's begin where we started this week. Psalm chapter 27.
On Day One, we studied David's words about waiting on the Lord.
And today, I want us to read those words again. Psalm 27, verses 13 and 14, from the King James Version. "I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living. Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD."
Now, I want you to notice something. David doesn't simply say... Wait.
He says... "Wait on the LORD."
And then he says... "Be of good courage."
Now, why would waiting require courage?
Because waiting can involve uncertainty.
Sometimes we don't know what will happen. Sometimes we don't know when something will change. And sometimes we don't even know what the next step should be.
Now, David's words remind us to place our confidence in the Lord.
Not in our ability to predict the future. Not in our preferred timeline. And not in our ability to control every outcome.
But in God's character.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful waiting doesn't require knowing how everything will turn out. It requires continuing to seek the Lord while living according to His Word.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
And I ask you a simple question. What are you waiting for?
Now, I don't mean what are you hoping happens someday.
I mean what is something you're carrying right now?
Maybe you're waiting for a phone call. Maybe you're waiting for medical results. Maybe you're waiting for a decision about your future. Maybe you're waiting for a relationship to improve. Or maybe you're waiting for a situation that's been weighing heavily on your heart to finally change.
Now, I want you to think about that situation.
And I want you to be honest about how it's affecting you.
Are you feeling hopeful?
Are you frustrated?
Are you afraid?
Or are you simply tired? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something important. You don't have to pretend you're handling everything perfectly.
You can acknowledge your emotions. You can bring them before God. And you can seek support when you need it.
Because faith isn't about pretending that difficult things don't hurt.
It's about continuing to turn toward the Lord even when they do.
LESSON ONE — FINDING FAITH IN THE IN-BETWEEN Now, let's revisit our first lesson from this week. Finding Faith in the In-Between.
We talked about those seasons when we've prayed, prepared, and taken responsible steps. But we're still waiting for an answer.
And we learned something important. Waiting doesn't mean our lives have to stop.
Now, think about that. Sometimes we become so focused on one particular outcome that we begin putting everything else on hold.
We tell ourselves... Once this situation changes, then I'll be happy.
Once I receive that answer, then I'll be able to relax.
Once that opportunity arrives, then I'll begin moving forward.
But here's something I want you to remember. Your life still matters while you're waiting.
Your relationships still matter. Your responsibilities still matter. And your opportunities to honor Christ still matter.
Now, that doesn't mean every waiting season is easy.
And it doesn't mean we should ignore serious circumstances.
But it does mean we can continue seeking the Lord.
We can continue growing spiritually.
And we can continue living faithfully.
Now, here's a question for you. Have you been putting an important part of your life on hold because you're waiting for something else?
Maybe it's time to reconsider that.
Maybe there's something meaningful you can begin doing today.
Not because you've stopped caring about the outcome you're waiting for.
But because today still matters.
LESSON TWO — WHEN WAITING TESTS YOUR PATIENCE Now, let's talk about our second lesson. Patience.
We studied James chapter 5.
And we talked about the farmer who waits for the harvest.
Now, think about that illustration. A farmer can prepare the soil. Plant the seed. And care for the field.
But the farmer cannot force the crop to mature overnight.
Some things take time.
Now, James uses that illustration to encourage believers to remain steadfast as they await the Lord's coming.
And we learned that patience doesn't mean doing nothing.
Sometimes patience involves preparation.
Sometimes it involves taking responsible action.
And sometimes it involves recognizing that we cannot control every outcome.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. Have you ever made a decision simply because you were tired of waiting?
Maybe you rushed into something.
Maybe you spoke out of frustration.
Or maybe you tried to force an answer.
Now, I think many of us can relate to that.
Because uncertainty can be uncomfortable.
But patience helps us slow down long enough to make wise decisions.
Now, remember Romans chapter 12, verse 12. "Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;"
Hope. Patience. Prayer.
Those three ideas belong together.
And they can help us respond faithfully during difficult seasons.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHEN PATIENCE RUNS OUT Now, let's imagine we're still sitting together around the fire.
And somebody says... "I've been patient for so long. I don't know how much more waiting I can handle."
Now, what would you say?
Would you tell them to stop complaining?
Would you tell them they just need more faith?
Or would you take time to listen?
Now, I want us to remember something. People who are struggling don't always need a quick explanation.
Sometimes they need compassion.
Sometimes they need practical help.
And sometimes they need someone to remind them that it's okay to acknowledge exhaustion.
Now, here's something important. Patience doesn't mean ignoring serious problems.
It doesn't mean remaining in an unsafe situation.
And it doesn't mean refusing to seek help.
Sometimes the wise next step is to take action.
Sometimes it's to ask for support.
And sometimes it's to establish healthy boundaries.
Now, those things can be part of faithful living.
Because patience and wisdom belong together.
LESSON THREE — WHEN YOU FEEL FORGOTTEN Now, let's revisit Day Three.
When You Feel Forgotten.
We studied Isaiah chapter 49.
And we read the words of Zion. "The LORD hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me."
Now, those words express a deep feeling of abandonment.
But God responds by reassuring His people of His faithfulness.
Let's read Isaiah chapter 49, verses 15 and 16. "Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee. Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me."
Now, in the original context, God is reassuring Zion that He hasn't abandoned His covenant people.
And the passage reveals something beautiful about His character.
He is faithful.
Now, we also studied David's prayer in Psalm 13.
And David asked... "How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD?"
Now, I want you to remember something. David brought his questions directly before God.
He didn't pretend that he wasn't hurting.
And he didn't hide his sorrow.
He prayed honestly.
Now, here's something important. Honest prayer is not the enemy of faith.
Sometimes honest prayer is how we continue turning toward God when life becomes difficult.
Now, maybe you've been feeling forgotten.
Maybe you've watched other people move forward while your circumstances remain unchanged.
Or maybe you're carrying something that nobody else seems to understand.
Now, I want you to remember that your worth isn't determined by public recognition.
Your value isn't measured by how quickly you reach a particular milestone.
And your hope doesn't have to depend on someone else's attention.
For those who belong to Christ, our identity is rooted in Him.
AROUND THE FIRE — THE POWER OF BEING SEEN Now, I want you to think about someone in your life.
Someone who may be feeling overlooked.
Maybe it's a friend.
A family member.
A coworker.
Or someone in your church.
Now, here's a question. When was the last time you checked on that person?
Not because you needed something.
Not because you wanted a favor.
But simply because you cared.
Now, sometimes a simple message can mean more than we realize.
A phone call. A handwritten note. An offer to help. Or simply taking time to listen.
Now, those things may seem small.
But they can be meaningful expressions of Christ's love.
And sometimes, while we're waiting for encouragement ourselves, we can still offer encouragement to someone else.
LESSON FOUR — SURRENDERING THE NEED FOR CONTROL Now, let's revisit yesterday's lesson.
When You Want to Take Control.
We studied Proverbs chapter 16, verse 9. "A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps."
Now, that's a powerful reminder.
We make plans.
We set goals.
And we think about the future.
But we don't control every circumstance that affects the outcome.
Now, here's something important. Making plans isn't wrong.
Taking responsibility isn't wrong.
And sometimes action is necessary.
But there's a difference between responsible action and trying to control everything.
Sometimes our desire for control comes from fear.
We're afraid of disappointment.
We're afraid of failure.
Or we're afraid that things won't happen according to our timeline.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Surrender doesn't mean abandoning responsibility. It means acting faithfully while recognizing that some outcomes remain outside our control.
Now, I want you to think about one situation you've been trying to control.
Maybe it's a relationship.
Maybe it's a decision.
Maybe it's a financial concern.
Or maybe it's an opportunity.
Now, ask yourself... What can I responsibly do?
And what do I need to entrust to God?
Those are important questions.
Because sometimes the desire to control everything can become exhausting.
And recognizing our limitations can help us approach life with greater humility.
PAUSE AND PRAY — LORD, HELP ME TRUST YOU Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about the situation you've been carrying this week.
Maybe it's something you've prayed about for a long time.
Maybe it's something that has tested your patience.
Or maybe it's something you've been trying to control.
Now, bring that before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the situations we're carrying. You know the answers we're waiting for. And You know the uncertainty we're experiencing. Lord, help us recognize what is ours to do. Give us wisdom when action is necessary. Patience when we need to wait. And humility when our plans need to change. Father, help us remember Your faithfulness. And help us continue seeking You through every season. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
LESSON FIVE — GROWING WHILE YOU WAIT Now, let's revisit our fifth lesson.
Growing While You Wait.
We studied James chapter 1.
And we talked about how trials can become occasions for spiritual endurance and maturity.
Now, let's read James chapter 1, verses 2 through 4. "My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing."
Now, remember what we learned.
James isn't telling believers to pretend that suffering is enjoyable.
He's encouraging them to recognize that faith can be tested and strengthened through difficulty.
Now, here's something important. Not every hardship has been arranged to teach us one particular lesson.
And we shouldn't assume that every delay has a hidden purpose we can identify.
But we can continue growing spiritually while we wait.
We can study Scripture.
We can practice patience.
We can learn to communicate more clearly.
And we can continue serving others.
Now, I want you to remember something. Your spiritual growth doesn't have to stop simply because your circumstances haven't changed.
Maybe you're waiting for an opportunity.
But you can still learn.
Maybe you're waiting for an answer.
But you can still prepare.
Maybe you're waiting for a difficult situation to improve.
But you can still seek wisdom and support.
And spiritually, you can continue growing in your relationship with Jesus Christ.
LAMENTATIONS — REMEMBERING GOD'S FAITHFULNESS Now, let's turn to Lamentations chapter 3.
We're going to read verses 21 through 23. The King James Version says: "This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."
Now, I want you to notice something. The writer says... "This I recall to my mind..."
In other words, he's intentionally remembering something.
Now, let's remember the context. Lamentations is filled with grief.
It reflects the suffering associated with Jerusalem's destruction.
And yet, in the midst of sorrow, the writer remembers God's mercy.
Now, that's meaningful.
Because sometimes remembering God's faithfulness is something we need to do intentionally.
Not because our pain isn't real.
But because our pain isn't the only truth about our circumstances.
We can acknowledge what hurts.
And still remember God's character.
We can grieve.
And still pray.
We can feel uncertain.
And still seek the Lord.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Hope doesn't require pretending that life is easy. Hope means continuing to look toward God's faithfulness even when life is difficult.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHAT HAS THIS WEEK TAUGHT YOU? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire one more time.
And I ask you this question. What has this week taught you about waiting?
Maybe you've realized that patience is something you need to practice.
Maybe you've recognized that you've been trying to control too much.
Maybe you've been feeling forgotten.
Or maybe you've realized that you can continue growing spiritually even while you're waiting for an answer.
Now, I want you to think about that. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] And here's another question. What is one thing you'd like to do differently moving forward?
Maybe you want to pray more honestly.
Maybe you want to stop comparing your circumstances with someone else's.
Maybe you want to seek wise counsel before making an important decision.
Or maybe you want to begin focusing on the responsibilities already before you.
Now, those are meaningful steps.
And they don't require you to know exactly how everything will turn out.
They simply require you to take the next faithful step.
FIVE TRUTHS TO CARRY FORWARD Now, before we move into our reflection questions, I want us to remember five truths from this week.
First... Waiting doesn't mean your life has stopped.
You can continue living faithfully.
Second... Patience and responsibility belong together.
You can wait while still taking appropriate action.
Third... Feeling forgotten doesn't mean God has forgotten you.
Your emotions matter, but Scripture gives us a foundation beyond our feelings.
Fourth... Surrender doesn't mean abandoning responsibility.
You can make wise decisions while acknowledging that some outcomes remain outside your control.
And fifth... Spiritual growth can continue through seasons of waiting.
You can keep learning. Keep praying. And keep growing in your relationship with Christ.
Now, those are five truths worth remembering.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What has been the hardest part of waiting for me?
Is it uncertainty?
Impatience?
Feeling forgotten?
Or the desire to control the outcome? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Which lesson from this week spoke most directly to my situation?
Was it finding faith in the in-between?
Practicing patience?
Remembering God's faithfulness?
Surrendering control?
Or continuing to grow? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What can I responsibly do while I wait?
Maybe you need to prepare.
Gather information.
Seek support.
Or continue fulfilling your current responsibilities. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What truth about God do I want to remember during this waiting season?
Maybe it's His faithfulness.
His mercy.
His wisdom.
Or His love revealed through Jesus Christ. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — OUR HOPE IS IN JESUS Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because the purpose of our Bible study isn't simply to become better at waiting.
It's to grow in our relationship with Jesus Christ.
Our ultimate hope isn't that every personal plan will succeed.
Our hope is rooted in the Savior who died for our sins and rose again.
Through Jesus Christ, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, that's the foundation of Christian hope.
And that hope remains meaningful even when our present circumstances are difficult.
Now, I want you to remember something. We don't earn God's love by waiting perfectly.
We don't earn salvation by becoming patient enough.
And we don't have to pretend that we've already reached spiritual maturity.
Our salvation rests in God's grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our growth is part of our response to that grace.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You don't have to know when the answer will come to remain faithful today. Seek God's wisdom, take the steps that are yours to take, and keep your hope rooted in Jesus Christ.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on tomorrow that we overlook the opportunities God has placed before us today.
But today still matters.
And we can continue living faithfully.
Even while we wait.
LIVING IT OUT — YOUR WAITING SEASON PLAN Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... My Waiting Season Plan.
Now, beneath that heading, I want you to answer three questions.
First... What am I waiting for?
Write down the situation honestly.
Second... What can I responsibly do?
Maybe there's a phone call to make.
A conversation to have.
An appointment to prepare for.
Or a skill to develop.
And third... What do I need to entrust to God?
Maybe it's the timing.
Maybe it's another person's decision.
Or maybe it's an outcome you cannot guarantee.
Now, after you've written those answers down, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom.
And choose one faithful action you can take today.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the waiting season I'm currently experiencing is...
Our second prompt is... The lesson from this week that I most need to remember is...
And our third prompt is... Help me remain faithful while I wait by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek God's wisdom, practice patience, and continue living faithfully while I wait.
Now, say that again. I will seek God's wisdom, practice patience, and continue living faithfully while I wait.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Return to Psalm 27, verse 14. "Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD."
Now, I want you to carry that verse with you throughout the day.
And whenever you begin feeling impatient, discouraged, or overwhelmed, take a moment to pause.
Pray.
Remember God's faithfulness.
And ask yourself... What is the next faithful step I can take?
CLOSING REFLECTION — THERE IS FAITH IN THE WAITING Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Maybe you're still waiting.
Maybe the situation you brought into this week hasn't changed.
Maybe the answer hasn't arrived.
Maybe the decision hasn't been made.
Or maybe you're still carrying questions you don't know how to answer.
Now, I can't promise that everything will change tomorrow.
I can't promise that every prayer will be answered according to your preferred timeline.
And I can't explain why every delay happens.
But I can encourage you to remember what Scripture teaches about the Lord.
He is faithful.
He is merciful.
And His love has been revealed through Jesus Christ.
Now, your circumstances may still be uncertain.
But you can continue seeking Him.
You can continue growing spiritually.
You can continue caring for others.
And you can continue making wise decisions.
Even while you wait.
So don't assume that your life has stopped.
Don't assume that your worth is measured by one unanswered prayer.
And don't assume that you have to control everything to move forward.
You can take the next faithful step.
One day at a time.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us through another day of Bible study. Thank You for everything we've learned this week. Lord, You know every person listening. You know the answers they're waiting for. The disappointments they've experienced. And the questions they're still carrying. Father, help us remember Your faithfulness. Give us patience when we need to wait. Wisdom when we need to act. And humility when our plans need to change. Lord, I pray for the person who's feeling forgotten. Remind them of Your love revealed through Jesus Christ. I pray for the person who's exhausted by uncertainty. Give them strength and appropriate support. I pray for the person who's struggling with the desire to control everything. Help them recognize what is truly their responsibility. And I pray for the person who's discouraged because their circumstances haven't changed. Help them continue seeking You. Father, shape our character through Your Word and Spirit. Help us grow in patience. In kindness. In wisdom. And in love. Thank You for Jesus Christ. Thank You for His sacrifice. His resurrection. And the promise of eternal life through Him. May our hope remain firmly rooted in our Savior. And may we continue following Him faithfully. Even while we wait. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Eight, Day Six. And I hope today's Around the Fire conversation has encouraged you.
Remember... Waiting doesn't mean your life has stopped.
You can continue growing. Continue serving. Continue praying. And continue following Jesus Christ.
Tomorrow, we're going to close out Week Eight with a final lesson called... Faithful in the Waiting — Trusting God with What Comes Next.
We'll bring our study of God's timing to a close and talk about how to move forward with faith, wisdom, and hope.
Until then, remember... You don't have to know how everything will turn out to remain faithful today.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Faithful in the Waiting: Trusting God with What Comes Next
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — THE WAITING ISN'T THE END OF YOUR STORY Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today. Whether you're listening while getting ready for church, enjoying your morning coffee, driving down the road, or sitting somewhere quiet with your Bible, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Eight, Day Seven. And that means we're closing out another full week of walking through God's Word together.
Can you believe we're already finishing Week Eight?
We've spent this week talking about something that touches every one of our lives. Waiting.
Waiting for answers. Waiting for opportunities. Waiting for circumstances to change. Waiting for prayers to be answered. And sometimes, waiting for something we don't even know how to put into words.
Now, I want you to think about something. When we started this week, I asked you to consider what you were waiting for.
Maybe you had a particular situation in mind. Maybe there was an unanswered prayer. Maybe there was a decision you were hoping someone would make. Or maybe you were simply in a season of uncertainty.
Now, here we are at the end of the week. And I want to ask you a question. Has anything changed?
Maybe it has. Maybe you received an answer. Maybe something began moving forward. Maybe you had a conversation that brought clarity.
But maybe nothing has changed.
Maybe you're still waiting. Still praying. Still hoping. And still wondering what comes next.
Now, if that's where you are today, I want you to hear something. You don't have to receive every answer before you can continue walking faithfully with God.
Now, that doesn't mean waiting is easy. It doesn't mean disappointment isn't real. And it doesn't mean we should pretend to understand everything that's happening.
But it does mean our relationship with God can continue growing even when our circumstances remain uncertain.
And today, as we close out Week Eight, I want us to focus on one important question. How do we move forward faithfully when we still don't know what comes next?
That's what we're going to study today. Our lesson is called... Faithful in the Waiting — Trusting God with What Comes Next.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for carrying us through this week of study. Lord, You know every person listening. You know the prayers they've prayed. The answers they're waiting for. And the uncertainty they're facing. Father, help us remember what we've learned. Teach us to trust Your character. Give us wisdom when we need to act. Patience when we need to wait. And courage when we need to move forward without knowing every detail. Lord, help us remain rooted in Jesus Christ. And may today's study strengthen our faith as we continue walking with You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — PSALM 37:3–7 Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 37.
We're going to read verses 3 through 7. But before we begin, let's talk about the context.
Psalm 37 is a psalm of David. And throughout this passage, David addresses a struggle that many people still experience today.
The temptation to become discouraged when people who do wrong appear to prosper.
David encourages God's people not to become consumed by envy, anger, or fear.
Instead, he calls them to trust the Lord and continue doing good.
Now, let's read Psalm 37, verses 3 through 7, from the King James Version. "Trust in the LORD, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart. Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass. And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday. Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass."
Now, I want us to slow down and look at four instructions in this passage.
Trust in the Lord.
Do good.
Commit your way to Him.
And rest in the Lord.
Now, think about that. David doesn't simply tell us to sit around and do nothing.
He calls us to trust. But he also calls us to do good.
He calls us to commit our way to the Lord. And to wait patiently for Him.
Now, that's a beautiful picture of faithful living.
Because waiting on God doesn't mean abandoning our responsibilities.
It means continuing to honor Him while recognizing that our lives are ultimately in His hands.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Faithfulness isn't measured by how quickly your circumstances change. It's reflected in how you continue following Christ while you wait.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on receiving an answer that we forget what faithful living looks like today.
We want to know what's next.
We want to know when things will change.
And we want to know whether everything will turn out the way we hoped.
But Scripture continually reminds us to trust the Lord and continue doing what is right.
Even when the future is uncertain.
TRUST IN THE LORD — EVEN WHEN YOU DON'T UNDERSTAND Now, let's begin with the first instruction. "Trust in the LORD."
Now, I think that's something many of us say easily.
We tell people... "Just trust God."
We remind ourselves... "God's got this."
And we encourage one another to have faith.
But what does trusting God actually look like when we're facing uncertainty?
Now, I want you to think about that. Because trusting God doesn't mean we suddenly understand everything.
It doesn't mean every fear disappears.
And it doesn't mean we never have questions.
Trusting God means placing our confidence in His character even when our understanding is limited.
Now, let's turn to Proverbs chapter 3, verses 5 and 6. The King James Version says: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."
Now, notice something. The passage doesn't say... Trust the Lord only when you understand.
It tells us not to rely entirely on our own understanding.
Now, that doesn't mean we stop thinking carefully.
It doesn't mean we ignore facts.
And it doesn't mean we make decisions without seeking wisdom.
But it does mean we recognize that our knowledge is limited.
We don't know everything.
We cannot predict every outcome.
And sometimes we have to make responsible decisions without having complete certainty.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Trusting God doesn't require having all the answers. It requires continuing to seek His wisdom with the information and responsibilities we have today.
DO GOOD — DON'T PUT YOUR FAITH ON HOLD Now, let's return to Psalm 37.
David says... "Trust in the LORD, and do good."
Now, I love how those instructions belong together.
Because sometimes, when we're waiting for something important, we begin putting our lives on hold.
We tell ourselves... Once I get this answer, then I'll move forward.
Once this situation improves, then I'll begin serving.
Once I reach that milestone, then I'll focus on growing spiritually.
But Scripture reminds us that faithful living isn't something we postpone until circumstances become ideal.
We can continue doing good today.
Now, that doesn't mean ignoring serious problems.
And it doesn't mean taking on responsibilities beyond our capacity.
But it does mean recognizing the opportunities already before us.
Maybe there's someone you can encourage.
Maybe there's a responsibility you can fulfill.
Maybe there's a relationship that needs your attention.
Or maybe there's a habit you can begin developing.
Now, those things matter.
Even while you're waiting for something else.
And here's something important. You don't have to accomplish something extraordinary every day to live faithfully.
Sometimes faithfulness looks like showing up.
Sometimes it looks like keeping your word.
Sometimes it looks like choosing kindness.
And sometimes it looks like resting when your body and mind need rest.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The next faithful step doesn't always have to be a big one.
Sometimes it's simply doing what is right in the circumstances before you.
COMMIT YOUR WAY — HOLDING YOUR PLANS WITH HUMILITY Now, let's look at the next instruction. "Commit thy way unto the LORD."
Now, think about that. We make plans.
We set goals.
We imagine what the future might look like.
And sometimes we become deeply attached to those plans.
We decide how things should happen.
When they should happen.
And what the outcome should be.
But sometimes life unfolds differently.
And that's when we need humility.
Now, here's something important. Committing our way to the Lord doesn't mean we stop making plans.
It means we approach our plans with a willingness to submit them to God's wisdom.
We seek His guidance through Scripture.
We pray.
We seek wise counsel.
And we remain willing to adjust our plans when necessary.
Now, I want you to think about something. Have you ever been so determined to reach a particular outcome that you ignored information suggesting you needed a different approach?
Maybe you were pursuing an opportunity.
Maybe you were trying to repair a relationship.
Or maybe you were working toward a personal goal.
Now, sometimes perseverance is important.
But sometimes wisdom requires changing direction.
And recognizing that difference matters.
Because our commitment to God should be greater than our attachment to any particular plan.
REST IN THE LORD — WHEN YOUR HEART IS TIRED Now, let's look at the fourth instruction. "Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him."
Now, I want you to think about the word rest.
Because sometimes waiting can be exhausting.
We keep checking for answers.
We keep thinking about what might happen.
And we keep imagining every possible outcome.
Now, sometimes we genuinely need to monitor a situation.
Maybe there's an important deadline.
Maybe there's a medical concern.
Or maybe there's a responsibility that requires follow-up.
But other times, we become consumed by things we cannot control.
And that can leave us emotionally exhausted.
Now, resting in the Lord doesn't mean neglecting our responsibilities.
It means recognizing that we don't have to carry every uncertainty as though the outcome depends entirely on us.
We can take appropriate action.
We can establish healthy routines.
We can seek support.
And we can continue praying.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes we need spiritual encouragement.
And sometimes we also need physical rest, emotional support, or professional care.
Those needs aren't signs of weak faith.
They're part of being human.
And caring for ourselves wisely matters.
ISAIAH 40 — STRENGTH FOR THE WEARY Now, let's turn to Isaiah chapter 40.
We're going to read verses 28 through 31.
This passage speaks to God's greatness and His care for weary people.
Let's read. "Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding. He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength. Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "He giveth power to the faint."
Now, that's a beautiful reminder of God's care.
Because sometimes we're tired.
Not just physically tired.
But emotionally tired.
Tired of waiting.
Tired of uncertainty.
And tired of carrying responsibilities that seem never-ending.
Now, here's something important. Isaiah 40 was spoken in a context of God's encouragement to His people.
It reminds them of His greatness and faithfulness.
And it calls them to place their hope in Him.
Now, this passage isn't a promise that believers will never experience exhaustion.
And it doesn't mean we should ignore our physical limitations.
But it does remind us that God's strength isn't limited in the way ours is.
And we can continue depending on Him.
Now, maybe someone listening today needs that reminder.
You don't have to pretend you're never tired.
You don't have to carry every burden alone.
And you don't have to prove your faith by refusing to rest.
You can pray.
You can seek support.
And you can care for yourself responsibly.
WHEN THE ANSWER IS DIFFERENT FROM WHAT YOU EXPECTED Now, let's talk about something that can be difficult.
Sometimes the answer we receive isn't the answer we wanted.
Maybe you prayed for a particular opportunity.
But it didn't happen.
Maybe you hoped a relationship would be restored.
But circumstances remained complicated.
Maybe you expected a situation to improve.
But instead, you had to make a difficult decision.
Now, those experiences can be painful.
And sometimes they involve real grief.
But here's something I want you to remember. A disappointing outcome doesn't mean your life has lost its purpose.
And it doesn't mean your relationship with God has to end.
We can bring our disappointment before Him.
We can ask questions.
We can seek wisdom.
And we can begin considering what faithful living looks like in the circumstances we now face.
Now, I want to be careful here. We shouldn't tell someone that every disappointment happened because God had something better planned in the way we might imagine.
Sometimes we simply don't know why things happen.
And sometimes the losses people experience are profound.
But we can continue turning toward the Lord.
And we can remember that our ultimate hope rests in Jesus Christ.
HEBREWS 10 — DON'T THROW AWAY YOUR CONFIDENCE Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 10.
We're going to read verses 35 and 36. The King James Version says: "Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward. For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise."
Now, let's understand the context.
The writer of Hebrews is encouraging believers who have endured suffering and opposition because of their faith.
And he calls them to persevere.
Now, the promise here is rooted in God's saving work and the hope believers have in Christ.
It isn't a guarantee that every personal goal will be fulfilled.
But it does encourage us to remain faithful.
Now, I want you to think about that. Sometimes waiting can make us question everything.
We begin wondering whether our prayers matter.
Whether our efforts matter.
And whether we should continue.
Now, Scripture encourages us not to abandon our confidence in Christ.
Our circumstances may change.
Our plans may change.
But our hope remains rooted in Him.
PAUSE AND PRAY — TRUSTING GOD WITH WHAT COMES NEXT Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about the situation you've been carrying throughout this week.
Maybe you're still waiting for an answer.
Maybe something has changed.
Or maybe you're beginning to recognize that your next step may look different from what you expected.
Now, ask yourself... What do I need from God today?
Is it wisdom?
Patience?
Courage?
Or strength? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, You know the situations we're carrying. You know the answers we're waiting for. And You know the uncertainty we're facing. Lord, help us trust Your character. Give us wisdom to recognize our responsibilities. Patience when we need to wait. And courage when we need to take the next step. Father, help us remain rooted in Jesus Christ. And remind us that our ultimate hope rests in Him. In His precious name, Amen.
PHILIPPIANS 3 — PRESSING FORWARD Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 3.
We're going to read verses 13 and 14. The King James Version says: "Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus."
Now, let's understand what Paul is saying.
He's describing his pursuit of knowing Christ and pressing toward the heavenly goal.
He's not simply talking about achieving personal success.
And he's not suggesting that we should ignore our past or refuse to process painful experiences.
Instead, he's emphasizing his continued pursuit of Christ.
Now, I think that connects beautifully with our lesson.
Because sometimes we become so focused on what hasn't happened that we stop considering how to live faithfully today.
We keep looking backward.
We keep replaying disappointments.
And we keep wondering whether things could have been different.
Now, reflection can be helpful.
And sometimes we need time to grieve or process what we've experienced.
But we can also continue moving forward in our relationship with Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Moving forward doesn't mean pretending the past didn't happen. It means continuing to pursue Christ while carrying the lessons we've learned.
MATTHEW 6 — FAITHFUL TODAY Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 6.
We're going to read verses 33 and 34. The King James Version says: "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
Now, let's remember the context.
Jesus is teaching about anxiety over daily necessities.
He speaks about food, clothing, and the Father's care.
And He calls His followers to seek God's kingdom first.
Now, here's something important. Jesus isn't telling us that responsible planning is wrong.
And He isn't promising a life without hardship.
But He is teaching us not to become consumed by tomorrow's worries.
Now, I want you to think about that. Sometimes we're so worried about next week that we overlook today.
We're so concerned about next month that we forget the responsibilities already before us.
And we're so focused on what might happen that we struggle to recognize what we can do right now.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. You can prepare for tomorrow without allowing tomorrow's uncertainty to consume today.
And sometimes that begins with asking a simple question. What is the next faithful step?
Not the next ten steps.
Not the entire plan for the next year.
Just the next faithful step.
WHEN YOU DON'T KNOW THE NEXT STEP Now, let's talk about something that can be frustrating.
Sometimes we don't know what the next step should be.
Maybe you're facing a decision.
Maybe you have several options.
Or maybe you're waiting for information that hasn't arrived.
Now, in those moments, we can begin by asking God for wisdom.
We can study Scripture.
We can seek wise counsel.
And we can gather reliable information.
Now, sometimes the next step becomes clear.
Other times, we may need to wait until we have enough information to make a responsible decision.
And sometimes we may need to choose between several reasonable options.
Now, here's something important. Not every decision comes with a dramatic sign.
And not every choice has one mysterious answer that we're supposed to discover.
Sometimes faithful decision-making involves wisdom, prayer, and careful consideration.
Now, I want you to remember something. You don't have to predict the future to make a responsible decision today.
You can seek wisdom.
Consider the information available.
And take the next appropriate step.
ROMANS 8 — HOPE FOR WHAT WE DO NOT SEE Now, let's turn to Romans chapter 8.
We're going to read verses 24 and 25. The King James Version says: "For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it."
Now, let's understand the context.
Paul is speaking about the Christian hope of redemption.
He describes believers waiting for the fullness of what God has promised.
Now, this isn't a promise that every personal wish will eventually happen.
It's pointing toward the future hope believers have through Jesus Christ.
And that's important.
Because Christian hope is deeper than optimism about our circumstances.
Our hope is rooted in God's saving work.
And His promises through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Even when our present circumstances remain uncertain, our ultimate hope in Christ remains secure.
THE DANGER OF COMPARING TIMELINES Now, I want to talk about something that can make waiting even harder.
Comparison.
Sometimes we look at other people's lives and begin wondering why things seem to be moving faster for them.
Maybe someone received an opportunity you were hoping for.
Maybe someone reached a milestone you've been working toward.
Or maybe someone seems to have received an answer while you're still waiting.
Now, those comparisons can be discouraging.
But here's something important. We rarely know everything happening in someone else's life.
We see accomplishments.
We see announcements.
And we see celebrations.
But we don't always see the struggles behind them.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Someone else's progress doesn't determine your worth.
And someone else's circumstances don't tell you everything about your own future.
We can celebrate others.
We can remain grateful.
And we can continue seeking the Lord.
Without turning every comparison into a judgment about ourselves.
WHAT IF THE WAITING CONTINUES? Now, let's talk about something important.
What if the waiting continues?
What if next week arrives and you still don't have an answer?
What if next month arrives and circumstances haven't changed?
Or what if the outcome is different from what you hoped for?
Now, those are real possibilities.
And I don't want to pretend otherwise.
But here's something I want you to remember. Your relationship with God doesn't have to depend on receiving one particular outcome.
You can continue praying.
You can continue seeking wisdom.
You can continue caring for yourself and others.
And you can continue growing in your relationship with Christ.
Now, sometimes that means adjusting your plans.
Sometimes it means seeking support.
And sometimes it means accepting that certain questions may remain unanswered for a while.
But you can continue walking faithfully.
One day at a time.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What has this week taught me about trusting God's timing?
Maybe you've learned something about patience.
Maybe you've recognized an area where you've been trying to control too much.
Or maybe you've been reminded that your worth isn't determined by one particular outcome. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... What situation am I still carrying into the next week?
Maybe it's an unanswered prayer.
Maybe it's a decision.
Or maybe it's something that continues weighing on your heart. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What is one responsible step I can take while I wait?
Maybe it's preparing.
Gathering information.
Seeking support.
Or continuing to fulfill a responsibility. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I keep my hope rooted in Jesus Christ rather than in one particular outcome?
Think about what Scripture teaches concerning God's character.
And the salvation we have through Christ. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — OUR HOPE BEYOND THE WAITING Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because the purpose of this week's study hasn't simply been to teach us how to wait more patiently.
It's been to help us grow in our relationship with Christ.
Now, Jesus lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, that's the foundation of Christian hope.
And that hope isn't dependent on every personal plan succeeding.
It isn't dependent on receiving every answer according to our preferred timeline.
And it isn't dependent on having a life without hardship.
Our hope is rooted in Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn God's love by waiting perfectly.
We don't earn salvation by becoming patient enough.
And we don't have to pretend that we've already reached spiritual maturity.
Our salvation rests in God's grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our growth is part of our response to that grace.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You don't have to know what comes next to remain faithful today. Trust God's character, seek His wisdom, and take the next step that's yours to take.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on tomorrow that we overlook the opportunities before us today.
But today still matters.
And we can continue living faithfully.
Even while we wait.
LIVING IT OUT — YOUR NEXT FAITHFUL STEP Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... My Next Faithful Step.
Now, beneath that heading, answer three questions.
First... What am I still waiting for?
Write down the situation honestly.
Second... What can I responsibly do?
Maybe there's a phone call to make.
An appointment to prepare for.
A conversation to have.
Or a responsibility that needs your attention.
And third... What do I need to entrust to God?
Maybe it's the timing.
Maybe it's another person's decision.
Or maybe it's an outcome you cannot guarantee.
Now, after you've written those answers down, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom.
And choose one faithful action you can take today.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the situation I'm still carrying is...
Our second prompt is... One truth about Your faithfulness I want to remember is...
And our third prompt is... Help me take the next faithful step by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will trust God's character, seek His wisdom, and continue walking faithfully with Christ, even when I don't know what comes next.
Now, say that again. I will trust God's character, seek His wisdom, and continue walking faithfully with Christ, even when I don't know what comes next.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Psalm 37, verse 3. "Trust in the LORD, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
"Trust in the LORD, and do good."
And whenever you begin feeling overwhelmed by uncertainty, ask yourself... What is the next faithful step I can take?
Then choose one responsible action.
AROUND THE FIRE — CLOSING OUT WEEK EIGHT Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire one more time.
And I ask you this question. When we began this week, what were you hoping would change?
Maybe it was a situation.
Maybe it was a relationship.
Maybe it was an answer.
Or maybe it was simply the way you were feeling.
Now, think about where you are today.
Maybe something has changed.
Maybe nothing has changed.
Or maybe you've begun seeing the situation differently. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What is one lesson from this week that you want to carry forward?
Maybe it's patience.
Maybe it's remembering God's faithfulness.
Maybe it's surrendering the desire to control everything.
Or maybe it's recognizing that spiritual growth can continue while you wait. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. You don't have to finish every waiting season before you can begin living faithfully in the next one.
You can carry what you've learned.
You can continue seeking the Lord.
And you can take the next faithful step.
CLOSING REFLECTION — KEEP WALKING Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Maybe you're still waiting.
Maybe the answer hasn't arrived.
Maybe the situation hasn't changed.
And maybe you're still carrying questions about what comes next.
Now, I can't promise that everything will change tomorrow.
I can't promise that every prayer will be answered according to your preferred timeline.
And I can't explain why every difficult season happens.
But I can encourage you to remember what Scripture teaches about the Lord.
He is faithful.
He is merciful.
And His love has been revealed through Jesus Christ.
Now, remember Psalm 37.
"Trust in the LORD, and do good."
Those words are simple.
But they give us something meaningful to carry into the next season.
Trust the Lord.
And continue doing good.
You don't have to control every outcome.
You don't have to predict every change.
And you don't have to understand everything before you can continue walking with Christ.
You can seek wisdom.
You can act responsibly.
And you can remain faithful.
One step at a time.
So whatever you're waiting for today...
Don't let uncertainty convince you that your life has lost its meaning.
Don't let disappointment convince you that your relationship with God has to end.
And don't let comparison convince you that your worth is determined by someone else's timeline.
Keep seeking the Lord.
Keep opening your Bible.
And keep walking faithfully with Jesus Christ.
Even when you don't know what comes next.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us through another week of Walking Through the Word. Thank You for everything we've learned about trusting Your timing. Lord, You know every person listening. You know the answers they're waiting for. The disappointments they've experienced. And the uncertainty they're carrying. Father, help us remember Your faithfulness. Give us patience when we need to wait. Wisdom when we need to act. And courage when we need to move forward. Lord, I pray for the person who's feeling discouraged. Remind them of Your mercy and love. I pray for the person who's overwhelmed by uncertainty. Give them wisdom and appropriate support. I pray for the person who's struggling with the desire to control everything. Help them recognize what is truly their responsibility. And I pray for the person who's disappointed because life hasn't followed their plans. Help them process that disappointment honestly. Father, teach us to seek Your kingdom first. Help us continue doing good. And help us remain rooted in Jesus Christ. Thank You for His sacrifice. His resurrection. And the promise of eternal life through Him. May our hope remain firmly rooted in our Savior. And may we continue following Him faithfully. Even while we wait. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO WEEK NINE Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Eight!
And I hope this week's study has encouraged you to remember that waiting doesn't mean your life has stopped.
You can continue growing. Continue serving. Continue praying. And continue following Jesus Christ.
Now, next week, we're beginning a brand-new study. And I'm especially excited about this one.
Our Week Nine theme is... Finding Joy in Every Season.
Because sometimes life is difficult. Sometimes circumstances don't turn out the way we expected. And sometimes we struggle to recognize joy in the middle of everything we're carrying.
But Scripture teaches us that Christian joy is rooted in something deeper than our circumstances.
And that's what we're going to explore together.
Our first lesson will be called... Joy That Doesn't Depend on Circumstances — Finding Strength in the Lord.
We'll study what it means to find joy in our relationship with Christ, even when life is challenging.
Until then, remember... You don't have to know what comes next to remain faithful today.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Joy That Doesn't Depend on Circumstances: Finding Strength in the Lord
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — CAN YOU HAVE JOY WHEN LIFE IS HARD? Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today. Whether you're listening while enjoying your morning coffee, driving to work, getting ready for the day, or sitting somewhere quiet with your Bible, I'm glad you're here.
Today is Week Nine, Day One. And we're beginning a brand-new study called... Finding Joy in Every Season.
Now, I want to start today by asking you a question. Have you ever looked at someone who was going through an incredibly difficult season... And wondered how they could still smile?
Maybe they were facing a serious illness. Maybe they were grieving someone they loved. Maybe they were dealing with financial struggles. Or maybe their life had changed in ways they never expected.
And yet, somehow, they still had moments of joy.
Now, I want you to think about that. Because sometimes we assume joy and happiness are the same thing.
We think joy means everything is going well. We think joy means we're smiling all the time. And we think joy means we don't have anything to worry about.
But biblical joy is deeper than that.
Now, let me explain what I mean. Happiness often responds to circumstances.
We receive good news, and we're happy. We spend time with people we love, and we're happy. Something exciting happens, and we're happy.
And there's nothing wrong with that.
Those are wonderful experiences.
But what happens when circumstances change?
What happens when the good news doesn't come? When the relationship becomes difficult? When the diagnosis isn't what we hoped? Or when life takes a turn we never expected?
Does that mean joy is no longer possible?
Well, Scripture teaches us that Christian joy is rooted in something deeper than temporary circumstances.
It's rooted in our relationship with God. In His faithfulness. In His promises. And in the salvation we have through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something important. That doesn't mean Christians should be happy all the time.
It doesn't mean we should hide our grief. And it certainly doesn't mean that struggling emotionally is a failure of faith.
But it does mean that even during difficult seasons, we can continue finding reasons to hope in the Lord.
And that's what we're going to explore today. Our lesson is called... Joy That Doesn't Depend on Circumstances — Finding Strength in the Lord.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for allowing us to begin this new week of study. Lord, today we're talking about joy. And You know that for some people listening, joy may feel very far away. You know the burdens they're carrying. The disappointments they've experienced. And the situations that have left them feeling discouraged. Father, help us understand what Your Word teaches about joy. Help us recognize the difference between temporary happiness and the deeper hope we have through Jesus Christ. Give us compassion for those who are hurting. And help us approach this study with honest hearts. Lord, may Your Word encourage us. May Your Spirit guide us. And may everything we learn draw us closer to Jesus. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — NEHEMIAH 8:10 Now, let's turn to Nehemiah chapter 8.
We're going to focus on verse 10. But before we read it, I want to explain what's happening in this passage.
The book of Nehemiah tells us about the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls and the restoration of the community after the exile.
God's people had experienced tremendous upheaval. Their city had been destroyed. Many had lived in exile. And now, as the community was being restored, they were returning to the Word of God.
In Nehemiah chapter 8, Ezra reads the Law before the assembled people.
And as the people hear God's Word explained, they begin to weep.
Now, think about that. They're listening to Scripture. They're recognizing its meaning. And they're responding emotionally.
But Nehemiah and the other leaders encourage them to recognize the holiness of the day and celebrate.
Now, let's read Nehemiah chapter 8, verse 10, from the King James Version. "Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength."
Now, I want you to hear those last words again. "For the joy of the LORD is your strength."
Now, that's a beautiful statement.
But I want us to understand it in context.
The people were being encouraged to celebrate a holy occasion.
They were reminded not only to enjoy the feast themselves, but also to share food with those who had nothing prepared.
Now, notice something important. Their joy wasn't simply about feeling good.
It was connected to worship. To hearing God's Word. To belonging to His people. And to caring for others.
Now, that's a much richer picture of joy than simply having a good day.
And it gives us a foundation for our study.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Biblical joy is rooted in the Lord's faithfulness, not in the expectation that every circumstance will be easy.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes life is difficult. Sometimes we experience disappointment. Sometimes we grieve. And sometimes we simply don't feel happy.
But our relationship with Christ gives us a foundation of hope that extends beyond our present circumstances.
JOY IS NOT THE SAME AS PRETENDING Now, let's talk about something important.
Sometimes people misunderstand what Christian joy means.
They assume that if you have faith, you should always be smiling.
You should never feel discouraged. You should never cry. And you should never admit that something is difficult.
But that's not what Scripture teaches.
The Bible contains many examples of faithful people experiencing sorrow.
David wrote psalms of lament.
Jeremiah grieved over Jerusalem.
Paul experienced hardship and distress.
And Jesus Himself wept.
Now, think about that. Jesus wept.
John chapter 11, verse 35, says: "Jesus wept."
Now, that's the shortest verse in the King James Bible.
But it communicates something meaningful.
Jesus wasn't indifferent to human suffering.
He experienced genuine sorrow at the tomb of Lazarus.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Having joy in Christ doesn't mean you never experience sadness.
You can grieve and still belong to Jesus.
You can cry and still have faith.
And you can acknowledge disappointment while continuing to trust the Lord.
Now, that matters. Because sometimes Christians feel pressure to hide their emotions.
They worry that admitting sadness will make others question their faith.
But honest emotions aren't something we need to hide from God.
We can bring them before Him in prayer.
And we can seek encouragement and support from others.
NEHEMIAH 8 — JOY SHARED WITH OTHERS Now, let's return to Nehemiah chapter 8.
I want us to look at something that can be easy to overlook.
When Nehemiah tells the people to celebrate, he also tells them to share with those who have nothing prepared.
Now, think about that. Their celebration wasn't meant to exclude people who had less.
They were instructed to include others.
And I think there's something beautiful about that.
Because sometimes joy becomes even more meaningful when it's shared.
Now, let me give you an example. Maybe you've experienced a difficult week.
And someone reaches out to check on you.
Maybe they bring you a meal.
Maybe they send an encouraging message.
Or maybe they simply take time to listen.
Now, that act of kindness may not solve every problem.
But it can remind you that you're not alone.
And sometimes those moments become sources of encouragement.
Now, here's something important. Christian joy isn't simply about what we receive.
It's also connected to how we love and serve others.
We can celebrate with those who are celebrating.
We can comfort those who are grieving.
And we can share what we have with those who are in need.
Now, those things reflect the love of Christ.
PHILIPPIANS 4 — REJOICE IN THE LORD Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 4.
We're going to read verses 4 through 7. The King James Version says: "Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice. Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand. Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."
Now, let's think about the context.
Paul wrote Philippians while imprisoned.
His circumstances were difficult.
And yet, throughout the letter, he repeatedly speaks about joy.
Now, that's significant.
Because Paul wasn't writing from a life free of hardship.
He understood suffering.
He understood uncertainty.
And he understood what it meant to face opposition because of his faith.
Yet he says... "Rejoice in the Lord alway."
Now, notice where he directs our joy.
"In the Lord."
Not in perfect circumstances.
Not in receiving every answer.
And not in having a life without difficulty.
But in the Lord.
Now, here's something important. Paul's instruction to rejoice isn't permission for us to shame people who are struggling.
We shouldn't tell someone who is grieving that they simply need to smile more.
And we shouldn't assume that emotional suffering means someone lacks faith.
Instead, we can encourage one another to remember the hope we have in Christ.
And we can offer compassion and practical support.
WHEN HAPPINESS DISAPPEARS Now, let's talk about something that happens to all of us.
Sometimes happiness disappears.
Maybe you wake up one morning feeling excited about the day.
Everything seems to be going well.
You have plans. You have energy. And you're looking forward to what's ahead.
But then something happens.
You receive disappointing news.
A conversation doesn't go well.
An unexpected problem appears.
And suddenly, your mood changes.
Now, that's normal.
Our emotions respond to our experiences.
And we shouldn't pretend otherwise.
But here's something important. Our relationship with God doesn't disappear every time our emotions change.
The truth of the gospel doesn't change because we have a difficult day.
And God's faithfulness isn't measured by how happy we feel in a particular moment.
Now, I want you to remember something. Your emotions can change throughout the day without changing the truth of who Jesus Christ is.
Now, that's a powerful reminder.
Because sometimes we begin measuring our spiritual lives by how we feel.
If we feel encouraged, we assume everything is going well.
If we feel discouraged, we begin questioning whether God is near.
But Scripture gives us a foundation beyond our changing emotions.
It reminds us of God's character.
His promises.
And His saving work through Jesus Christ.
HABAKKUK — REJOICING WHEN EVERYTHING IS UNCERTAIN Now, let's turn to the book of Habakkuk.
We're going to read chapter 3, verses 17 through 19.
But before we read, I want to explain what's happening.
Habakkuk was a prophet who wrestled with difficult questions about injustice, judgment, and suffering.
He questioned what he was seeing.
And he brought those questions before God.
Now, by the end of the book, Habakkuk expresses confidence in the Lord even while anticipating difficult circumstances.
Let's read Habakkuk chapter 3, verses 17 through 19. "Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation. The LORD God is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds' feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places. To the chief singer on my stringed instruments."
Now, I want you to think about those words.
The fig tree isn't blossoming.
The vines aren't producing fruit.
The fields aren't yielding food.
And the flocks are gone.
Now, in an agricultural society, those things represented serious hardship.
They weren't minor inconveniences.
They affected people's livelihoods and survival.
And yet Habakkuk says... "Yet I will rejoice in the LORD."
Now, I want you to notice that word. "Yet."
Even though circumstances are difficult...
Even though the harvest has failed...
Even though the future is uncertain...
Yet I will rejoice in the Lord.
Now, here's something important. Habakkuk isn't denying the seriousness of the situation.
He's acknowledging it.
But he's also expressing confidence in God.
Now, that's a beautiful picture of biblical joy.
It's not pretending that everything is fine.
It's continuing to place our hope in the Lord even when life is difficult.
THE POWER OF THE WORD "YET" Now, I want us to stay with that word for a moment.
Yet.
Sometimes one small word can change the direction of a sentence.
Now, think about how we might use that word in our own lives.
I'm disappointed... Yet I can still pray.
I'm grieving... Yet I can still seek comfort in Christ.
I'm uncertain about the future... Yet I can still make wise decisions today.
I'm struggling... Yet I can still ask for help.
