Lord, today we're looking at Mary's response to Your message. Help us understand the significance of this moment in the Christmas story. Teach us to approach Your Word with humility. Give us wisdom when we face unexpected circumstances. Help us ask honest questions. And help us respond faithfully to what You've revealed in Scripture. Father, may today's lesson encourage those who are facing uncertainty. And may everything we study draw us closer to Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — LUKE 1:26–38 Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 1. We're going to read verses 26 through 38.
Before we begin, let's understand the setting. Luke tells us that the angel Gabriel was sent by God to Nazareth, a town in Galilee.
There he appeared to Mary, who was betrothed to Joseph.
Betrothal in that culture was a serious commitment, more binding than a modern engagement.
And the announcement Mary was about to receive would be extraordinary.
Let's read Luke chapter 1, verses 26 through 38, from the King James Version. "And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary. And the angel came in unto her, and said, Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women. And when she saw him, she was troubled at his saying, and cast in her mind what manner of salutation this should be. And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end. Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God. And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren. For with God nothing shall be impossible. And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her."
Now, I want you to hear Mary's final response again. "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word."
Now, that's the heart of today's lesson. Mary received an extraordinary message. She asked a sincere question. And she responded with humble willingness.
But let's slow down and look at what this passage actually teaches us.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Faithful obedience doesn't require knowing every detail of the future. It begins with trusting God's revealed Word and responding with humility and wisdom.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we think faith means never having questions.
Or never feeling uncertain.
But Mary's story reminds us that sincere questions and faithful responses can exist together.
MARY WAS TROUBLED — AND THAT MATTERS Now, let's go back to verse 29. Luke tells us that Mary was troubled by Gabriel's greeting.
Now, I think that's important. Because sometimes we read the Christmas story so quickly that we overlook the human experience of the people involved.
We know how the story unfolds. We know Jesus will be born. We know the shepherds will hear the announcement. And we know the significance of His coming.
But Mary was hearing this message for the first time.
Now, Scripture doesn't tell us every thought that went through her mind. And we shouldn't invent details that Luke doesn't provide.
But Luke does tell us that she was troubled.
And that she considered what the greeting meant.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we assume that faithful people never experience uncertainty.
We imagine that strong faith always looks calm. Always confident. And always completely certain.
But Scripture gives us a more honest picture of human responses.
People ask questions. People experience fear. And people seek understanding.
Now, here's something important. Experiencing uncertainty doesn't automatically mean someone lacks faith.
And asking sincere questions isn't the same as rejecting God's Word.
Sometimes questions are part of seeking understanding.
"FEAR NOT, MARY" Now, let's look at verse 30. Gabriel says: "Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God."
Now, notice that Gabriel addresses her fear.
He doesn't shame her for being troubled.
He reassures her.
And then he explains the announcement.
Now, I want you to remember something. The Christmas story includes people facing extraordinary circumstances.
Mary receives an announcement that changes her understanding of what lies ahead. Joseph later receives a message concerning Mary's pregnancy. And the shepherds are afraid when the angel appears to them.
Yet throughout these accounts, we see God's saving purposes being revealed.
Now, that doesn't mean every fear we experience is connected to a divine assignment.
And it doesn't mean we should ignore warning signs or make unsafe decisions.
But it does remind us that fear doesn't have to prevent us from seeking God's wisdom.
We can acknowledge our concerns. We can pray. We can seek wise counsel. And we can continue studying Scripture.
THE ANNOUNCEMENT WAS ABOUT JESUS Now, I want us to notice something that can easily get overlooked.
Sometimes when we study Mary, we focus so much on her response that we forget the central message of Gabriel's announcement.
The announcement was about Jesus.
Gabriel says Mary will give birth to a son. His name will be Jesus. He will be called the Son of the Highest. He will receive the throne of David. And His kingdom will have no end.
Now, that's extraordinary.
Remember what we studied on Day One. Isaiah spoke about a child who would be born. A son who would be given. And a kingdom established with justice and righteousness.
Now, Luke connects Jesus with the promises concerning David's throne and an everlasting kingdom.
So Mary's story isn't simply an example of a person responding to unexpected news.
It's part of the announcement that the promised Messiah is coming.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The greatest significance of Mary's story isn't that she faced an unexpected change. It's that she was chosen to bear Jesus Christ, the promised Savior.
And that keeps our Christmas study centered where it belongs. On Jesus.
MARY ASKED A QUESTION Now, let's look at verse 34. Mary asks: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
Now, I love that Luke includes this question.
Because Mary doesn't pretend to understand something she doesn't understand.
She asks how the announced birth will happen.
And Gabriel answers by explaining the work of the Holy Spirit.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes Christians feel pressure to pretend they understand every passage of Scripture.
They worry that asking questions will make them appear less faithful.
But studying God's Word involves learning.
And learning often involves questions.
We may need to examine the context.
Compare passages.
Seek guidance from trusted teachers.
Or spend additional time studying.
Now, here's something important. We shouldn't treat every personal impression as though it carries the same authority as Scripture.
But we can approach God's revealed Word with humility and a sincere desire to understand.
And when we don't know something, it's okay to acknowledge that.
"FOR WITH GOD NOTHING SHALL BE IMPOSSIBLE" Now, let's look at verse 37. Gabriel says: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
Now, this is one of the most familiar verses in the Christmas story.
And it's a beautiful declaration of God's power.
But I want us to understand it in context.
Gabriel has just explained the miraculous conception of Jesus.
And he has told Mary that Elisabeth, who had been considered barren, is also expecting a child.
The verse emphasizes God's ability to accomplish what He has declared.
Now, here's something important. This doesn't mean that every outcome we desire is guaranteed to happen.
It doesn't mean every illness will be healed in the way we hope.
It doesn't mean every relationship will be restored.
And it doesn't mean every personal plan will succeed.
But it does remind us that God's power is not limited by human ability.
And in the Christmas story, we see His power at work in accomplishing His promise concerning Jesus Christ.
Now, that's the truth we can hold on to.
MARY'S RESPONSE — HUMILITY AND FAITH Now, let's return to verse 38. Mary says: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word."
Now, I want you to notice something. Mary identifies herself as the Lord's servant.
And she responds according to the message she has received.
Now, that is an example of humility.
And it is an example of faith.
But we should remember that Mary was responding to a specific revelation delivered by Gabriel.
We shouldn't use her response to suggest that people must agree to every unexpected request or accept every difficult situation without question.
God doesn't call us to abandon discernment.
And humility doesn't mean allowing someone to manipulate or harm us.
Instead, we can learn from Mary's willingness to respond to God's revealed Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Biblical humility doesn't mean turning off our judgment. It means recognizing God's authority and seeking to respond faithfully to His truth.
PROVERBS 3 — TRUSTING GOD WITH OUR PATH Now, let's turn to Proverbs chapter 3. We're going to read verses 5 and 6. The King James Version says: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart..."
Now, trusting God doesn't mean refusing to think carefully.
It doesn't mean ignoring facts.
And it doesn't mean making decisions without considering consequences.
Instead, it means recognizing that our own understanding is limited.
We seek God's wisdom.
We study His Word.
We pray.
And we make thoughtful decisions.
Now, sometimes our plans change.
Sometimes circumstances surprise us.
And sometimes we need to reconsider what we thought would happen.
But through those changes, we can continue seeking the Lord.
WHEN THE PLAN CHANGES Now, I want to talk about something many of us can relate to.
The moment when life doesn't go according to plan.
Maybe you thought you would be in a different place by now.
Maybe you expected a relationship to unfold differently.
Maybe you had a career plan.
A family plan.
Or a particular goal.
And then something changed.
Now, here's something important. Not every unexpected change is good.
And not every difficult circumstance should be described as something God specifically arranged.
Sometimes people experience injustice.
Sometimes they face illness.
Sometimes they experience loss.
And sometimes they encounter situations that require practical help and wise decisions.
But through those circumstances, we can continue seeking God.
We can pray for wisdom.
We can ask for support.
And we can take responsible steps forward.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Trusting God doesn't require pretending that every unexpected change is easy or good. It means continuing to seek Him while responding wisely to the circumstances before us.
PSALM 119 — ONE STEP AT A TIME Now, let's turn to Psalm 119. We're going to read verse 105. The King James Version says: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
Now, I love that picture.
A lamp. A path. And enough light to see where you're going.
Now, think about walking outside at night with a small flashlight.
You may not be able to see the entire road.
But you can see the next few steps.
And you can move carefully.
Now, that's a helpful picture of how Scripture guides our lives.
We don't know everything that will happen tomorrow.
We can't predict every challenge.
And we can't control every outcome.
But we can study God's Word.
We can seek wisdom.
And we can make faithful choices with the information we have.
Now, I want you to think about something. Maybe you've been putting pressure on yourself to figure out your entire future.
Maybe you've been worried about decisions that are still months away.
Or maybe you've been trying to solve problems that haven't happened yet.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Sometimes the most responsible thing we can do is focus on the next faithful step.
Not because the future doesn't matter.
But because we can only act in the present.
And we can seek God's wisdom as we move forward.
PAUSE AND PRAY — LORD, GIVE ME WISDOM Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about an area of your life where you need wisdom.
Maybe it's a decision.
Maybe it's a responsibility.
Maybe it's an unexpected change.
Or maybe it's something you've been praying about.
Now, take a moment to bring that concern before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word. Thank You for the example of Mary's faith and humility. Lord, You know the decisions we're facing. You know the questions we're carrying. And You know the circumstances we cannot control. Father, give us wisdom. Help us distinguish Your truth from our own assumptions. Teach us to seek wise counsel when needed. And help us respond faithfully to what You've revealed in Scripture. Lord, when we're uncertain, help us continue praying. When we're afraid, help us seek Your guidance. And when our plans change, help us respond with wisdom and courage. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
JAMES 1 — ASKING GOD FOR WISDOM Now, let's turn to James chapter 1. We're going to read verse 5. The King James Version says: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him."
Now, I want you to notice something. James encourages believers to ask God for wisdom.
Not simply for the outcomes they prefer.
But for wisdom.
Now, that's important. Because sometimes we pray only for a particular result.
We say... "Lord, please make this happen."
Or... "Lord, please let this work out the way I want."
Now, it's okay to bring our desires before God.
But we can also pray for wisdom.
Wisdom to make decisions.
Wisdom to recognize unhealthy situations.
Wisdom to know when to seek help.
And wisdom to respond faithfully.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Sometimes the most important prayer isn't simply, "Lord, change my circumstances." It's also, "Lord, give me wisdom to respond faithfully."
LUKE 1 — MARY VISITS ELISABETH Now, let's return to Luke chapter 1. We're going to read verses 39 through 45.
After Gabriel's announcement, Mary visits Elisabeth.
And this meeting becomes another meaningful moment in the Christmas story.
Let's read. "And Mary arose in those days, and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Juda; And entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elisabeth. And it came to pass, that, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost: And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For, lo, as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy. And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord."
Now, I want you to notice Elisabeth's final words. "Blessed is she that believed..."
Now, that's a beautiful affirmation of Mary's faith.
And I also want you to notice something else. Mary wasn't experiencing this moment entirely alone.
She visited Elisabeth.
And Elisabeth responded with encouragement and recognition of what God was doing.
Now, here's something we can learn from that. When we're facing unexpected circumstances, meaningful support matters.
We may need someone to listen.
Someone to encourage us.
Someone to pray with us.
Or someone who can offer wise guidance.
Now, asking for support isn't a failure of faith.
And we don't have to pretend we can handle everything alone.
Sometimes God uses relationships within the body of Christ to provide encouragement and care.
MATTHEW 1 — JOSEPH'S RESPONSE Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 1. We're going to read verses 18 through 25.
Because Mary's story is connected to Joseph's story.
And Matthew gives us important details about his response.
Let's read. "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily. But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
Now, I want you to notice something. Joseph was facing a serious situation.
And Matthew tells us that he considered what to do.
Then he received a specific message from the angel of the Lord.
And he responded according to that message.
Now, just like Mary's experience, Joseph's situation was unique.
But we can learn from the importance of responding thoughtfully rather than acting carelessly.
Now, here's something else I want you to notice. The angel explains the meaning of Jesus' name. "For he shall save his people from their sins."
Now, that's the center of the Christmas story.
The promised Savior has come.
And His mission is salvation.
MARY'S SONG — MAGNIFYING THE LORD Now, let's return to Luke chapter 1. We're going to read verses 46 through 49.
These verses begin Mary's song of praise, often called the Magnificat.
Let's read. "And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name."
Now, I want you to notice where Mary's praise is directed.
Toward the Lord.
She magnifies Him.
She rejoices in God her Savior.
And she recognizes His holiness.
Now, that's a beautiful response.
Because even though Mary has been given an extraordinary role, her praise points toward God.
And that reminds us of something important. Our lives should ultimately point toward the Lord.
Not simply toward our own accomplishments.
Not toward recognition.
And not toward personal importance.
But toward His grace and goodness.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... How do I usually respond when life doesn't unfold according to my plans?
Do I become discouraged?
Do I try to control everything?
Or do I pause and seek wisdom? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... What can Mary's response teach me about humility and faith?
Think about her willingness to respond to God's revealed message. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... Is there an area of my life where I need to seek wisdom rather than rush into a decision?
Maybe it's a relationship.
A responsibility.
A financial decision.
Or an unexpected change. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... Who can I turn to for wise, trustworthy encouragement when I'm facing uncertainty?
Maybe it's a pastor.
A trusted friend.
A family member.
Or someone with experience in the situation you're facing. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE PROMISED SAVIOR Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because Mary's story is ultimately part of the story of His coming.
Gabriel announced that Mary would give birth to Jesus.
The Son of the Highest.
The promised King.
And Matthew tells us that He came to save His people from their sins.
Now, that's why the Christmas story matters.
Jesus Christ is the eternal Son of God who became flesh.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation through perfect obedience.
We don't earn it by never having questions.
And we don't earn it by making every decision correctly.
Salvation is God's gift of grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our obedience is a response to His grace.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. Mary didn't know every detail of the future, but she responded faithfully to God's revealed Word. We can learn from her humility while remembering that our greatest hope is found in the Savior she carried.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on figuring out the future that we forget to seek God in the present.
We can pray.
We can study Scripture.
We can ask for wisdom.
And we can take the next responsible step.
LIVING IT OUT — MY NEXT FAITHFUL STEP Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... My Next Faithful Step.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... One situation in your life that feels uncertain.
Second... One Scripture that can help guide your response.
Third... One person you could ask for wise counsel.
And fourth... One practical step you can take responsibly.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom.
Ask Him to help you recognize what Scripture teaches.
And seek to respond faithfully.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, one unexpected circumstance I'm facing is...
Our second prompt is... One truth from Your Word that can guide me is...
And our third prompt is... Help me respond with humility and wisdom by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek God's wisdom, trust His revealed Word, and respond faithfully one step at a time.
Now, say that again. I will seek God's wisdom, trust His revealed Word, and respond faithfully one step at a time.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Luke chapter 1, verse 38. "And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about what Mary's response teaches us about humility.
Maybe you'll spend time praying about a decision.
Maybe you'll seek wise counsel.
Or maybe you'll study a passage of Scripture that speaks to a responsibility you're facing.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHEN YOUR PLANS CHANGE Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The fire is burning.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied today.
Now, I want to ask you something. Can you remember a time when your plans changed unexpectedly?
Maybe it was a major life event.
Maybe it was a relationship.
Maybe it was a career decision.
Or maybe it was something that seemed small at the time. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What did that experience teach you about your need for wisdom and support?
Maybe you learned to slow down.
Maybe you learned to ask questions.
Maybe you learned to seek advice.
Or maybe you learned that you didn't have to handle everything alone. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. We can't always control the circumstances that come into our lives.
But we can seek wisdom in how we respond.
We can pray.
We can study Scripture.
We can ask for help.
And we can take responsible steps forward.
CLOSING REFLECTION — A FAITHFUL YES Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
When we think about the Christmas story, we often picture Mary holding baby Jesus.
We think about the manger.
The shepherds.
And the angels.
But before Jesus was born, there was an extraordinary announcement.
And Mary responded with humility.
"Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word."
Now, I want you to remember something. Mary's response wasn't based on knowing every detail of the future.
It was a response to God's revealed message.
And her story reminds us of the importance of faith.
Humility.
And obedience.
Now, maybe you're facing uncertainty today.
Maybe your plans have changed.
Maybe you're trying to make a difficult decision.
Or maybe you're simply unsure what comes next.
Now, I can't promise that every circumstance will unfold the way you hope.
And I can't tell you that every unexpected change is part of a specific plan God has revealed to you.
But I can encourage you to seek His wisdom.
Study His Word.
Pray honestly.
And take the next responsible step.
Because faithful living isn't about having every answer.
It's about responding to the truth God has given us.
And above all, remembering the Savior at the center of the Christmas story.
Jesus Christ.
The promised Messiah.
The Son of God.
And the greatest gift of all.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for allowing us to study Mary's response to Your message. Lord, help us learn from her humility and faith. Teach us to seek Your wisdom. Help us ask sincere questions. And give us discernment when we face unexpected circumstances. Father, You know every person listening. You know the decisions they're facing. The responsibilities they're carrying. And the uncertainty they may be experiencing. Lord, give them wisdom. Help them find trustworthy guidance. And encourage them to take faithful, responsible steps forward. Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ. Thank You for His birth. His sinless life. His sacrifice on the cross. And His resurrection. Thank You for the hope of salvation through Him. May this Christmas season draw us closer to our Savior. And may our lives reflect Your grace and love. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY FOUR Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Ten, Day Three!
And I hope today's lesson has encouraged you to remember that faith doesn't require knowing every detail of the future.
We can seek God's wisdom.
Trust His revealed Word.
And respond faithfully.
Tomorrow, we're continuing our Christmas study. And our next lesson is called... Joseph's Faith — Choosing Obedience When the Road Is Difficult.
We'll explore Joseph's response to the angel's message, the importance of compassion, and what we can learn about faithful responsibility.
Until then, remember... You don't have to have every answer to take the next faithful step.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Joseph's Faith: Choosing Obedience When the Road Is Difficult
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — THE QUIET FAITH OF JOSEPH Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today.
Today is Week Ten, Day Four. And we're continuing our Christmas study called... The Greatest Gift — Preparing Our Hearts for Christmas.
Yesterday, we spent time studying Mary's response to the angel Gabriel. We talked about her humility. Her questions. And her willingness to respond to God's extraordinary announcement.
But today, we're going to look at another person whose life was deeply affected by the coming of Jesus Christ.
A man named Joseph.
Now, when we think about the Christmas story, we often picture Mary holding baby Jesus. We think about the manger. The shepherds. And the angels.
And Joseph is usually there, standing nearby.
But have you ever stopped to think about what Joseph experienced?
Imagine preparing to begin your married life. You have responsibilities. You have expectations. And you have a future you're planning.
Then suddenly, you discover something you don't understand.
Something that changes everything.
Now, Joseph found himself in a situation that required serious consideration. And Matthew tells us that he was a just man.
He didn't want to expose Mary to public disgrace.
And while he was considering what to do, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream.
Joseph received a specific message concerning Mary and the child she was carrying.
And he responded with obedience.
Now, here's something I want us to think about today. Sometimes faithfulness isn't dramatic.
Sometimes it isn't recognized publicly.
Sometimes it looks like doing the right thing when nobody is applauding.
Sometimes it looks like compassion.
Sometimes it looks like taking responsibility.
And sometimes it looks like responding faithfully when the road ahead is difficult.
Now, Joseph's experience was unique. He received direct revelation from God concerning the birth of Jesus Christ.
We shouldn't assume that every dream or unexpected circumstance in our own lives carries the same authority.
But we can learn from Joseph's character. His compassion. His thoughtful response. And his obedience to God's revealed message.
Our lesson today is called... Joseph's Faith — Choosing Obedience When the Road Is Difficult.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the opportunity to continue studying the Christmas story. Lord, today we're looking at Joseph's response to the extraordinary circumstances surrounding the birth of Jesus Christ. Help us understand what Scripture teaches about his character. Teach us to respond with compassion. Give us wisdom when we face difficult decisions. Help us take our responsibilities seriously. And help us remain faithful to Your revealed Word. Father, may today's lesson encourage those who are carrying burdens or facing uncertainty. And may everything we study draw us closer to Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — MATTHEW 1:18–25 Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 1. We're going to read verses 18 through 25.
Before we begin, let's understand the setting. Mary and Joseph were betrothed.
In their culture, betrothal was a serious and legally binding commitment.
But before they came together as husband and wife, Mary was found to be pregnant.
Now, Matthew tells us that the child was conceived by the Holy Spirit.
But Joseph was facing a situation he needed to understand.
Let's read Matthew chapter 1, verses 18 through 25, from the King James Version. "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily. But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
Now, I want you to notice something. Matthew tells us that Joseph was a just man.
He considered his situation.
He received a specific message from the angel.
And then he acted.
Now, let's look more closely at what we can learn from this passage.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Faithfulness is often demonstrated through compassion, wise decisions, and responsible obedience to God's revealed Word—even when the road ahead is difficult.
Now, I want you to remember that. Because sometimes we think faith has to be something extraordinary.
Something dramatic.
Something everyone can see.
But faithful living often involves ordinary decisions.
How we treat people.
How we respond to difficult circumstances.
How we carry our responsibilities.
And whether we seek to live according to God's Word.
JOSEPH WAS A JUST MAN Now, let's go back to Matthew chapter 1, verse 19. The King James Version says: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
Now, I want you to notice two things. Matthew describes Joseph as just.
And he tells us Joseph didn't want to make Mary a public example.
Now, Joseph was facing a serious situation.
And in the circumstances as he understood them, he was considering ending the betrothal privately.
But Matthew also draws attention to his concern about Mary's public humiliation.
Now, that's meaningful.
Because sometimes when people feel hurt, confused, or disappointed, their first reaction is to expose someone else.
They want everyone to know what happened.
They want other people to take sides.
Or they want to respond immediately.
But Joseph's example invites us to think carefully about how we treat others during difficult situations.
Now, here's something important. Compassion doesn't mean ignoring wrongdoing.
And it doesn't mean hiding abuse or refusing to seek appropriate help.
But it does mean recognizing that people deserve to be treated with dignity.
Even when circumstances are complicated.
Now, I want you to ask yourself something. When I'm disappointed or confused, do I respond with care?
Or do I allow my emotions to determine how I treat other people?
JOSEPH TOOK TIME TO CONSIDER Now, let's look at verse 20. Matthew says: "But while he thought on these things..."
Now, I want you to focus on that phrase. While he thought on these things.
Joseph was considering what to do.
And I think that's an important detail.
Because sometimes we rush into decisions when our emotions are strong.
We respond before we have enough information.
We make assumptions.
Or we act out of frustration.
Now, Joseph's situation was unique, and we shouldn't turn every detail into a universal rule.
But we can still recognize the value of thoughtful decision-making.
Sometimes the wisest thing we can do is slow down.
Gather information.
Consider the consequences.
Seek counsel when appropriate.
And pray for wisdom.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Not every difficult decision needs an immediate reaction. Sometimes wisdom begins by taking time to consider what is true and what is right.
THE ANGEL'S MESSAGE — FEAR NOT Now, let's continue in Matthew chapter 1.
The angel says: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife..."
Now, notice something. The angel addresses Joseph as a son of David.
And that connects Joseph with the royal family line described earlier in Matthew's genealogy.
Now, remember what we've studied throughout this Christmas series.
The Old Testament contains promises concerning David's throne.
And the coming of Jesus Christ is connected with those promises.
So this message isn't simply about Joseph's personal situation.
It's part of God's larger redemptive plan.
Now, the angel also tells Joseph not to fear taking Mary as his wife.
And then explains that the child was conceived by the Holy Spirit.
Now, that's an extraordinary revelation.
And it provides Joseph with information he could not have discovered through ordinary means.
Now, here's something important. Joseph received a specific message concerning the birth of Jesus Christ.
We shouldn't assume that every dream we experience is a message from God.
And we shouldn't make serious decisions based solely on dreams or impressions.
But we can learn from Joseph's willingness to respond faithfully to what God had clearly revealed to him.
THE NAME ABOVE EVERY NAME Now, let's look at Matthew chapter 1, verse 21. The angel says: "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins."
Now, I want you to hear that final phrase again. "For he shall save his people from their sins."
Now, that's the heart of the Christmas story.
Jesus came to save.
Not simply to inspire people.
Not merely to demonstrate kindness.
And not only to provide a good example.
He came to accomplish salvation.
Now, I want you to think about something. Joseph was being called to take Mary as his wife and to name the child Jesus.
But the child at the center of this story is no ordinary child.
He is the promised Savior.
The eternal Son of God who became flesh.
And through Him, we have the hope of forgiveness and eternal life.
Now, that's why the Christmas story matters.
EMMANUEL — GOD WITH US Now, let's continue with Matthew chapter 1, verses 22 and 23.
Matthew connects the birth of Jesus with Isaiah's prophecy.
And he explains the name Emmanuel.
God with us.
Now, I want you to think about those words. God with us.
Not simply a distant idea.
Not merely a religious tradition.
But the eternal Son of God entering human history.
Now, here's something important. Jesus didn't cease to be God when He became human.
And He didn't merely appear to be human.
Christian teaching recognizes Him as truly God and truly man.
And through His coming, God's saving purposes are revealed.
Now, that's the greatest gift of Christmas.
JOSEPH OBEYED Now, let's look at verse 24. The King James Version says: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"
Now, I want you to notice the simplicity of that statement.
Joseph did what he had been instructed to do.
Now, Matthew doesn't record a long speech from Joseph.
He doesn't describe Joseph making a public announcement.
And he doesn't tell us that Joseph sought recognition for his decision.
He simply tells us that Joseph acted.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. Sometimes we spend a lot of time talking about what we believe.
But our actions matter, too.
The way we treat people.
The responsibilities we fulfill.
The choices we make.
And the way we respond to God's Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithfulness isn't measured by how loudly we talk about our faith. It's also reflected in how we live.
LUKE 2 — THE JOURNEY TO BETHLEHEM Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 2.
We're going to read verses 1 through 7.
This passage describes the circumstances surrounding the birth of Jesus.
Let's read from the King James Version. "And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed. (And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.) And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn."
Now, I want you to think about this journey.
Joseph and Mary traveled to Bethlehem.
And while they were there, Jesus was born.
Now, Scripture doesn't give us every detail of their journey.
It doesn't tell us exactly how they traveled.
Or describe every challenge they encountered along the way.
But it does tell us that Jesus was born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger.
Now, that's a humble beginning.
And it's a reminder that the coming of the Savior didn't take place in the kind of setting the world might associate with royal power.
The promised King entered the world in humble circumstances.
And Joseph was part of the household into which Jesus was born.
RESPONSIBILITY WHEN LIFE IS DIFFICULT Now, let's talk about responsibility.
Because one of the things we can recognize in Joseph's story is his willingness to fulfill the role before him.
He took Mary as his wife.
He named the child Jesus.
And later, Matthew describes him taking action to protect the family.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes responsibility is difficult.
Sometimes it requires sacrifice.
Sometimes it involves decisions we didn't expect to make.
And sometimes it means doing something important without receiving recognition.
Now, here's something important. Taking responsibility doesn't mean carrying every burden alone.
And it doesn't mean ignoring our own limitations.
We can seek help.
We can ask for guidance.
And we can recognize when a situation requires professional assistance.
But we can also take seriously the responsibilities God has entrusted to us.
MATTHEW 2 — PROTECTING THE FAMILY Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 2.
We're going to read verses 13 through 15.
At this point in Matthew's account, the wise men have visited Jesus.
And the family faces danger because of Herod's intentions.
Let's read. "And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt: And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son."
Now, I want you to notice something. Joseph took action.
He didn't remain in a dangerous situation.
He took Mary and Jesus to Egypt.
And they remained there until the danger from Herod had passed.
Now, here's something important. This was a specific warning given to Joseph in the biblical account.
We shouldn't assume that our dreams function the same way.
But we can recognize the importance of protecting those in our care.
And we can learn that faithfulness doesn't mean remaining in danger when protective action is needed.
Sometimes responsibility requires making difficult decisions for the safety and well-being of others.
THE RETURN FROM EGYPT Now, let's continue in Matthew chapter 2.
We're going to read verses 19 through 23.
The King James Version says: "But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, Saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young child's life. And he arose, and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee: And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene."
Now, I want you to notice something. Joseph's responsibilities didn't end when Jesus was born.
He continued caring for the family.
And Matthew describes several decisions connected to their safety and where they would live.
Now, sometimes we think obedience is one dramatic moment.
One decision.
One act of courage.
But faithful living often continues over time.
It involves repeated choices.
Daily responsibilities.
And ongoing care.
Now, that's something we can learn from Joseph's example.
PAUSE AND PRAY — FAITHFUL IN THE DIFFICULT MOMENTS Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about a responsibility you're carrying right now.
Maybe it's caring for a family member.
Maybe it's making a difficult decision.
Maybe it's managing responsibilities at work.
Or maybe it's trying to respond wisely to an unexpected situation.
Now, take a moment to bring that responsibility before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word. Thank You for the example of Joseph's faithfulness. Lord, help us respond to difficult situations with wisdom and compassion. Give us patience when we need to consider our choices. Help us treat others with dignity. And teach us to take our responsibilities seriously. Father, when we're overwhelmed, help us recognize when we need support. When we're uncertain, give us wisdom. And when we face difficult decisions, help us seek truth and respond faithfully. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
PROVERBS 3 — TRUSTING GOD Now, let's turn to Proverbs chapter 3. We're going to read verses 5 and 6. The King James Version says: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart..."
Now, trusting God doesn't mean refusing to think carefully.
It doesn't mean ignoring facts.
And it doesn't mean making decisions without considering consequences.
Instead, it means recognizing that our understanding is limited.
We seek God's wisdom.
We study His Word.
We pray.
And we make thoughtful decisions.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Trusting God and acting responsibly are not opposites. Faith can shape the way we make careful, compassionate decisions.
JAMES 1 — WISDOM FOR THE ROAD Now, let's turn to James chapter 1. We're going to read verse 5. The King James Version says: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him."
Now, sometimes we pray for our circumstances to change.
And it's okay to bring those desires before God.
But we can also pray for wisdom.
Wisdom to make decisions.
Wisdom to recognize our responsibilities.
Wisdom to know when to seek help.
And wisdom to treat people well.
Now, that's a prayer we can continue praying throughout our lives.
PHILIPPIANS 2 — HUMILITY IN ACTION Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 2. We're going to read verses 3 through 8. The King James Version says: "Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross."
Now, I want you to notice something. Paul points believers toward the humility of Jesus Christ.
And he encourages them to consider the needs of others.
Now, that connects beautifully with what we've been studying.
Joseph's actions demonstrate concern for Mary and Jesus.
But Jesus Himself is the ultimate example of humility and obedience.
He came into the world.
He took the form of a servant.
And He became obedient unto death on the cross.
Now, that's the heart of the gospel.
And it's the reason the Christmas story matters so much.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... How do I usually respond when I'm faced with a difficult decision?
Do I react immediately?
Do I become overwhelmed?
Or do I take time to consider my options? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... What can Joseph's example teach me about compassion?
Think about how he considered Mary's dignity. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What responsibility in my life requires wisdom and faithful attention right now?
Maybe it's a family responsibility.
A relationship.
A decision.
Or a commitment. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I demonstrate faith through my actions this week?
Maybe it's showing kindness.
Following through on a responsibility.
Seeking wise counsel.
Or helping someone who needs support. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE SAVIOR AT THE CENTER Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because Joseph's story is ultimately part of the story of Christ's coming.
Joseph was instructed to name the child Jesus.
And the angel explained why.
"For he shall save his people from their sins."
Now, that's the heart of the Christmas message.
Jesus Christ is the eternal Son of God who became flesh.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation through perfect responsibility.
We don't earn it by never making mistakes.
And we don't earn it by being admired for our faithfulness.
Salvation is God's gift of grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our obedience is a response to His grace.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. Joseph's faith wasn't recorded through impressive speeches, but through thoughtful, compassionate actions. Faithfulness often grows through the quiet decisions we make when nobody is watching.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we think our faith only matters when we're doing something extraordinary.
But the ordinary choices matter, too.
How we treat people.
How we carry our responsibilities.
And how we respond to God's Word.
LIVING IT OUT — FAITHFUL IN THE QUIET MOMENTS Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... Faithful in the Quiet Moments.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... One responsibility you want to approach more faithfully.
Second... One relationship where you can demonstrate greater compassion.
Third... One decision where you need wisdom.
And fourth... One practical action you can take this week.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom.
Ask Him to help you respond with compassion.
And seek to live faithfully in the responsibilities before you.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, one responsibility I need to approach with greater faithfulness is...
Our second prompt is... One person I can treat with greater compassion is...
And our third prompt is... Help me demonstrate my faith through my actions by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek God's wisdom, treat others with compassion, and demonstrate my faith through responsible, faithful actions.
Now, say that again. I will seek God's wisdom, treat others with compassion, and demonstrate my faith through responsible, faithful actions.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Matthew chapter 1, verse 24. "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about what Joseph's actions teach us about faithfulness.
Maybe you'll take time to make a thoughtful decision.
Maybe you'll follow through on a responsibility.
Or maybe you'll show compassion to someone who's facing a difficult situation.
AROUND THE FIRE — THE FAITH NOBODY SEES Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The fire is burning.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied today.
Now, I want to ask you something. Can you think of someone whose faithfulness has encouraged you, even though they rarely receive recognition?
Maybe it's a parent.
A caregiver.
A church volunteer.
A friend.
Or someone who quietly serves others. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What does quiet faithfulness look like in your own life?
Maybe it's caring for someone.
Keeping a commitment.
Being honest.
Or choosing compassion when you're disappointed. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something I want you to remember. Not every act of faithfulness will receive public recognition.
And that's okay.
Because our purpose isn't simply to impress other people.
It's to live in a way that honors God.
CLOSING REFLECTION — WHEN OBEDIENCE ISN'T EASY Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Joseph's story reminds us that faithfulness isn't always easy.
Sometimes circumstances are confusing.
Sometimes decisions are difficult.
And sometimes responsibilities require courage.
But Joseph's actions demonstrate compassion and obedience.
He considered Mary's dignity.
He responded to the message he received.
And he took action to care for the family.
Now, I want you to think about something. Maybe you're facing a difficult decision today.
Maybe you're carrying responsibilities that feel overwhelming.
Maybe you're trying to respond wisely to an unexpected circumstance.
Or maybe you're simply tired.
Now, I can't promise that every situation will become easy.
And I can't promise that every decision will have a simple answer.
But I can encourage you to seek God's wisdom.
Study His Word.
Treat people with compassion.
And take responsible steps forward.
Because sometimes faithfulness isn't loud.
Sometimes it isn't dramatic.
Sometimes it looks like doing the right thing quietly.
And remembering the Savior at the center of the Christmas story.
Jesus Christ.
The promised Messiah.
The One who came to save His people from their sins.
And the greatest gift of all.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for allowing us to study Joseph's example. Lord, help us learn from his compassion. His thoughtful response. And his obedience to Your revealed message. Father, give us wisdom when we face difficult decisions. Help us treat others with dignity. Teach us to take our responsibilities seriously. And remind us that we can seek support when we need it. Lord, I pray for the person who's carrying a heavy responsibility. Give them wisdom and encouragement. I pray for the person who's facing a difficult decision. Help them seek truth and trustworthy guidance. And I pray for the person who feels unnoticed. Remind them that their faithful actions can be meaningful, even when they receive no public recognition. Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ. Thank You for His birth. His sinless life. His sacrifice on the cross. And His resurrection. Thank You for the hope of salvation through Him. May this Christmas season draw us closer to our Savior. And may our lives reflect His love. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY FIVE Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Ten, Day Four!
And I hope today's lesson has reminded you that faithfulness isn't always loud or dramatic.
Sometimes it looks like compassion.
Sometimes it looks like responsibility.
And sometimes it looks like making a difficult but faithful decision.
Tomorrow, we're continuing our Christmas study. And our next lesson is called... Making Room for Jesus — When Life Becomes Too Busy for What Matters Most.
We'll explore the circumstances surrounding Jesus' birth and reflect on how we can make room for worship, Scripture, and prayer during a busy Christmas season.
Until then, remember... Your quiet faithfulness matters.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Making Room for Jesus: When Life Becomes Too Busy for What Matters Most
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WHEN CHRISTMAS BECOMES TOO BUSY Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today.
Today is Week Ten, Day Five. And we're continuing our Christmas study called... The Greatest Gift — Preparing Our Hearts for Christmas.
Yesterday, we studied Joseph's faith. We talked about compassion. Responsibility. And the quiet decisions that demonstrate faithful obedience.
But today, I want to talk about something that I believe many of us can relate to.
Being busy.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever reached the end of a day and wondered where all the time went?
You woke up with a list of things you needed to accomplish.
You started checking things off.
You answered messages.
You handled responsibilities.
And before you knew it, the day was over.
Now, during the Christmas season, that feeling can become even more familiar.
There are decorations to put up.
Presents to purchase.
Meals to prepare.
Family gatherings to organize.
Church activities.
Work responsibilities.
And all the ordinary things that don't stop simply because Christmas is approaching.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we become so focused on preparing for Christmas that we forget to prepare our hearts.
We make room in our schedules for shopping.
We make room in our homes for decorations.
We make room in our budgets for gifts.
But do we intentionally make room for prayer?
For Scripture?
For worship?
And for remembering why Jesus came?
Now, I don't want today's lesson to become another source of pressure.
Because many people are already carrying heavy responsibilities.
And spending time with God isn't about adding another exhausting task to an already overwhelming schedule.
It's about remembering what matters most.
And learning to seek Christ in the middle of everyday life.
Our lesson today is called... Making Room for Jesus — When Life Becomes Too Busy for What Matters Most.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the opportunity to continue studying the coming of Jesus Christ. Lord, You know how busy our lives can become. You know the responsibilities we carry. The demands on our time. And the things competing for our attention. Father, help us remember what matters most. Teach us to seek You in the middle of ordinary life. Help us approach this Christmas season with gratitude. And remind us that our relationship with You is more important than creating a perfect celebration. Lord, may today's study encourage us to slow down where we can. To seek Your wisdom. And to make meaningful time for Scripture, prayer, and worship. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — LUKE 2:1–7 Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 2.
We're going to read verses 1 through 7.
This is one of the most familiar passages in the Christmas story.
But today, I want us to read it carefully.
Because sometimes we become so familiar with a passage that we overlook what it actually says.
Let's read Luke chapter 2, verses 1 through 7, from the King James Version. "And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed. (And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.) And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn."
Now, I want you to focus on that final phrase. "Because there was no room for them in the inn."
Now, that's a familiar part of the Christmas story.
But I want us to be careful with what we assume.
Luke tells us there was no room for them in the lodging place.
He doesn't tell us that an innkeeper deliberately rejected Jesus.
And he doesn't tell us that people were too busy to recognize the Savior.
Those details sometimes appear in Christmas plays and retellings, but they aren't stated in the passage.
Now, the Greek word translated "inn" can refer to a guest room or lodging space.
And scholars discuss the precise setting of Jesus' birth.
But what Luke clearly tells us is that Mary laid Jesus in a manger because suitable lodging space was unavailable.
Now, here's something important. Today's lesson about making room for Jesus is a personal application.
It's not a claim that Luke was condemning an innkeeper for having a busy schedule.
But the passage can still invite us to reflect on the humility of Christ's birth.
And on the place we give Him in our own lives.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Making room for Jesus isn't about creating a perfect schedule. It's about intentionally seeking Him through Scripture, prayer, worship, and faithful living.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we think spending time with God has to look a certain way.
We imagine a perfectly quiet house.
A beautifully arranged Bible study space.
A cup of coffee.
And an entire hour without interruptions.
Now, those moments can be wonderful.
But not everyone has that kind of schedule.
Some people are raising young children.
Some are caring for aging parents.
Some work long hours.
And some are managing difficult circumstances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Your relationship with God isn't measured by how impressive your devotional routine looks.
We can seek Him faithfully in the circumstances of everyday life.
THE HUMILITY OF THE MANGER Now, let's return to Luke chapter 2.
Mary gave birth to Jesus.
She wrapped Him in swaddling clothes.
And she laid Him in a manger.
Now, a manger is a feeding trough for animals.
And that detail highlights the humble circumstances of Jesus' birth.
Now, think about that. The eternal Son of God entered human history.
And His birth was marked by humility rather than royal luxury.
Now, when we think about kings, we often imagine palaces.
We imagine wealth.
Power.
And public recognition.
But the Christmas story presents a very different picture.
Jesus was born in humble circumstances.
And that reminds us that God's saving purposes don't depend on worldly appearances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The significance of Jesus' birth wasn't found in the luxury of His surroundings. It was found in who He is.
The promised Savior.
The Son of God.
The greatest gift of all.
JOHN 1 — THE WORD DWELT AMONG US Now, let's turn to John chapter 1.
We're going to read verse 14. The King James Version says: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us."
Now, that's the miracle of the incarnation.
The eternal Son of God became truly human.
He entered our world.
He lived among people.
And through Him, God's grace and truth were revealed.
Now, that's the heart of Christmas.
Not simply a holiday tradition.
Not merely a celebration.
But the coming of Jesus Christ.
And when we remember that, it helps us keep the season in perspective.
WHEN GOOD THINGS BECOME TOO MUCH Now, let's talk about something important.
Because sometimes the things filling our schedules aren't bad things.
They're good things.
Family gatherings.
Church activities.
Helping other people.
Preparing meals.
And spending time with those we love.
Now, those can all be meaningful.
But even good things can become overwhelming when we try to do everything.
Sometimes we say yes to every invitation.
We volunteer for every responsibility.
And we place pressure on ourselves to make every moment special.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to create a perfect Christmas to honor Jesus.
You don't have to attend every event.
You don't have to purchase expensive gifts.
And you don't have to exhaust yourself trying to meet every expectation.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithfulness doesn't require doing everything. It involves seeking God's wisdom about what matters most.
LUKE 10 — MARY AND MARTHA Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 10.
We're going to read verses 38 through 42.
Now, this passage takes place during Jesus' ministry.
And the Mary in this account is Mary of Bethany, not Mary the mother of Jesus.
Let's read. "Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house. And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word. But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me. And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her."
Now, I want you to think about this scene.
Martha welcomed Jesus into her home.
She was busy serving.
And Mary was sitting at Jesus' feet, listening to His teaching.
Now, Martha became frustrated.
She felt that Mary should be helping her.
And she brought her concern to Jesus.
But Jesus responded by pointing Martha toward what was most important.
Now, here's something I want us to understand. Jesus wasn't teaching that hospitality is wrong.
And He wasn't saying that serving others doesn't matter.
In fact, Scripture repeatedly encourages hospitality and service.
But in this moment, Martha had become distracted and troubled by many things.
And Mary had chosen to listen to Jesus.
Now, that's the lesson.
Sometimes we become so occupied with doing things that we neglect the importance of listening to God's Word.
BUSY FOR JESUS, BUT NOT SPENDING TIME WITH JESUS Now, I want to talk about something that can happen in Christian life.
Sometimes we become very busy doing things connected to our faith.
We volunteer.
We organize events.
We prepare lessons.
We help with church activities.
And we serve other people.
Now, those are meaningful responsibilities.
But sometimes we can become so busy with those responsibilities that we neglect our own spiritual growth.
We spend time preparing something for others.
But we don't spend time personally reflecting on Scripture.
We become focused on completing tasks.
But we forget to pray.
Now, I want you to hear something. Serving God and spending time with God aren't supposed to compete with each other.
They belong together.
Our service should grow out of our relationship with Jesus Christ.
And our relationship with Him should shape the way we serve.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Don't become so busy doing things associated with your faith that you forget to nurture your relationship with Christ.
MATTHEW 6 — SEEK FIRST THE KINGDOM Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 6.
We're going to read verse 33. The King James Version says: "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you."
Now, let's understand the context.
Jesus is teaching about anxiety concerning daily needs.
Food.
Drink.
And clothing.
He reminds His listeners of their heavenly Father's care.
And He calls them to seek God's kingdom and righteousness.
Now, here's something important. This verse isn't a guarantee that Christians will always have financial abundance.
And it doesn't mean we should ignore practical responsibilities.
But it does call us to make God's kingdom central in our lives.
Now, during Christmas, that can be a meaningful reminder.
We can celebrate.
We can enjoy traditions.
And we can spend time with family.
But we can also intentionally remember Jesus Christ.
And seek to honor Him in the way we live.
THE PRESSURE OF A PERFECT CHRISTMAS Now, let's talk about something I think many people experience.
The pressure to create a perfect Christmas.
Sometimes we see beautiful pictures online.
Perfectly decorated homes.
Elaborate meals.
Expensive gifts.
And families who appear to have everything together.
Now, those images can be enjoyable.
But they can also create unrealistic expectations.
We start comparing our homes.
Our budgets.
Our traditions.
And our circumstances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Christmas isn't a competition.
And your worth isn't measured by how much money you spend.
Or how many decorations you put up.
Or how impressive your celebrations look.
The meaning of Christmas is rooted in Jesus Christ.
And that meaning remains the same whether your celebration is elaborate or simple.
WHEN CHRISTMAS LOOKS DIFFERENT Now, I want to speak to someone who may be facing a difficult Christmas season.
Maybe this year looks different from previous years.
Maybe someone you love is no longer here.
Maybe finances are tight.
Maybe you're dealing with illness.
Or maybe family circumstances have changed.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to pretend that everything is wonderful.
And you don't have to force yourself to feel cheerful.
It's okay to acknowledge grief.
It's okay to recognize disappointment.
And it's okay to simplify your celebrations.
Now, here's something important. Making room for Jesus doesn't require denying your emotions.
You can bring your grief before Him.
You can pray honestly.
You can seek support.
And you can remember the hope of the gospel even when the season feels difficult.
PSALM 46 — BE STILL Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 46.
We're going to read verse 10. The King James Version says: "Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth."
Now, this psalm speaks about God's power and His rule over the nations.
And verse 10 calls attention to His sovereignty.
Now, sometimes we use the words "be still" as a reminder to slow down.
And while that's a helpful personal application, we should remember the verse's larger context.
It's a declaration of God's authority.
Now, that truth can encourage us when life feels overwhelming.
Because we're reminded that God is not dependent on our ability to control everything.
We can pause.
We can pray.
And we can remember who He is.
PAUSE AND PRAY — LORD, HELP ME SLOW DOWN Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about your schedule.
The responsibilities you're carrying.
The expectations you've placed on yourself.
And the things competing for your attention.
Now, ask yourself something. Is there one area where I could simplify my schedule and make more meaningful time for God? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word. Thank You for reminding us of the importance of seeking You. Lord, You know how busy our lives can become. You know the responsibilities we carry. And You know the things that compete for our attention. Father, give us wisdom to recognize what matters most. Help us simplify where we can. Teach us to make meaningful time for Scripture and prayer. And remind us that our relationship with You isn't measured by a perfect routine. Lord, help us seek You faithfully in the middle of everyday life. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
MATTHEW 11 — COME UNTO ME Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 11.
We're going to read verses 28 through 30. The King James Version says: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."
Now, I want you to hear those first words again. "Come unto me..."
Now, isn't that beautiful?
Jesus invites those who are weary and burdened to come to Him.
Now, this passage isn't a promise that following Jesus will eliminate every responsibility or hardship.
But it does point us toward the rest found in relationship with Him.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we treat our spiritual lives like another performance.
We think we need to pray perfectly.
Study perfectly.
Serve perfectly.
And never miss a day.
But our relationship with Jesus isn't built on earning His love through flawless performance.
We come to Him through faith.
And we continue growing in His grace.
Now, that's something worth remembering during a busy season.
COLOSSIANS 3 — LET THE WORD OF CHRIST DWELL IN YOU Now, let's turn to Colossians chapter 3.
We're going to read verses 15 through 17. The King James Version says: "And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him."
Now, I want you to notice something. Paul doesn't describe Christian life as something limited to one hour on Sunday.
He speaks about the Word of Christ dwelling richly in believers.
About gratitude.
About worship.
And about honoring Jesus in whatever we do.
Now, that's a beautiful reminder.
Because making room for Jesus isn't only about setting aside a particular time.
It's also about allowing our relationship with Him to shape our everyday lives.
How we speak.
How we treat people.
How we respond to responsibilities.
And how we express gratitude.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Making room for Jesus means more than finding time on the calendar. It means allowing His Word to shape the way we live.
SMALL MOMENTS THAT MATTER Now, let's talk about something practical.
Because not everyone can set aside an entire hour every morning.
And I don't want anyone to feel discouraged because their schedule looks different.
Sometimes meaningful time in God's Word happens in small moments.
Maybe you read a Psalm before beginning your day.
Maybe you listen to Scripture while preparing breakfast.
Maybe you spend a few minutes praying during your lunch break.
Or maybe you reflect on a Bible passage before going to bed.
Now, those moments don't have to be elaborate.
And they don't have to look exactly like someone else's routine.
The goal isn't to impress anyone.
The goal is to continue growing in your relationship with Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something important. Spiritual growth isn't a competition.
And we shouldn't compare our devotional habits with someone else's.
We can seek meaningful, sustainable ways to spend time in God's Word.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What usually receives most of my attention during the Christmas season?
Maybe it's shopping.
Decorating.
Family gatherings.
Or work responsibilities. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Is there something I've been placing unnecessary pressure on myself to accomplish?
Maybe it's creating a perfect celebration.
Meeting everyone's expectations.
Or saying yes to too many commitments. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What is one realistic way I can make meaningful time for Scripture and prayer?
Maybe it's five minutes in the morning.
A short prayer during the day.
Or reading a Bible passage with your family. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I keep Jesus Christ at the center of my Christmas celebrations?
Maybe it's reading the Christmas story.
Attending a worship service.
Helping someone in need.
Or expressing gratitude for God's gift of salvation. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE SAVIOR WHO CAME NEAR Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because He's the center of the Christmas story.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He entered human history.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation by having a perfect devotional routine.
We don't earn it by attending every church event.
And we don't earn it by creating an impressive Christmas celebration.
Salvation is God's gracious gift through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our worship, prayer, and obedience grow out of that relationship.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. You don't have to create a perfect Christmas to honor Jesus. Make meaningful room for His Word, His truth, and His love in the life you're actually living.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because sometimes we become so focused on doing everything that we forget what matters most.
Our relationship with Jesus Christ.
LIVING IT OUT — MAKING ROOM FOR JESUS Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... Making Room for Jesus.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... One activity or commitment that has been taking more time than you expected.
Second... One thing you could simplify or postpone.
Third... One realistic way you can spend meaningful time in Scripture or prayer.
And fourth... One way you can reflect Christ's love in your everyday responsibilities.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom.
Ask Him to help you recognize what matters most.
And seek to honor Him in the way you use your time.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, one thing that has been competing for my attention is...
Our second prompt is... One way I can simplify my schedule and make meaningful time for You is...
And our third prompt is... Help me keep Jesus at the center of this Christmas season by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek Jesus Christ in the middle of everyday life, make meaningful time for His Word, and remember that my faith isn't measured by a perfect schedule.
Now, say that again. I will seek Jesus Christ in the middle of everyday life, make meaningful time for His Word, and remember that my faith isn't measured by a perfect schedule.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Matthew chapter 6, verse 33. "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about one meaningful way you can keep Christ at the center of your life.
Maybe you'll spend time reading Scripture.
Maybe you'll simplify part of your schedule.
Or maybe you'll intentionally pause to pray.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHAT REALLY MATTERS? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
