LIVING IT OUT — RECOGNIZING JOY IN CHRIST Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... Recognizing Joy in Christ.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... One truth about Jesus Christ that gives you a reason for joy.
Second... One blessing or meaningful experience you're grateful for today.
Third... One difficult circumstance you want to bring honestly before God.
And fourth... One way you can share kindness or encouragement with someone else.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Thank God for the gift of Jesus Christ.
Bring your concerns before Him.
And ask for opportunities to reflect His love.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the good news of Jesus Christ gives me joy because...
Our second prompt is... One area where I'm struggling to experience joy is...
And our third prompt is... Help me remember Your goodness and share Your love by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. My joy is rooted in Jesus Christ. Even when life is difficult, I can remember God's goodness and the salvation I have through my Savior.
Now, say that again. My joy is rooted in Jesus Christ. Even when life is difficult, I can remember God's goodness and the salvation I have through my Savior.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Luke chapter 2, verses 10 and 11. "And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about why the coming of Jesus Christ is such good news.
Maybe you'll spend time thanking God for the Savior.
Maybe you'll read Luke chapter 2 again.
Or maybe you'll encourage someone who's struggling.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHERE DOES YOUR JOY COME FROM? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The fire is burning.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied today.
Now, I want to ask you something. What does the joy of the Lord mean to you personally?
Maybe it reminds you of God's faithfulness.
Maybe it reminds you of the salvation you have through Jesus Christ.
Or maybe it reminds you that your circumstances don't determine the truth of the gospel. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. How can you celebrate the coming of Jesus Christ while still being honest about the difficulties you're facing?
Maybe it's through prayer.
Maybe it's through worship.
Maybe it's through gratitude.
Or maybe it's through receiving support from people who care about you. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. Christian joy doesn't require denying sorrow.
And it doesn't require pretending that life is perfect.
It's rooted in the goodness of God.
And the salvation we have through Jesus Christ.
CLOSING REFLECTION — GREAT JOY FOR ALL PEOPLE Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Imagine those shepherds in the fields.
An ordinary night.
An ordinary responsibility.
And suddenly, an extraordinary announcement.
"Fear not..."
"I bring you good tidings of great joy..."
Now, that joy wasn't based on the shepherds' circumstances becoming perfect.
It was based on the coming of Jesus Christ.
The promised Savior.
The One who would die for our sins.
And rise again.
Now, that's the foundation of Christian joy.
So if you're celebrating today...
Give thanks to God.
If you're grieving...
Bring your sorrow before Him.
If you're facing uncertainty...
Seek His wisdom.
And if you're struggling to feel joyful...
Remember that you don't have to pretend everything is wonderful.
You can continue seeking Jesus Christ.
Because the greatest reason for joy isn't found in perfect circumstances.
It's found in the Savior.
Jesus Christ.
The greatest gift of all.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for the good tidings of great joy announced at the birth of Jesus Christ. Thank You for sending the promised Savior into the world. Lord, help us understand that Christian joy is rooted in You. Not in perfect circumstances. Not in expensive celebrations. And not in the absence of hardship. Father, I pray for those who are grieving. Surround them with comfort and care. I pray for those who are facing uncertainty. Give them wisdom. I pray for those who are struggling emotionally. Help them find encouragement and meaningful support. And I pray for those who are celebrating wonderful blessings. Help them remember to give You thanks. Lord, teach us to rejoice in the salvation we have through Jesus Christ. Help us show compassion to others. And may our lives reflect the goodness of our Savior. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY FIVE Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Eleven, Day Four!
And I hope today's lesson has reminded you that Christian joy isn't dependent on everything in life being perfect.
It's rooted in the goodness of God and the salvation we have through Jesus Christ.
Tomorrow, we're continuing our study of The Promise of Christmas — Hope, Peace, and Jesus. And our next lesson is called... Love Came Down — The Greatest Expression of God's Love.
We'll explore how the coming of Jesus Christ reveals God's love and why that love calls us to respond with faith, gratitude, and compassion.
Until then, remember... The joy of the Lord is your strength.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Love Came Down: The Greatest Expression of God's Love
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WHAT DOES REAL LOVE LOOK LIKE? Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today.
Today is Week Eleven, Day Five. And we're continuing our study called... The Promise of Christmas — Hope, Peace, and Jesus.
This week, we've been talking about some beautiful truths. We've talked about living hope. We've studied the peace Jesus gives. We've remembered Emmanuel, God with us. And yesterday, we talked about the joy of the Lord.
Now, today, we're going to talk about something that connects all of those things. Love.
But not just any kind of love. We're talking about the love of God.
Now, let me ask you something. When you hear the word love, what comes to mind?
Maybe you think about your family. Your spouse. Your children. Your grandchildren. Or someone who has been there for you through difficult times.
Maybe you think about a special memory. A thoughtful gift. Or someone who showed up when you needed them.
But perhaps the word love brings up something painful.
Maybe you've experienced rejection. Maybe someone you trusted hurt you. Maybe you've been disappointed by people who promised they would always be there. Or maybe you're struggling to believe that you're worthy of being loved.
Now, I want you to think about something. Human love can be beautiful. But human beings are imperfect.
We make mistakes. We disappoint one another. And sometimes we fail to demonstrate love in the ways we should.
But the love of God is different.
His love is holy. Righteous. Faithful. And revealed most clearly through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The greatest expression of God's love isn't found in a Christmas present beneath a tree. It's found in the Savior who came into the world and gave His life for our sins.
And that's what we're going to study today.
Our lesson is called... Love Came Down — The Greatest Expression of God's Love.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the gift of Jesus Christ. And thank You for the love You have demonstrated through Him. Lord, today we're studying what Your Word teaches about love. Help us understand that Your love is more than a feeling. Help us recognize the significance of Christ's coming into the world. His sinless life. His sacrifice on the cross. And His resurrection. Father, I pray for those who have experienced rejection, disappointment, or heartbreak. Help them understand the truth of Your Word. Teach us to receive Your grace through faith. And help us reflect the love of Jesus Christ in the way we treat others. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — 1 JOHN 4:7–12 Now, let's turn to 1 John chapter 4. We're going to read verses 7 through 12.
Before we begin, let's understand the setting. The apostle John is writing to believers about the importance of truth, obedience, and love.
Throughout this letter, John emphasizes that genuine Christian faith should be reflected in the way believers live.
And in chapter 4, he connects our love for one another to God's love revealed through Jesus Christ.
Let's read 1 John chapter 4, verses 7 through 12, from the King James Version. "Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God. He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love. In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another. No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us."
Now, I want you to hear verses 9 and 10 again. "In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins."
Now, that's the heart of today's lesson.
God demonstrated His love by sending His Son.
And Jesus Christ came to accomplish our salvation.
Now, here's something important. John doesn't simply tell us that God loves us.
He tells us how that love was demonstrated.
Through Jesus Christ.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH God's love is revealed through Jesus Christ. He came into the world, died for our sins, and rose again so that through faith in Him we might receive forgiveness and eternal life.
Now, I want you to hold on to that truth. Because the Christmas story isn't simply about a beautiful birth.
It's about the Savior who came to redeem sinners.
PART ONE — GOD IS LOVE Now, let's return to 1 John chapter 4.
Verse 8 says: "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love."
Now, I want you to think about those final words. "God is love."
That's a beautiful statement.
But it's important that we understand what it means.
John isn't saying that every feeling people call love automatically reflects God's character.
And he's not saying that love is the only thing Scripture teaches us about God.
The Bible also teaches that God is holy. Righteous. Just. Merciful. And faithful.
His love is consistent with His perfect character.
Now, that's important. Because sometimes people define love according to whatever feels good in the moment.
But biblical love is deeper than emotion.
It is connected to truth. Righteousness. Faithfulness. And sacrificial care.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We understand the meaning of God's love by looking at His character and the saving work of Jesus Christ.
PART TWO — LOVE TOOK THE FIRST STEP Now, let's look at verse 10.
John says: "Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us..."
Now, I want you to think about that.
God's love wasn't a response to humanity first becoming worthy.
It wasn't something we earned.
And it wasn't something we purchased through good behavior.
God demonstrated His love by sending His Son.
Now, let's turn to Romans chapter 5. We're going to read verses 6 through 8. The King James Version says: "For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly. For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die. But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."
Now, I want you to hear that last verse again. "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."
Now, that's extraordinary.
Christ died for sinners.
Not for people who had already made themselves perfect.
Not for people who had never made mistakes.
But for sinners.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God's saving love is an expression of His grace, not a reward for human perfection.
PART THREE — THE MANGER POINTS TO THE CROSS Now, let's return to the Christmas story.
When we think about Christmas, we often picture Mary holding the baby Jesus.
Joseph standing nearby.
Shepherds coming to see the child.
And angels announcing His birth.
Now, those are meaningful parts of the story.
But I want us to remember something. Jesus didn't come into the world simply to remain a baby in a manger.
He came to save.
Let's turn to Luke chapter 2. We're going to read verses 10 and 11. The King James Version says: "And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord."
Now, notice those words. "A Saviour..."
That's why His birth is such good news.
Because Jesus came to accomplish salvation.
Now, let's connect that to the cross.
Jesus lived a sinless life.
He willingly gave His life for our sins.
And He rose again.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The manger and the cross are part of the same story of God's redeeming love.
PART FOUR — FOR GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD Now, let's turn to John chapter 3. We're going to read verses 16 and 17. The King James Version says: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "For God so loved the world..."
Now, sometimes we read that verse so quickly that we forget how extraordinary it is.
God gave His Son.
And through faith in Jesus Christ, we have the promise of everlasting life.
Now, here's something important. The love of God isn't simply an invitation to feel better about ourselves.
It's connected to the saving work of Jesus Christ.
And the call to believe in Him.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The greatest gift of God's love is the salvation He provides through Jesus Christ.
PART FIVE — WHAT DOES PROPITIATION MEAN? Now, let's return to 1 John chapter 4, verse 10.
John says that God sent His Son... "To be the propitiation for our sins."
Now, that's a word we don't use very often in everyday conversation.
Propitiation.
So let's talk about what it means.
In this passage, John is describing the atoning work of Jesus Christ.
Christ's sacrifice addresses the guilt of sin and satisfies God's righteous judgment.
Now, that's important. Because sometimes people talk about God's love without talking about sin.
But Scripture connects God's love to His saving work.
Sin is serious.
And salvation is necessary.
But through Jesus Christ, God has provided the way of forgiveness and reconciliation.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The cross reveals both the seriousness of sin and the extraordinary love and grace of God.
PART SIX — LOVE IS MORE THAN A FEELING Now, let's talk about something practical.
Because we often use the word love to describe how we feel about someone.
We say we love our families.
We love our friends.
And we love the people who are important to us.
Now, those feelings can be beautiful.
But biblical love is more than emotion.
It is demonstrated through action.
Now, let's turn to 1 Corinthians chapter 13. We're going to read verses 4 through 7. The King James Version says: "Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things."
Now, I want you to think about those qualities. Patience.
Kindness.
Humility.
Truthfulness.
And perseverance.
Now, here's something important. Biblical love isn't simply saying the right words.
It's reflected in how we treat others.
How we respond to difficulties.
How we handle disagreements.
And how we demonstrate compassion.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Love becomes visible through our actions, not merely through our words.
PART SEVEN — LOVING PEOPLE WHO ARE DIFFICULT TO LOVE Now, let's talk about something that can be challenging.
Loving people who have hurt us.
Now, I want to be careful here.
Because sometimes people hear the command to love others and assume it means they must tolerate mistreatment.
But that's not what Scripture requires.
Love doesn't mean ignoring wrongdoing.
It doesn't mean refusing to establish boundaries.
And it doesn't mean remaining in an abusive or unsafe situation.
Now, here's something important. We can seek to act with integrity and compassion while also protecting ourselves and others from harm.
Sometimes love involves forgiveness.
Sometimes it involves honest conversations.
Sometimes it involves accountability.
And sometimes it involves maintaining appropriate distance.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Biblical love is consistent with truth, righteousness, and appropriate boundaries.
PART EIGHT — JESUS COMMANDS US TO LOVE ONE ANOTHER Now, let's turn to John chapter 13. We're going to read verses 34 and 35. The King James Version says: "A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "As I have loved you..."
Now, that's the standard Jesus gives His disciples.
His own love.
Now, here's something important. Jesus doesn't simply command His followers to speak about love.
He calls them to demonstrate it.
Now, I want you to think about something. How would our churches change if we consistently demonstrated patience and compassion?
How would our families change if we listened more carefully?
How would our communities change if we looked for opportunities to serve others?
Now, we won't always do these things perfectly.
But as believers, we're called to grow in love.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. One of the clearest ways Christians demonstrate their discipleship is through love for one another.
PART NINE — LOVE DURING THE CHRISTMAS SEASON Now, let's bring this back to Christmas.
Because sometimes we become so focused on buying gifts that we forget the importance of showing love.
We spend time making lists.
Shopping.
Wrapping presents.
And preparing for gatherings.
Now, those things can be meaningful.
But here's something I want you to remember. Love isn't measured by the amount of money we spend.
Sometimes the most meaningful expressions of love cost very little.
A thoughtful conversation.
A meal shared with someone who's lonely.
An encouraging message.
Or offering practical assistance to someone who's struggling.
Now, I want you to think about something. Is there someone in your life who needs to experience kindness this Christmas season?
Maybe someone who's grieving.
Maybe someone who's struggling financially.
Maybe someone who's facing illness.
Or someone who simply feels forgotten.
Now, you may not be able to solve every problem.
But perhaps you can demonstrate the love of Christ through a meaningful act of compassion.
PART TEN — WHEN YOU STRUGGLE TO FEEL LOVED Now, I want to speak to someone who may be struggling with feelings of rejection.
Maybe you've been hurt by someone you trusted.
Maybe you've experienced abandonment.
Maybe you've been told things that made you question your worth.
Or maybe you're carrying painful memories.
Now, I want you to hear something. Your experiences with imperfect human love do not define the character of God.
We learn about God's love through His Word.
And especially through the person and work of Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something important. The Bible doesn't teach that every relationship will be restored.
And it doesn't promise that every painful experience will immediately disappear.
But it does reveal the love and grace of God through Christ.
Now, let's turn to Romans chapter 8. We're going to read verses 38 and 39. The King James Version says: "For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."
Now, that's a powerful reminder of the security of God's love for His people in Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our understanding of God's love should be shaped by Jesus Christ, not simply by the ways people have treated us.
PART ELEVEN — LOVE THAT LEADS TO HUMILITY Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 2. We're going to read verses 5 through 8. The King James Version says: "Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "He humbled himself..."
Now, this passage reveals the humility of Jesus Christ.
The eternal Son of God became human.
He took the form of a servant.
And He became obedient unto death.
Even the death of the cross.
Now, here's something important. Paul uses the example of Christ to encourage believers toward humility and concern for others.
Now, that means our response to God's love should include humility.
Not pride.
Not self-importance.
But a willingness to serve.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The love of Christ should move us toward humility, compassion, and service.
PART TWELVE — LOVE THAT TRANSFORMS OUR LIVES Now, let's turn to Ephesians chapter 2. We're going to read verses 8 through 10. The King James Version says: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them."
Now, I want you to notice something. We are saved by grace through faith.
Not by our works.
But those who belong to Christ are called to walk in good works.
Now, that's important. Because we don't love others in order to purchase God's salvation.
We love others as a response to the grace we've received.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We don't earn God's grace by loving others. We seek to love others because of the grace God has shown us through Jesus Christ.
PAUSE AND PRAY — LORD, TEACH ME TO LOVE Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about someone in your life.
Maybe someone who needs encouragement.
Someone who's struggling.
Someone who's grieving.
Or someone who could benefit from a simple act of kindness.
Now, take a moment to pray for that person. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for the love You've demonstrated through Jesus Christ. Thank You for sending Your Son into the world. Thank You for His sacrifice on the cross. And thank You for the hope of salvation through Him. Lord, teach us to love others with patience and compassion. Help us demonstrate kindness. Give us wisdom in difficult relationships. And help us establish appropriate boundaries where necessary. Father, open our eyes to opportunities to serve others. May our words and actions reflect the love of Jesus Christ. And may our lives bring glory to You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
PART THIRTEEN — LOVE THAT DOESN'T SEEK APPLAUSE Now, I want to talk about something important.
Because sometimes we do kind things and hope someone notices.
Maybe we want recognition.
Maybe we want appreciation.
Or maybe we want someone to understand how much effort we put into helping them.
Now, it's natural to appreciate encouragement.
But Christian love shouldn't depend on receiving applause.
Sometimes the most meaningful acts of kindness happen quietly.
Without photographs.
Without public recognition.
And without anyone else knowing what happened.
Now, I want you to think about something. What would it look like to serve someone simply because it's the right thing to do?
Not because you'll receive attention.
Not because someone will owe you a favor.
But because you want to reflect the love of Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Love is not measured by how much attention it receives. It is demonstrated through faithful care for others.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... How does the coming of Jesus Christ reveal the love of God?
Think about His birth. His mission. His sacrifice. And His resurrection. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... How has my understanding of love been shaped by my experiences with other people?
And how does Scripture help me understand God's love more clearly? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What is one relationship where I can demonstrate greater patience, compassion, or humility? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... Who could I encourage or serve through a meaningful act of love this week? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE GREATEST EXPRESSION OF LOVE Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because He's the center of today's lesson.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He entered human history.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation by loving perfectly.
We don't earn it through generosity.
And we don't earn it by doing enough good deeds.
Salvation is God's gracious gift through faith in Jesus Christ.
And the love we show others should flow from the grace we've received.
Now, that's the heart of the gospel.
And that's the greatest expression of God's love.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. God didn't simply tell us He loves us. He demonstrated His love through Jesus Christ. And because of His grace, we're called to reflect that love in the way we live.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because love isn't simply a Christmas decoration.
It's not merely a beautiful song.
And it's not just a feeling we experience during the holiday season.
It's something we're called to demonstrate throughout our lives.
LIVING IT OUT — PUTTING LOVE INTO ACTION Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... Putting Love Into Action.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... One truth about God's love that you want to remember.
Second... One person you can encourage this week.
Third... One practical act of kindness you can offer.
And fourth... One way you can demonstrate patience, humility, or compassion in your relationships.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Thank God for the gift of Jesus Christ.
Ask Him to help you grow in love.
And seek opportunities to reflect His grace.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the greatest expression of Your love reminds me that...
Our second prompt is... One area where I need to grow in love is...
And our third prompt is... Help me demonstrate the love of Christ this week by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. God demonstrated His love through Jesus Christ. Because of His grace, I will seek to love others with patience, humility, truth, and compassion.
Now, say that again. God demonstrated His love through Jesus Christ. Because of His grace, I will seek to love others with patience, humility, truth, and compassion.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize 1 John chapter 4, verses 9 and 10. "In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about what they teach us concerning the love of God.
Maybe you'll read 1 John chapter 4 again.
Maybe you'll spend time thanking God for the gift of Jesus Christ.
Or maybe you'll demonstrate His love through a meaningful act of kindness.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHAT DOES LOVE LOOK LIKE? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The fire is burning.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied today.
Now, I want to ask you something. When you think about God's love, what part of the gospel stands out to you most?
Maybe it's the incarnation.
Maybe it's the sacrifice of Jesus Christ.
Maybe it's the forgiveness we have through Him.
Or maybe it's the promise of eternal life. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. How can the love of God shape the way you treat others?
Maybe through patience.
Kindness.
Forgiveness.
Or generosity. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. The love of God isn't simply a subject we study.
It's a truth that should shape our lives.
And the greatest demonstration of that love is found in Jesus Christ.
CLOSING REFLECTION — LOVE CAME DOWN Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Every Christmas, we celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ.
We remember Mary and Joseph.
The shepherds.
The angels.
And the manger.
But I want you to remember something.
The Christmas story is about more than a baby being born.
It's about God's saving love being revealed through His Son.
Jesus Christ came into the world.
He lived a sinless life.
He died for our sins.
And He rose again.
Now, that's the greatest expression of God's love.
Not because we earned it.
Not because we deserved it.
But because of His grace.
So this Christmas season...
Remember the Savior.
Remember the cross.
Remember the resurrection.
And remember the love God has demonstrated through Jesus Christ.
Then ask yourself... How can I reflect that love in my everyday life?
Maybe it's through a kind word.
Maybe it's through a thoughtful act.
Maybe it's through serving someone who's struggling.
Or maybe it's through showing patience in a difficult situation.
Because love isn't simply something we talk about.
It's something we're called to live.
And the greatest example of that love is Jesus Christ.
Love came down.
And His name is Jesus.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for the love You've demonstrated through Jesus Christ. Thank You for sending Your Son into the world. Thank You for His sinless life. His sacrifice on the cross. And His resurrection. Lord, help us understand the depth of Your grace. Teach us to love others with patience. Kindness. Humility. And compassion. Father, I pray for those who have experienced rejection or heartbreak. Help them find encouragement in the truth of Your Word. I pray for those who are struggling during this Christmas season. Surround them with meaningful support. And I pray for those who have opportunities to serve others. Give them wisdom and generous hearts. Lord, may our lives reflect the love of Jesus Christ. And may everything we do bring glory to You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY SIX Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Eleven, Day Five!
And I hope today's lesson has reminded you that God's love is more than a beautiful Christmas message.
It's revealed through the saving work of Jesus Christ.
Tomorrow, we're continuing our study of The Promise of Christmas — Hope, Peace, and Jesus. And our next lesson is called... Around the Fire — Holding On to Hope, Peace, Joy, and Love.
We'll take time to reflect on everything we've studied this week and consider how these truths can shape our everyday lives.
Until then, remember... Love came down.
And His name is Jesus.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Around the Fire: Holding On to Hope, Peace, Joy, and Love
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — COME SIT AROUND THE FIRE Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today.
Today is Week Eleven, Day Six. And you know what that means. It's time for another one of our special... Around the Fire conversations.
Now, if you've been walking through this Bible study with me, you know these episodes are a little different.
We slow down. We reflect. We talk about what we've learned. And we consider how God's Word applies to our everyday lives.
Now, this week, we've been studying... The Promise of Christmas — Hope, Peace, and Jesus.
And we've covered some beautiful truths.
On Day One, we talked about living hope.
On Day Two, we studied the Prince of Peace.
On Day Three, we remembered Emmanuel. God with us.
On Day Four, we talked about the joy of the Lord.
And yesterday, we studied the greatest expression of God's love.
Now, today, we're bringing all of those truths together.
Hope. Peace. Joy. And love.
Four words we hear so often during the Christmas season.
But I want us to think about something. What do those words mean when life isn't easy?
What does hope mean when you're waiting for answers?
What does peace mean when your circumstances feel overwhelming?
What does joy mean when you're grieving?
And what does love mean when you've experienced disappointment or rejection?
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The promises of Christmas aren't dependent on a perfect holiday season. They're rooted in the Savior who came into the world.
So today, I want you to imagine we're sitting together around a warm fire.
Maybe you've got a cup of coffee. Maybe you're wrapped in a blanket. Maybe you're sitting somewhere quiet.
And we're simply opening God's Word together.
No pressure to have everything figured out.
No expectation that life has to be perfect.
Just an opportunity to reflect on the goodness of God.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the gift of Jesus Christ. And thank You for everything we've studied this week. Lord, today we're reflecting on hope, peace, joy, and love. And You know that each person listening is facing different circumstances. Some are celebrating blessings. Some are grieving. Some are waiting for answers. And some are carrying responsibilities that feel overwhelming. Father, help us understand these truths through Scripture. Remind us of the salvation we have through Jesus Christ. Teach us to trust Your promises. And help us demonstrate compassion toward others. May this time of reflection strengthen our faith and draw us closer to You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — ROMANS 15:13 Now, let's turn to Romans chapter 15. We're going to read verse 13.
This is a beautiful verse for today's reflection. Because it brings together several truths we've been studying.
Let's read Romans chapter 15, verse 13, from the King James Version. "Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost."
Now, I want you to hear that again. "Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing..."
Now, isn't that beautiful?
The God of hope.
Joy.
Peace.
And the power of the Holy Spirit.
Now, Paul is praying for believers.
And he connects their hope, joy, and peace to faith in God.
Now, here's something important. He's not simply wishing that their circumstances would become comfortable.
He's praying that God would strengthen them in believing.
And that's something we can pray for today.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH The hope, peace, joy, and love revealed through Jesus Christ are not merely seasonal feelings. They are gospel truths that can shape our lives throughout the year.
Now, I want you to hold on to that truth as we reflect together.
AROUND THE FIRE — REFLECTION ONE: HOPE Now, let's begin with hope.
On Day One, we studied 1 Peter chapter 1.
And we learned about living hope.
Let's read 1 Peter chapter 1, verse 3. The King James Version says: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,"
Now, I want you to focus on those words. "A lively hope..."
By the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
Now, that's the foundation of Christian hope.
Not simply the belief that everything will happen the way we want.
But confidence rooted in the risen Savior.
Now, let me ask you something. What are you hoping for right now?
Maybe you're hoping for healing.
Maybe you're hoping for reconciliation.
Maybe you're hoping for financial stability.
Maybe you're hoping for an answer to prayer.
Or maybe you're simply hoping for a little relief from a difficult season.
Now, there's nothing wrong with bringing those desires before God.
But here's something I want you to remember. Our ultimate Christian hope isn't based on receiving every outcome we desire.
It's rooted in the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 6, verse 19. The King James Version says: "Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;"
Now, think about that picture. An anchor.
When a storm comes, an anchor provides stability.
It doesn't necessarily stop the wind.
And it doesn't necessarily make the waves disappear.
But it helps keep the vessel secure.
Now, that's a helpful picture of Christian hope.
We may still face difficult circumstances.
But our hope is anchored in Jesus Christ.
Now, I want to ask you a reflection question. Where have you been placing your hope lately?
Has it been in a particular outcome?
In someone else's promises?
In your ability to solve a problem?
Or in the promises of God? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something to think about. Sometimes we don't realize how much we're relying on a particular outcome until it doesn't happen.
And when that happens, disappointment can be overwhelming.
But Scripture reminds us that the resurrection of Jesus Christ is the foundation of our living hope.
Now, that doesn't mean disappointment won't hurt.
It means disappointment doesn't have the final word over our eternal hope.
REFLECTION TWO — PEACE Now, let's talk about peace.
On Day Two, we studied Jesus as the Prince of Peace.
And we looked at John chapter 14.
Let's read verse 27. The King James Version says: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "My peace I give unto you..."
Now, Jesus spoke these words to His disciples before His arrest and crucifixion.
He knew that difficult events were approaching.
And yet, He spoke to them about peace.
Now, that's meaningful.
Because sometimes we assume that peace means nothing difficult is happening.
But the peace Jesus gives is deeper than comfortable circumstances.
Through Him, believers have peace with God.
And His promises give us a foundation for trust.
Now, let me ask you something. What has been disturbing your peace lately?
Maybe it's a financial concern.
Maybe it's a relationship.
Maybe it's uncertainty about the future.
Or maybe it's the pressure of trying to manage too many responsibilities. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something I want you to remember. You can bring those concerns before God.
You can seek wisdom.
You can take responsible action.
And you can ask others for help.
Now, prayer doesn't mean we ignore our responsibilities.
And faith doesn't mean we refuse support.
But it does mean we can approach our circumstances with trust in the Lord.
Now, let's take a moment.
Think about one concern you've been carrying.
And silently bring it before God. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
REFLECTION THREE — EMMANUEL, GOD WITH US Now, let's talk about the beautiful truth we studied on Day Three.
Emmanuel.
God with us.
Let's turn to Matthew chapter 1, verse 23. The King James Version says: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."
Now, I want you to think about those words. God with us.
Now, that's the miracle of the incarnation.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He entered human history.
And through Him, God's saving purposes were fulfilled.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. Have you ever felt spiritually alone?
Maybe you were praying and didn't feel encouraged.
Maybe you were grieving.
Maybe you were facing uncertainty.
Or maybe you were simply exhausted.
Now, here's something important. Our feelings about God's nearness can change.
But the truth of who Jesus Christ is doesn't change.
Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 34, verse 18. The King James Version says: "The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit."
Now, I want you to hear that again. "The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart..."
Now, that's a beautiful reminder of God's compassion.
And I want to speak to someone who may be grieving this Christmas season.
Maybe you're missing someone you love.
Maybe there's an empty chair at the table.
Maybe a familiar Christmas song brings tears to your eyes.
Or maybe you're simply trying to navigate a season that looks very different from what you expected.
Now, I want you to hear something. It's okay to grieve.
It's okay to remember.
And it's okay to acknowledge that someone's absence hurts.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The truth of Emmanuel doesn't require us to deny our pain. It points us toward the Savior who came into the world to accomplish our salvation.
Now, let me ask you something. What does Emmanuel mean to you personally?
Does it remind you of God's faithfulness?
The incarnation?
The saving work of Jesus Christ?
Or the hope we have through Him? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
REFLECTION FOUR — JOY Now, let's talk about joy.
On Day Four, we studied the announcement of Jesus' birth.
And we learned that the angel brought good tidings of great joy.
Let's turn to Luke chapter 2. We're going to read verses 10 and 11. The King James Version says: "And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord."
Now, I want you to focus on those words. "Good tidings of great joy..."
Now, why was the announcement joyful?
Because the Savior had come.
Not because every difficulty in the world had disappeared.
Not because every person suddenly had a perfect life.
But because Jesus Christ had been born.
Now, that's the foundation of Christian joy.
The good news of salvation through Jesus Christ.
Now, let me ask you something. What brings you joy?
Maybe it's spending time with family.
Maybe it's serving others.
Maybe it's a meaningful conversation.
Or maybe it's simply taking a quiet moment to reflect on God's goodness.
Now, those things can be wonderful.
But here's something important. Our deepest reason for Christian joy is the Savior.
Now, I want to ask you another question. Can you think of a time when you experienced gratitude or joy even though your circumstances were difficult? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something I want you to remember. Joy and sorrow can exist together.
You can be thankful for the salvation you have through Jesus Christ.
And still grieve someone you love.
You can worship God.
And still have questions.
You can remember His goodness.
And still acknowledge that life is difficult.
Now, that's an important truth. Because Christian joy doesn't require pretending everything is wonderful.
It is rooted in the goodness of God.
REFLECTION FIVE — LOVE Now, let's talk about love.
Yesterday, we studied 1 John chapter 4.
And we learned that God's love is revealed through Jesus Christ.
Let's read 1 John chapter 4, verses 9 through 11. The King James Version says: "In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another."
Now, I want you to think about those words. God sent His Son.
And through Jesus Christ, He accomplished our salvation.
Now, that's the greatest expression of God's love.
Not simply a beautiful message.
Not merely a comforting feeling.
But the saving work of Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God's love is revealed through Christ, and that love calls believers to love one another.
Now, let me ask you something. Who has demonstrated meaningful love or kindness toward you?
Maybe someone who encouraged you.
Someone who helped you during a difficult season.
Someone who listened.
Or someone who showed up when you needed support. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. Who could you demonstrate love toward this week?
Maybe someone who's grieving.
Someone who's lonely.
Someone who's struggling financially.
Or someone who simply needs encouragement. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something important. Love doesn't always require expensive gifts.
Sometimes it's a phone call.
A thoughtful message.
A meal.
Or offering practical assistance.
And sometimes love also involves truth, accountability, and appropriate boundaries.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Love is not measured by how much money we spend. It is demonstrated through faithful care for others.
PART SIX — WHAT IF CHRISTMAS FEELS DIFFERENT THIS YEAR? Now, I want us to spend a few minutes talking about something.
Because Christmas can look very different from one year to the next.
Sometimes we're surrounded by family.
Sometimes we're celebrating new blessings.
Sometimes we're welcoming new people into our lives.
And sometimes we're facing changes we never expected.
Maybe someone you love is no longer here.
Maybe your family traditions have changed.
Maybe you're dealing with financial challenges.
Or maybe you're navigating a difficult relationship.
Now, here's something I want you to hear. Christmas doesn't have to look like it did in previous years to remain meaningful.
And it doesn't have to be perfect.
The heart of Christmas is Jesus Christ.
The promised Savior.
The One who came into the world.
The One who died for our sins.
And the One who rose again.
Now, that truth doesn't change when our circumstances change.
And that's something worth remembering.
PART SEVEN — WHEN YOU'RE CARRYING TOO MUCH Now, I want to speak to someone who may be feeling overwhelmed.
Maybe you're trying to manage everything.
Work.
Family.
Responsibilities.
Appointments.
Financial concerns.
And the expectations that often come with the holiday season.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we become so focused on doing everything that we forget to consider what truly matters.
We feel pressure to make every celebration perfect.
Every gift meaningful.
Every gathering successful.
And every detail beautiful.
But here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to create a perfect Christmas to honor Jesus Christ.
You can simplify.
You can establish healthy boundaries.
You can ask for help.
And you can make meaningful room for Scripture, prayer, and worship.
Now, that's not about doing less simply for the sake of doing less.
It's about remembering the purpose of the season.
Jesus Christ.
PART EIGHT — THE PROMISES OF CHRISTMAS ARE CONNECTED Now, I want us to bring these truths together.
Hope.
Peace.
Joy.
And love.
Now, these aren't simply four separate subjects.
They're connected through Jesus Christ.
We have living hope because He rose from the dead.
We have peace with God through His saving work.
We have reason for great joy because the Savior has come.
And we know the love of God because He sent His Son into the world.
Now, that's beautiful.
Because it reminds us that the Christmas story isn't simply about one day.
It's about the Savior.
And the salvation He accomplished.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The greatest promises of Christmas point us toward the person and work of Jesus Christ.
PAUSE AND PRAY — BRINGING IT ALL TO JESUS Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about the four words we've been studying.
Hope. Peace. Joy. Love.
Which one stands out to you most today?
Maybe you need encouragement in hope.
Maybe you're longing for peace.
Maybe you're struggling to experience joy.
Or maybe you need to grow in your understanding of God's love.
Now, take a moment to bring that before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for the gift of Jesus Christ. Thank You for the living hope we have through His resurrection. Thank You for the peace we have with You through His saving work. Thank You for the great joy announced at His birth. And thank You for the love You demonstrated by sending Your Son. Lord, You know what each person listening needs today. Some need encouragement. Some need wisdom. Some need comfort. And some need meaningful support. Father, help us remember Your promises. Teach us to trust Your Word. And help us reflect the love of Jesus Christ in our everyday lives. May this Christmas season draw our attention toward our Savior. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
PART NINE — MAKING ROOM FOR WHAT MATTERS Now, I want us to think about something practical.
If you could simplify one thing about this Christmas season, what would it be?
Maybe it's the pressure to buy expensive gifts.
Maybe it's the expectation that every gathering has to be perfect.
Maybe it's trying to attend every event.
Or maybe it's the pressure to make everyone happy.
Now, here's something important. We can celebrate Christmas in meaningful ways without placing unrealistic expectations on ourselves.
We can worship.
Spend time with loved ones.
Serve others.
And remember the coming of Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The purpose of Christmas isn't to impress people. It's to remember and celebrate the Savior.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... Which truth from this week's study has encouraged me most: hope, peace, Emmanuel, joy, or love? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... How has studying the Christmas story helped me understand Jesus Christ more clearly? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What is one concern I need to bring before God rather than trying to manage entirely on my own? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I demonstrate the love of Christ to someone during this Christmas season? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, take a moment to look over your answers.
And think about one practical step you can take this week.
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE CENTER OF EVERY PROMISE Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because He's the center of every truth we've studied this week.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He entered human history.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through Him, we have forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation by having perfect hope.
We don't earn it by always feeling peaceful.
We don't earn it by being cheerful.
And we don't earn it by loving others perfectly.
Salvation is God's gracious gift through faith in Jesus Christ.
And the hope, peace, joy, and love we demonstrate should flow from our relationship with Him.
Now, that's the heart of the gospel.
And that's the greatest promise of Christmas.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. The promises of Christmas aren't wrapped in perfect circumstances. They're revealed through Jesus Christ, our living hope, our Prince of Peace, the source of our joy, and the greatest expression of God's love.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because Christmas comes once a year.
But the truth of Jesus Christ remains the same every day.
LIVING IT OUT — CARRYING CHRISTMAS INTO EVERYDAY LIFE Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... Carrying the Promises of Christmas Into Everyday Life.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... Hope: One promise of Scripture you want to remember when life feels uncertain.
Second... Peace: One concern you want to bring before God in prayer.
Third... Joy: One reason you're grateful for the salvation you have through Jesus Christ.
And fourth... Love: One meaningful way you can encourage or serve someone else.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Thank God for the gift of Jesus Christ.
Ask Him for wisdom.
And seek opportunities to reflect His love.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, the truth from this week's study that I most need to remember is...
Our second prompt is... One area where I need to grow in hope, peace, joy, or love is...
And our third prompt is... Help me carry the message of Christmas into everyday life by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. My hope, peace, joy, and love are rooted in Jesus Christ. I will remember His saving work and seek to reflect His grace in my everyday life.
Now, say that again. My hope, peace, joy, and love are rooted in Jesus Christ. I will remember His saving work and seek to reflect His grace in my everyday life.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Romans chapter 15, verse 13. "Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about the God of hope.
Maybe you'll spend time thanking Him for the gift of Jesus Christ.
Maybe you'll pray for someone who's struggling.
Or maybe you'll demonstrate His love through a meaningful act of kindness.
AROUND THE FIRE — ONE LAST QUESTION Now, before we close, I want us to imagine we're still sitting together around that fire.
The evening is quiet.
The flames are beginning to settle.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied.
Now, I want to ask you one final question. If you could carry one truth from this week's study into the rest of your life, what would it be?
Would it be living hope?
The peace of Christ?
The truth of Emmanuel?
The joy of the Lord?
Or the love of God revealed through Jesus Christ? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. You don't have to choose only one forever.
These truths are connected.
And they all point us toward the Savior.
Jesus Christ.
The greatest gift of Christmas.
CLOSING REFLECTION — THE PROMISES THAT REMAIN Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Christmas is a beautiful season.
But it isn't always an easy one.
Sometimes we're celebrating new blessings.
Sometimes we're remembering people we love.
Sometimes we're facing difficult circumstances.
And sometimes we're simply trying to make it through another day.
But here's something I want you to remember.
The truth of Jesus Christ doesn't change with our circumstances.
He is the promised Savior.
The Word made flesh.
The One who died for our sins.
And the One who rose again.
Now, that's the foundation of our hope.
Our peace with God.
Our reason for joy.
And our understanding of God's love.
So this Christmas season...
Don't become so overwhelmed by the preparations that you forget the Savior.
Make meaningful room for Scripture.
For prayer.
For worship.
And for demonstrating compassion toward others.
Because the greatest gift of Christmas isn't found beneath a tree.
It's found in Jesus Christ.
And His saving work remains the foundation of our faith every day.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for everything we've studied this week. Thank You for the living hope we have through Jesus Christ. Thank You for the peace we have with You through His saving work. Thank You for the joy of the gospel. And thank You for the love You've demonstrated through Your Son. Lord, help us carry these truths into our everyday lives. Strengthen those who are discouraged. Comfort those who are grieving. Give wisdom to those facing uncertainty. And help us show compassion to those who are struggling. Father, may this Christmas season remind us of the Savior. May our homes reflect gratitude. May our relationships reflect love. And may our hearts remain focused on Jesus Christ. Thank You for His birth. His sinless life. His sacrifice on the cross. And His resurrection. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY SEVEN Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Eleven, Day Six!
And I hope today's Around the Fire conversation has given you an opportunity to reflect on the promises of Christmas.
Hope. Peace. Joy. And love.
Tomorrow, we're finishing Week Eleven with a special lesson called... Carrying the Light of Christmas — Living as a Reflection of Jesus.
We'll explore how the truth of Jesus Christ should shape our lives long after the Christmas decorations are put away.
Until then, remember... The promises of Christmas point us toward the Savior.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Carrying the Light of Christmas: Living as a Reflection of Jesus
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WHEN THE CHRISTMAS LIGHTS COME DOWN Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today.
Today is Week Eleven, Day Seven! And that means we're completing another full week of studying God's Word together.
This week has been especially meaningful because we've been studying... The Promise of Christmas — Hope, Peace, and Jesus.
We've talked about living hope. We've studied the Prince of Peace. We've remembered Emmanuel, God with us. We've explored the joy of the Lord. And we've reflected on the greatest expression of God's love.
Yesterday, during our Around the Fire conversation, we brought all those truths together.
And today, I want to ask you something. What happens when Christmas is over?
Think about it. We spend weeks preparing.
We decorate our homes. We put up Christmas trees. We hang lights. We buy gifts. And we make plans to celebrate with the people we love.
Then Christmas comes.
And eventually, the decorations come down.
The lights are packed away.
The wrapping paper is thrown away.
And life begins returning to its normal routine.
But here's something I want you to think about. The message of Christmas was never meant to be packed away with the decorations.
The birth of Jesus Christ is something we celebrate during Christmas. But the truth of who He is should shape the way we live every single day.
Now, that brings us to today's lesson. Because Jesus calls His followers to be a light in the world.
Not just during December.
Not just when we're at church.
And not just when life is going well.
But in our everyday lives.
At home. At work. In our communities. And in the way we treat other people.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We don't create the light of salvation ourselves. Jesus Christ is the Light of the World, and His followers are called to reflect His truth through faithful living.
And that's what we're studying today.
Our lesson is called... Carrying the Light of Christmas — Living as a Reflection of Jesus.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for carrying us through another week of Bible study. And thank You for the gift of Jesus Christ. Lord, today we're studying what it means to live as a light in the world. Help us understand that Jesus is the true Light. Teach us to reflect His truth through our words, actions, and relationships. Father, help us grow in humility. Compassion. Patience. And obedience. May our lives point others toward Jesus Christ rather than toward ourselves. And may everything we study today bring glory to You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S SCRIPTURE — MATTHEW 5:14–16 Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 5. We're going to read verses 14 through 16.
Before we begin, let's understand the setting. Jesus is teaching during what we commonly call the Sermon on the Mount.
He's explaining what life in the kingdom of heaven looks like.
And He's teaching His followers about righteousness, obedience, and the way they should live.
Now, in this passage, Jesus uses the picture of light.
Let's read Matthew chapter 5, verses 14 through 16, from the King James Version. "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven."
Now, I want you to hear that last verse again. "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven."
Now, I want you to notice something important. Jesus doesn't say that the purpose of our good works is to make people admire us.
He says that they should glorify our Father in heaven.
Now, that's a powerful distinction.
Because Christian living isn't supposed to be about building our own reputation.
It's about bringing glory to God.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Jesus Christ is the Light of the World. Through faith in Him, believers are called to live in a way that reflects His truth, demonstrates His love, and brings glory to God.
Now, I want you to hold on to that truth. Because it's going to shape everything we study today.
PART ONE — JESUS IS THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD Now, let's turn to John chapter 8. We're going to read verse 12. The King James Version says: "Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life."
Now, I want you to hear those words again. "I am the light of the world..."
Now, that's an extraordinary statement.
Jesus doesn't simply say that He knows where the light is.
He doesn't simply say that He can point people toward the light.
He declares that He is the Light of the World.
Now, here's something important. Throughout Scripture, light is often associated with God's truth, holiness, and saving revelation.
And darkness is frequently associated with sin, ignorance, and separation from God's truth.
Now, Jesus is declaring something about His identity.
He is the One through whom we receive the light of life.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We don't become the source of salvation for other people. Jesus Christ is the Savior, and our lives should point toward Him.
PART TWO — THE LIGHT SHINES IN DARKNESS Now, let's turn to John chapter 1. We're going to read verses 4 and 5. The King James Version says: "In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "The light shineth in darkness..."
Now, John's Gospel begins by telling us about the eternal Word.
And it reveals that the Word became flesh.
Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something important. The coming of Jesus into the world is the fulfillment of God's saving purposes.
And John describes Him as the true Light.
Now, I want you to think about something. Have you ever walked into a dark room and turned on a light?
Suddenly, you can see things that were difficult to recognize before.
You can see where you're going.
You can recognize obstacles.
And you can move with greater understanding.
Now, that gives us a simple picture of why Scripture uses the imagery of light.
Jesus reveals the truth about God.
He reveals the seriousness of sin.
And He provides the way of salvation.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Jesus doesn't simply make life more comfortable. He reveals the truth and calls us to follow Him.
PART THREE — A GREAT LIGHT HAS COME Now, let's turn to Isaiah chapter 9. We're going to read verse 2. The King James Version says: "The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined."
Now, this passage is part of the prophetic hope that Christians understand as fulfilled in Jesus Christ.
And it gives us a beautiful picture.
People walking in darkness.
And a great light appearing.
Now, I want you to think about that in connection with Christmas.
The coming of Jesus Christ is not simply the beginning of a beautiful holiday tradition.
It's the arrival of the promised Messiah.
The Savior.
The Light of the World.
Now, here's something important. The birth of Jesus is connected to the entire work He came to accomplish.
His sinless life.
His teaching.
His death on the cross.
And His resurrection.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The light of Christmas points us toward the Savior who came to redeem sinners.
PART FOUR — LET YOUR LIGHT SHINE Now, let's return to Matthew chapter 5.
Jesus says: "Let your light so shine before men..."
Now, I want you to think about something. What does that look like in everyday life?
Does it mean we have to preach a sermon every time we speak to someone?
Does it mean we have to talk about ourselves constantly?
Or make sure everyone notices our good deeds?
No.
Jesus tells us that our good works should lead others to glorify our Father in heaven.
Now, that means our lives should reflect the character of Christ.
Through honesty.
Kindness.
Humility.
Compassion.
And faithful obedience.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we imagine that making a difference requires doing something enormous.
Starting a major project.
Speaking in front of thousands of people.
Or accomplishing something extraordinary.
But sometimes meaningful Christian witness happens in ordinary moments.
When we tell the truth even when it's difficult.
When we help someone who needs assistance.
When we listen to someone who's grieving.
Or when we treat another person with dignity and respect.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful Christian living is demonstrated through everyday obedience, not simply through extraordinary accomplishments.
PART FIVE — A CITY SET ON A HILL Now, let's look at another part of Matthew chapter 5.
Jesus says: "A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid."
Now, I want you to picture that.
A city elevated above the surrounding landscape.
Visible from a distance.
Now, Jesus uses this picture to teach His followers about the visible nature of their witness.
Their lives should reflect the truth they profess.
Now, here's something important. Being a visible witness doesn't mean seeking attention for ourselves.
It means living consistently with our faith.
Now, let me ask you something. Do the people around you see patience in the way you respond to frustration?
Do they see honesty in the way you handle responsibilities?
Do they see compassion in the way you treat people who are struggling?
And do they see humility in the way you handle success?
Now, none of us will demonstrate these things perfectly.
But as followers of Jesus Christ, we're called to grow.
And to live in ways that honor Him.
PART SIX — DON'T HIDE THE LIGHT Now, let's look at Matthew chapter 5, verse 15.
Jesus says: "Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house."
Now, think about that.
A lamp is meant to provide light.
Covering it defeats its purpose.
Now, Jesus uses this illustration to encourage His followers toward visible faithfulness.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. Sometimes we hesitate to live openly according to our faith.
Maybe we're worried about what other people will think.
Maybe we don't want to seem different.
Or maybe we're afraid of making mistakes.
Now, here's something important. Living as a Christian doesn't mean we have to be loud.
It doesn't mean we have to argue with everyone.
And it doesn't mean we need to draw attention to ourselves.
But it does mean we should be willing to live according to the truth of God's Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We can demonstrate our faith with both courage and humility.
PART SEVEN — WALK AS CHILDREN OF LIGHT Now, let's turn to Ephesians chapter 5. We're going to read verses 8 through 10. The King James Version says: "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light: (For the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth;) Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord."
Now, I want you to focus on those words. "Walk as children of light..."
Now, Paul is speaking to believers about the way they should live.
And he connects their identity in Christ to their conduct.
Now, that's important. Because Christianity isn't simply about what we say we believe.
Our faith should influence the way we live.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. How do you respond when someone frustrates you?
How do you handle disagreements?
How do you treat people who cannot offer you anything in return?
And how do you behave when nobody else is watching?
Now, those are meaningful questions.
Because Christian character isn't simply demonstrated in public.
It's also reflected in private decisions.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Walking as children of light means seeking to live according to God's truth in both public and private life.
PART EIGHT — SHINING WITHOUT COMPLAINING Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 2. We're going to read verses 14 through 16. The King James Version says: "Do all things without murmurings and disputings: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world; Holding forth the word of life; that I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, neither laboured in vain."
Now, I want you to notice something. Paul connects shining as lights in the world with the way believers conduct themselves.
He specifically mentions avoiding murmurings and disputings.
Now, that's challenging.
Because sometimes complaining becomes such a regular part of our conversations that we barely notice it.
We complain about traffic.
About responsibilities.
About other people.
And about circumstances we cannot control.
Now, here's something important. This passage doesn't mean we should never express legitimate concerns.
And it doesn't mean we should remain silent about injustice or wrongdoing.
But it does challenge us to consider the attitude and spirit with which we respond to everyday difficulties.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our words and attitudes can either support or undermine the witness of our faith.
PART NINE — WHEN YOU DON'T FEEL LIKE A LIGHT Now, I want to talk about something important.
Because sometimes we hear lessons about being a light in the world and immediately begin thinking about all the ways we've fallen short.
Maybe you lost your patience.
Maybe you said something you regret.
Maybe you missed an opportunity to encourage someone.
Or maybe you're simply going through a difficult season and don't feel spiritually strong.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Being a follower of Jesus Christ doesn't mean we become perfect overnight.
Christian growth is an ongoing process.
We continue learning.
Repenting.
Seeking forgiveness.
And growing in obedience.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation by shining brightly enough.
We receive salvation by God's grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our good works should flow from that relationship.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our calling to reflect Christ is a response to God's grace, not a way of earning it.
PART TEN — THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT Now, let's turn to Galatians chapter 5. We're going to read verses 22 and 23. The King James Version says: "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law."
Now, I want you to think about those qualities. Love.
Joy.
Peace.
Patience.
Kindness.
Goodness.
Faithfulness.
Gentleness.
And self-control.
Now, those qualities help us understand what it means to live in a way that reflects Christ.
Now, let me ask you something. Which of those qualities do you find most challenging?
Maybe patience.
Maybe self-control.
Maybe kindness when you're frustrated.
Or maybe maintaining a peaceful attitude during difficult circumstances.
Now, here's something important. Spiritual growth isn't simply about trying harder through our own strength.
It's connected to the work of the Holy Spirit in believers.
And our ongoing response through faith and obedience.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. As we grow in Christ, the fruit of the Spirit should become increasingly evident in our lives.
PART ELEVEN — LIGHT IN THE MIDDLE OF DIFFICULT SEASONS Now, I want to speak to someone who may be facing a difficult season.
Maybe you're grieving.
Maybe you're struggling financially.
Maybe you're dealing with a health concern.
Or maybe you're simply overwhelmed by responsibilities.
Now, here's something I want you to hear. You don't have to pretend everything is wonderful in order to reflect Jesus Christ.
Sometimes our faith is demonstrated through quiet perseverance.
Through honest prayer.
Through seeking wisdom.
And through continuing to trust God's promises.
Now, here's something important. Being a light doesn't mean we never need help ourselves.
Sometimes we need encouragement.
Sometimes we need practical assistance.
And sometimes we need professional support.
Now, receiving help doesn't make our faith less meaningful.
We are members of the body of Christ, and we're called to care for one another.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We can reflect Christ through faithful living while also acknowledging our own needs and limitations.
PART TWELVE — SHARING THE LIGHT THROUGH SERVICE Now, let's talk about something practical.
Because one of the ways we can reflect the love of Jesus Christ is through service.
Now, I want you to think about your community.
Maybe there are families who are struggling financially.
Maybe there are people who are lonely.
Maybe there are individuals who are grieving.
Or maybe there are people who simply need someone to listen.
Now, we may not be able to solve every problem.
But we can look for meaningful opportunities to serve.
Sometimes it's preparing a meal.
Sometimes it's helping someone with a practical need.
Sometimes it's offering transportation.
Or simply spending time with someone who feels forgotten.
Now, here's something important. Christian service shouldn't be about gaining recognition.
It should be motivated by love and a desire to glorify God.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Small acts of faithful service can become meaningful expressions of Christlike love.
PART THIRTEEN — LET THE LIGHT POINT TO JESUS Now, let's return to Matthew chapter 5, verse 16.
Jesus says: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven."
Now, I want you to notice the purpose again.
That they may glorify your Father in heaven.
Now, that's important. Because sometimes we become so focused on doing good things that we forget why we're doing them.
We want people to notice.
We want recognition.
Or we want others to appreciate our efforts.
Now, it's natural to appreciate encouragement.
But the ultimate purpose of Christian witness is to bring glory to God.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The light we reflect should direct attention toward Jesus Christ, not simply toward ourselves.
PAUSE AND PRAY — LORD, HELP ME REFLECT YOUR LIGHT Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about one area of your life where you want to grow as a follower of Jesus Christ.
Maybe it's patience.
Maybe it's kindness.
Maybe it's honesty.
Maybe it's humility.
Or maybe it's being more intentional about serving others.
Now, take a moment to bring that before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for Jesus Christ, the Light of the World. Thank You for revealing Your truth through Him. And thank You for the salvation we have through His saving work. Lord, help us live in ways that reflect His character. Teach us to demonstrate love. Patience. Kindness. Humility. And truthfulness. Father, help us recognize opportunities to serve others. Give us wisdom in difficult situations. And remind us that our purpose is to bring glory to You. May our lives point others toward Jesus Christ. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
PART FOURTEEN — THE LIGHT DOESN'T END WITH CHRISTMAS Now, let's bring this back to the Christmas season.
Because we've spent this entire week studying the promises of Christmas.
Hope. Peace. Emmanuel. Joy. And love.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. What would happen if we carried those truths into the rest of the year?
What if we continued encouraging people who were struggling?
What if we continued showing kindness?
What if we continued serving our communities?
What if we continued opening our Bibles?
And what if we continued making meaningful time for prayer?
Now, that's what I want us to remember as we finish Week Eleven.
The message of Christmas isn't meant to be limited to one season.
It's meant to shape the way we understand Jesus Christ and live as His followers.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The decorations may come down, but our calling to follow Jesus Christ continues every day.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
