But Scripture teaches that our hearts matter.
Our desires. Our motives. Our attitudes. And our relationship with God.
Now, I want you to think about something. It's possible to appear kind while secretly holding on to bitterness.
It's possible to appear generous while seeking recognition.
And it's possible to participate in religious activities without genuinely trusting God.
Now, that doesn't mean outward actions are unimportant.
But it does mean that genuine spiritual transformation goes deeper than appearances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God calls us toward inward renewal that becomes evident through the way we live.
PART TWO — THE STONY HEART Now, let's return to Ezekiel chapter 36.
God says: "I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh."
Now, I want you to picture that. A heart of stone.
Hard. Unresponsive. And resistant.
Now, in Ezekiel's message, this imagery describes the spiritual condition of God's people and His promise to renew them.
But it also gives us an opportunity to examine our own hearts.
Sometimes we become resistant to correction.
Sometimes pride makes it difficult to admit we're wrong.
Sometimes bitterness shapes the way we respond to other people.
And sometimes we become so accustomed to a sinful pattern that we stop questioning it.
Now, let me ask you something. Is there an area of your life where you've become resistant to what God's Word teaches?
Maybe it's forgiveness.
Maybe it's honesty.
Maybe it's humility.
Or maybe it's a habit you've been unwilling to address.
Now, here's something important. Recognizing an area of resistance doesn't mean we're beyond God's mercy.
It means we need to respond honestly to His Word.
PART THREE — A HEART THAT RESPONDS TO GOD Now, let's look at the other part of Ezekiel's promise.
God says He will give His people a heart of flesh.
Now, this imagery points toward a heart that responds to Him.
A heart no longer characterized by the same stubborn resistance.
Now, here's something important. God's promise of renewal isn't simply about changing how people feel.
It's connected to obedience.
Look at verse 27. "And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes..."
Now, notice that. The work of God's Spirit is connected to walking according to His ways.
Now, that means genuine spiritual renewal should influence our conduct.
How we speak.
How we respond to correction.
How we treat others.
And how we make decisions.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Spiritual transformation isn't simply about having different feelings. It involves a growing desire to honor God through obedience.
PART FOUR — DAVID'S PRAYER FOR A CLEAN HEART Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 51. We're going to read verse 10. The King James Version says: "Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me."
Now, that's a beautiful prayer.
But let's remember the setting. Psalm 51 is traditionally associated with David's repentance after serious sin.
David isn't simply asking God to help him feel more motivated.
He's asking for cleansing and renewal.
Now, I want you to think about something. How often do we ask God to change our circumstances without asking Him to change our hearts?
We pray for difficult people to become easier to deal with.
We pray for stressful situations to improve.
We pray for problems to disappear.
And those can be appropriate things to bring before the Lord.
But sometimes we also need to ask... Lord, what needs to change in me?
Now, here's something important. That question should never be used to blame someone for harm another person has caused.
But it can help us examine our own attitudes and responsibilities honestly.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A prayer for spiritual renewal begins with humility before God.
PART FIVE — YOU CANNOT SAVE YOURSELF THROUGH SELF-IMPROVEMENT Now, let's turn to Titus chapter 3. We're going to read verses 4 through 7. The King James Version says: "But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life."
Now, I want you to focus on those words. "Not by works of righteousness which we have done..."
Now, that's important. Because sometimes we approach our relationship with God as though salvation is something we can accomplish through personal improvement.
We think... If I become patient enough...
If I do enough good deeds...
If I stop making mistakes...
Then perhaps God will accept me.
But Scripture teaches that salvation is by God's mercy and grace through Jesus Christ.
We cannot earn it through our own righteousness.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Spiritual transformation is not a project we complete in order to earn salvation. It flows from the saving grace of God through Jesus Christ.
PART SIX — WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO BE BORN AGAIN? Now, let's turn to John chapter 3.
Jesus is speaking with a man named Nicodemus.
Nicodemus is a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
And Jesus begins teaching him about the necessity of being born again.
Let's read John chapter 3, verses 3 through 6. The King James Version says: "Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother's womb, and be born? Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
Now, I want you to think about that conversation.
Nicodemus is confused because he's thinking about physical birth.
But Jesus is teaching about spiritual birth.
A work of the Spirit.
Now, that's important. Because becoming a Christian isn't simply deciding to become a more religious person.
It's not simply attending church more often.
And it's not merely adopting better habits.
It's about the new life God gives through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The Christian life begins with God's saving work, not merely with our determination to improve ourselves.
PART SEVEN — BE NOT CONFORMED TO THIS WORLD Now, let's return to Romans chapter 12, verse 2.
Paul says: "And be not conformed to this world..."
Now, what does that mean?
Paul is warning believers against allowing the patterns of a fallen world to shape their thinking and conduct.
Now, I want you to think about something. We're influenced by many things.
The conversations we participate in.
The media we consume.
The people we spend time with.
And the habits we practice.
Now, not every cultural influence is sinful.
But we should evaluate what shapes our thinking.
Are we becoming more truthful?
More compassionate?
More humble?
Or are we becoming more bitter, prideful, or dishonest?
Now, here's something important. Christian discernment requires more than simply following what everyone else is doing.
It requires comparing our beliefs and actions with the teaching of Scripture.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Following Jesus Christ means allowing God's truth to shape our lives rather than automatically adopting the values around us.
PART EIGHT — THE RENEWING OF YOUR MIND Now, let's focus on the next part of Romans chapter 12, verse 2.
"Be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind..."
Now, I want you to think about something. Our thinking influences our decisions.
And our decisions influence our habits.
Now, sometimes we develop patterns of thinking that don't align with God's Word.
Maybe we justify dishonesty because it's convenient.
Maybe we excuse unkindness because someone upset us.
Maybe we begin believing that our worth depends entirely on what other people think.
Or maybe we assume that making a mistake means we're incapable of growing.
Now, renewing our minds involves learning to evaluate those patterns according to God's truth.
We read Scripture.
We study it carefully.
We pray for wisdom.
And we seek to apply what we've learned.
Now, here's something important. Renewing the mind isn't simply repeating positive statements.
It's about being shaped by the truth of God.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A renewed mind learns to recognize and respond to life according to God's Word.
PART NINE — CHANGE IS OFTEN A PROCESS Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 1. We're going to read verse 6. The King James Version says: "Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:"
Now, Paul expresses confidence in God's continuing work among the Philippian believers.
And this reminds us that Christian growth isn't completed overnight.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we become discouraged because we're still struggling with something we thought we'd already overcome.
Maybe we're still learning patience.
Maybe we're still working on self-control.
Maybe we're still learning how to respond with kindness when we're frustrated.
Or maybe we're still learning to trust God in uncertain circumstances.
Now, here's something important. Growth doesn't mean we never struggle.
And progress doesn't always happen in a straight line.
But we should continue seeking the Lord.
Continue studying His Word.
Continue repenting when we sin.
And continue learning to walk in obedience.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Spiritual maturity develops through God's ongoing work in our lives as we continue following Jesus Christ.
PART TEN — PUTTING OFF THE OLD AND PUTTING ON THE NEW Now, let's turn to Ephesians chapter 4. We're going to read verses 22 through 24. The King James Version says: "That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts; And be renewed in the spirit of your mind; And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness."
Now, I want you to notice something. Paul uses the imagery of taking something off and putting something on.
Now, that's a helpful picture.
Because Christian growth isn't simply about stopping sinful behavior.
It also involves learning to live in righteousness and holiness.
For example...
If we've struggled with dishonesty, we should pursue truthfulness.
If we've struggled with bitterness, we should seek to grow in forgiveness and compassion.
If we've struggled with selfishness, we should learn to serve others.
And if we've struggled with pride, we should pursue humility.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Biblical transformation involves turning away from sinful patterns and learning to live according to our new identity in Christ.
PART ELEVEN — THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT Now, let's turn to Galatians chapter 5. We're going to read verses 22 and 23. The King James Version says: "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law."
Now, I want you to think about those qualities. Love.
Joy.
Peace.
Patience.
Kindness.
Goodness.
Faithfulness.
Gentleness.
And self-control.
Now, those qualities give us a meaningful picture of spiritual growth.
But I want you to notice something. Paul calls this the fruit of the Spirit.
Not simply the achievements of human willpower.
Now, that doesn't mean we have no responsibility.
We are called to walk in the Spirit.
To resist sinful desires.
And to live in obedience.
But spiritual fruit is connected to the work of the Holy Spirit in believers.
Now, let me ask you something. Which of these qualities do you most want to grow in?
Maybe patience.
Maybe gentleness.
Maybe self-control.
Or maybe learning to respond to difficult circumstances with greater peace.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Spiritual growth should increasingly reflect the character of Jesus Christ.
PART TWELVE — WHEN CHANGE FEELS SLOW Now, I want to speak to someone who may be discouraged.
Maybe you've been praying about the same struggle for a long time.
Maybe you've made progress, but you've also experienced setbacks.
Maybe you're tired of feeling like you should be further along.
Or maybe you're comparing your spiritual growth to someone else's.
Now, I want you to hear something. Comparison isn't always a helpful measure of spiritual maturity.
People have different experiences. Different responsibilities. And different areas where they need to grow.
Now, that doesn't mean we should become comfortable with sin.
But it does mean we should approach spiritual growth with humility and perseverance.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes we need encouragement from other believers.
Sometimes we need accountability.
Sometimes we need practical changes in our routines.
And sometimes we need professional support for struggles that involve mental or emotional health.
Seeking appropriate help is not a rejection of faith.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful growth involves perseverance, honesty, and a willingness to receive help when needed.
PART THIRTEEN — A NEW HEART CHANGES OUR RELATIONSHIPS Now, let's talk about something practical.
Because spiritual transformation should affect the way we treat other people.
It should influence our relationships.
Our conversations.
Our decisions.
And the way we respond when things don't go our way.
Now, I want you to think about something. How do you respond when someone corrects you?
Do you become defensive?
Do you immediately look for someone else to blame?
Or are you willing to consider whether you need to change something?
Now, here's another question. How do you treat people who disagree with you?
Do you respond with respect?
Do you listen carefully?
Or do you allow frustration to control your words?
Now, here's something important. Spiritual transformation doesn't mean we never experience difficult emotions.
But it should influence how we respond to them.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A renewed heart should increasingly become evident through humility, honesty, and compassion toward others.
PART FOURTEEN — DON'T CONFUSE ACTIVITY WITH TRANSFORMATION Now, I want us to consider something.
Because sometimes we become so busy doing good things that we neglect our relationship with God.
We volunteer.
We attend church.
We participate in ministry activities.
And we take on responsibilities.
Now, those can all be meaningful ways to serve.
But here's something important. Being busy with religious activities doesn't automatically mean we're growing spiritually.
We still need time for Scripture.
For prayer.
For repentance.
And for examining our motives.
Now, let me ask you something. Are you spending more time doing things for God than seeking to know Him through His Word?
Now, that's not a question meant to create guilt.
It's an invitation to examine our priorities.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Spiritual transformation is not measured simply by how busy we are. It is reflected in our growing faith, obedience, and Christlike character.
PART FIFTEEN — PREPARING OUR HEARTS FOR A NEW YEAR Now, let's bring this back to our weekly theme.
Leaving the old behind. Preparing for a new year.
Now, I want you to think about something. When we prepare for a new year, we often make plans for what we want to accomplish.
And that's not wrong.
But what if we also made time to examine our spiritual lives?
What if we asked... Lord, where do I need to grow?
What sinful patterns do I need to address?
What attitudes need correction?
And how can I become more faithful in the responsibilities You've given me?
Now, here's something important. We don't need to wait for January first to begin responding to God's Word.
We can begin today.
Through prayer.
Through repentance.
Through Scripture.
And through taking practical steps toward obedience.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The most meaningful preparation for a new year may begin with examining our hearts before God.
PAUSE AND PRAY — CREATE IN ME A CLEAN HEART Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about one area of your life where you want to grow spiritually.
Maybe it's patience.
Maybe it's humility.
Maybe it's self-control.
Maybe it's forgiveness.
Or maybe it's learning to trust God more consistently.
Now, take a moment to bring that before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your mercy and grace. Thank You for the saving work of Jesus Christ. And thank You for the work of the Holy Spirit in the lives of believers. Lord, we acknowledge that we cannot transform ourselves through human determination alone. We need Your grace. Your truth. And Your renewing work. Father, reveal the areas where we need to grow. Help us recognize sinful attitudes and habits. Give us humility to repent. And wisdom to live according to Your Word. Teach us to respond with patience. Kindness. Honesty. And compassion. May our lives increasingly reflect the character of Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
PART SIXTEEN — THE NEXT STEP IN SPIRITUAL GROWTH Now, before we move into our reflection questions, I want us to consider something practical.
Because sometimes we hear a message about transformation and immediately feel pressure to change everything.
But perhaps a more meaningful starting point is to identify one area where you need to grow.
Not ten things.
Not twenty things.
One.
Maybe you need to develop a more consistent prayer routine.
Maybe you need to become more intentional about reading Scripture.
Maybe you need to address a habit that has been affecting your relationships.
Or maybe you need to seek accountability from a trusted Christian friend.
Now, here's something important. Practical steps don't replace the work of God.
But they can be part of how we respond faithfully to His Word.
Now, I want you to remember something. Spiritual transformation is God's work, and believers are called to respond through faith, repentance, and obedience.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... When I think about changing my life, do I focus more on outward accomplishments or inward spiritual growth? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Is there an attitude, habit, or pattern of thinking that needs to be examined in light of God's Word? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... Which quality of the fruit of the Spirit do I most want to grow in? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What is one practical step I can take to become more intentional about prayer, Scripture, repentance, or Christian accountability? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE SOURCE OF NEW LIFE Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because genuine spiritual renewal is inseparable from Him.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through faith in Him, sinners receive forgiveness and new life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation by becoming more patient.
We don't earn it by developing better habits.
And we don't earn it by accomplishing spiritual goals.
Salvation is God's gracious gift through faith in Jesus Christ.
And the Holy Spirit works in believers, transforming us as we grow in faith and obedience.
Now, that's the heart of the gospel.
Not simply becoming a better version of ourselves.
But receiving new life through Jesus Christ.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. God's grace doesn't simply call us to improve our outward behavior. Through Jesus Christ and the work of the Holy Spirit, He brings new life and teaches us to grow in truth, holiness, and love.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because real transformation begins with the work of God.
And it should become evident in the way we live.
LIVING IT OUT — A HEART MADE NEW Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... A Heart Made New.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... One area of my spiritual life where I want to grow.
Second... One attitude or habit I need to examine according to God's Word.
Third... One Scripture passage I can study to help guide my growth.
And fourth... One practical step I can take this week.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom.
Thank Him for His grace.
And seek His help as you continue growing in faith.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, one area of my heart where I need Your renewing work is...
Our second prompt is... Help me recognize the attitudes or habits that do not align with Your Word, especially...
And our third prompt is... As I prepare for a new year, help me grow spiritually by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. Through Jesus Christ, God has given me new life. I will seek His truth, respond to His Word, and continue growing through the work of the Holy Spirit.
Now, say that again. Through Jesus Christ, God has given me new life. I will seek His truth, respond to His Word, and continue growing through the work of the Holy Spirit.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Romans chapter 12, verse 2. "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about what it means to have your mind renewed according to God's truth.
Maybe you'll spend time reading Scripture.
Maybe you'll pray about an attitude that needs correction.
Maybe you'll seek accountability.
Or maybe you'll take a practical step toward changing a sinful habit.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHAT NEEDS TO CHANGE WITHIN? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The fire is burning.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied today.
Now, I want to ask you something. If God were to reveal one area where you need to grow spiritually, what do you think it might be?
Maybe patience.
Maybe humility.
Maybe forgiveness.
Maybe self-control.
Or maybe a deeper commitment to prayer and Scripture. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would it look like to approach that area with repentance, faith, and a willingness to grow?
Maybe it would involve an honest conversation.
Maybe it would involve seeking support.
Maybe it would involve changing a habit.
Or maybe it would involve spending more meaningful time studying God's Word. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. You don't have to become perfect overnight.
But you can continue seeking the Lord.
You can continue learning.
And you can continue growing in faith.
CLOSING REFLECTION — A HEART MADE NEW Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
As we prepare for a new year, it's natural to think about change.
We think about goals.
Responsibilities.
Habits.
And things we want to accomplish.
But I want you to remember something. The most important transformation isn't simply changing our schedule.
Or improving our appearance.
Or accomplishing more things.
It's the spiritual renewal that comes through Jesus Christ.
A renewed heart.
A renewed mind.
And a growing desire to live according to God's Word.
Now, that doesn't mean every struggle will disappear.
And it doesn't mean we'll never make mistakes.
But it does mean we can continue growing in faith.
We can continue repenting.
We can continue learning.
And we can continue pursuing Jesus Christ.
So as you look toward the future...
Don't simply ask what you want to accomplish.
Ask how you need to grow.
Ask what attitudes need to change.
Ask what sinful habits need to be addressed.
And ask how you can become more faithful in the responsibilities God has given you.
Because the greatest new beginning isn't simply a new year.
It's the new life we receive through Jesus Christ.
And the continuing work of the Holy Spirit as we grow in Him.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for the promise of spiritual renewal. And thank You for the saving work of Jesus Christ. Lord, help us examine our hearts honestly. Reveal the areas where we need to grow. Give us humility to acknowledge sin. Courage to repent. And wisdom to walk in obedience. Father, help us resist the sinful patterns of this world. Renew our minds through Your truth. And teach us to live in ways that reflect the character of Jesus Christ. Help us grow in love. Joy. Peace. Patience. Kindness. And self-control. Lord, as we prepare for a new year, help us remember that true transformation begins with Your work in our lives. May everything we do bring glory to You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY FOUR Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Twelve, Day Three!
And I hope today's lesson has reminded you that genuine transformation begins with the work of God.
Not simply with our own determination.
Tomorrow, we're continuing our final week with a lesson called... Faithful Steps Forward — Trusting God One Day at a Time.
We'll explore what Scripture teaches about daily faithfulness, wise decisions, and learning to trust God without needing to know everything the future holds.
Until then, remember... A new year may bring new opportunities. But the greatest new beginning is found in Jesus Christ.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Faithful Steps Forward: Trusting God One Day at a Time
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WHEN YOU CAN'T SEE THE WHOLE ROAD Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today.
Today is Week Twelve, Day Four. And we're continuing our final week of this twelve-week Bible study journey.
Our theme this week is... Leaving the Old Behind — Preparing for a New Year.
On Day One, we talked about trusting God with what comes next. On Day Two, we studied what it means to let go of yesterday and walk forward in grace. And yesterday, we talked about allowing God to transform us from within.
Now, today, we're taking those lessons and bringing them into our everyday lives.
Because it's one thing to say we trust God.
But it's another thing to continue walking when we don't know exactly where the road is leading.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever been driving somewhere unfamiliar at night?
Maybe the road was dark. Maybe there weren't many streetlights. And maybe you couldn't see very far ahead.
But your headlights gave you enough light to see the road immediately in front of you.
You couldn't see every turn. You couldn't see every mile. But you could see enough to keep moving carefully.
Now, I think that's a helpful picture of something we experience in our walk with God.
Sometimes we want to know the entire plan.
We want to know how everything will turn out.
We want to know whether the decisions we're making will lead to the outcomes we're hoping for.
And sometimes we want God to show us what the next five years will look like before we're willing to take the next step.
But Scripture calls us to something different.
It calls us to trust God. To seek His wisdom. To live according to His Word. And to remain faithful with the responsibilities in front of us.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to know every step of the journey to be faithful with the step God has placed before you today.
And that brings us to our lesson. Faithful Steps Forward — Trusting God One Day at a Time.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for Your faithfulness. Your mercy. And Your grace. Lord, today we're studying what it means to trust You one day at a time. You know the decisions we're facing. You know the responsibilities we're carrying. And You know the things about the future that remain uncertain to us. Father, help us seek Your wisdom. Teach us to live according to Your Word. Give us patience when answers take time. Courage when obedience is difficult. And humility when our plans don't unfold the way we expected. Help us remember that our greatest confidence is found in Jesus Christ. May today's study strengthen our faith and guide our steps. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S FIRST SCRIPTURE — PSALM 37:23–24 Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 37. We're going to read verses 23 and 24.
Before we begin, let's understand the setting. Psalm 37 is a Psalm of David.
And throughout this Psalm, David encourages God's people not to become consumed by envy or frustration when those who do wrong appear to prosper.
Instead, he calls them to trust the Lord. To do good. And to remain faithful.
Now, let's read Psalm 37, verses 23 and 24, from the King James Version. "The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way. Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand."
Now, I want you to hear that again. "The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD..."
And then... "Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down..."
Now, those are encouraging words.
But I want us to understand something important. This Psalm isn't promising that faithful people will never experience difficulty.
In fact, it acknowledges that a person may fall.
But it points toward the Lord's sustaining care.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. Sometimes we assume that if we're following God, everything should happen smoothly.
But Scripture doesn't teach that.
Faithful people experience hardship.
They face uncertainty.
And they sometimes struggle.
But they are called to continue trusting the Lord.
TODAY'S SECOND SCRIPTURE — MATTHEW 6:33–34 Now, let's turn to Matthew chapter 6. We're going to read verses 33 and 34.
These verses come from Jesus' Sermon on the Mount.
And in this section, Jesus is teaching His followers about worry, daily needs, and the importance of seeking God's kingdom.
Let's read Matthew chapter 6, verses 33 and 34, from the King James Version. "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
Now, I want you to focus on those words. "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness..."
And then... "Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
Now, Jesus is teaching His followers to prioritize God's kingdom rather than allowing anxiety about material needs to dominate their lives.
He isn't forbidding responsible planning.
And He isn't telling people to ignore genuine needs.
But He is calling them to trust their heavenly Father and focus on faithful living.
Now, that brings us to today's key truth.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH God calls us to seek His kingdom, trust His faithfulness, and respond responsibly to today's opportunities and challenges without allowing tomorrow's uncertainty to control us.
Now, let's walk through this together.
PART ONE — GOD CARES ABOUT OUR DAILY WALK Now, let's begin with something important.
Sometimes we think God is only concerned with the major moments of our lives.
The big decisions.
The major opportunities.
The life-changing circumstances.
But Scripture teaches us that our everyday conduct matters.
How we speak.
How we treat people.
How we handle responsibilities.
And how we respond when things don't go our way.
Now, I want you to think about something. Most of our lives are not made up of extraordinary moments.
They're made up of ordinary days.
We wake up. We go to work. We care for our families. We handle responsibilities. And we make decisions.
Now, those ordinary moments provide opportunities for faithfulness.
We can demonstrate honesty.
Patience.
Kindness.
And obedience to God's Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithfulness isn't limited to extraordinary moments. It is often demonstrated through ordinary decisions.
PART TWO — WHAT DOES IT MEAN FOR GOD TO ORDER OUR STEPS? Now, let's return to Psalm 37, verse 23.
"The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD..."
Now, I want you to think about those words.
God's sovereignty.
His wisdom.
And His care for His people.
Now, here's something important. This verse doesn't mean that every decision we make is automatically wise.
It doesn't mean every desire we have comes from God.
And it doesn't mean that every opportunity is something we should pursue.
We still need discernment.
We still need to study Scripture.
And we still need to seek wise counsel.
Now, sometimes people say... If the door opens, it must be God's will.
But an open opportunity isn't always proof that something is right.
We need to evaluate our decisions according to God's Word.
We need to consider our responsibilities.
And we need to use wisdom.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Trusting God's guidance doesn't remove our responsibility to make thoughtful, biblically informed decisions.
PART THREE — THE NEXT STEP MAY BE SMALL Now, I want to talk about something that I think can encourage many of us.
Sometimes we become discouraged because the next step seems too small.
Maybe you're trying to rebuild a relationship.
Maybe you're working toward a goal.
Maybe you're developing a new habit.
Or maybe you're simply trying to become more consistent in your spiritual life.
And the progress feels slow.
Now, I want you to think about something. Not every meaningful step is dramatic.
Sometimes faithfulness looks like reading one chapter of Scripture.
Having one honest conversation.
Making one responsible decision.
Or offering one act of kindness.
Now, here's something important. Small actions aren't automatically insignificant.
They can become part of a larger pattern of faithful living.
Now, let me ask you something. What is one small step you've been overlooking because it doesn't seem important enough? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to accomplish everything today to make a meaningful step forward.
PART FOUR — SEEK FIRST THE KINGDOM OF GOD Now, let's return to Matthew chapter 6, verse 33.
Jesus says: "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness..."
Now, I want you to notice the priority.
Seek first the kingdom of God.
Now, that doesn't mean we neglect our families.
It doesn't mean we ignore our work.
And it doesn't mean we abandon practical responsibilities.
Instead, it means our relationship with God and our commitment to His righteousness should shape the way we approach those responsibilities.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. What usually receives your attention first?
Your worries?
Your schedule?
Your responsibilities?
Or your relationship with God?
Now, I'm not suggesting that every person must follow the exact same daily routine.
Some people work early mornings.
Some care for children.
Some have demanding schedules.
And some face health limitations.
But we can all seek meaningful ways to prioritize God.
Through Scripture.
Prayer.
Worship.
And obedience.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Seeking God's kingdom first means allowing His truth and righteousness to guide the priorities of our lives.
PART FIVE — TOMORROW HAS ENOUGH CONCERNS OF ITS OWN Now, let's look at Matthew chapter 6, verse 34.
Jesus says: "Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
Now, I want you to think about that.
Jesus recognizes that each day has its own troubles.
He doesn't pretend that life is free from difficulty.
And He doesn't promise that tomorrow will be easy.
Instead, He teaches His followers not to become consumed by anxious preoccupation with the future.
Now, here's something important. There's a difference between planning for tomorrow and worrying about tomorrow.
Planning asks... What responsibilities do I need to prepare for?
What information do I need?
What action should I take?
But worry can become a cycle of imagining every possible negative outcome.
And sometimes that cycle leaves us feeling overwhelmed.
Now, I want you to remember something. Responsible preparation can be wise. But we don't have to carry every possible future problem as though it has already happened.
PART SIX — WHEN YOUR MIND WON'T STOP THINKING Now, I want to speak to someone who may be struggling with worry.
Maybe you lie awake at night thinking about everything that needs to be done.
Maybe you replay conversations.
Maybe you're worried about finances.
Maybe you're concerned about someone you love.
Or maybe you're facing a situation with no clear answer.
Now, here's something important. Experiencing anxiety doesn't automatically mean you're failing spiritually.
Our emotions are affected by many things.
And some people experience anxiety that requires professional care.
Seeking appropriate support is not a rejection of faith.
But Scripture also encourages us to bring our concerns before God.
Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 4. We're going to read verses 6 and 7. The King James Version says: "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."
Now, I want you to notice something. Paul directs believers toward prayer.
And he connects that prayer with the peace of God through Jesus Christ.
Now, this doesn't mean that every anxious feeling will disappear immediately.
But it reminds us that we can bring our concerns before God.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We can pray about our concerns while also taking responsible action and receiving appropriate support.
PART SEVEN — GOD'S WORD IS A LAMP Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 119. We're going to read verse 105. The King James Version says: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
Now, I love that picture.
A lamp.
A light.
Something that helps us see where we're going.
Now, I want you to think back to the example we talked about at the beginning of today's lesson.
Driving down a dark road.
You may not be able to see every mile ahead.
But you have enough light to travel carefully.
Now, Scripture is not a personalized map that tells us every detail of our future.
But it does reveal God's truth.
It teaches us about His character.
It instructs us in righteousness.
And it gives us wisdom for faithful living.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes we spend so much time asking God for information He hasn't revealed that we neglect the truth He has already given us in Scripture.
We want to know exactly what will happen next year.
But we may be ignoring clear instructions about honesty, compassion, humility, or forgiveness today.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God's Word may not reveal every detail of tomorrow, but it provides the truth we need for faithful living today.
PART EIGHT — ASK GOD FOR WISDOM Now, let's turn to James chapter 1. We're going to read verse 5. The King James Version says: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him."
Now, that's a beautiful encouragement.
James tells believers to ask God for wisdom.
Now, I want you to think about something. How often do we ask God to remove a difficult decision when we also need wisdom to handle it?
Maybe you're facing a financial decision.
Maybe you're considering a new responsibility.
Maybe you're trying to resolve a disagreement.
Or maybe you're uncertain about how to respond to a difficult situation.
Now, asking God for wisdom doesn't mean we'll always receive an immediate or unmistakable answer.
But it does mean we can approach Him in prayer.
And we can seek to make decisions according to His Word.
Now, here's something important. Wisdom also involves gathering appropriate information.
Considering consequences.
And listening to trustworthy counsel.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful decision-making involves prayer, Scripture, humility, and responsible discernment.
PART NINE — WHEN GOD'S TIMING ISN'T YOUR TIMING Now, let's talk about something that can be difficult.
Waiting.
Because sometimes we know what we want to happen.
We've prayed about it.
We've prepared.
We've taken responsible steps.
And yet, nothing seems to be changing.
Now, I want you to think about something. Waiting doesn't automatically mean we've done something wrong.
And a delay isn't always evidence that God is displeased with us.
Sometimes circumstances are outside our control.
Sometimes more information is needed.
And sometimes we simply don't know why something is taking longer than expected.
Now, here's something important. We should be careful about claiming to know God's hidden reasons for every delay.
Scripture doesn't give us that kind of certainty.
But it does call us to trust His character.
To remain faithful.
And to continue doing what is right.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. When we cannot control the timing of an outcome, we can still seek to honor God in the way we wait.
PART TEN — FAITHFUL IN LITTLE THINGS Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 16. We're going to read verse 10. The King James Version says: "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much."
Now, Jesus is teaching about faithfulness and the proper use of resources.
And He emphasizes that character is revealed in seemingly small matters.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we become so focused on the big opportunities we hope to receive that we neglect the responsibilities we already have.
We want greater influence.
But we struggle with faithfulness in ordinary commitments.
We want more resources.
But we may not be managing what we already have responsibly.
We want larger opportunities to serve.
But we overlook the people who need our help right now.
Now, here's something important. This verse isn't a guarantee that being faithful with small things will automatically result in wealth or promotion.
But it does teach us that integrity matters in every responsibility.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithfulness in ordinary responsibilities is valuable because it reflects our character before God.
PART ELEVEN — WHEN YOU MAKE A MISTAKE Now, let's return to Psalm 37, verse 24.
"Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand."
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we become afraid to move forward because we're worried about making a mistake.
Maybe we've made decisions in the past that didn't turn out well.
Maybe we've experienced disappointment.
Or maybe we're afraid of failing again.
Now, here's something important. Following Jesus Christ doesn't mean we become incapable of making mistakes.
We still need wisdom.
We still need humility.
And we still need to take responsibility for our actions.
But we don't have to build our entire identity around the idea that we must never fail.
Now, if we sin, we're called to repent.
If we make a poor decision, we should learn from it.
And if we need help, we can seek it.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful perseverance doesn't mean never stumbling. It means continuing to seek the Lord with humility and obedience.
PART TWELVE — ONE DAY AT A TIME DOESN'T MEAN NO PLANNING Now, I want to clarify something.
Because when we talk about trusting God one day at a time, someone might think that means we shouldn't plan for the future.
But that's not what Scripture teaches.
Planning can be wise.
Saving money responsibly can be wise.
Preparing for appointments can be wise.
And organizing our responsibilities can be wise.
Now, let's turn to James chapter 4. We're going to read verses 13 through 15. The King James Version says: "Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that."
Now, James isn't condemning responsible planning.
He's warning against arrogant confidence in our control over the future.
Now, here's something important. We can make plans.
We can prepare.
And we can take responsible action.
But we should remain humble before God's will.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Trusting God one day at a time means preparing responsibly without pretending we control every outcome.
PART THIRTEEN — WHEN LIFE FEELS OVERWHELMING Now, I want to speak to someone who may feel like they're carrying too much.
Maybe you're responsible for your family.
Your work.
Your finances.
Your health.
Or other people who depend on you.
And sometimes it feels like there's simply too much to manage.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to handle every responsibility without help.
Sometimes faithful stewardship involves asking for assistance.
Delegating a task.
Setting a boundary.
Or recognizing that you have limitations.
Now, here's something important. We should be careful not to confuse being constantly busy with being faithful.
Sometimes we take on more than we can responsibly manage.
And sometimes we need to reevaluate our priorities.
Now, let me ask you something. Is there a responsibility you're carrying that needs to be handled differently?
Maybe you need help.
Maybe you need a better plan.
Maybe you need to say no to something.
Or maybe you need to make time for rest. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful living includes wise stewardship of our time, energy, relationships, and responsibilities.
PART FOURTEEN — FIX YOUR EYES ON JESUS Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 12. We're going to read verses 1 and 2. The King James Version says: "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."
Now, I want you to focus on those words. "Looking unto Jesus..."
Now, that's the center of Christian perseverance.
Not simply believing in ourselves.
Not simply becoming more disciplined.
And not simply working harder.
But continuing to look toward Jesus Christ.
The One who endured the cross.
The One who rose again.
And the One in whom our salvation is found.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our ultimate confidence is not in our ability to control the journey, but in Jesus Christ, the author and finisher of our faith.
PAUSE AND PRAY — LORD, GUIDE MY STEPS Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about one decision or responsibility that's been weighing on your mind.
Maybe it's something you need to do today.
Maybe it's a conversation you've been postponing.
Maybe it's a financial decision.
Or maybe it's a responsibility you've been avoiding because it feels overwhelming.
Now, take a moment to bring that before the Lord. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word. Thank You for Your faithfulness. And thank You for the wisdom You provide. Lord, You know the responsibilities we're carrying. You know the decisions we're facing. And You know the uncertainties that concern us. Father, help us seek Your kingdom first. Teach us to make wise decisions. Give us patience when answers take time. Courage when obedience is difficult. And humility when we need help. Lord, keep us from becoming consumed by tomorrow's worries. Help us respond faithfully to today's responsibilities. And remind us that our greatest hope is found in Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
PART FIFTEEN — THE NEXT FAITHFUL STEP Now, before we move into our reflection questions, I want us to consider something practical.
Sometimes we become overwhelmed because we're thinking about everything at once.
The entire week.
The entire month.
The entire year.
And every possible problem that might arise.
But here's something I want you to think about. What is one faithful step you can take today?
Maybe it's making an important phone call.
Maybe it's completing a responsibility you've been postponing.
Maybe it's spending time in prayer.
Maybe it's reading Scripture.
Or maybe it's asking someone for help.
Now, here's something important. That one step may not solve everything.
It may not remove every concern.
And it may not produce immediate results.
But it can still be a meaningful act of faithfulness.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. You don't have to solve tomorrow today. You can seek God's wisdom and respond faithfully to the responsibilities in front of you.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What future concern has been taking up more of my attention than it should? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... How can I seek God's kingdom first in the responsibilities I already have? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... Is there an ordinary responsibility I've been overlooking because I'm focused on something bigger? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... What is one faithful step I can take today without needing to know the entire outcome? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — OUR HOPE IS IN JESUS Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because He's the foundation of our faith.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through faith in Him, sinners receive forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation by making perfect decisions.
We don't earn it by completing every responsibility.
And we don't earn it by never worrying.
Salvation is God's gracious gift through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our daily obedience should flow from that relationship.
Now, that's the heart of the gospel.
Not simply becoming better planners.
Not simply becoming more productive.
But living as followers of Jesus Christ.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. God doesn't ask us to control tomorrow. He calls us to seek His kingdom, trust His faithfulness, and walk in obedience today.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because the future may be uncertain.
But we can continue seeking the Lord one day at a time.
LIVING IT OUT — ONE FAITHFUL STEP Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... One Faithful Step at a Time.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... One responsibility I need to address today.
Second... One future concern I need to bring before God in prayer.
Third... One way I can seek God's kingdom first in my daily routine.
And fourth... One practical step I can take without knowing the entire outcome.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Ask God for wisdom.
Thank Him for His faithfulness.
And seek His help as you continue walking forward.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, one area where I need to trust You more consistently is...
Our second prompt is... Help me focus on today's responsibilities instead of becoming overwhelmed by...
And our third prompt is... The next faithful step I can take is...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will seek God's kingdom first, trust His faithfulness, and respond responsibly to today's opportunities and challenges. My hope is in Jesus Christ, not in my ability to control the future.
Now, say that again. I will seek God's kingdom first, trust His faithfulness, and respond responsibly to today's opportunities and challenges. My hope is in Jesus Christ, not in my ability to control the future.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Matthew chapter 6, verse 33. "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about what it means to seek God's kingdom first.
Maybe you'll begin your day with prayer.
Maybe you'll make time to study Scripture.
Maybe you'll handle a difficult responsibility with greater patience.
Or maybe you'll take one meaningful step toward something you've been postponing.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHAT IS YOUR NEXT STEP? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The flames are burning.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied today.
Now, I want to ask you something. What is one area of your life where you've been waiting to know the entire outcome before taking the next step?
Maybe it's a decision.
Maybe it's a responsibility.
Maybe it's a conversation.
Or maybe it's a goal you've been afraid to pursue. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What would it look like to approach that situation with prayer, wisdom, and faithful action?
Maybe it would mean gathering more information.
Maybe it would mean seeking counsel.
Maybe it would mean taking one practical step.
Or maybe it would mean recognizing that waiting is the wisest choice for now. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. Faithfulness doesn't always mean moving quickly.
Sometimes it means waiting patiently.
Sometimes it means preparing carefully.
And sometimes it means taking action.
But in every season, we're called to seek the Lord.
CLOSING REFLECTION — ONE DAY AT A TIME Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Sometimes we become so focused on tomorrow that we overlook today.
We're thinking about what might happen.
What could go wrong.
What decisions we'll need to make.
And what challenges may be ahead.
But Jesus reminds us to seek first the kingdom of God.
And not to become consumed by tomorrow's worries.
Now, that doesn't mean we stop planning.
It doesn't mean we ignore responsibilities.
And it doesn't mean we pretend that life is easy.
It means we approach each day with faith.
We seek God's wisdom.
We live according to His Word.
And we trust His faithfulness.
So as you prepare for the year ahead...
Don't allow uncertainty to prevent you from doing what is right today.
Don't become so focused on big opportunities that you overlook ordinary responsibilities.
And don't assume that faithfulness requires you to have every answer.
Instead, take the next faithful step.
One decision.
One responsibility.
One day at a time.
And keep looking toward Jesus Christ.
Because He is the author and finisher of our faith.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for Your faithfulness. And thank You for the hope we have through Jesus Christ. Lord, help us seek Your kingdom first. Teach us to trust You with the future. And give us wisdom for the responsibilities in front of us. Father, help us make thoughtful decisions. Give us patience when answers take time. Courage when obedience is difficult. And humility when we need assistance. Lord, keep us from becoming consumed by worry. Help us prepare responsibly while remembering that our plans are subject to Your will. And may our lives reflect the truth and love of Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY FIVE Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Twelve, Day Four!
And I hope today's lesson has reminded you that faithful living happens one day at a time.
Tomorrow, we're continuing our final week with a lesson called... Gratitude for the Journey — Remembering God's Faithfulness.
We'll look back at the lessons we've learned, reflect on God's goodness, and explore how gratitude can help us approach the future with faith.
Until then, remember... You don't have to see the entire road to take the next faithful step.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Gratitude for the Journey: Remembering God's Faithfulness
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — LOOKING BACK WITH A GRATEFUL HEART Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're joining me today.
Today is Week Twelve, Day Five. And can you believe it? We're nearing the end of our twelve-week Bible study journey together.
This week, our theme has been... Leaving the Old Behind — Preparing for a New Year.
On Day One, we talked about trusting God with what comes next. On Day Two, we studied letting go of yesterday and walking forward in grace. On Day Three, we explored what it means to allow God to transform us from within. And yesterday, we talked about taking faithful steps forward, one day at a time.
Now, today, I want us to do something a little different. I want us to look back.
Not to become trapped in the past. Not to replay every disappointment. And not to wish we could change things that have already happened.
But to remember.
To remember what we've learned. To remember the people who've encouraged us. To remember the prayers we've prayed. And most importantly... To remember the faithfulness of God.
Now, let me ask you something. Have you ever reached the end of a difficult season and realized just how much you'd been through?
Maybe while you were walking through it, you were simply trying to make it through each day.
You were handling responsibilities. Making difficult decisions. Praying for strength. And trying to understand what was happening.
But then, when you finally had a moment to look back, you began recognizing things you hadn't noticed before.
Maybe someone showed up when you needed encouragement. Maybe a friend helped you through a difficult situation. Maybe you found comfort in a passage of Scripture. Maybe you learned something about patience. Or maybe you realized that even though the season was painful, you were still able to continue moving forward.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude doesn't require us to pretend that everything we've experienced was good.
It doesn't mean we have to be thankful for abuse. For injustice. For illness. Or for the loss of someone we love.
But even in a world where suffering is real, we can recognize God's goodness and give thanks for His mercy.
Now, that's what we're studying today. Our lesson is called... Gratitude for the Journey — Remembering God's Faithfulness.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for Your mercy. Your patience. Your love. And Your faithfulness. Lord, today we're taking time to remember Your goodness. Help us recognize the blessings we may have overlooked. Teach us to give thanks without denying the reality of our struggles. Give comfort to those who are grieving. Strength to those who are weary. And encouragement to those who are facing uncertainty. Father, help us remember what You've revealed about Yourself through Scripture. And may our gratitude lead us toward deeper worship, humility, and obedience. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S FIRST SCRIPTURE — PSALM 103:1–5 Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 103. We're going to read verses 1 through 5.
This Psalm is attributed to David. And it begins with a personal call to praise the Lord.
David reminds himself not to forget God's benefits.
Now, that's interesting. Because sometimes we think gratitude is something that simply happens when life is going well.
But David deliberately calls himself to remember.
Let's read Psalm 103, verses 1 through 5, from the King James Version. "Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's."
Now, I want you to hear verse 2 again. "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:"
Now, that's the heart of today's lesson. Don't forget.
Don't forget God's mercy.
Don't forget His forgiveness.
Don't forget His lovingkindness.
And don't forget His faithfulness.
Now, I want to clarify something. Psalm 103 celebrates God's power to heal and restore. But it should not be interpreted as a promise that every believer will be healed of every illness during this earthly life.
Scripture acknowledges that faithful people still experience sickness, suffering, and death.
Our ultimate hope rests in God's saving work through Jesus Christ and the resurrection to come.
Now, that brings us to something important. Gratitude is not based on the idea that our circumstances will always be comfortable.
It's grounded in the goodness and mercy of God.
TODAY'S SECOND SCRIPTURE — 1 THESSALONIANS 5:16–18 Now, let's turn to 1 Thessalonians chapter 5. We're going to read verses 16 through 18.
The apostle Paul is giving instructions to believers about Christian living.
And these verses are short. But they're powerful.
Let's read them from the King James Version. "Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you."
Now, I want you to notice something. Paul says... "In every thing give thanks..."
He doesn't say that every circumstance is good.
And he doesn't tell believers to celebrate wrongdoing or suffering.
Instead, he calls them to maintain a life of prayer, rejoicing, and thanksgiving.
Now, that's important. Because gratitude is not the same thing as pretending.
We can acknowledge pain. We can grieve. We can seek help. And we can still give thanks to God for His mercy and faithfulness.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Biblical gratitude means remembering God's goodness, acknowledging His gifts, and giving thanks for His faithfulness without denying the reality of life's difficulties.
Now, let's walk through this together.
PART ONE — WHY WE NEED TO REMEMBER Now, let's begin with something simple.
Human beings forget things.
We forget appointments. We forget conversations. We forget where we put our keys.
And sometimes, we forget the ways we've been helped.
Now, I want you to think about something. When life becomes difficult, our attention naturally moves toward the problem.
We think about what needs to be fixed. What needs to change. And what we're worried about.
Now, that's understandable.
But sometimes, if we're not intentional, our problems can become the only things we notice.
We forget the encouragement we've received.
We forget the lessons we've learned.
And we forget the blessings that are still present.
Now, that's why remembering is important.
It helps us recognize that our current circumstances are not the entire story.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude often begins with intentionally remembering what is good, true, and worthy of praise.
PART TWO — DON'T FORGET HIS BENEFITS Now, let's return to Psalm 103, verse 2.
"Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:"
Now, I want you to think about that word. Benefits.
David goes on to speak about forgiveness. Healing. Redemption. Lovingkindness. And mercy.
Now, those are far greater than material possessions.
Sometimes when we think about blessings, we immediately think about things we own.
Our homes. Our vehicles. Our finances. Or opportunities we've received.
And it's appropriate to thank God for material provision.
But Scripture reminds us that God's greatest gifts are not measured by money.
Forgiveness. Mercy. Grace. And salvation through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The greatest blessings of God are not always the things we can hold in our hands.
PART THREE — GRATITUDE ISN'T DENIAL Now, I want to talk about something important.
Because sometimes people hear messages about gratitude and feel pressured to pretend they're happy.
Maybe they're grieving.
Maybe they're dealing with illness.
Maybe they're facing financial hardship.
Or maybe they're simply exhausted.
And someone tells them... Just be thankful.
Now, gratitude is biblical. But we need to approach it with compassion.
Because Scripture gives us room for lament.
For sorrow.
For honest questions.
And for bringing our pain before God.
Now, here's something important. We can be thankful for God's faithfulness while still acknowledging that something hurts.
We can appreciate the people who support us while still grieving someone we've lost.
And we can recognize blessings while still working to address difficult circumstances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude and grief can exist together.
PART FOUR — REMEMBER THE WILDERNESS Now, let's turn to Deuteronomy chapter 8. We're going to read verse 2. The King James Version says: "And thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no."
Now, let's understand the setting. Moses is speaking to Israel before they enter the promised land.
And he reminds them of their years in the wilderness.
Now, those years weren't easy.
They involved hardship. Dependence. Testing. And lessons about obedience.
But Moses tells them to remember.
Now, here's something important. Remembering the wilderness doesn't mean pretending it was comfortable.
It means recognizing what God had done and what His people had learned.
Now, I want you to think about your own journey.
Are there difficult seasons that taught you something important?
Maybe you learned patience.
Maybe you learned to ask for help.
Maybe you discovered the importance of wise boundaries.
Or maybe you learned that you needed to depend more deeply on God's Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We can remember difficult seasons honestly while recognizing the lessons and mercies that accompanied them.
PART FIVE — WHEN GOD'S FAITHFULNESS LOOKS DIFFERENT THAN WE EXPECTED Now, I want you to think about something.
Sometimes we pray for a particular outcome.
We pray for healing.
We pray for restoration.
We pray for an opportunity.
Or we pray for a difficult circumstance to change.
And sometimes the outcome isn't what we hoped for.
Now, that can be deeply painful.
And I want to make something clear. We shouldn't assume we know God's hidden reasons for every disappointment.
Scripture doesn't give us permission to explain every tragedy as though we understand exactly why it happened.
But Scripture does reveal God's character.
His holiness.
His mercy.
His wisdom.
And His faithfulness.
Now, here's something important. Our trust in God shouldn't depend entirely on receiving the outcome we wanted.
Instead, it should be rooted in who He has revealed Himself to be.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. God's faithfulness is greater than our ability to understand every circumstance.
PART SIX — REMEMBERING GOD'S WORKS Now, let's turn to Psalm chapter 77. We're going to read verses 11 and 12. The King James Version says: "I will remember the works of the LORD: surely I will remember thy wonders of old. I will meditate also of all thy work, and talk of thy doings."
Now, I want you to notice something. The writer makes a deliberate decision to remember.
"I will remember..."
Now, Psalm 77 begins with distress.
The writer is troubled.
He cries out to God.
And he struggles with difficult questions.
But then he turns his attention toward remembering God's mighty works.
Now, that's meaningful.
Because remembering doesn't erase his distress.
But it helps him direct his attention toward what God has revealed through His actions.
Now, I want you to think about something. When you're struggling, what truths from Scripture help you remember God's faithfulness?
Maybe it's the Exodus.
Maybe it's God's covenant promises.
Maybe it's the birth of Jesus Christ.
Or maybe it's His death and resurrection.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The clearest foundation for remembering God's faithfulness is what He has revealed through Scripture, especially through Jesus Christ.
PART SEVEN — THE TEN LEPERS Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 17.
We're going to look at the account of Jesus healing ten men with leprosy.
These men were suffering from a serious condition that affected their lives and their place in society.
They called out to Jesus for mercy.
And He instructed them to go show themselves to the priests.
As they went, they were cleansed.
Now, let's read Luke chapter 17, verses 15 through 19. The King James Version says: "And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole."
Now, I want you to think about that. Ten men were cleansed.
But one returned to give thanks.
Now, Jesus draws attention to the gratitude of this man.
And the fact that he was a Samaritan is significant in the setting of the story.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. How often do we receive something good and immediately move on to the next concern?
Maybe someone helps us.
Maybe a prayer is answered.
Maybe a difficult responsibility is completed.
And before long, we're focused on something else.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude invites us to recognize God's gifts rather than treating them as things we're automatically entitled to receive.
PART EIGHT — DON'T OVERLOOK THE ORDINARY BLESSINGS Now, let's talk about something practical.
Because sometimes we're waiting for something extraordinary before we feel thankful.
A major breakthrough.
A big opportunity.
Or a dramatic change.
But many meaningful blessings are found in ordinary life.
A conversation with someone we love.
A meal shared with family.
A quiet moment of rest.
A friend who checks on us.
Or someone who offers help when we need it.
Now, I want you to think about something. What ordinary blessing have you overlooked recently?
Maybe it's something you experience every day.
Something so familiar that you've stopped noticing it.
Now, here's something important. Recognizing ordinary blessings doesn't mean ignoring serious problems.
But it can help us develop a more balanced and grateful perspective.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Not every blessing arrives with a dramatic announcement. Some of God's gifts are found in ordinary moments.
PART NINE — EVERY GOOD GIFT Now, let's turn to James chapter 1. We're going to read verse 17. The King James Version says: "Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning."
Now, I want you to think about those words. "Every good gift..."
Now, James reminds us that God is the source of what is good.
And he emphasizes God's unchanging character.
Now, here's something important. We shouldn't assume that every event in our lives is good.
Sin is real.
Suffering is real.
And injustice is real.
But God Himself is good.
And His character doesn't change.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our gratitude is ultimately directed toward the goodness of God, not toward the idea that every circumstance is good.
PART TEN — GRATITUDE DURING DIFFICULT SEASONS Now, I want to speak to someone who's having a difficult time feeling thankful.
Maybe this year has been painful.
Maybe you've experienced a loss.
Maybe you're facing uncertainty.
Or maybe you're simply exhausted.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to force yourself to feel cheerful in order to pray.
You can come before God honestly.
You can acknowledge your grief.
You can ask for help.
And you can still recognize His mercy.
Now, let's turn to Lamentations chapter 3. We're going to read verses 21 through 23. The King James Version says: "This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."
Now, remember the setting.
Lamentations is a book of sorrow.
It reflects on the destruction of Jerusalem.
And yet, in the middle of grief, the writer remembers God's mercy.
Now, that's a powerful picture.
Not because the suffering has disappeared.
But because hope is grounded in God's faithfulness.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude can be an expression of faith even when life remains difficult.
PART ELEVEN — LEARNING CONTENTMENT Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 4. We're going to read verses 11 through 13. The King James Version says: "Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me."
Now, I want you to notice something. Paul speaks about learning contentment.
He has experienced both abundance and need.
And he describes the strength he receives through Christ.
Now, here's something important. Philippians 4:13 isn't a promise that we can accomplish anything we imagine.
In context, Paul is describing Christ's strength in circumstances of both plenty and hardship.
Now, that's meaningful.
Because contentment isn't the same thing as having everything we want.
It involves learning to trust Christ in changing circumstances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Christian contentment is rooted in Christ's sustaining strength, not in the guarantee of comfortable circumstances.
PART TWELVE — GRATITUDE SHOULD LEAD TO HUMILITY Now, I want us to think about something.
Sometimes when things go well, we begin assuming that everything happened because of our own efforts.
We worked hard.
We made good decisions.
We accomplished our goals.
Now, hard work and wise decisions matter.
But Scripture reminds us that every good gift comes from God.
Now, that should lead us toward humility.
We can appreciate the work we've done without becoming prideful.
We can celebrate accomplishments without looking down on others.
And we can recognize that our abilities, opportunities, and resources are things we should steward responsibly.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude reminds us that our lives are dependent on God's goodness rather than entirely on our own abilities.
PART THIRTEEN — GRATITUDE SHOULD LEAD TO GENEROSITY Now, let's talk about something practical.
Because gratitude shouldn't remain only a feeling.
It should influence the way we treat others.
When we recognize the kindness we've received, we can become more intentional about showing kindness.
When we remember people who've helped us, we can look for opportunities to help others.
And when we recognize God's generosity, we can seek to steward our resources responsibly.
Now, that doesn't mean we give beyond what we can safely afford.
And it doesn't mean we neglect our responsibilities.
But generosity can take many forms.
Time.
Encouragement.
Practical assistance.
Hospitality.
Or sharing resources with someone in need.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A grateful heart should increasingly become evident through humility, compassion, and generosity.
PART FOURTEEN — LOOKING BACK OVER OUR TWELVE-WEEK JOURNEY Now, I want us to take a moment and think about this Bible study journey.
We've spent nearly twelve weeks opening God's Word together.
We've studied faith.
We've talked about trusting God when we cannot see the way.
We've explored waiting.
We've studied joy.
We've reflected on the promises of Christmas.
And now we're preparing to walk forward into a new year.
Now, I want you to think about something. Has there been a Scripture passage that stayed with you?
A lesson that challenged you?
A prayer that helped you put something into words?
Or a truth that encouraged you during a difficult day?
Now, here's something important. The goal of Bible study isn't simply to finish a series.
It's to grow in our knowledge of God and His Word.
To understand the gospel more deeply.
And to live in faithful response to what we've learned.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The value of our time in Scripture isn't measured only by the number of lessons completed, but by how we respond to God's truth.
PART FIFTEEN — WHAT IF THIS YEAR WASN'T WHAT YOU HOPED? Now, I want to speak to someone who may be approaching the end of the year with disappointment.
Maybe you had goals that didn't happen.
Maybe you hoped a relationship would be restored.
Maybe you prayed for a particular outcome.
Or maybe you're still waiting for something important.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to pretend the year was wonderful.
And you don't have to describe every painful event as a blessing.
But you can still recognize God's mercy.
You can still remember His promises.
And you can still approach the future with faith.
Now, here's something important. Sometimes gratitude looks like joyful celebration.
And sometimes it looks like a quiet prayer.
Lord, thank You for Your mercy.
Thank You for Your Word.
And thank You for the hope I have through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude doesn't require a perfect year. It calls us to remember the goodness of God.
PAUSE AND PRAY — THANK YOU, LORD Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about three things.
First... One blessing you've experienced this year.
Second... One person who has encouraged or helped you.
And third... One truth from Scripture that has strengthened your faith.
Now, take a moment to remember those things. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your goodness. Thank You for Your mercy. And thank You for Your faithfulness. Lord, as we look back over this year, help us remember the blessings we've received. Thank You for the people who've encouraged us. For the opportunities we've been given.
