And for the ways Your Word has guided us. Father, we also acknowledge the difficult moments. The grief. The disappointments. And the circumstances we still don't understand. Help us bring those things before You honestly. Teach us to give thanks without denying our pain. And remind us that our greatest hope is found in Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
PART SIXTEEN — A GRATEFUL HEART PREPARES FOR THE FUTURE Now, before we move into our reflection questions, I want us to consider something.
As we prepare for a new year, it's natural to think about what we want to change.
New goals.
New responsibilities.
New opportunities.
And new habits.
But perhaps we should also ask... What do I want to remember?
What lessons do I want to carry forward?
What blessings have I overlooked?
And how can I become more intentional about giving thanks?
Now, here's something important. Gratitude isn't meant to replace wise planning.
But it can shape the attitude with which we approach the future.
Instead of assuming we're entitled to every opportunity, we can recognize God's goodness.
Instead of focusing only on what we lack, we can acknowledge what we've received.
And instead of measuring our lives only by accomplishments, we can remember the mercy of God.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A grateful heart can help us approach the future with humility, wisdom, and faith.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What are three blessings from this past year that I may have overlooked? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... Who has encouraged, supported, or helped me during this journey, and how can I express my appreciation? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What Scripture passage or biblical truth has helped me remember God's faithfulness during a difficult season? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I make gratitude a more intentional part of my daily relationship with God? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — OUR GREATEST REASON FOR GRATITUDE Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because He is our greatest reason for thanksgiving.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through faith in Him, sinners receive forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. Our greatest hope isn't found in having a perfect year.
It isn't found in financial success.
And it isn't found in accomplishing every goal.
Our greatest hope is found in Jesus Christ.
Salvation is God's gracious gift through faith in Him.
And that gives us a reason for gratitude that extends beyond our changing circumstances.
Now, that's the heart of the gospel.
And that's why remembering God's faithfulness matters so much.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. Gratitude doesn't mean every chapter of your story was easy or good. It means remembering God's mercy, recognizing His gifts, and trusting His faithfulness even when life remains difficult.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because you can be grateful without pretending.
And you can remember God's goodness while still acknowledging your pain.
LIVING IT OUT — A GRATITUDE REFLECTION Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... Gratitude for the Journey.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... Three blessings from this past year that I want to remember.
Second... One person I want to thank for their encouragement or support.
Third... One lesson from a difficult season that I want to carry forward.
And fourth... One way I can practice gratitude more intentionally in the coming year.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Thank God for His mercy.
Remember His faithfulness.
And ask Him to help you approach the future with wisdom and gratitude.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, as I look back over this year, I'm especially thankful for...
Our second prompt is... One difficult season where I need to remember Your faithfulness is...
And our third prompt is... Help me develop a more grateful heart by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will remember God's mercy, recognize His gifts, and give thanks for His faithfulness. My gratitude is rooted in Jesus Christ, not in the expectation that every circumstance will be easy.
Now, say that again. I will remember God's mercy, recognize His gifts, and give thanks for His faithfulness. My gratitude is rooted in Jesus Christ, not in the expectation that every circumstance will be easy.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Psalm 103, verse 2. "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:"
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about what it means to remember God's goodness.
Maybe you'll write down three things you're thankful for.
Maybe you'll reach out to someone who's helped you.
Maybe you'll spend time praising God in prayer.
Or maybe you'll encourage someone who's struggling to recognize the blessings still present in their life.
AROUND THE FIRE — WHAT ARE YOU THANKFUL FOR? Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The fire is burning.
And we're reflecting on everything we've studied today.
Now, I want to ask you something. When you look back over this year, what are you most thankful for?
Maybe it's a relationship.
Maybe it's an opportunity.
Maybe it's a lesson you've learned.
Or maybe it's simply the encouragement you've received during a difficult season. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. How has remembering God's faithfulness changed the way you think about the future?
Maybe it's helped you become more patient.
Maybe it's encouraged you to pray more consistently.
Maybe it's reminded you to seek wisdom.
Or maybe it's helped you recognize that your hope rests in Jesus Christ. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. You don't have to describe every experience as good.
And you don't have to pretend the past year was perfect.
But you can recognize God's mercy.
You can remember His faithfulness.
And you can continue walking forward in faith.
CLOSING REFLECTION — DON'T FORGET Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
David said... "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:"
Now, I want you to think about those words. Don't forget.
Don't forget God's mercy.
Don't forget His lovingkindness.
Don't forget His forgiveness.
And don't forget His faithfulness.
As we prepare for a new year, it's natural to think about what lies ahead.
The decisions we'll make.
The responsibilities we'll carry.
And the opportunities we hope to receive.
But before we rush toward tomorrow, let's take a moment to remember.
Remember the truth of God's Word.
Remember the people who've encouraged us.
Remember the lessons we've learned.
And remember the hope we have through Jesus Christ.
Because gratitude isn't simply about looking backward.
It can also help shape the way we move forward.
With humility.
With wisdom.
And with faith.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for Your mercy. Your lovingkindness. And Your faithfulness. Lord, as we look back over this year, help us remember the blessings we've received. Thank You for the people who've encouraged us. For the lessons we've learned. And for the ways Your Word has strengthened our faith. Father, we also bring before You the difficult moments. The grief. The disappointments. And the circumstances we still don't understand. Help us approach those experiences with truth and wisdom. Teach us to give thanks without denying our pain. And remind us that our greatest hope is found in Jesus Christ. Lord, as we prepare for a new year, help us carry gratitude into our everyday lives. May our words and actions reflect humility, compassion, and love. And may everything we do bring glory to You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — LOOKING AHEAD TO DAY SIX Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Twelve, Day Five!
And I hope today's lesson has encouraged you to remember God's faithfulness.
Not because every moment has been easy.
But because His mercy and goodness are worthy of our praise.
Tomorrow, we're continuing our final week with a special Around the Fire reflection called... Around the Fire — Looking Back With Gratitude, Moving Forward With Faith.
We'll reflect on the lessons we've learned throughout this twelve-week journey and begin preparing our hearts for our final day together.
Until then, remember... Gratitude doesn't require a perfect journey. It calls us to remember the faithful God who has been with us through it.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking the Lord.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: Around the Fire: Looking Back With Gratitude, Moving Forward With Faith
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — ONE MORE EVENING AROUND THE FIRE Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles, and I'm so thankful you're here with me today.
Today is Week Twelve, Day Six. And I have to tell you... This one feels a little different.
Because tomorrow, we'll reach the final day of our twelve-week Bible study journey.
Twelve weeks. Eighty-two episodes by the time we're finished. And so many opportunities to open God's Word together.
Now, I don't know about you, but whenever I reach the end of something meaningful, I like to take a moment to reflect.
Not because I want to live in the past. But because I don't want to rush past the things I've learned.
And that's exactly what we're doing today.
We're gathering around the fire one more time before our final lesson.
Now, I want you to imagine something. The evening is quiet. The sun has gone down. There's a fire burning in front of us. And we're sitting together, reflecting on the journey we've shared.
Some of us may be smiling as we remember the good moments.
Some of us may be thinking about prayers we've prayed.
Some may be remembering difficult seasons.
And some may be wondering what the future holds.
But tonight, we're not going to rush.
We're going to remember. We're going to give thanks. And we're going to look toward Jesus Christ.
Because the purpose of this Bible study was never simply to complete a series.
It was to grow in our understanding of God's Word. To know Jesus more deeply. And to learn what it means to walk with Him in everyday life.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Finishing a Bible study is a meaningful accomplishment, but continuing to follow Jesus Christ is the lifelong calling.
And that's what we're talking about today. Around the Fire — Looking Back With Gratitude, Moving Forward With Faith.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us together for another day in Your Word. Thank You for the time we've spent studying Scripture. Thank You for every lesson that has challenged us. Every truth that has encouraged us. And every opportunity we've had to grow. Lord, as we reflect on this journey, help us remember Your faithfulness. Teach us to recognize Your mercy without pretending that every season has been easy. Give comfort to those who are grieving. Strength to those who are weary. And wisdom to those facing uncertain circumstances. Father, help us carry the truth of Your Word into our daily lives. And may everything we've studied draw us closer to Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S FIRST SCRIPTURE — JOSHUA 4:1–7 Now, let's turn to Joshua chapter 4. We're going to read verses 1 through 7.
Before we begin, let's understand the setting. The Israelites have crossed the Jordan River.
God has brought them through the river on dry ground as they prepare to enter the promised land.
And after this remarkable event, the Lord gives Joshua instructions.
Twelve men are to take twelve stones from the Jordan.
These stones will serve as a memorial.
A reminder of what God has done.
Let's read Joshua chapter 4, verses 1 through 7, from the King James Version. "And it came to pass, when all the people were clean passed over Jordan, that the LORD spake unto Joshua, saying, Take you twelve men out of the people, out of every tribe a man, And command ye them, saying, Take you hence out of the midst of Jordan, out of the place where the priests' feet stood firm, twelve stones, and ye shall carry them over with you, and leave them in the lodging place, where ye shall lodge this night. Then Joshua called the twelve men, whom he had prepared of the children of Israel, out of every tribe a man: And Joshua said unto them, Pass over before the ark of the LORD your God into the midst of Jordan, and take you up every man of you a stone upon his shoulder, according unto the number of the tribes of the children of Israel: That this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean ye by these stones? Then ye shall answer them, That the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD; when it passed over Jordan, the waters of Jordan were cut off: and these stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever."
Now, I want you to think about that. Twelve stones.
A memorial.
Something future generations could see.
And when the children asked what those stones meant, their families could tell them about God's mighty work.
Now, that's important. Because the stones weren't magical.
They weren't meant to become objects of worship.
They were reminders of what the Lord had done for His people.
And they created an opportunity to pass that testimony from one generation to the next.
TODAY'S SECOND SCRIPTURE — HEBREWS 12:1–2 Now, let's turn to Hebrews chapter 12. We're going to read verses 1 and 2.
These verses follow Hebrews chapter 11, where we read about people who lived by faith.
And the writer encourages believers to persevere.
Let's read Hebrews chapter 12, verses 1 and 2, from the King James Version. "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."
Now, I want you to focus on those words. "Let us run with patience the race that is set before us..."
And then... "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith..."
Now, those two passages give us a beautiful picture for today's lesson.
Joshua reminds us of the importance of remembering God's works.
And Hebrews reminds us to continue persevering in faith.
We remember.
And we keep walking.
We give thanks.
And we keep looking toward Jesus.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Remembering God's faithfulness should strengthen our gratitude, deepen our trust in His Word, and encourage us to continue following Jesus Christ.
Now, let's spend some time reflecting together.
PART ONE — WHY GOD TOLD ISRAEL TO REMEMBER Now, let's return to Joshua chapter 4.
God instructed Israel to set up a memorial.
And I want you to notice something. He didn't simply tell them to enjoy the moment and move on.
He gave them a way to remember.
Now, that's meaningful. Because sometimes extraordinary events become distant memories.
Generations pass. Circumstances change. And people may forget the significance of what happened.
But the memorial stones would help future generations learn about God's mighty work.
Now, here's something important. We're not called to recreate Israel's memorial exactly.
But we can learn from the biblical emphasis on remembering and teaching God's works.
Now, I want you to think about something. What truths from Scripture do you want the next generation to know?
What do you want your children or grandchildren to understand about Jesus Christ?
What lessons have you learned that could help someone else?
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Remembering God's faithfulness should lead us to teach His truth, not simply celebrate our own experiences.
PART TWO — WHAT ARE YOUR MEMORIAL STONES? Now, I want to ask you something.
If you were to identify a few meaningful reminders from your own journey, what would they be?
Maybe a Scripture passage.
Maybe a prayer you wrote down.
Maybe a lesson you learned during a difficult season.
Or maybe a moment when someone encouraged you through God's Word.
Now, I want you to think about something. Sometimes we need reminders.
Not because God has changed.
But because our circumstances can make it difficult to remember what we know to be true.
Now, perhaps you keep a prayer journal.
Maybe you write down meaningful Scripture passages.
Maybe you have notes from Bible studies.
Or maybe you share testimonies with your family.
Now, those things can help us remember.
But here's something important. Our personal experiences should always be understood in light of Scripture.
We shouldn't treat every event as though we know God's hidden purpose behind it.
Instead, we can remember what His Word clearly reveals.
His holiness. His mercy. His faithfulness. And His saving work through Jesus Christ.
PART THREE — REMEMBERING DOESN'T MEAN LIVING IN THE PAST Now, let's talk about something important.
Because there is a difference between remembering and becoming trapped in the past.
Remembering can help us learn.
It can help us give thanks.
And it can help us recognize God's faithfulness.
But sometimes we become so focused on yesterday that we neglect the responsibilities in front of us today.
Maybe we're replaying a mistake.
Maybe we're holding on to disappointment.
Or maybe we're comparing everything happening now to something that happened years ago.
Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 3. We're going to read verses 13 and 14. The King James Version says: "Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus."
Now, Paul isn't saying that we should erase every memory.
He's describing his continuing pursuit of Christ.
And that's the balance I want us to remember.
We can learn from the past.
We can give thanks for what God has done.
And we can continue moving forward.
Remember faithfully. But keep following Jesus.
PART FOUR — GRATITUDE FOR THE GOOD SEASONS Now, let's take a moment to reflect on the good things.
Because sometimes we move so quickly from one responsibility to the next that we forget to appreciate the blessings we've received.
Maybe this year included a meaningful accomplishment.
Maybe you developed a new friendship.
Maybe you had an opportunity to serve.
Maybe you experienced encouragement from someone you didn't expect.
Or maybe you simply enjoyed moments with the people you love.
Now, let's turn to Psalm 103. We're going to read verses 1 and 2. The King James Version says: "Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:"
Now, I want you to notice those words. "Forget not..."
Now, here's something I want you to think about. Have you taken time to thank God for the good things you've experienced?
Have you thanked the people who've helped you?
Have you recognized the opportunities you've been given?
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude helps us recognize God's gifts rather than taking them for granted.
PART FIVE — REMEMBERING THE HARD SEASONS HONESTLY Now, I want to talk about the difficult seasons.
Because not every memory from this year will be joyful.
Some of us have experienced grief.
Some have faced illness.
Some have dealt with financial struggles.
Some have experienced broken relationships.
And some are still walking through circumstances that haven't been resolved.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to pretend those experiences were good.
And you don't have to describe every painful event as a blessing.
Scripture gives us room for lament.
For sorrow.
And for honest prayer.
Now, here's something important. We can remember God's faithfulness without claiming to understand why every difficult thing happened.
We can acknowledge suffering while continuing to trust His character.
And we can seek support when the burdens we're carrying are too heavy to manage alone.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful remembrance includes honesty about suffering, not denial of it.
PART SIX — THE SCRIPTURES THAT CARRIED US Now, let's think about the Word of God.
Because throughout this journey, we've opened Scripture together.
We've studied passages about faith.
Trust.
Hope.
Peace.
Joy.
And perseverance.
Now, I want you to think about something. Has there been a particular verse that stayed with you?
Maybe Proverbs 3:5. "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding."
Maybe Psalm 119:105. "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."
Or maybe Lamentations 3:23. "They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."
Now, I want you to remember something. Scripture isn't simply a collection of inspirational sayings.
It's God's Word.
And we should seek to understand it carefully, in context, and apply it faithfully.
Now, let's turn to 2 Timothy chapter 3. We're going to read verses 16 and 17. The King James Version says: "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works."
Now, that's why Bible study matters.
Because Scripture teaches us.
Corrects us.
And equips us for faithful living.
PART SEVEN — WHAT HAS CHANGED IN YOUR WALK WITH GOD? Now, I want to ask you something personal.
As you think back over these twelve weeks, what has changed in your relationship with God?
Maybe you've become more consistent in prayer.
Maybe you've developed a stronger habit of reading Scripture.
Maybe you've begun asking better questions when studying the Bible.
Maybe you've recognized an area where you need to repent.
Or maybe you've become more willing to seek wisdom before making decisions.
Now, here's something important. Not everyone will experience dramatic changes in twelve weeks.
Some growth is gradual.
Some lessons take time to understand.
And some areas of our lives require ongoing attention.
But we can continue learning.
Continue repenting.
And continue pursuing Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Spiritual growth is not measured only by dramatic experiences, but by a continuing life of faith and obedience.
PART EIGHT — THE PEOPLE WHO WALKED BESIDE US Now, I want us to think about something else.
The people who have encouraged us along the way.
Maybe someone invited you to join this Bible study.
Maybe someone shared a Scripture passage with you.
Maybe someone prayed with you.
Maybe someone listened when you needed to talk.
Or maybe someone offered practical help during a difficult season.
Now, I want you to think about something. Have you thanked them?
Sometimes we appreciate people deeply, but we never actually tell them.
Now, perhaps today would be a good opportunity.
A phone call.
A message.
Or a simple conversation.
Thank you for being there.
Thank you for encouraging me.
Thank you for helping me.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Gratitude toward God should also shape the way we recognize and appreciate the people He's placed in our lives.
PART NINE — THE RACE ISN'T OVER Now, let's return to Hebrews chapter 12.
The writer says: "Let us run with patience the race that is set before us..."
Now, I want you to think about those words. The race.
Not a single step.
Not one day.
Not one Bible study.
But a continuing journey of faith.
Now, here's something important. Completing this twelve-week series doesn't mean we've completed our spiritual growth.
We still have Scripture to study.
Prayers to pray.
Responsibilities to fulfill.
And opportunities to serve others.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Our Bible study series may be approaching its conclusion, but our calling to follow Jesus Christ continues.
PART TEN — LAYING ASIDE WHAT HINDERS US Now, let's look at another part of Hebrews chapter 12, verse 1.
"Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us..."
Now, I want you to think about that.
As we prepare for a new year, perhaps there are things we need to address.
Sinful habits.
Unhealthy patterns.
Unnecessary distractions.
Or responsibilities we've been avoiding.
Now, here's something important. Not every burden is sin.
Grief isn't automatically sin.
Illness isn't automatically sin.
And struggling emotionally doesn't mean someone is spiritually failing.
But we can ask God for wisdom to recognize what needs repentance, what needs practical attention, and what requires support.
Now, let me ask you something. Is there something you need to address before moving into the next season of your life? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's something I want you to remember. Moving forward faithfully involves honesty about what needs to change and wisdom about how to respond.
PART ELEVEN — LOOKING UNTO JESUS Now, let's focus on Hebrews chapter 12, verse 2.
"Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith..."
Now, I love those words.
Because they remind us where our attention belongs.
Not simply on our accomplishments.
Not simply on our failures.
And not simply on our plans for the future.
But on Jesus Christ.
The One who endured the cross.
The One who rose again.
And the One in whom our salvation is found.
Now, here's something important. Christian perseverance isn't simply about becoming more determined.
It's about continuing in faith through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The center of our journey is not our personal success. It is Jesus Christ.
PART TWELVE — GRATITUDE FOR UNANSWERED QUESTIONS Now, I want to speak to someone who may still have unanswered questions.
Maybe you prayed for something throughout this series.
And you're still waiting.
Maybe you're facing a difficult decision.
Maybe you're still grieving.
Or maybe you're still trying to understand a painful experience.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to resolve every question before this Bible study ends.
You don't have to pretend that every concern has disappeared.
And you don't have to manufacture a happy ending.
But you can continue seeking the Lord.
You can continue praying.
You can continue studying Scripture.
And you can seek appropriate support when needed.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. An unfinished circumstance doesn't mean your relationship with God has stopped growing.
PART THIRTEEN — WHAT WILL YOU CARRY FORWARD? Now, let's begin looking toward the future.
Because tomorrow is our final day together in this series.
And I want you to think about something. What will you carry forward?
Maybe it's a stronger commitment to Scripture.
Maybe it's a more consistent prayer routine.
Maybe it's a lesson about patience.
Maybe it's a deeper understanding of the gospel.
Or maybe it's a willingness to ask for help when you need it.
Now, here's something important. We don't have to carry every habit or pattern from the past into the future.
We can repent where repentance is needed.
We can learn from our experiences.
And we can continue growing in faith.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The goal isn't simply to remember what we've studied. It's to continue responding faithfully to God's Word.
PART FOURTEEN — YOUR NEXT CHAPTER MAY LOOK DIFFERENT Now, I want to talk about something.
Because sometimes we assume that moving forward means life will become easier.
But Scripture doesn't promise that.
The next year may include blessings.
It may include responsibilities.
It may include unexpected changes.
And it may include challenges.
Now, here's something important. We don't know exactly what the future holds.
But we do know what Scripture teaches about God's character.
He is faithful.
He is wise.
He is holy.
And He is merciful.
Now, that gives us a foundation for trust.
Not because we know every outcome.
But because we know the God revealed in Scripture.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. We can approach an uncertain future with faith because our confidence rests in God's character rather than in our ability to predict what will happen.
PART FIFTEEN — PASS THE TESTIMONY FORWARD Now, let's return one more time to Joshua chapter 4.
Remember what God said about the memorial stones?
When the children asked what they meant, their families were to explain what the Lord had done.
Now, that's a beautiful reminder of the importance of teaching future generations.
And I want you to think about something. Who could benefit from what you've learned?
Maybe your children.
Maybe your grandchildren.
Maybe a friend.
Maybe someone at church.
Or maybe someone who's going through a difficult season.
Now, you don't have to have every answer to share what Scripture teaches.
And you don't have to be a professional speaker.
You can simply encourage someone.
Share a passage.
Pray with them.
Or invite them to study God's Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. What we learn from Scripture can become an opportunity to encourage and teach others.
PAUSE AND PRAY — THANK YOU FOR THE JOURNEY Now, let's take a moment to pause.
I want you to think about three things.
First... One truth from Scripture that has strengthened your faith.
Second... One blessing or act of kindness you're thankful for.
And third... One area where you want to continue growing.
Now, take a moment to reflect. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Let's pray. Heavenly Father, Thank You for this journey through Your Word. Thank You for every lesson we've studied. Every Scripture passage we've read. And every opportunity we've had to grow. Lord, help us remember Your faithfulness. Teach us to give thanks for Your mercy. And give us wisdom to apply what we've learned. Father, I pray for those who are still facing difficult circumstances. Comfort those who are grieving. Strengthen those who are weary. And guide those who need wisdom. Help us continue pursuing Jesus Christ. May our lives reflect Your truth, love, and grace. In His precious name, Amen.
PART SIXTEEN — OUR FINAL DAY IS ALMOST HERE Now, before we move into our reflection questions, I want to take a moment to speak from my heart.
If you've been walking through this Bible study with me, I want to thank you.
Thank you for making time to open God's Word.
Thank you for being willing to learn.
Thank you for reflecting on difficult questions.
And thank you for allowing me to be part of your Bible study journey.
Now, I want you to understand something. My hope has never been that you would simply listen to me.
My hope is that you would open your Bible.
Read Scripture for yourself.
Grow in your understanding of God's truth.
And continue developing your relationship with Jesus Christ.
Because this journey isn't about me.
And it's not about completing a podcast.
It's about the Lord.
His Word.
And the saving grace we have through Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. The greatest outcome of this Bible study would be a deeper love for God's Word and a continuing commitment to follow Jesus.
LET'S REFLECT TOGETHER Now, let's work through today's reflection questions.
If you have your journal nearby, take a moment to write down your answers.
Our first question is... What Scripture passage from these twelve weeks has had the greatest impact on me, and why? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our second question is... What have I learned about God's character that I want to remember when life becomes difficult? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our third question is... What area of my spiritual life has grown, and where do I still need to mature? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Our fourth question is... How can I continue studying Scripture and encouraging others after this series ends? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS]
CHRIST CONNECTION — THE CENTER OF OUR JOURNEY Now, let's bring everything back to Jesus.
Because He's the reason this journey matters.
The eternal Son of God became flesh.
He lived a sinless life.
He died on the cross for our sins.
And He rose again.
Through faith in Him, sinners receive forgiveness and the promise of eternal life.
Now, here's something important. We don't earn salvation by completing a Bible study.
We don't earn it by memorizing enough Scripture.
And we don't earn it by accomplishing spiritual goals.
Salvation is God's gracious gift through faith in Jesus Christ.
And our study of Scripture should help us know Him more deeply and respond to His grace with faith and obedience.
Now, that's the heart of the gospel.
And that's the foundation of everything we've studied together.
GRACE NOTE Now, here's today's Grace Note. Remember what God has revealed. Give thanks for His faithfulness. Learn from the journey behind you, and keep looking toward Jesus Christ as you walk into what comes next.
Now, I want you to remember that.
Because our Bible study series may be nearing its conclusion.
But our walk with Jesus continues.
LIVING IT OUT — MY TWELVE-WEEK REFLECTION Now, let's make today's lesson practical.
I want you to take a page in your journal.
And write down the words... My Twelve-Week Faith Journey.
Now, beneath that heading, write down four things.
First... Three Scripture passages I want to remember.
Second... Two lessons that challenged or encouraged me.
Third... One area where I want to continue growing spiritually.
And fourth... One way I can encourage someone else through what I've learned.
Now, after you've written those things down, take a moment to pray.
Thank God for His Word.
Remember His faithfulness.
And ask Him for wisdom as you continue growing in faith.
PRAYER JOURNAL Our first journal prompt is... Lord, one truth from Your Word that I want to carry forward is...
Our second prompt is... As I reflect on this journey, I'm especially thankful for...
And our third prompt is... Help me continue growing in faith by...
Now, take time to pray over those answers.
FAITH BUILDER Here's today's Faith Builder. I will remember God's faithfulness, continue studying His Word, and keep looking toward Jesus Christ. My journey of faith does not end when this Bible study ends.
Now, say that again. I will remember God's faithfulness, continue studying His Word, and keep looking toward Jesus Christ. My journey of faith does not end when this Bible study ends.
FAITH CHALLENGE Here's today's Faith Challenge. Memorize Hebrews chapter 12, verse 2. "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."
Now, throughout the day, return to those words.
And think about what it means to keep your attention on Jesus Christ.
Maybe you'll spend time reviewing your notes from this Bible study.
Maybe you'll share a meaningful Scripture passage with someone.
Maybe you'll write down a testimony of God's mercy.
Or maybe you'll make a plan to continue studying Scripture after our final episode.
AROUND THE FIRE — ONE LAST REFLECTION BEFORE TOMORROW Now, let's imagine we're sitting together around the fire.
The evening is quiet.
The flames are burning.
And we're reflecting on the journey we've shared.
Now, I want you to look back over these twelve weeks.
Think about the lessons.
The Scriptures.
The prayers.
And the moments that challenged you to grow.
Now, I want to ask you something. If you could share one thing you've learned with someone who's just beginning their walk with Jesus, what would it be? [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, here's another question. What do you want your relationship with God to look like as you continue into the next season of your life?
Maybe you want to become more consistent in prayer.
Maybe you want to study Scripture more deeply.
Maybe you want to serve others more intentionally.
Or maybe you want to develop greater trust in God's faithfulness. [PAUSE FOR 10 SECONDS] Now, I want you to remember something. You don't have to have every answer.
You don't have to become perfect overnight.
And you don't have to know everything the future holds.
But you can continue seeking Jesus Christ.
You can continue studying His Word.
And you can continue walking forward in faith.
CLOSING REFLECTION — THE JOURNEY CONTINUES Now, before we close, I want to leave you with one final thought.
Joshua chapter 4 reminds us to remember God's works.
And Hebrews chapter 12 reminds us to keep running the race set before us.
Now, I think those two truths belong together.
Remember.
And keep walking.
Give thanks.
And keep following Jesus.
Learn from yesterday.
And remain faithful today.
Because the Christian life isn't simply about reaching a particular milestone.
It's about continuing in faith.
Continuing in obedience.
And continuing to grow in our knowledge of Jesus Christ.
Now, tomorrow we'll complete this twelve-week series.
But I hope you'll remember something. The end of this study doesn't have to mean the end of your time in God's Word.
In fact, I hope it encourages you to keep going.
Keep reading.
Keep learning.
Keep praying.
And keep sharing the hope of Jesus Christ with others.
Because there is still so much to learn from God's Word.
And our journey of faith continues.
CLOSING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for Your Word today. Thank You for this journey we've shared. And thank You for every opportunity we've had to grow in faith. Lord, help us remember Your goodness. Teach us to give thanks for Your mercy. And remind us of the hope we have through Jesus Christ. Father, help us learn from the past. Give us wisdom for today. And strengthen our faith as we look toward the future. May we continue studying Scripture. Growing in obedience. And encouraging others. Lord, help us keep our eyes on Jesus Christ. The author and finisher of our faith. And may everything we do bring glory to You. In His precious name, Amen.
OUTRO — TOMORROW IS OUR FINAL DAY Thank you so much for joining me today on Walking Through the Word. We've officially completed Week Twelve, Day Six!
And tomorrow... We'll reach the final day of our twelve-week Bible study journey.
Our final episode is called... The Journey Continues — Walking Into the New Year With Jesus.
We'll celebrate what we've learned, reflect on our commitment to continue growing in faith, and close this series by looking toward the One who has been at the center of every lesson. Jesus Christ.
Until then, remember... The most important thing isn't simply how far you've come. It's continuing to walk with the Lord.
Keep opening your Bible. Keep praying. And keep seeking Him.
And as always... You don't have to walk through the fire alone. Keep the faith. Keep walking. There is another side of the fire. God bless you, and I'll see you tomorrow!

lessons.title: The Journey Continues: Walking Into the New Year With Jesus
lessons.body:
INTRODUCTION — WE MADE IT, BUT THE JOURNEY ISN'T OVER Hey, everyone! Welcome back to Walking Through the Word. I'm your host, Jessica Riles. And today...
Today is a very special day.
Because we've officially reached Week Twelve, Day Seven. Our eighty-second episode. And the final day of this twelve-week Bible study journey.
Can you believe it?
Twelve weeks of opening God's Word together. Twelve weeks of prayer. Reflection. Encouragement. And learning what it means to walk with Jesus Christ through the different seasons of life.
Now, I have to tell you something. As I prepared for this final episode, I found myself thinking about the journey we've shared.
I thought about the Scriptures we've studied. The questions we've asked. The prayers we've prayed. And the lessons that have challenged us to grow.
And I realized something. This may be our final episode of this particular series...
But it is not the end of our journey with Jesus.
In fact, I hope it's just the beginning of an even deeper relationship with Him.
Because the purpose of this Bible study was never simply to complete eighty-two episodes.
It was never about checking another item off a list.
And it was never about listening to my voice every day.
My prayer has always been that you would grow in your love for God's Word. That you would open your Bible for yourself. That you would come to know Jesus Christ more deeply. And that you would learn to trust Him through whatever life brings.
Now, maybe you've listened to every episode.
Maybe you've missed a few days.
Maybe you're still catching up.
Or maybe you joined us somewhere in the middle.
Whatever your journey has looked like, I'm thankful you're here today.
And I want you to hear something. Your relationship with God isn't measured by how many podcast episodes you've completed.
It's about knowing Jesus Christ. Trusting Him. Learning His Word. And following Him.
So today, we're going to look back with gratitude. We're going to reflect on what Scripture has taught us. And we're going to look forward with faith.
Because today's lesson is called... The Journey Continues — Walking Into the New Year With Jesus.
Let's begin with prayer.
OPENING PRAYER Heavenly Father, Thank You for bringing us to this final day of our twelve-week Bible study journey. Thank You for every opportunity we've had to open Your Word. Thank You for the Scriptures that have encouraged us. The truths that have challenged us. And the lessons that have helped us grow. Lord, today we're not simply celebrating the completion of a series. We're celebrating the opportunity to know You through Jesus Christ. Father, I pray for every person listening. For those who have been encouraged. For those who are still struggling. For those who are grieving. And for those who are uncertain about what comes next. Help us remember that our walk with You continues beyond this moment. Give us a deeper hunger for Scripture. A stronger commitment to prayer. And a growing desire to live according to Your truth. May everything we study today point us toward Jesus Christ. In His precious name, Amen.
TODAY'S FIRST SCRIPTURE — COLOSSIANS 2:6–7 Now, let's turn to Colossians chapter 2. We're going to read verses 6 and 7.
Before we begin, let's understand the setting. The apostle Paul is writing to believers in Colossae.
And throughout this letter, he emphasizes the supremacy and sufficiency of Jesus Christ.
He warns believers against teachings that would draw them away from the truth of the gospel.
And he encourages them to remain grounded in Christ.
Now, let's read Colossians chapter 2, verses 6 and 7, from the King James Version. "As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving."
Now, I want you to hear those words again. "As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him:"
Now, I love that.
Because Paul doesn't tell believers to simply remember the day they first believed.
He calls them to continue walking in Christ.
To remain rooted in Him.
To be built up in Him.
And to remain established in the faith.
Now, that's the heart of today's lesson.
Our walk with Jesus doesn't end when we finish a Bible study.
It continues.
Day after day.
Season after season.
And year after year.
TODAY'S SECOND SCRIPTURE — PHILIPPIANS 1:6 Now, let's turn to Philippians chapter 1. We're going to read verse 6.
The apostle Paul is writing to the believers in Philippi.
And he expresses gratitude for their partnership in the gospel.
He also expresses confidence in God's continuing work among them.
Let's read Philippians chapter 1, verse 6, from the King James Version. "Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:"
Now, I want you to think about that.
"He which hath begun a good work in you..."
And... "Will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ."
Now, that's a beautiful reminder.
The Christian life isn't something we complete in twelve weeks.
God continues His work in His people.
And we're called to continue responding through faith and obedience.
Now, that brings us to today's key truth.
TODAY'S KEY TRUTH Our journey of faith doesn't end with the completion of a Bible study. Through Jesus Christ, we are called to continue growing, learning, serving, and walking in obedience to God's Word.
Now, let's spend this final lesson reflecting on what that means.
PART ONE — WE DIDN'T REACH THE FINISH LINE OF FAITH Now, let's begin with something important.
Today marks the end of a series.
But it doesn't mark the end of our spiritual growth.
Now, I want you to think about something. When we finish a project, we often celebrate because the work is complete.
We reach a goal.
We check something off our list.
And we move on to something else.
But our relationship with Jesus Christ isn't a project we finish.
It's a continuing life of faith.
We keep learning.
We keep praying.
We keep repenting when we sin.
And we keep growing in our understanding of God's Word.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Completing this Bible study is worth celebrating, but continuing to follow Jesus Christ is what matters most.
PART TWO — STAY ROOTED IN CHRIST Now, let's return to Colossians chapter 2, verse 7.
"Rooted and built up in him..."
Now, I want you to picture a tree.
A tree with deep roots.
Those roots help anchor the tree.
They help it draw nourishment from the soil.
And they help it remain standing when the wind blows.
Now, Paul uses the image of being rooted in Christ.
And that's important.
Because our spiritual foundation shouldn't rest on temporary emotions.
It shouldn't rest on a particular speaker.
And it shouldn't rest on a single Bible study series.
Our foundation is Jesus Christ.
Now, here's something I want you to think about. When life becomes difficult, where do you turn first?
Do you seek God's Word?
Do you pray?
Do you seek wisdom from mature believers?
Or do you allow your circumstances to determine everything you believe?
Now, here's something I want you to remember. A life rooted in Christ is built on His truth rather than on changing circumstances.
PART THREE — KEEP OPENING YOUR BIBLE Now, let's talk about something practical.
Because one of my greatest hopes for this series is that it has encouraged you to develop a deeper relationship with Scripture.
Not simply listening to someone explain the Bible.
But opening it for yourself.
Reading it.
Studying it.
And asking questions.
Now, let's turn to 2 Timothy chapter 3. We're going to read verses 16 and 17. The King James Version says: "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works."
Now, I want you to notice something. Scripture teaches.
It corrects.
And it equips.
Now, that's why studying the Bible matters.
It's not simply about finding a verse that makes us feel better.
It's about learning what God has revealed.
Understanding the gospel.
And allowing His truth to shape our lives.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Don't let the end of this series become the end of your daily time in God's Word.
PART FOUR — YOU DON'T HAVE TO UNDERSTAND EVERYTHING IMMEDIATELY Now, I want to encourage someone who may feel intimidated by Bible study.
Maybe you've opened Scripture and come across a passage you didn't understand.
Maybe you've struggled with unfamiliar names.
Historical events.
Or difficult teachings.
Now, I want you to hear something. You don't have to understand every passage immediately.
Bible study is a process.
And growing in our understanding takes time.
Sometimes we need to read a passage more than once.
Sometimes we need to study the historical setting.
Sometimes we need to compare Scripture with Scripture.
And sometimes we need guidance from trustworthy teachers.
Now, here's something important. We should approach Scripture with humility.
Not assuming that our first interpretation is always correct.
And not treating every verse as though it was written directly about our individual circumstances.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Faithful Bible study involves patience, context, humility, and a willingness to keep learning.
PART FIVE — WALK WITH JESUS DAILY Now, let's turn to Luke chapter 9. We're going to read verse 23. The King James Version says: "And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me."
Now, I want you to focus on one word. Daily.
Jesus calls His followers to a life of discipleship.
Not simply a one-time emotional experience.
Not simply attending a church service.
And not simply completing a Bible study.
But following Him.
Now, here's something important. Taking up our cross isn't simply a phrase for dealing with ordinary inconveniences.
In the context of Jesus' teaching, it points toward costly discipleship and willingness to follow Him even when obedience involves sacrifice.
Now, I want you to think about something. What does following Jesus look like in your everyday life?
Maybe it means choosing honesty when dishonesty would be easier.
Maybe it means showing kindness when you're frustrated.
Maybe it means resisting a sinful habit.
Or maybe it means remaining faithful when obedience comes at a cost.
Now, here's something I want you to remember. Following Jesus is a daily commitment, not simply an event we attend or a lesson we complete.
PART SIX — ABIDE IN CHRIST Now, let's turn to John chapter 15. We're going to read verses 4 and 5. The King James Version says: "Abide in me, and I in you.
